He grants grace when we drink the sweet, pure Tamil nectar of the hymns composed by our three flawless saints.
commentary: Past mistakes and wasted time must be left behind. Chanting the sweet Tamil hymns of the ancient saints opens a door to divine grace and offers a clear path forward.

translit: nāṭṭam uṟṟeṉai eḻumaiyum piriyā nalla neñcamē naṅkaiyar mayalāl vāṭṭam uṟṟivaṇ mayaṅkiṉai aiyō vāḻa vēṇṭiṭil varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē kōṭṭam aṟṟiru malarkkaram kūppik kumpi ṭumperum kuṇattavar tamakkut tāḷta lantarum oṟṟiyūrc celvat tantai yāraṭic caraṇpuka lāmē.
translation: O good heart, you love me and never part from me across seven births. Alas, you have faded and grown deluded here through infatuation with women. If you wish to live well, come with me. Let us take refuge at the feet of our wealthy Father of Otriyur. He grants the sanctuary of His feet to people of great character who worship Him by joining their two lotus-like hands without crookedness.
commentary: The heart is a loyal companion that travels with the soul across seven births, but it easily exhausts itself chasing worldly infatuations. Sanctuary requires straightforward devotion, approaching God with folded hands and an honest, uncrooked mind.

translit: uṭukka vēṇṭimuṉ uṭai-iḻan tārpōl uḷḷa vākumeṉ ṟuṉṉiṭā tiṉpam maṭukka vēṇṭimuṉ vāḻviḻan tāyē vāḻa vēṇṭiṭil varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē aṭukka vēṇṭiniṉ ṟaḻutaḻu tētti arunta vattiṉar aḻivuṟāp pavattait taṭukka vēṇṭinal oṟṟiyūrc celvat tantai yāraṭic caraṇpuka lāmē.
translation: Like those who lose their very clothes while desiring to dress better, you failed to consider what is true. You ruined your life by craving endless pleasures. If you wish to live well, come with me. Great ascetics stand, cry, and praise Him in their desire to draw near to Him and stop the endless cycle of birth. Let us take refuge at the feet of our wealthy Father of good Otriyur.
commentary: Greed for endless worldly pleasures is a trap that causes people to lose even what they already have. The wise weep for divine grace to break the cycle of birth and death, finding their only lasting security in God.

translit: mōka mātiyāl vellumaim pulaṉām mūṭa vēṭarai mutalaṟa eṟintu vākai īkuvaṉ varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē vañca vāḻkkaiyiṉ mayaṅkumeṉ neñcē pōka nīkkinal puṇṇiyam purintu pōṟṟi nāḷtoṟum pukaḻntiṭum avarkkuc cākai nīttaruḷ oṟṟiyūrc celvat tantai yāraṭic caraṇpuka lāmē.
translation: O my heart, you are deluded by this deceitful life. I will completely destroy the foolish hunters known as the five senses, who conquer through lust and other desires. I will grant you victory. Come with me. Let us take refuge at the feet of our wealthy Father of Otriyur. He grants the grace that conquers death to those who cast aside worldly pleasures, perform good deeds, and praise Him daily.
commentary: The five senses act like foolish hunters that trap the mind in deceitful desires. By rejecting these worldly distractions and focusing on good deeds and daily devotion, a person receives the grace that conquers death itself.

translit: paci-e ṭukkumuṉ amutucē karippār pāri ṉōrkaḷap paṇpaṟin tilaiyō vaci-e ṭukkumuṉ piṟappatai māṟṟā matiyil neñcamē varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē nici-e ṭukkumnal caṅkavai īṉṟa nitti lakkuvai neṟippaṭa ōṅkic caci-e ṭukkunal oṟṟiyūrc celvat tantai yāraṭic caraṇpuka lāmē.
translation: People of this world gather food before hunger strikes. Do you not know this habit? O mindless heart, you fail to prevent future births before your life force departs. Come with me. Heaps of pearls yielded by fine conches gathered in the night rise high and touch the moon in good Otriyur. Let us take refuge at the feet of our wealthy Father who dwells there.
commentary: Ordinary people prepare food long before hunger strikes. In the same way, the soul must seek divine refuge and secure its spiritual freedom before the life force departs, rather than waiting until the final moment.

sections.title: Ten Verses on the Bliss of Siva

note: Editor's note: sung at Otriyur and at Thillai (Chidambaram) (tiruvoṟṟiyūrum tiruttillaiyum, திருவொற்றியூரும் திருத்தில்லையும்).
translit: iccai uṇṭeṉak kuṉtiru malarttāḷ eytum vaṇṇamiṅ keṉceya vallēṉ koccai neñcameṉ kuṟippilnil lātu kutippil niṉṟatu matippiṉiv vulakil piccai uṇṭeṉiṟ piccariṟ cīṟum pēya ruṇmaṉai nāyeṉa uḻaittēṉ ceccai mēṉi-em tiruvoṟṟi aracē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: I desire to reach your sacred flower-feet. What can I do here? My base heart does not abide by my intention. It leaps restlessly. I have toiled like a dog in the houses of demonic people who hiss at beggars seeking alms in this world. O my king of sacred Otriyur with a form red as the ixora flower! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: A restless mind easily overwhelms the desire for grace. This sorrow is sharpened by the world's harsh reality, where one toils for uncharitable people just to survive. Refuge is found only in the sweet bliss of the Divine.

translit: aiya niṉṉuṭai aṉparkaḷ ellām aḻivil iṉpamuṟ ṟarukiruk kiṉṟār veyya neñcakap pāviyēṉ koṭiya vīṇa ṉēṉiṅku vīḻkatik kiṭamāy vaiya vāḻkkaiyiṉ mayaṅkukiṉ ṟaṉaṉmēl varuva tōrntilaṉ vāḻvaṭai vēṉō ceyya vaṇṇaṉē oṟṟiyam poruḷē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: O Lord! All your devotees experience imperishable bliss and remain near you. I am a sinner with a cruel heart. I am a terrible waster. I am deluded by worldly life here, fit only for a fallen state. I do not foresee what is to come. Will I ever attain true life? O crimson-hued one! O truth of Otriyur! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: While devotees live in lasting joy close to the Divine, the worldly mind feels cut off from that peace. Worldly life acts as a delusion. It leaves a person blind to the future and terrified of being permanently lost.

translit: maṭikoḷ neñciṉāl vaḷḷaluṉ malarttāḷ maṟantu vañcaka vāḻkkaiyai matittēṉ tuṭikoḷ nēriṭai maṭaviyark kurukic cuḻalkiṉ ṟēṉaruḷ cukampeṟu vēṉō vaṭikoḷ vēlkarat taṇṇalai īṉṟa vaḷḷa lē-eṉa vāḻttukiṉ ṟavartam ceṭikaḷ nīkkiya oṟṟiyam paraṉē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: With a lazy heart, I forgot your flower-feet, O benevolent Lord, and esteemed this deceitful life. I melt and wander after young women with waists slender as an hourglass drum. Will I ever attain the bliss of your grace? O supreme Lord of Otriyur, you remove the flaws of those who praise you as the benevolent one who begot the Lord holding the sharp spear! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: Sensual desires and spiritual laziness make people forget the Divine and value a deceitful way of life. Recognizing this failure is the first step toward asking for grace. Vallalar trusts that the supreme Lord removes the flaws of those who turn to him in praise.

translit: irukka vāvuṟa ulakelām uyya eṭutta cēvaṭik keḷḷaḷa vēṉum urukkam oṉṟilēṉ otiyiṉil periyēṉ oṇmai eytutal veṇmaimaṟ ṟaṉṟē tarukka niṉṟa-eṉ taṉmaiyai niṉaikkil tamiya ṉēṉukkē talainaṭuk kuṟuṅkāṇ tirukkaṇ mūṉṟuṭai oṟṟi-em poruḷē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: I have not even a sesame seed's worth of melting love for your red feet, raised in the cosmic dance so the Vedas flourish and the whole world is saved. I am bloated with useless talk. For me to attain brilliance is sheer foolishness. When I think of my arrogant nature, I tremble in terror. O our truth of Otriyur possessing three sacred eyes! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: Real devotion requires a heart that melts with love, not a mind full of empty, arrogant talk. Realizing one's own arrogance and lack of sincere feeling brings terror. Only the grace of the Lord, who dances to sustain the world, can bridge this gap.

translit: eṇpe ṟāviṉaik kētucey uṭalai eṭutta nāḷmutal intanāḷ varaikkum naṇpu ṟāppavam iyaṟṟiṉaṉ allāl naṉmai eṉpatōr nāḷiṉum aṟiyēṉ vaṇpe ṟāveṉak kuṉtiru aruḷām vāḻvu nērntiṭum vakai-enta vakaiyō tiṇpe ṟāniṟka aruḷoṟṟi amutē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: From the day I took this body forged by countless karmas until this day, I have committed nothing but hostile sins. I have never known goodness on any day. How will the true life of your sacred grace ever come to me, devoid of inner wealth? O nectar of Otriyur who grants grace to me as I stand bereft of strength! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: A life driven by past actions (karma) often feels like an unbroken chain of mistakes and hostility. Looking back and seeing no goodness in their actions, a person realizes they have no inner wealth to offer. In this state of exhaustion, they can only wait for Divine grace to save them.

translit: pētai neñciṉēṉ ceypiḻai ellām pēci ṉālperum piṇakkiṉuk kiṭamām tātai nī-avai eṇṇalai eḷiyēṉ taṉakku niṉtirut taṇaḷi purivāy kōtai nīkkiya muṉivarkaḷ kāṇak kūttu kantaruḷ kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟē tītai nīkkiya oṟṟi-em perumāṉ tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: If I speak of all the wrongs committed by my foolish heart, it will become a cause for great conflict. You are the Father. Do not count them. Grant your holy, cool grace to me, a lowly one. O great mountain of virtue who rejoices in the dance to bestow grace, witnessed by the flawless sages! Our Lord of Otriyur who dispels evil! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: God is a father who must overlook his child's mistakes. Counting every wrong thought or action only leads to argument and distance. Vallalar asks the Divine to ignore the tally and respond only with grace. He calls God the honey of Sivananda (the supreme bliss of the Divine), a presence that dispels evil by its nature.

translit: vañca neñcartam cērkkaiyait tuṟantu vaḷḷal uṉtiru malaraṭi ētti viñcu neñcartam aṭittuṇaik kēval virumpi niṟkumap perumpayaṉ peṟavē tañcam eṉṟaruḷ niṉtiruk kōyil cārntu niṉṟaṉaṉ tarutalmaṟ ṟiṉṟō ceñcol ōṅkiya oṟṟi-em perumāṉ tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: I abandoned the company of those with deceitful hearts. I praised your holy lotus feet, O benevolent Lord. To attain the great reward of standing with the desire to serve the two feet of those with exalted hearts, I came to your gracious holy temple declaring it my refuge. Will you not grant this to me today? Our Lord of Otriyur where pure words rise high! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: The greatest reward in spiritual life is the chance to serve people with compassionate hearts. Leaving behind deceitful company, Vallalar takes refuge in the Divine to earn this privilege. Seeking God's grace is the foundation for a life dedicated to serving others.

translit: pulla ṉēṉpuvi naṭaiyiṭai alaiyum pulaiya neñciṉāl poruntiṭum koṭiya allal eṉpataṟ kellai-oṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ aruntu kiṉṟaṉaṉ viruntiṉaṉ āki ollai uṉtiruk kōyilmuṉ aṭuttēṉ utta mā-uṉtaṉ uḷḷamiṅ kaṟiyēṉ cellal nīkkiya oṟṟiyam poruḷē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: I am a lowly one wandering in the ways of the world. I know no limit to the cruel afflictions that come through my base heart. I feast on them like a guest. I swiftly approached the front of your holy temple. O supreme one, I do not know your mind in this matter. O beautiful reality of Otriyur who removes distress! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: The human mind traps itself in worldly suffering and feeds on its own miseries like a guest at a feast. Realizing this endless cycle, Vallalar rushes to the Divine for rescue. He stands before God vulnerable, admitting his flaws and waiting to see how the supreme reality will respond.

translit: eḷiya ṉēṉpiḻai iyaṟṟiya ellām eṇṇi ṉuṭpaṭā vēṉummaṟ ṟavaiyai aḷiya nallaruḷ īntiṭum poruṭṭāl āytal naṉṟala ātaliṉ īṇṭē kaḷiya neñcamām karuṅkalaik karaittuk karuṇai īkutal kaṭaṉuṉak kaiyā teḷiya ōṅkiya oṟṟi-eṉ amutē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: All the wrongs I, a lowly one, have committed are beyond counting. Still, it is not good to investigate them when your purpose is to grant sweet, good grace. Therefore, right here, you must melt the black stone of this hardened heart. It is your duty to grant compassion, O Lord! My nectar of Otriyur rising in clarity! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: Because God's purpose is to give grace, judging a person's countless mistakes contradicts that nature. Vallalar reminds the Divine that it is God's duty to step in and melt the hardened human heart with compassion. Transforming a flawed soul through love is God's responsibility.

translit: veṟipi ṭikkiṉum makaṉtaṉaip peṟṟōr viṭutti ṭāranta veṟiyatu tīrum neṟipi ṭittuniṉ ṟāyvareṉ aracē nīyum appaṭi nīcaṉēṉ taṉakkup poṟipi ṭittanal pōtakam aruḷip puṉmai yāvaiyum pōkkiṭal vēṇṭum ceṟipi ṭittavāṉ poḻiloṟṟi amutē tillai ōṅkiya civāṉantat tēṉē.
translation: Even if a son goes mad, the parents who bore him will not abandon him. They will pursue the path to cure his madness and seek the remedy, O my King. You too must act that way for me, a base one. You must grant the good wisdom that masters the senses and remove all my baseness. O nectar of Otriyur with dense, sky-reaching groves! O honey of Siva's bliss exalted in Thillai!
commentary: Just as parents never abandon a child who loses their mind, God cannot abandon a soul trapped in worldly delusion. A mother or father will search for a cure to heal their child's madness. Similarly, the Divine must step in and provide the spiritual wisdom needed to cure the wandering mind and master the senses.

note: Editor's note: sung at Otriyur and at Thillai (Chidambaram) (tiruvoṟṟiyūrum tiruttillaiyum, திருவொற்றியூரும் திருத்தில்லையும்).
translit: oṟṟi mēviya uttama ṉēmaṇit teṟṟi mēviya tillaiyap pāviḻi neṟṟi mēviya niṉmala ṉē-uṉaip paṟṟi mēviya neñcamuṉ pālatē.
translation: O supreme Lord abiding in Otri! O Father of Thillai seated on the gem-studded dais! O pure Lord with an eye on your forehead! The heart that grasped you and held on remains entirely yours.
commentary: God is invoked through two sacred temples: Otri (Otriyur) and Thillai (Chidambaram). Once the heart takes hold of the divine, it remains bound to it completely.

translit: pāliṉ nīṟṟup parañcuṭa rēmalark kāliṉ īṟṟuk katipeṟa ēḻaiyēṉ māliṉ īṟṟu mayakkaṟal eṉṟukal āliṉ īṟṟup poruḷaruḷ ātiyē.
translation: O supreme flame wearing sacred ash white as milk! O primal Lord who imparted the ultimate truth beneath the stone banyan tree! When will the delusion born of my ignorance dispel so this poor wretch can attain the final state at your lotus feet?
commentary: Vallalar asks when his spiritual ignorance will end. The "stone banyan tree" refers to a story where Siva sat as a silent teacher to reveal the highest truth to seekers. Vallalar longs for that same clarity to wash away his confusion.

translit: āti yētillai ampalat tāṭalcey cōti yētirut tōṇipu rattaṉē ōti yētarum oṟṟiyap pā-itu nīti yē-eṉai nīmaru vātatē.
translation: O primal Lord! O Jothi dancing in the hall of Thillai! O Lord of sacred Thonipuram! O Father of Otri who imparts wisdom! Is it justice that you do not embrace me?
commentary: The longing for connection turns into a demand for justice. Vallalar questions whether it is fair for God to withhold a direct spiritual embrace.

translit: vātam ōtiya vañcaraik kāṇilōr kātam ōṭum kaṭiyaṉai āḷvatu nīta mō-aṉṟi nēruma nītamō ōtam ōtoli oṟṟitta lattaṉē.
translation: O Lord of Otri resounding with the roar of ocean waves! Is it justice or injustice to rule over this cruel one who runs a league away upon seeing deceitful people shouting empty arguments?
commentary: Vallalar expresses a strong distaste for religious debates. He tells God how he runs far away to avoid people who shout empty, deceitful arguments. He wonders aloud if saving someone who flees from such conflicts is an act of justice.

translit: talatta ṉētillaic caṅkara ṉētalaik kalatta ṉēneṟṟik kaṇṇuṭai yāḷaṉē nalatta ṉē-oṟṟi nāyaka ṉē-inta malatta ṉēṉaiyum vāḻvittal māṇpatē.
translation: O Lord of sacred places! O Shankara of Thillai! O Lord holding a skull for a bowl! O Lord possessing a forehead eye! O embodiment of goodness! O Lord of Otri! It is your great glory to uplift even this impurity-filled wretch.
commentary: Siva appears in his traditional form as a wandering ascetic holding a skull for a begging bowl. Vallalar contrasts this divine majesty with his own sense of impurity. Uplifting a flawed soul is the measure of God's greatness.

translit: māṇkoḷ ampala māṇikka mēviṭam ūṇkoḷ kaṇṭattem oṟṟiyap pā-uṉtaṉ ēṇkoḷ cēvaṭi iṉpukaḻ ēttiṭāk kōṇkoḷ neñcak koṭiyaṉum uyvaṉē.
translation: Glorious ruby of the Hall! Our Father of Otriyur with the poison-consuming throat! Will even I, a cruel one with a crooked heart who does not sing the sweet praise of your strong red feet, be saved?
commentary: Is there hope for a heart that feels flawed and disconnected from the divine? Vallalar calls on the ancient story of Siva swallowing deadly ocean poison to save the universe. If God's mercy is vast enough to consume poison to protect all beings, it is vast enough to save a stubborn, wandering mind.

translit: uyyum vaṇṇamiṅ kuṉaruḷ eytanāṉ ceyyum vaṇṇamte rintilaṉ celvamē peyyum vaṇṇappe rumuki lēpuram eyyum vaṇṇame rittaruḷ entaiyē.
translation: I do not know what I must do to attain your grace and be saved here. Oh Wealth! Oh great pouring cloud! Oh Father who shot an arrow to burn the cities and granted grace!
commentary: Sometimes a seeker does not know what actions to take to find peace. Comparing God to a pouring rain cloud, Vallalar asks for grace to fall freely and wash away confusion. He recalls the myth of God shooting a single arrow to burn three flying cities of demons, asking that same sudden divine power to destroy inner ignorance.

translit: entai yētillai emiṟai yēkukaṉ tantai yē-oṟṟit taṇamu tē-eṉtaṉ muntai ēḻpava mūṭama yakkaṟac cintai ētamti runta-a ruḷvaiyē.
translation: Oh my Father! Our Lord of Thillai! Father of Guhan! Oh cool ambrosia of Otriyur! Grant your grace to correct the flaws in my mind and sever the ignorant delusion of my past seven births.
commentary: The soul carries a heavy burden of habits and delusions built up over countless past lives, referred to here as the seven births. Vallalar pleads for divine grace to cut through this rooted ignorance and heal the mind's flaws. God is addressed intimately as a father, specifically of Guhan (the warrior god Murugan), and asked for cool, soothing nectar rather than harsh discipline.

translit: tirunta nāṉmaṟait tillaicciṟ ṟampalat tirunta ñāṉa-i yaloḷi yē-oṟṟip porunta niṉṟaruḷ puṇṇiya mē-iṅku varunta eṉtaṉai vaittata ḻakatō.
translation: Oh natural light of wisdom seated in the Little Hall of Thillai praised by the flawless four Vedas! Oh Merit who stands in harmony in Otriyur and grants grace! Is it fair that you have left me here to suffer?
commentary: God is recognized as the supreme light of wisdom praised by the Vedas, the ancient scriptures. Despite this immense reverence, Vallalar makes a human complaint: is it fair for such a perfect, harmonious God to leave a devoted seeker suffering alone in the world?

translit: vaitta niṉaruḷ vāḻiya vāḻiya meytta tillaiyiṉ mēviya iṉpamē uytta nalaruḷ oṟṟiyap pā-eṉaip poytta cintaiviṭ ṭuṉtaṉaip pōṟṟavē.
translation: Long live the grace you have bestowed, long live! Oh true bliss seated in Thillai! Oh Father of Otriyur who guides with good grace! Let me abandon my false mind and praise you.
commentary: Genuine devotion becomes possible only when the deceptive, wandering mind steps aside. Vallalar blesses the grace already received, celebrating it as the source of joy and direction. He trusts this divine guidance to help drop his false mind so he can offer pure praise.

translit: pōṟṟa vaittaṉai puṇṇiya ṉē-eṉaic cāṟṟa vaittaṉai niṉpukaḻt taṉmaiyait tēṟṟa vaittaṉai neñcaitte ḷintaṉpai ūṟṟa vaittaṉai uṉoṟṟi mēviyē.
translation: O Holy One residing in Your Otri! You made me offer praise. You made me proclaim the nature of Your glory. You brought clarity to my heart, and You made love spring forth.
commentary: Every step of a person's spiritual growth comes from divine grace. Vallalar acknowledges that he did not find devotion on his own. It was the Holy One, residing in Otri, who moved him to offer praise, cleared his mind, and made love well up in his heart.

tamil: வில்வத் தொடும்பொன் கொன்றைஅணி வேணிப் பெருமான் ஒற்றிநகர்
செல்வப் பெருமான் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருஅழகைக்
கல்வைப் புடைய மனம்களிக்கக் கண்கள் களிக்கக் கண்டுநின்றேன்
இல்வைப் புடையேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: vilvat toṭumpoṉ koṉṟai-aṇi vēṇip perumāṉ oṟṟinakar celvap perumāṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiru-aḻakaik kalvaip puṭaiya maṉamkaḷikkak kaṇkaḷ kaḷikkak kaṇṭuniṉṟēṉ ilvaip puṭaiyēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: I stood and gazed upon the divine beauty of the wealthy Lord of Otri city, Lord Siva, Lord Thyagar, who wears vilva leaves and golden konrai flowers in His matted hair. My stone-like heart rejoiced and my eyes delighted. Though bound to a household life, O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: Vallalar feels unworthy of the vision. She marvels that someone leading an ordinary family life, with a heart hard as stone, could be granted a sight of divine beauty.

tamil: கூடும் படிமுன் திருமாலும் கோல மாகிப் புவி இடந்து
தேடும் திருத்தாள் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருப்பவனி
நாடும் புகழ்சேர் ஒற்றிநகர் நாடிப் புகுந்து கண்டேனால்
ஈடும் அகன்றேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: kūṭum paṭimuṉ tirumālum kōla mākip puvi iṭantu tēṭum tiruttāḷ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiruppavaṉi nāṭum pukaḻcēr oṟṟinakar nāṭip pukuntu kaṇṭēṉāl īṭum akaṉṟēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: Seeking the renowned city of Otri, I entered it and beheld the divine procession of Lord Siva, Lord Thyagar, whose sacred feet Thirumal once sought by taking the form of a boar and digging up the earth. I have gone beyond all earthly comparisons. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: Thirumal (Vishnu) once took the form of a boar and dug into the earth to find the bottom of the divine light, but failed. Vallalar marvels that she, an ordinary person, has seen the feet the great gods could not find.

tamil: ஆர்க்கும் கடற்கண் அன்றெழுந்த ஆல காலம் அத்தனையும்
சேர்க்கும் களத்தான் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருநடத்தைக்
கார்க்கண் பொழில்சூழ் ஒற்றியில்போய்க் கண்டேன் பிறவி கண்டிலனே
யார்க்கென் றுரைப்பேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: ārkkum kaṭaṟkaṇ aṉṟeḻunta āla kālam attaṉaiyum cērkkum kaḷattāṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tirunaṭattaik kārkkaṇ poḻilcūḻ oṟṟiyilpōyk kaṇṭēṉ piṟavi kaṇṭilaṉē yārkkeṉ ṟuraippēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: I went to Otri surrounded by dark groves and beheld the divine dance of Lord Siva, Lord Thyagar, who holds in His throat all the deadly poison that once rose from the roaring ocean. Now I see no more rebirth. To whom shall I tell this? O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: God once swallowed the ocean's deadly poison to save all creatures. Witnessing the divine dance of this compassionate Lord brings liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

tamil: உள்ளும் புறமும் நிறைந்தடியார் உள்ளம் மதுரித் தூறுகின்ற
தெள்ளும் அமுதாம் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருமுகத்தைக்
கள்ளம் தவிர்க்கும் ஒற்றியில்போய்க் கண்டேன் பசியைக் கண்டிலனே
எள்ளல் இகந்தேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: uḷḷum puṟamum niṟaintaṭiyār uḷḷam maturit tūṟukiṉṟa teḷḷum amutām civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tirumukattaik kaḷḷam tavirkkum oṟṟiyilpōyk kaṇṭēṉ paciyaik kaṇṭilaṉē eḷḷal ikantēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: I went to deceit-dispelling Otri and beheld the divine face of Lord Siva, Lord Thyagar, the clear nectar who fills the inside and outside and wells up sweetly in the hearts of devotees. I no longer feel hunger and have escaped all scorn. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: The divine presence is a sweet nectar that fills a person inside and out. This spiritual nourishment is so complete that it erases all physical hunger and earthly suffering.

tamil: ஆவல் உடையார் உள்ளுடையார் அயன்மால் மகவான் ஆதியராம்
தேவர் பெருமான் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருவடிவைக்
காவம் பொழில்சூழ் ஒற்றியில்போய்க் கண்டேன் கண்ட காட்சிதனை
யாவர் பெறுவார் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: āval uṭaiyār uḷḷuṭaiyār ayaṉmāl makavāṉ ātiyarām tēvar perumāṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiruvaṭivaik kāvam poḻilcūḻ oṟṟiyilpōyk kaṇṭēṉ kaṇṭa kāṭcitaṉai yāvar peṟuvār ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: I went to Otri surrounded by shady groves and beheld the divine form of Lord Siva, Lord Thyagar, the Lord of gods like Brahma, Vishnu, and Indra, who dwells in the hearts of those filled with yearning. Who else could attain the vision I saw? O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: True longing is the key to the divine presence. Vallalar realizes this yearning has granted her a vision that even the highest traditional deities struggle to attain.

tamil: மறப்பை அகன்ற மனத்துரவோர் வாழ்த்த அவர்க்கு வான்கதியின்
சிறப்பை அளிக்கும் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருநடத்தைப்
பிறப்பை அகற்றும் ஒற்றியில்போய்ப் பேரா னந்தம் பெறக்கண்டேன்
இறப்பைத் தவிர்த்தேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: maṟappai akaṉṟa maṉatturavōr vāḻtta avarkku vāṉkatiyiṉ ciṟappai aḷikkum civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tirunaṭattaip piṟappai akaṟṟum oṟṟiyilpōyp pērā ṉantam peṟakkaṇṭēṉ iṟappait tavirttēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: Praised by ascetics who have banished forgetfulness from their minds, Lord Siva, the great Lord Thyagar, grants them the supreme heavenly state. I went to Otriyur, which removes the cycle of birth, and saw His divine dance. I attained immense bliss and escaped death. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: The vision of the divine dance brings spiritual victory. Seeing the Lord at Otriyur ends the cycle of physical birth and death. Overwhelmed by this gift, Vallalar wonders what past penance could have earned such a reward.

tamil: வில்லாம் படிப்பொன் மேருவினை விரைய வாங்கும் வெற்றியினான்
செல்லாம் கருணைச் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருகூத்தைக்
கல்லாம் கொடிய மனம்கரையக் கண்டேன் பண்டு காணாத
எல்லாம் கண்டேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: villām paṭippoṉ mēruviṉai viraiya vāṅkum veṟṟiyiṉāṉ cellām karuṇaic civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tirukūttaik kallām koṭiya maṉamkaraiyak kaṇṭēṉ paṇṭu kāṇāta ellām kaṇṭēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: He is the victorious one who swiftly bent the golden Mount Meru into a bow. I saw the divine dance of Lord Siva, the great Lord Thyagar of unfailing grace. It melted my cruel heart of stone, and I saw everything I had never seen before. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: The Lord once bent the golden Mount Meru into a weapon to destroy evil. Yet the greater miracle happens within Vallalar. The sight of the divine dance melts a stonelike heart and opens the soul's eyes to realities never seen before.

tamil: ஒல்லை எயில்மூன் றெரிகொளுவ உற்று நகைத்தோன் ஒற்றியுளான்
தில்லை நகரான் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருப்பவனி
கல்லை அளியும் கனியாக்கக் கண்டேன் கொண்ட களிப்பினுக்கோர்
எல்லை அறியேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: ollai eyilmūṉ ṟerikoḷuva uṟṟu nakaittōṉ oṟṟiyuḷāṉ tillai nakarāṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiruppavaṉi kallai aḷiyum kaṉiyākkak kaṇṭēṉ koṇṭa kaḷippiṉukkōr ellai aṟiyēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: He resides in Otriyur, the one who smiled and swiftly set the three fortresses ablaze. I saw the divine procession of the Lord of Thillai city, Lord Siva, the great Lord Thyagar. It turned a stone into a tender, ripe fruit. I know no bounds to the joy I felt. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: The Lord once destroyed three flying fortresses by smiling at them. Watching the temple procession in Otriyur, Vallalar experiences a similar sudden transformation. The joy of the vision turns a hard heart into something as soft and sweet as a ripe fruit.

tamil: துன்னும் சோம சுந்தரனார் தூய மதுரை நகர்அளித்த
தென்னர் பெருமான் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருஅழகைப்
பன்னும் ஒற்றி நகர்தன்னில் பார்த்தேன் வினைபோம் வழிபார்த்த
என்னை மறந்தேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: tuṉṉum cōma cuntaraṉār tūya maturai nakaraḷitta teṉṉar perumāṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiru-aḻakaip paṉṉum oṟṟi nakartaṉṉil pārttēṉ viṉaipōm vaḻipārtta eṉṉai maṟantēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: He is Lord Somasundarar who ruled the pure city of Madurai. In the praised city of Otriyur, I saw the divine beauty of the great Lord of the South, Lord Siva, the great Lord Thyagar. Seeking a path to dispel my karma, I forgot myself entirely. O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: Somasundarar is the Lord worshipped in the southern city of Madurai. Seeking to clear away karma (the accumulated weight of past actions), Vallalar is captivated by the Lord's beauty in Otriyur. In that moment of devotion, the soul forgets its separate identity.

tamil: முன்னம் காழி வள்ளலுக்கு முத்துச் சிவிகை குடையொடுபொன்
சின்னம் அளித்தோன் சிவபெருமான் தியாகப் பெருமான் திருவடியைக்
கன்னின் றுருகா நெஞ்சுருகக் கண்டேன் கண்ட காட்சிதனை
என்என் றுரைப்பேன் அம்மாநான் என்ன தவந்தான் செய்தேனோ.
translit: muṉṉam kāḻi vaḷḷalukku muttuc civikai kuṭaiyoṭupoṉ ciṉṉam aḷittōṉ civaperumāṉ tiyākap perumāṉ tiruvaṭiyaik kaṉṉiṉ ṟurukā neñcurukak kaṇṭēṉ kaṇṭa kāṭcitaṉai eṉeṉ ṟuraippēṉ ammānāṉ eṉṉa tavantāṉ ceytēṉō.
translation: In the past, He gave a pearl palanquin, a pearl umbrella, and golden insignia to the benevolent master of Kazhi. I saw the sacred feet of Lord Siva, the great Lord Thyagar, and my unyielding stony heart melted. How can I describe the vision I saw? O mother, what penance did I perform?
commentary: The master of Kazhi is an ancient child saint who received miraculous gifts of pearl and gold from the divine. Just as the Lord rewarded that saint, He now grants Vallalar a vision of His sacred feet. This sight dissolves all inner resistance and leaves the soul speechless.

sections.title: Exhorting the Mind in Sacred Nerisai

translit: poṉṉār viṭaikkoṭi-em puṇṇiyaṉaip puṅkavaṉai oṉṉār purameritta uttamaṉai - maṉṉāya attaṉainam oṟṟiyūr appaṉai-el lāmvalla cittaṉainī vāḻttutineñ cē.
translation: O mind, praise the all-powerful Siddha. Praise our virtuous Lord who holds the golden bull banner. Praise the supreme being, the perfect one who burned the cities of his foes. Praise the eternal Father, our Lord of Otriyur.
commentary: God is a Siddha, an all-powerful being of absolute spiritual perfection. Classic images of Siva, such as the golden bull banner and the destruction of demonic cities, describe a divine father offering eternal protection.

translit: neñcē ulaka neṟiniṉṟu nīmayalāl añcēleṉ piṉvan taruḷkaṇṭāy - eñcāt tavakkoḻuntām caṟkuṇavar tāḻntēttum oṟṟic civakkoḻuntai vāḻttutumnām ceṉṟu.
translation: O mind, do not fear in your delusion by standing in the worldly path. Follow me and behold his grace. Let us go and praise the tender flame of Siva in Otriyur, whom the virtuous people of unceasing penance bow down and praise.
commentary: The ways of the world bring only confusion and fear. Vallalar urges the mind to step off that path and seek divine grace instead. Peace is found by praising God, following the example of those who dedicate their lives to spiritual discipline.

translit: ceṉṟuceṉṟu nalkāta celvartalai vāyililē niṉṟu niṉṟu vāṭukiṉṟa neñcamē - iṉṟutiru oṟṟiyappaṉ tāṇmalarai uṉṉutiyēl kātalittu maṟṟicaippa tellām varum.
translation: O mind, you wither away by going again and again to stand at the front gates of wealthy people who give nothing. If you lovingly meditate today upon the lotus feet of the Lord of Otriyur, everything you ask for will come to you.
commentary: Seeking help from the wealthy only exhausts the soul. Meditating on God with love provides everything one needs, replacing the humiliation of begging with divine abundance.

translit: varunāḷ uyirvāḻum māṇpaṟiyōm neñcē orunāḷum nīvēṟoṉ ṟuṉṉēl - tirunāḷaip pōvāṉ toḻumaṉṟil puṇṇiyaṉai oṟṟiyiltāy āvāṉ tiruvaṭi-al lāl.
translation: O mind, we do not know how long this life will last in the days to come. Do not ever think of anything else. Think of nothing other than the holy feet of the virtuous Lord worshipped in the hall by Tirunalaippovan, the Lord who becomes a mother to us in Otriyur.
commentary: Human life is fragile and uncertain. Because we do not know how many days we have left, Vallalar tells the mind to waste no time on worldly distractions. God acts as a mother offering unconditional love, the same divine presence worshipped by the saint Tirunalaippovan, who was famous for his pure devotion.

translit: allālam uṇṭamiṭaṟ ṟāramutai aṟputattaik kallāla nīḻalamar kaṟpakattaic - colārnta viṇmaṇiyai eṉuyirai meypporuḷai oṟṟiyileṉ kaṇmaṇiyai neñcē karutu.
translation: O mind, contemplate the precious pupil of my eye in Otriyur. He is the rare nectar whose throat consumed the deadly poison. He is the supreme wonder. He is the wish-fulfilling tree seated under the shade of the stone banyan tree. He is the gem of the resonant sky, my very life, and the ultimate truth.
commentary: God is the very core of the self, as vital as the pupil of the eye. Siva drinking deadly poison to save the universe shows the divine as a force of self-sacrifice. This supreme truth acts as a wish-fulfilling tree, granting spiritual shelter and eternal life.

translit: karutāyō neñcē katikiṭaikka eṅkaḷ marutā eḻiltillai maṉṉā - erutēṟum eṉarumait teyvatamē eṉarumaic caṟkuruvē eṉarumai appāvē eṉṟu.
translation: O heart, to attain salvation, will you not meditate by saying, "Our Lord of Maruthur, King of beautiful Thillai, rider of the bull, my precious Deity, my precious true Guru, my precious Father"?
commentary: The path to spiritual freedom begins by calling out to God using intimate, local names. Vallalar tells his mind to address the divine as the Lord of Maruthur (his own birth village), the King of Thillai (the sacred city of Chidambaram), his precious teacher, and his father. These close, personal titles show that the divine is not distant, but connected to everyday life and ready to guide him.

translit: eṉṟumuṉak kāḷāvēṉ eṉneñcē vaṉneñcar oṉṟum iṭam ceṉṟaṅ kuḻalātē - naṉṟutarum oṟṟiyappaṉ poṉaṭiyai uṉṉukiṉṟōr tampatattaip paṟṟiniṟpai yākil parintu.
translation: O my heart, I will forever be a servant to you if you lovingly hold fast to the feet of those who meditate on the golden feet of the Father of Otriyur, which bestow goodness. Do not go and wander in places where hard-hearted people gather.
commentary: Spiritual progress depends on avoiding those who lack compassion and keeping the company of those who love the divine. Vallalar makes a striking bargain with his mind, promising to be its servant if it will cling to the followers of the Lord of Otriyur (a sacred temple town near Chennai). He warns his heart to stay away from hard-hearted people.

translit: parintuṉakkuc colkiṉṟēṉ pāvaṅkaḷ ellām erintuviḻa nāmkatiyil ēṟat - terintu viṭaiyāṉai oṟṟiyūr vittakaṉai mātōr puṭaiyāṉai neñcamē pōṟṟu.
translation: O heart, I speak to you with love. So that all our sins burn away and we ascend to salvation, know and praise the rider of the bull, the wise Lord of Otriyur, who holds the Goddess on one side of His form.
commentary: Praising God is the fire that burns away past wrongdoings and opens the way to spiritual liberation. Vallalar directs his heart toward the traditional form of Siva, who rides a bull and shares half his body with the Goddess. This classic image presents reality as a perfect, loving union of male and female energies.

translit: pōṟṟuti-eṉ neñcē puramnakaiyāl cuṭṭavaṉai ēṟṟukanta pemmāṉai emmavaṉai - nīṟṟoḷicēr avvaṇṇat tāṉai aṇipoḻilcūḻ oṟṟiyūrc cevvaṇṇat tāṉait terintu.
translation: My heart, know and praise Him. Praise our Lord who burned the cities with a smile and who rejoices in the bull. Praise the red-hued Lord of Otriyur surrounded by beautiful groves, whose form shines with the radiance of sacred ash.
commentary: Divine power conquers darkness effortlessly. Siva destroyed three flying citadels of evil by smiling, and Vallalar tells his mind to meditate on this supreme power. The sacred ash shining on God's red-hued body represents purity and the eternal truth that remains after worldly illusions are burned away.

translit: terintu niṉakkaṉantam teṇṭaṉiṭu kiṉṟēṉ virintaneñcē oṟṟiyiṭai mēvum -parintaneṟṟik kaṇṇāṉai mālayaṉum kāṇap paṭātāṉai eṇṇārai eṇṇātē eṉṟu.
translation: Realizing this truth, I offer you endless prostrations, O expansive heart. Do not even think of those who fail to meditate on the Lord abiding in Otriyur, who bears an eye on His forehead and who remains unseen by Vishnu and Brahma.
commentary: A spiritual seeker must focus on the divine and ignore the influence of anyone who does not remember God. Vallalar goes as far as bowing down in respect to his own mind, begging it to maintain this single-minded focus. He reminds his heart of God's limitless nature by referencing the classic story where the creator deities, Brahma and Vishnu, could not fathom the top or bottom of God's infinite form.

translit: eṉṟeṉ ṟaḻutāy ilaiyē-eṉ neñcamē oṉṟeṉṟu niṉṟa uyarvuṭaiyāṉ - naṉṟeṉṟa cemmait toḻumpartoḻum cīroṟṟi yūraṇṇal nammait toḻumpukoḷḷum nāḷ.
translation: My heart, you have never wept asking when the day will come. When is the day the supreme one who stands as the One, the Lord of excellent Otriyur worshipped by flawless devotees who praise his goodness, will take us into his service?
commentary: Vallalar challenges his own heart, wondering why it does not weep with longing for the day the supreme Lord will accept him as a servant. Devotion requires an intense, aching desire to be claimed by the divine.

translit: nāḷāku muṉeṉatu naṉneñcē oṟṟiyappaṉ tāḷākum tāmaraippoṉ taṇmalarkkē - āḷākum tīrttar tamakkaṭimai ceytavartam cīrccamukam pārttumakiḻ vāyatuvē pāṅku.
translation: My good heart, before your days run out, look upon the excellent presence of those who serve the pure devotees. Those pure devotees are themselves servants of the cool, golden lotus feet of the Father of Otriyur. Look upon them and rejoice. That is the proper way.
commentary: Time is short in this human life. Vallalar urges his heart to find joy in the company of those who serve the devotees of God. He presents humility as the proper spiritual path: rather than seeking the Lord directly, the soul finds grace by serving those who serve Him.

translit: pāṅkuṭaiyār meyyil palittatiru nīṟaṇiyāt tīṅkuṭaiyār tīmaṉaiyil cellātē - ōṅkuṭaiyāḷ uṟṟamarnta pākattem oṟṟiyappaṉ poṉaruḷaip peṟṟamarti neñcē peritu.
translation: O heart, do not enter the evil homes of wicked people who fail to wear potent sacred ash on their bodies. Receive the golden grace of our Father of Otriyur, who holds the exalted Goddess on his side, and abide in greatness.
commentary: Sacred ash is a physical mark of devotion and spiritual purity. Vallalar tells his heart to avoid the company of those who lack this inner devotion, and to focus on receiving the grace of the Lord.

translit: periyāṉai mātarp piṟaikkaṇṇi yāṉai ariyāṉai aṅkaṇaṉai ārkkum - kariyāṉait tōlāṉaic cīroṟṟic cuṇṇaveṇ nīṟṟāṉai mēlāṉai neñcē virumpu.
translation: O heart, desire the great one, the wearer of the beautiful crescent moon wreath, the rare one, the Lord of beautiful eyes, the one draped in the skin of the roaring elephant, the supreme one of excellent Otriyur smeared with fine white ash.
commentary: Devotion deepens when the mind focuses on the qualities of the divine. Vallalar guides his heart to desire the Lord by recalling classic mythological symbols: the crescent moon in his hair, the skin of a conquered wild elephant, and the white ash covering his body.

translit: virumpit tirumāl vilaṅkāy neṭunāḷ arumpit taḷaintuḷ ayarntē - tirumpiviḻi nīrkoṇṭum kāṇāta nittaṉoṟṟi yūraṉaṭic cīrkoṇṭu neñcē tikaḻ.
translation: O heart, shine by holding fast to the excellent feet of the eternal Lord of Otriyur. Even Vishnu desired to see them, taking the form of a beast. He strove and grew exhausted over a long time, turning back in tears, yet still unable to see them.
commentary: Vallalar reminds his heart of the immense greatness of the Lord. According to legend, Vishnu took the form of a wild boar and dug into the earth for ages to find the bottom of the Lord's feet, but failed. Yet through devotion, the human heart can hold fast to those same unreachable feet.

translit: tikaḻkiṉṟa ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarai vāṉōr pukaḻkiṉṟa teyvattaip pōtam - nikaḻkiṉṟa oṟṟik kaṉiyai ulakuṭaiya nāyakattai veṟṟit tuṇaiyaineñcē vēṇṭu.
translation: O heart, desire the shining rich flame of wisdom, the God praised by the celestials, the fruit of Otriyur where awakening flourishes, the Lord of the world, and the victorious companion.
commentary: Vallalar speaks directly to his own heart, telling it what to desire. God is a bright flame of wisdom and a steadfast companion on the spiritual path. Framing the divine as a sweet fruit found in Otriyur, he presents God as the source of both knowledge and joy.

translit: vēṇṭāmai vēṇṭuvatu mēvāt tavamuṭaiyōr tīṇṭāmai yātatunī tīṇṭātē - īṇṭāmai oṉṟuvapōl neñcēnī oṉṟi-oṟṟi yūraṉpāl ceṉṟutoḻu kaṇṭāy tiṉam.
translation: O heart, do not touch what is untouched by ascetics who are free from both aversion and desire. Unite closely with love, go to the Lord of Otriyur, and worship Him daily.
commentary: Spiritual masters have moved beyond the pull of both desire and aversion. Vallalar warns his heart to avoid the worldly distractions that these sages leave behind. The only daily task that matters is to draw close to God with pure love.

translit: tiṉantōṟum uḷḷurukic cīrpāṭum aṉpar maṉantōṟum ōṅkum maṇiyai - iṉantōṟum vētamalar kiṉṟa viyaṉpoḻilcūḻ oṟṟinakarp pōta malaraineñcē pōṟṟu.
translation: O heart, praise the gem who rises in the minds of devotees who melt inwardly and sing His glory every day. Praise the flower of wisdom in the city of Otriyur, a place surrounded by vast groves where the Vedas blossom in clusters.
commentary: God appears vividly in the minds of those who love him. Vallalar describes devotion as a melting of the heart. When a person turns to the divine with this tender feeling, God shines within them like a bright gem.

translit: pōṟṟār purampoṭitta puṇṇiyaṉai viṇṇavarkaḷ āṟṟāta nañcamuṇṭa āṇtakaiyaik - kūṟṟāvi koḷḷum kaḻaṟkāl kurumaṇiyai oṟṟiyiṭam koḷḷum poruḷaineñcē kūṟu.
translation: O heart, speak of the virtuous One who reduced the cities of His foes to dust, the supreme Lord who consumed the poison the celestials could not endure, the master gem whose ankleted feet took the life of the god of death, and the supreme Reality enshrined in Otriyur.
commentary: The divine is the protector who drank poison to save the universe and conquered the god of death. Vallalar tells his heart to constantly speak of this fierce, protecting Lord.

translit: kūṟumaiyāṭ kīntaruḷum kōmāṉaic ceñcaṭaiyil āṟumalark koṉṟai aṇivōṉait - tēṟumaṉam uḷḷavarkaṭ kuḷḷapaṭi uḷḷavaṉai oṟṟi-amar naḷḷavaṉai neñcamē nāṭu.
translation: O heart, seek the Lord who gave half His form to the Goddess. Seek the One who wears the river and konrai flowers in His red matted hair, the One who reveals His true nature to those with clear minds, the good Lord residing in Otriyur.
commentary: While picturing God with river waters and golden flowers in his hair, Vallalar states a deeper truth. God reveals his reality only to those who have cleared their minds of confusion.

translit: nāṭum civāya nama-eṉṟu nāṭukiṉṟōr kūṭum tavaneṟiyil kūṭiyē - nīṭumaṉpar cittamaṉait tīpakamām ciṟparaṉai oṟṟiyūr uttamaṉai neñcamē ōtu.
translation: O heart, join the path of austerity where those who seek by chanting Sivayanama gather. Praise the supreme being of consciousness, the perfect one of Otriyur, who shines as a lamp in the house of the mind of steadfast devotees.
commentary: Sivayanama is the traditional five-syllable prayer to Siva. By joining the company of those who chant it with devotion, the mind finds its true spiritual path.

translit: ōtuneṟi oṉṟuḷateṉ uḷḷamē ōrti-atu tītuneṟi cērāc civaneṟiyil - pōtuneṟi ōtam piṭikkumvayal oṟṟiyappaṉ toṇṭartirup pātam piṭikkum payaṉ.
translation: O my heart, realize there is one path to praise. It is the fruit of clasping the sacred feet of the devotees of the Lord of Otriyur, whose fields capture the ocean tide. This path progresses along the path of Siva and never joins the ways of evil.
commentary: The surest way to reach God is to honor those who already love Him. This reverence keeps the mind grounded on a pure path, safe from the pull of evil.

translit: payaṉaṟiyāy neñcē pavañcārti mālō ṭayaṉaṟiyāc cīruṭaiya ammāṉ - nayaṉaṟiyār uḷḷat taṭaiyāṉ uyaroṟṟi yūravaṉvāḻ uḷḷat tavarai uṟum.
translation: O heart, you do not know the true benefit and instead embrace the cycle of birth. The Lord of eminent Otriyur possesses greatness unknown even to Vishnu and Brahma. He does not enter the hearts of those who do not understand virtue. He reaches only those whose hearts are fit for Him to dwell within.
commentary: God's greatness is beyond the reach of traditional deities like Brahma and Vishnu, yet He makes Himself intimately available to humans. Without inner virtue, however, the soul remains trapped in the endless cycle of birth and death.

translit: tavarāyi ṉumtēvar tāmāyi ṉummaṟ ṟevarā yiṉumnamakkiṅ keṉṉām - kavarāta nintai akaṉṟiṭa-eṉ neñcamē oṟṟiyilvāḻ entai aṭivaṇaṅkā rēl.
translation: O my heart, if they do not bow to the feet of my Father residing in Otriyur to banish their blame, what does it matter to us whether they are great ascetics, celestial gods, or anyone else?
commentary: A person's status means absolutely nothing without true devotion to God. Whether someone is a severe ascetic or a celestial being, their rank is useless if they lack the humility to bow to the divine.

translit: ēlak kuḻalār iṭaikkīḻp paṭuṅkoṭiya ñālak kiṭaṅkariṉai nampātē - nīla maṇikaṇṭā eṉṟuvantu vāḻttineñcē nāḷum paṇikaṇṭāy aṉṉōṉ patam.
translation: Do not trust the cruel worldly pit found below the waists of women with fragrant hair. O heart, approach Him, praise Him by calling out, "O Lord with a throat like a blue gem!" and bow daily to His feet.
commentary: Sexual desire can easily trap the mind. The heart must instead turn its attention to God. Praising Him as the blue-throated Lord refers to the ancient story where Siva drank deadly poison to save the universe, reminding the mind of divine grace and protection.

translit: patantaruvāṉ celvap payaṉtaruvāṉ maṉṉum catantaruvāṉ yāvum taruvāṉ - itamtarumeṉ neñcameṉkol vāṭukiṉṟāy niṉmalā niṉaṭiyē tañcameṉṟāl oṟṟiyappaṉ tāṉ.
translation: My good heart, why do you wither? If you say, "O pure one, your feet alone are my refuge," the Father of Otriyur himself will give the highest state. He will give the reward of wealth. He will give enduring eternity. He will give everything.
commentary: Total surrender to the divine provides everything a person could ever need, guaranteeing both earthly provisions and eternal spiritual life. When God is accepted as the only refuge, there is no reason left for despair.

note: Editor's note: sung at Pullirukkuvelur (puḷḷirukkuvēḷūr, புள்ளிருக்குவேளூர்), today Vaitheeswaran Koil, where Siva is worshipped as the divine physician.
translit: valviṉai yēṉai-iv vāḻkkaik kaṭalniṉṟum vaḷḷaluṉtaṉ nalviṉai vāḻkkaik karai-ēṟṟi meyaruḷ nalkukaṇṭāy kolviṉai yāṉai urittōy vayittiya nātakuṉṟāc celviṉai mēlavar vāḻvē amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: O benevolent Lord, lift me, a soul bound by harsh karma, from this ocean of worldly life to the shore of your divine life and grant me true grace. You flayed the murderous elephant. O Vaithiyanatha, you are the life of the exalted ones who walk the unfailing path. O crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: Worldly life is a restless ocean of actions and consequences. Vallalar asks the divine healer, Vaithiyanatha, to pull him onto the solid shore of a life rooted in grace. The reference to flaying a murderous elephant recalls a traditional story where God strips away the beast of human arrogance.

translit: poyyē pulampip puḻuttalai nāyiṉ puṟattiluṟṟēṉ meyyē uraikkumniṉ aṉpartam cārpai virumpukilēṉ paiyēl aravaṉai yēṉpiḻai nōkkip parāmukamnī ceyyēl vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: Lamenting only lies, I have become worse than a dog with a worm-infested head. I do not desire the company of your devotees who speak only the truth. Do not look at the faults of this person who is like a hooded snake and turn your face away. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: Guilt makes the mind recoil from those living in truth. Comparing his thoughts to a diseased dog or an angry snake, Vallalar begs God not to turn away. He asks for healing precisely because the soul is sick.

translit: kallēṉ maṉakkaruṅ kallēṉ ciṟitum karuttaṟiyāp pollēṉpoy vāñcitta pullēṉ irakkam poṟaiciṟitum illēṉ eṉiṉumniṉ pālaṉṟi maṟṟai iṭattilcaṟṟum cellēṉ vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: I do not learn. My mind is like black stone. I am an evil person who does not understand your intention at all. I am a lowly person who desires falsehood. I possess no compassion or patience. Even so, I will not go anywhere else except to you. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: The mind often feels hard as stone, empty of patience or compassion. Yet even in this bleak state, Vallalar vows to seek refuge nowhere but at the divine feet, showing absolute reliance on grace regardless of personal flaws.

translit: ārppār kaṭalnañ camutucey tāyniṉ aṭikkaṉpiṉṟi vērppār tamakkum viruntaḷit tāyveḷḷi veṟpeṭutta kārppāḷa ṉukkum karuṇaicey tāykaṭai yēṉtuyarum tīrppāy vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: You consumed the poison from the roaring ocean as sweet nectar. You provided a feast even for those who lack love for your feet and turn away from you. You showed compassion even to the dark-natured one who lifted the silver mountain. You will end the sorrow of this lowest person too. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: God's mercy is so vast it embraces the destructive and hostile. The divine swallows deadly poison to save the world, feeds enemies, and forgives the arrogant king who tried to uproot heaven itself. Because grace protects even these beings, Vallalar trusts it will cure his sorrow too.

translit: nāṉē niṉakkup paṇiceyal vēṇṭumniṉ nāṇmalarttāḷ tāṉē eṉakkut tuṇaiceyal vēṇṭum tayānitiyē kōṉē karumpiṉ cuvaiyēcem pāloṭu kūṭṭunaṟun tēṉē vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: I must serve you, and your fresh lotus feet must serve as my support. O treasure of compassion, O King, O sweetness of sugarcane, O fragrant honey blended with pure milk. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: True spiritual life is a pure exchange of devotion and grace. The soul offers willing service, and the divine responds by holding it steady. In this perfect balance, the experience of God becomes as sweet as milk blended with honey.

translit: maruvār kuḻaliyar maiyal kaṭalviḻum vañcaneñcāl veruvā uyaṅkum aṭiyēṉ piṇiyai vilakkukaṇṭāy uruvāy aruvum oḷiyum veḷiyumeṉ ṟōtaniṉṟa tiruvār vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: Full of divine grace, O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals praised as form, the formless, light, and vast space. Please remove the disease of this devotee who languishes in fear, troubled by a deceitful heart that plunges into the ocean of infatuation for women with fragrant hair.
commentary: Vallalar asks the divine healer to cure a specific sickness: not a physical illness, but a deceitful heart trapped by sensual obsession. God is addressed in his complete nature as physical form, unseen presence, pure light, and infinite space.

translit: tavanēya mākumniṉ tāḷnēya miṉṟit taṭamulaiyār avanēya mēṟkoṇ ṭalaikiṉṟa pētaik karuḷpurivāy navanēya māki maṉavāk kiṟanta naṭu-oḷiyām civaṉē vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: O Siva, O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals. You are the fresh love and the central light transcending mind and speech. Bestow your grace on this fool who wanders with vain desires for full-breasted women, lacking the true love for your feet which is the essence of asceticism.
commentary: True spiritual discipline begins with devotion to the divine. Vallalar asks for grace to save a foolish mind chasing physical lust instead of seeking this higher love. God is described as a renewing force of love and a central light far beyond human thought or speech.

translit: aivāy aravil tuyilkiṉṟa mālum ayaṉumtaṅkaḷ kaivāy putaittup paṇikēṭka mēvummuk kaṇaracē poyvāy viṭā-ip pulaiyēṉ piḻaiyaip poṟuttaruḷnī ceyvāy vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: O Three-eyed King. Vishnu, who sleeps on the five-headed serpent, and Brahma come before you, covering their mouths with their hands in reverence to hear your commands. Forgive the faults of this base man whose mouth never stops telling lies, and grant me your grace. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: Even cosmic deities like Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver stand humbly before the supreme Lord to await his commands. Against this image of vast divine majesty, Vallalar presents himself as a flawed, dishonest man begging God to overlook a lifetime of lies and grant healing grace.

translit: pulvāyiṉ muṉṉarp pulippōt teṉa-eṉmuṉ pōntuniṉṟa kalvāy maṉattaraik kaṇṭañci ṉēṉaik kaṭaikkaṇippāy alvāy maṇimiṭaṟ ṟāramu tē-aruḷ āṉṟaperum celvā vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: O rare nectar with a throat like a dark sapphire, possessing the vast wealth of grace. Look upon me with compassion. I am terrified, seeing stone-hearted men stand before me like a fierce male tiger confronting a deer. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: The world can be terrifying for a gentle soul. Vallalar fears facing hard, unyielding people, comparing himself to a fragile deer cornered by a fierce tiger, and calls to the divine healer for protection.

translit: ārttār kaṭalnañ camutucey tāyeṉṉai aṉparkaḷpāl cērttāyeṉ tuṉpam aṉaittaiyum tīrttut tiru-aruṭkaṇ pārttāy parama kuruvāki eṉṉuḷ parintamarnta tīrttā vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: You consumed the poison of the roaring ocean as nectar. You placed me among your devotees, ended all my sorrows, and looked upon me with your eyes of divine grace. Becoming the supreme Guru, you sit affectionately within my heart. O pure one, O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals.
commentary: The tone shifts from desperate pleading to gratitude. The divine healer has answered the call, curing Vallalar's sorrows and bringing him into the safety of true devotees. God does not remain a distant ruler, but becomes the supreme teacher who takes up loving, permanent residence inside the human heart.

translit: aṟattāyai ōrpuṭai koṇṭōr puṭaimaṇ aḷantamukil niṟattāyai vaittula kellām naṭattum nirutta-aṇṭap puṟattāyeṉ tuṉpam tuṭaittāṇṭu meyaruṭ pōtantanta tiṟattāy vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: O Dancer, you keep the Mother of Dharma on one side and the cloud-colored Lord who measured the earth on another side, directing all the worlds. You stand beyond the universe. You wiped away my sorrow, ruled over me, and gave me the true knowledge of grace. O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals!
commentary: The divine is a cosmic dancer who orchestrates the entire universe while holding all other ruling powers within himself. Though this Lord stands far beyond the edges of the universe, he reaches down to wipe away personal sorrow and grant true spiritual knowledge.

translit: alai-ōy kaṭalil civayōkam mēviya antaṇartam nilai-ōr ciṟitum aṟiyēṉ eṉakkuṉ nimala-aruḷ malai-ōṅku vāḻkkaiyum vāykkuṅ kolōpoṉ malai-eṉkiṉṟa cilaiyōy vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: I do not know even a little of the state of the pure seers who merge in Siva-yoga like an ocean with still waves. Will the lofty life on the mountain of your immaculate grace ever become possible for me? O Lord who wields the golden mountain as a bow, O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals!
commentary: Spiritual union is often compared to an ocean where the waves have finally stopped. Confessing that his mind lacks this stillness, Vallalar wonders if he will ever reach the towering heights of divine grace. He calls out to the Lord who once used golden Mount Meru as a bow, asking if such magnificent power might also lift him up.

translit: ūṉkoṇṭa tēkattum uḷḷattum mēvi uṟumpiṇiyāl nāṉkoṇṭa tuṉpam tavirppāy vayittiya nāta-eṉṟē vāṉkoṇṭa niṉaruṭ cīrēttu kiṉṟa vakai-aṟiyēṉ tēṉkoṇṭa koṉṟaic caṭaiyāy amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: I do not know how to praise the vast glory of your grace and cry out, "O Vayittiyanata, remove the sorrow I suffer from the afflictions in my fleshly body and my mind." O Lord with honey-laden konrai flowers in your matted hair, crest-jewel of the immortals!
commentary: Sickness in body and mind can overwhelm a person until they feel unable to ask for help. Admitting he lacks the right words to call upon the cosmic healer, Vallalar trusts that God will hear the suffering itself. The divine is adorned with sweet koṉṟai (golden shower tree) flowers, ready to accept sincere humility over perfect prayers.

translit: kaḷivē taṉumantak kālaṉum eṉṉaik karuta-oṭṭā oḷivē tarattiru vuḷḷañcey vāyaṉpar uḷḷameṉṉum taḷivē taṉattuṟum taṟpara mē-aruḷ taṇṇamutat teḷivē vayittiya nātā amarar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: Please graciously grant the light that prevents the proud creator and the god of death from even thinking of me. O Supreme Being dwelling in the temple of your devotees' hearts! O clear essence of the cool nectar of grace! O Vaithiyanatha, crest-jewel of the immortals!
commentary: True spiritual liberation means breaking free from the cycles of physical birth and death. The prayer asks for a divine light so powerful that neither the god who creates bodies nor the god who ends them will even notice the soul anymore. This protective light shines directly inside the sanctuary of a devoted heart.

translit: mālviṭai mēṟkoṇṭu vanteḷi yēṉuṭai valviṉaikku mēlviṭai īntiṭa vēṇṭuṅkaṇ ṭāyitu vēcamayam nīlviṭa muṇṭa miṭaṟṟāy vayittiya nātaniṉpāl cēlviṭu vāṭkaṇ umaiyoṭum tēvar cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: You must come mounted on the great bull along with Uma whose bright eyes dart like carp. This is the very moment to dismiss the strong karmas of this poor one. O Lord whose throat swallowed the dark poison! O Vayittiyanata, crest-jewel of the gods!
commentary: The perfect moment for divine intervention is right now. God is invited to arrive in his majestic form alongside the goddess Uma to wipe out the heavy burden of past actions known as karma.

translit: poyviṭu kiṉṟilaṉ eṉṟem puṇṇiyā kaiviṭu kiṉṟiyō kaṭaiya ṉēṉtaṉaip paiviṭam uṭaiyavem pāmpum ēṟṟanī peyviṭam aṉaiya-eṉ piḻaipo ṟukkavē.
translation: O our virtuous Lord, are you abandoning me, the lowest of the low, thinking I will not give up my falsehood? You accepted the fierce snake with its hooded poison. Please forgive my faults, which are just like poured poison.
commentary: Vallalar asks God not to give up on him for struggling with falsehood. Lord Siva is known for accepting dangerous things, like the poisonous snake he wears as an ornament. Vallalar asks for the same acceptance of his own poisonous faults.

translit: poṟukkiṉum aṉṟi-eṉ poymai nōkkiyē veṟukkiṉum niṉalāl vēṟu kāṇkilēṉ maṟukkiṉum toṇṭarai valiya āṇṭupiṉ ciṟukkiṉum perukkamē ceyyum celvamē.
translation: Whether you forgive me or despise me for my falsehood, I see no one but you. O true wealth who forcefully takes charge of your devotees even when they refuse, and who brings them greatness even when you seem to diminish them!
commentary: True devotion means relying on the Divine no matter what happens. Even if God rejects him, Vallalar has nowhere else to turn. He trusts that divine grace works in hidden ways, breaking down a person's pride only to lift them up higher.

translit: cellalum ciṟumaiyum ciṉamum pullaraip pullalum koṇṭa-eṉ poymai kaṇṭunī kollalum takumeṉaik koṉṟi ṭātaruḷ mallalum takumcaṭā makuṭa vaḷḷalē.
translation: Seeing my falsehood in embracing distress, baseness, anger, and the company of shallow people, it is fitting for you to kill me. Yet it is also fitting for you to grant me abundant grace instead of killing me, O generous Lord crowned with matted hair!
commentary: Vallalar confesses his worst habits and admits he deserves destruction for them. Yet he appeals to God's generosity, asking to be saved by grace rather than punished by strict justice.

translit: vaḷḷalē niṉaṭi malarai naṇṇiya uḷḷalēṉ poymaiyai uṉṉi eṉṉaiyāṭ koḷḷalē iṉṟeṉil koṭiya eṉtaṉai eḷḷalē aṉṟimaṟ ṟeṉcey kiṟpaṉē.
translation: O generous Lord, if you consider my falsehood in failing to think of your lotus feet and refuse to accept me today, what can this cruel one do except suffer ridicule?
commentary: Without divine grace, a person feels lost and exposed to the mockery of the world. Vallalar admits his mind frequently wanders away from God, but begs not to be abandoned for this weakness.

translit: ceyyanaṉ ṟaṟikilāc ciṟiya ṉēṉtaṉaip poyyaṉeṉ ṟeṇṇinī puṟampo ḻippaiyēl vaiyaniṉ ṟaiyavō mayaṅkal aṉṟiyāṉ uyyaniṉ ṟuṇarkuva toṉṟum illaiyē.
translation: O Lord, if you judge me a liar and cast me out, a lowly person who does not know how to do good, I will only stand bewildered in this world. I know no other way to survive.
commentary: Vallalar stakes his existence on divine mercy. If God judges him on his merits, he will fail. His only path to survival is dependence on grace.

translit: illai eṉpa tilā-aruḷ veḷḷamē tillai maṉṟil civaparañ cōtiyē vallai yāṉceyum vañcame lāmpoṟut tollai iṉpam utavutal vēṇṭumē.
translation: O flood of grace that knows no denial. O supreme Siva Jothi in the Hall of Thillai. You must quickly forgive all the deceit I commit and grant me the ancient bliss.
commentary: God is an endless flood of grace and the supreme light (Jothi) residing in the Hall of Thillai, the sacred temple space of Chidambaram. Vallalar asks for immediate forgiveness for his deceit, seeking the ancient, eternal bliss only this divine light can provide.

translit: illaiyē eṉpatiṅ killai eṉṟaruḷ nallaiyē nī-aruḷ nayantu nalkiṉāl kallaiyē aṉaiya-eṉ kaṉma neñcakam ollaiyē vañcamviṭ ṭuvakkum uṇmaiyē.
translation: You are truly good. If you lovingly bestow your grace by declaring there is no denial here, my karmic heart, hard as stone, will swiftly abandon its deceit and rejoice. This is the truth.
commentary: Grace alone has the power to transform the human heart. Vallalar compares his mind, weighed down by worldly habits (karma), to a hard stone. A single word of divine acceptance will dissolve his deceit and fill him with joy.

translit: uṇmaiyē aṟikilā otiya ṉēṉpaṭum eṇmaiyē kaṇṭumuḷ irakkam vaittilai aṇmaiyē ampalat tāṭum aiyanī vaṇmaiyē aruṭperu vāri allaiyō.
translation: I am a fool who does not know the truth. Even seeing my lowly state, you have not felt pity in your heart. O Lord who dances so near in the Hall, are you not the vast, generous ocean of grace?
commentary: Vallalar asks why an all-merciful God has not yet shown him pity. Contrasting his own foolishness with God's nature as a vast ocean of grace, he wonders how the Lord, who feels so close, can withhold compassion from someone who needs it so much.

translit: allalaṅ kaṭaliṭai āḻnta nāyiṉēṉ collalaṅ kaṭalviṭait tōṉṟal niṉaruḷ mallalaṅ kaṭaliṭai makiḻntu mūḻkiṉāl kalalaṅ kaṭalmaṉam kaṉital meymaiyē.
translation: I am a dog sunken in the sea of sorrow. O Lord who appears on the bull amidst a sea of praises. If I joyfully plunge into the fertile ocean of your grace, my stony mind, turbulent as the sea, will truly soften.
commentary: Plunging into the ocean of God's grace is the only cure for a turbulent mind. Vallalar feels drowned in worldly sorrow, his mind hard as stone and restless as the waves. Bathing in divine grace will soften his heart and bring him peace.

translit: meymaiyē aṟikilā vīṇa ṉēṉivaṉ uymaiyē peṟa-uṉai uṉṉi ēttiṭāk kaimaiyē aṉaiyartam kaṭaiyil cellavum poymaiyē uraikkavum puṇartta teṉkolō.
translation: I am a useless person who does not know the truth. Instead of thinking of you and praising you to attain salvation, I go to the doors of the base and speak only lies. Why have you ordained this?
commentary: It is a tragedy to waste life seeking favors from ordinary people instead of liberation from God. Vallalar feels he has wasted his time catering to the worldly rather than praising the divine. He asks God why he has been subjected to this humiliating struggle.

translit: eṉṉuṭai vañcaka iyaṟkai yāvaiyum poṉṉuṭai viṭaiyiṉōy poṟuttuk koṇṭuniṉ taṉṉuṭai aṉpartam caṅkam cārntunāṉ niṉṉuṭaip pukaḻtaṉai nikaḻttac ceykavē.
translation: O rider of the golden bull! Forgive my entire deceitful nature. Make me join the gathering of your devotees and proclaim your glory.
commentary: Vallalar asks for forgiveness of his human flaws. He calls upon the divine as the rider of the golden bull, a traditional image of Lord Siva. His request is a place among devotees so he can spend his time singing the Lord's praise.

translit: nikaḻumniṉ tiruvaruḷ nilaiyaik koṇṭavar tikaḻumnal tiruccapai ataṉuṭ cērkkamuṉ akaḻumāl ēṉmāy aḷavum cemmalarp pukaḻumā ṟaruḷuka poṟukka poymaiyē.
translation: Forgive my falseness. Include me in the radiant holy assembly of those who abide in the state of your manifest grace. Grant me the grace to praise your red lotus feet which Vishnu took the form of a boar and dug the earth to reach.
commentary: Vallalar seeks a place in the holy gathering of those who live in the state of divine grace. To show the immeasurable greatness of the divine, he refers to an ancient story where the god Vishnu took the form of a boar and dug into the earth to find the bottom of the Lord's feet, failing to reach them. Vallalar asks for the grace to praise those same unsearchable feet.

translit: āṉantak kūttaṉai ampalat tāṉai aṟputat tēṉai-em ātippi rāṉait tēṉantak koṉṟai-am ceñcaṭai yāṉaic ceṅkaṇvi ṭaiyaṉai eṅkaṇma ṇiyai mōṉantat tārpeṟum tāṉantat tāṉai muttaṉai muttiyiṉ vittaṉai muttai īṉantak kāteṉai ēṉṟukoṇ ṭāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: The joyful dancer, the Lord of the hall, the wondrous honey, our primal Lord, the one whose red matted hair wears beautiful honey-laden konrai flowers, the rider of the red-eyed bull, the apple of our eye, the supreme state attained by those steeped in silence, the liberated one, the seed of liberation, the pearl, the one who accepted me without regard for my baseness. I will welcome him tonight.
commentary: The soul waits to receive the divine through familiar images of Siva. Behind these traditional forms is an inner reality: God is silence and the seed of spiritual liberation. Vallalar marvels that such a supreme being accepts him despite his worldly flaws.

translit: aṭuttavark kellāma ruḷpuri vāṉai ampalak kūttaṉai emperu māṉait taṭuttemai āṇṭukoṇ ṭaṉpaḷit tāṉaic caṅkaraṉ taṉṉai-eṉ tantaiyait tāyaik kaṭuttatum pummaṇi kaṇṭatti ṉāṉaik kaṇṇuta lāṉai-em kaṇṇaka lāṉai eṭutteṉait tuṉpamviṭ ṭēṟavait tāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: The one who grants grace to all who approach him, the dancer in the hall, our Lord, the one who halted me, took me as his own and bestowed his love, Sankara, my father and my mother, the one whose beautiful jewel-like throat holds the fierce poison, the one with an eye on his forehead, the one who never departs from my eyes, the one who lifted me out of sorrow and elevated me. I will welcome him tonight.
commentary: The divine is both a fierce cosmic figure and a tender parent. Siva drank deadly poison to save the universe, holding it safely in his throat. Yet this same powerful Lord acts as a mother and father, lifting Vallalar out of sorrow and granting love.

translit: mālayaṉ tēṭiyum kāṇāma laiyai vantaṉai ceypavar kaṇṭama runtai ālama mutiṉa runtalcey tāṉai ātiyai ātiyō ṭantami lāṉaik kālaṉva runtivi ḻavutait tāṉaik karuṇaikka ṭalai-eṉ kaṇṇaṉai yāṉai ēlama ṇikuḻa lāḷiṭat tāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: The mountain that Vishnu and Brahma searched for but could not find, the medicine discovered by those who revere him, the one who drank poison as if it were nectar, the primal one, the one without beginning or end, the one who kicked Death and made him fall in agony, the ocean of grace, the one as precious as my own eyes, the one who keeps the lady with fragrant tresses on his left side. I will welcome him tonight.
commentary: Vallalar cites the classical legend where Brahma and Vishnu searched for the top and bottom of Siva's fiery form but failed, showing God cannot be grasped by pride or effort. Instead, he reveals himself to those who approach with devotion, acting as a healing medicine who conquers death and protects life.

translit: cuntarark kākamuṉ tūtuceṉ ṟāṉait tūyaṉai yāvarum collari yāṉaip pantama ṟukkumpa rāparaṉ taṉṉaip pattaru ḷaṅkoḷpa rañcuṭa rāṉai mantara veṟpiṉma kiḻntamarn tāṉai vāṉavar ellāmva ṇaṅkaniṉ ṟāṉai entamai āṇṭunal iṉpaḷit tāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: The one who went as a messenger for Sundarar long ago, the pure one, the one whom no one can adequately praise, the supreme Lord who severs worldly attachments, the supreme light enshrined in the hearts of devotees, the one who joyfully abides on the Mandara mountain, the one who stands while all the celestial gods bow to him, the one who ruled over me and granted sweet bliss. I will welcome him tonight.
commentary: God is willing to serve his devotees, just as Siva once acted as a messenger for the ancient saint Sundarar. While the celestial gods stand and bow from afar, the supreme light dwells in the hearts of those who love him. This intimate presence cuts away worldly attachments and brings joy.

translit: aṉparkaḷ vēṇṭuma vai-aḷip pāṉai ampalat tēnaṭam āṭukiṉ ṟāṉai vaṉparkaḷ neñcilma ruvalil lāṉai vāṉavar kōṉai-em vāḻmuta lāṉait tuṉpam tavirttuccu kaṅkoṭup pāṉaic cōtiyaic cōtiyuḷ cōtiyai nāḷum eṉpaṇi koṇṭeṉai ēṉṟukoṇ ṭāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: The one who grants whatever his devotees desire, the one who dances in the hall, the one who never enters the hearts of the cruel, the king of the gods, the source of our life, the one who dispels sorrow and grants joy, the Jothi, the Jothi within the Jothi, the one who takes my daily service and accepts me. I will welcome him tonight.
commentary: Divine experience is closed only to those with cruel hearts. To all others, God is the source of life who drives away sorrow. Vallalar names this presence as the Jothi (the supreme light of grace), noting that this light accepts the daily service of a devoted soul.

translit: kaṇṇuta lāṉai-eṉ kaṇṇamarn tāṉaik karuṇāni tiyaikka ṟaimiṭaṟ ṟāṉai oṇṇuta lāḷumai vāḻiṭat tāṉai oruvaṉai oppilā uttamaṉ taṉṉai naṇṇutal yārkkuma rumaiyi ṉāṉai nātaṉai ellārkkum nallavaṉ taṉṉai eṇṇutal ceyteṉak kiṉpaḷit tāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: Tonight I will receive him. He is the one with an eye on his forehead, the one who resides in my eyes. He is the treasure of compassion, the Lord with a dark-stained throat. He shares his left side with Umai of the radiant forehead. He is the peerless supreme One. He is difficult for anyone to approach, yet he is the Lord who is good to all. He granted me bliss when I thought of him. Tonight I will receive him.
commentary: The divine is painted with ancient symbols like the third eye of wisdom and a form shared equally with the goddess Umai. Despite this majesty, God is not remote. A single heartfelt thought is enough to draw him near and experience his joy.

translit: veḷviṭai mēlvarum vīṟuṭai yāṉai vētamu ṭiviṉil vīṟṟirun tāṉaik kaḷvirai yārmalark koṉṟaiyi ṉāṉaik kaṟpakan taṉṉaimuk kaṇkoḷka rumpai uḷviṉai nīkki-eṉ uḷḷamarn tāṉai ulakuṭai yāṉai-eṉ uṟṟatu ṇaiyai eḷviṉai oṉṟumi lātavaṉ taṉṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: Tonight I will receive him. He is the majestic one who arrives on a white bull. He sits majestically at the crown of the Vedas. He wears konrai flowers dripping with fragrant honey. He is the wish-granting tree, the sweet three-eyed sugarcane. He removed my inner karma and resides in my heart. He is the master of the world, my close companion. He is entirely free of even a sesame seed's worth of blemish. Tonight I will receive him.
commentary: God stands at the summit of the ancient scriptures, the Vedas, while dwelling within the human heart. He is compared to the mythic karpagam tree that grants wishes, and to sweet sugarcane. When the divine enters the heart, it sweeps away the burden of past actions, known as karma, leaving the mind spotless.

translit: peṇṇamar pākaṉaip pēraru ḷōṉaip periyavark kellāmpe riyavaṉ taṉṉaik kaṇṇamar neṟṟik kaṭavuḷpi rāṉaik kaṇṇaṉai āṇṭamuk kaṇṇaṉai eṅkaḷ paṇṇamar pāṭalpa ricaḷit tāṉaip pārmutal aṇṭampa ṭaittaḷip pāṉai eṇama rāta-e ḻiluṭai yāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: Tonight I will receive him. He gives half his form to the Lady. He is the Lord of immense grace, the greatest among all great ones. He is the Lord God with an eye on his forehead. He is the three-eyed Lord who reigns over Vishnu. He granted us the gift of musical songs. He creates and sustains the earth and all universes. He possesses beauty beyond all calculation. Tonight I will receive him.
commentary: The creator who spins the earth and endless universes into existence also gives humanity the gift of song. While traditional lore places gods in a hierarchy, here the supreme Lord rules over all deities, including Vishnu. His beauty defies calculation, yet he pours out grace in a form shared with the feminine.

translit: vaḷaṅkoḷum tillaippoṉ maṉṟuṭai yāṉai vāṉavar ceṉṉiyiṉ māṇikkam taṉṉaik kaḷaṅkami lātaka ruttuṭai yāṉaik kaṟpaṉai muṟṟumka ṭantuniṉ ṟāṉai uḷaṅkoḷum eṉtaṉu yirttuṇai yāṉai uṇmaiyai ellāmu ṭaiyavaṉ taṉṉai iḷampiṟai cūṭiya ceñcaṭai yāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: Tonight I will receive him. He is the Lord of the flourishing golden hall of Thillai. He is the ruby crown on the heads of the celestials. He possesses a spotless will. He stands utterly beyond imagination. He is the life companion who captivated my heart. He possesses all truth. He is the one with matted red hair adorned with a crescent moon. Tonight I will receive him.
commentary: Thillai is the ancient temple town of Chidambaram, where God is worshipped as the cosmic dancer in a golden hall. Humans build shrines and visualize the divine with crowns, red hair, and crescent moons, but divinity stands beyond the limits of imagination. He is absolute truth, choosing to become a life companion to the one who loves him.

translit: kuṟṟamel lāmkuṇa mākakkoḷ vāṉaik kūttuṭai yāṉaippeṇ kūṟuṭai yāṉai maṟṟavar yārkkuma riyavaṉ taṉṉai vantippa varkkumi ka-eḷi yāṉaip peṟṟama tēṟumpe riyapi rāṉaip piṟaimuṭi yōṉaippem māṉai-em māṉai eṟṟi-eṉ tuṉpame lāmoḻit tāṉai iṉṟai-i ravile tirntukoḷ vēṉē.
translation: Tonight I will receive him. He accepts all faults as virtues. He is the cosmic dancer, the one who shares his body with the Lady. He is difficult for all others to reach, yet incredibly accessible to those who worship him. He is the great Lord who rides the bull. He wears a crescent moon on his crown. He is the supreme Lord, my Lord. He shattered and banished all my sorrows. Tonight I will receive him.
commentary: Divine grace does not demand perfection. The supreme Lord accepts all human flaws and embraces them as virtues. While God remains out of reach for the proud, he makes himself accessible to anyone who approaches with genuine devotion, stepping in to shatter their sorrows.

note: Editor's note: sung at Chidambaram, which Saiva tradition calls simply “the Temple” (kōyil, கோயில்).
translit: aṇikoḷ kōvaṇak kantaiyē namakkiṅ kaṭutta āṭai-eṉ ṟaṟimaṭa neñcē kaṇikoḷ māmaṇik kalaṉkaḷnam kaṭavuḷ kaṇṇuṇ māmaṇik kaṇṭikai kaṇṭāy piṇikoḷ vaṉpavam nīkkumveṇṇīṟē perumaic cāntamām piṟaṅkoḷi maṉṟil tiṇikoḷ caṅkara civaciva eṉṟu ceṉṟu vāḻttalē ceytoḻi lāmē.
translation: O foolish heart, know that a patched loincloth is the only garment suited for us here. Our exquisite ornaments are the rudraksha beads, the precious gems of our God's eyes. The white ash that removes the severe disease of worldly birth is our great sandal paste. Our only work is to go and praise the resolute Lord Sankara in the brilliantly radiant hall, chanting "Siva, Siva."
commentary: True spiritual life strips away worldly wealth and status. A simple loincloth replaces fine clothes, and rudraksha (sacred beads used in prayer) replace gold ornaments. Holy ash cures the disease of worldly attachment, leaving only one task: praising the divine, Sankara and Siva, in the radiant hall.

translit: ceyta naṉṟimēl tīṅkiḻaip pāril tiruppum eṉtaṉait tiruppukiṉ ṟaṉainī peyta pāliṉaik kamariṭaik kaviḻkkum pētai yātalil piṟaḻntaṉai uṉaināṉ vaita pōtiṉum vāḻtteṉa niṉaittu maṟuttu nīkki-av vaḻinaṭak kiṉṟāy koyta kōṭṭiṉai naṭṭaṉai vaḷarppāy koṭiya neñcamē maṭiyakiṟ ṟilaiyē.
translation: You turn me away like those who repay good deeds with evil. You are ruined, acting like a fool who pours fresh milk into a dry crack in the ground. Even when I curse you, you take it as praise, reject my words, brush them aside, and keep walking on that same wrong path. You plant a severed branch and expect it to grow. O cruel heart, you refuse to perish.
commentary: The human mind can be stubborn, working against its own peace. Left to its own habits, it wastes spiritual energy like pouring fresh milk into a dry crack in the earth. Even when scolded, it ignores the warning and tries to grow life from a dead branch, refusing to let go of its foolish ways.

translit: ilai-e ṉātaṇu vaḷavumoṉ ṟīya eṇṇu kiṉṟilai eṉpeṟu vāyō kolai-i ṉāteṉa aṟintilai neñcē kollu kiṉṟa-ak kūṟṟiṉum koṭiyāy talaiyiṉ mālaitāḻ caṭaiyuṭaip perumāṉ tāḷni ṉaintilai ūṇniṉain tulakil pulaiyi ṉārkaḷpāl pōtiyō vīṇil pōkap pōka-ip pōkkiṉil aḻintē.
translation: You do not think of giving even an atom's worth of charity without refusing. What will you achieve? O heart, you do not understand that murder is cruel. You are crueler than the murderous God of Death. You do not think of the feet of the great Lord with hanging matted hair who wears a garland of skulls. Thinking only of food, do you go to the vile people in this world? You are destroyed by going endlessly down this vain path.
commentary: A heart without compassion is worse than death itself. Refusing to give even a tiny bit of charity and failing to see the cruelty of murder (kolai) are direct obstacles to grace. Instead of seeking the divine, the distracted mind chases after mere survival and food, wandering endlessly down a path that leads only to ruin.

translit: aḻinta vāḻkkaiyiṉ avalamiṅ kaṉaittum aiyam iṉṟinī aṟintaṉai neñcē kaḻinta eccilai viḻaintiṭu vārpōl kalantu mīṭṭunī kalaṅkukiṉ ṟaṉaiyē moḻinta muṉṉaiyōr peṟumciva katikkē muṉṉu ṟāvakai eṉṉuṟum uṉṉāl iḻinta nāyiṉum kaṭaiyaṉāy niṉṟēṉ eṉcey vēṉuṉai ēṉaṭut tēṉē.
translation: O heart, you have known without a doubt all the sorrows of this perishing life here. Yet, like someone desiring discarded scraps of food, you entangle yourself again and become confused. Because of you, I am kept from reaching the supreme state of Siva attained by the ancient sages. What will happen to me? I stand lower than a lowly dog. What shall I do? Why did I ever associate with you?
commentary: Even when we know worldly life brings only sorrow, the mind craves its familiar illusions. It acts like someone eating discarded scraps of food, tangling itself back up in the suffering it just escaped. This stubborn confusion drags the soul down, keeping it from the supreme state of peace that earlier sages achieved.
