translit: tēṉney āṭiya ceñcaṭaik kaṉiyait tēṉai meyaruḷ tiruviṉai aṭiyar ūṉai nekkiṭa urukkiya oḷiyai uḷḷat tōṅkiya uvappiṉai mūvar kōṉai āṉantak koḻuṅkaṭal amutaik kōma ḷattiṉaik kuṉṟavil liyai-em māṉai ampala vāṇaṉai niṉaiyāy vañca neñcamē māyntilai iṉumē.
translation: You do not think of the ripe fruit with red matted hair bathed in honey and ghee. You do not think of the sweet honey, the wealth of true grace, the light that melts the flesh of devotees, the joy rising in the heart, the Lord of the three primal gods, the nectar from the rich ocean of bliss, the beautiful one, the wielder of the mountain bow, our Master, the dweller of the Hall. O deceitful heart, you have still not perished.
commentary: The divine presence is a source of intense bliss, often described as a light that physically melts the flesh of those who experience its grace. Yet the deceitful mind ignores this inner joy. It turns a blind eye to the master of the spiritual hall, choosing its own illusions over the nectar of freedom.

translit: iṉṉum eṅṅaṉam ēkukiṉ ṟaṉaiyō ēḻai neñcamē iṅkumaṅ kuntāṉ muṉṉai nāmpiṟan tuḻaṉṟa-at tuyarai muṉṉil eṉkulai muṟukkukiṉ ṟaṉakāṇ eṉṉai nī-eṉak kuṟutuṇai antō eṉcol ēṟṟilai eḻilkoḷum potuvil maṉṉu nammuṭai vaḷḷalai niṉaṉattāl maṟṟu nāmpiṟa vāvakai varumē.
translation: Where else are you wandering, my poor heart, roaming here and there? When I recall the sorrow we suffered in our past births, it twists my very core. You are my close companion. Alas, you do not heed my words. If you would only think of our generous Lord who abides in the beautiful Hall, we will attain the state of never being born again.
commentary: The memory of suffering in past lives is physically painful to the awakened soul. Vallalar addresses his own mind as a stubborn but close friend who keeps wandering away from this truth. The only way to stop the endless cycle of birth and death is to turn inward and focus on the Lord.

translit: piṟantu muṉṉariv vulakiṉām peṇṭu piḷḷai ātiya peruntoṭak kuḻantē iṟantu vīḻkati iṭaiviḻun tuḻaṉṟē irunta cēṭattiṉ ittaṉai ellām maṟantu viṭṭaṉai neñcamē nītāṉ matiyi lāyatu maṟantilaṉ eḷiyēṉ tuṟantu nāmpeṟum cukattiṉai aṭaiyac collum vaṇṇamnī toṭaṅkiṭil naṉṟē.
translation: My heart, we were born in this world before and suffered deeply, entangled in the massive bonds of family. We died, fell into lower realms, and wandered endlessly in that state. You lack wisdom and have forgotten all of this. I, a poor soul, have not forgotten it. It is best that you begin to follow my words so we can renounce these bonds and attain true bliss.
commentary: Worldly attachments pull the soul down into cycles of suffering. Vallalar warns his own mind that while human memory easily forgets this past pain, the awakened soul remembers it. He urges the mind to wake up, leave these heavy bonds behind, and seek lasting peace.

translit: naṉṟu ceyvataṟ kuṭaṉpaṭu vāyēl nalla neñcamē valla-iv vaṇṇam iṉṟu ceytinī nāḷai-eṉ pāyēl iṉṟi runtavar nāḷainiṉ ṟilarē oṉṟu kēṇmati cukarmutal muṉivōr ukka akkaṇam cikkeṉat tuṟantār aṉṟu muṉṉarē kaṭantaṉar aṉṟi ataṟku muṉṉarē akaṉṟaṉar aṉṟē.
translation: My good heart, if you agree to do what is good, do it right now with all your might. If you say you will do it tomorrow, remember that those who are here today do not remain tomorrow. Listen to this one truth: sages like Suka firmly renounced the world the very moment they realized the truth. They crossed the worldly ocean instantly in those ancient days, having detached themselves even before that moment.
commentary: Spiritual practice cannot wait for tomorrow. Human life is fragile, and the people we see today may be gone the next day. Vallalar points to the ancient sages who walked away from worldly attachments the second they saw the truth. When the mind agrees to do what is right, the action must be immediate and absolute.

translit: aṉṟi ṉērkilai nammuṭaip perumāṉ añce ḻuttaiyum aṭikkaṭi maṟantāy oṉṟi mēṟkati uṟavakai antō uṇarki lāyvayiṟ ṟūṇporuṭ ṭayalōr muṉṟil kāttaṉai avvaḷa vēṉum muyaṉṟu kāttilai muṉṉavaṉ kōyil tuṉṟi niṉṟanal toṇṭartam toḻumpu toṭaṅku vāṉavar tūyamuṉ ṟilaiyē.
translation: You do not accept this. You repeatedly forget the five sacred letters of our Lord. Alas, you do not understand how to unite with the divine and reach the highest state. Just to fill your stomach, you waited patiently in the front yards of strangers. You did not make even a fraction of that effort to wait in the pure courtyards of the noble devotees who gather for service at the Primal Lord's temple.
commentary: People often endure great humiliation to survive in the material world. We stand outside a stranger's door seeking food or wealth, yet refuse to spend a fraction of that effort on spiritual life. Vallalar tells his mind to stop forgetting God's holy name and to seek the company of those who dedicate their lives to serving the divine.

translit: tūya neñcamē cukampeṟa vēṇṭil collu vāmatu collaḷa vaṉṟāl kāya māyamām kāṉceṟin tulavum kaḷvar aivaraik kaiviṭut tataṉmēl pāya āṇavap pakaikeṭa murukkip pakali rā-ilāp pāṅkariṉ niṉṟē āya vāṉantak kūttuṭaip paramā kāya cōtikaṇ ṭamarutal aṇiyē.
translation: My pure heart, if you wish to attain bliss, I will tell you the way. It is not a matter of mere words. You must abandon the five thieves who roam densely in the illusory forest of this body. Then you must crush and destroy the leaping enemy of ego. You must stand in that realm where there is neither day nor night, behold the supreme expanse of Jothi belonging to the Lord of the blissful dance, and gracefully abide there.
commentary: True spiritual bliss requires absolute inner transformation beyond spoken words. The seeker must fight the distractions of the physical senses, which Vallalar calls five thieves roaming the illusion of the body. Once the fierce enemy of human ego is crushed, the soul reaches a state beyond time where there is neither day nor night. In that stillness, the seeker witnesses the supreme Jothi (the divine light) and rests in peace.

translit: kaṇkaḷ mūṉṟiṉār kaṟaimaṇi miṭaṟṟār kaṅkai nāyakar maṅkaipaṅ kuṭaiyār paṇkaḷ nīṭiya pāṭalār maṉṟil pāta nīṭiya paṅkayap patattār oṇkaṇ mātarār naṭampayil oṟṟi yūra marntuvāḻ vuṟṟavark kēnam maṇkoṇ mālaipōm vaṇṇamnal tamiḻppū mālai cūṭṭutum varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: He has three eyes and a throat like a dark gem. He is the Lord of the Ganges and shares his form with the Goddess. He is praised in enduring melodic songs. His lotus feet stretch out in the dancing hall. He dwells and thrives in Otriyur where bright-eyed women practice dance. To banish our earthly delusion, let us crown Him with a beautiful garland of Tamil flowers. Come, my heart.
commentary: The Lord appears in his classic forms: with three eyes, a throat stained dark from swallowing poison to save the world, and sharing half his body with the Goddess. To dispel the illusions of earthly life, Vallalar invites his heart to worship him with a garland of Tamil songs.

translit: kariya mālaṉṟu kariyamā vākik kalaṅka niṉṟapoṉ kaḻalpuṉai patattār periya aṇṭaṅkaḷ yāvaiyum paṭaittum pittar eṉṉumap pērtaṉai akalār uriya cīrkoḷum oṟṟiyūr amarntār umpar nāyakar tampuyam puṉaiya variya kaṉṟanaṉ malarkoṭu terintu mālai cūṭṭutum varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: When the dark Lord Vishnu once became a black boar and stood bewildered, His feet wore golden anklets. Though He created all the vast universes, He never sheds the name of Madman. The Lord of the celestials dwells in Otriyur of fitting greatness. Let us gather select, fresh, beautifully lined flowers to adorn His shoulders with a garland. Come, my heart.
commentary: Vishnu once took the form of a giant boar to search for the bottom of Siva's feet, but failed to find their limit. Even though he is the creator of vast universes, the Lord accepts the name of Madman, wandering freely outside conventional norms. Vallalar calls his heart to honor this boundless divine presence with fresh flowers.

translit: tiruviṉ nāyakaṉ kaippaṭai peṟuvāṉ tirukkaṇ cāttiya tirumalarp patattār karuviṉ niṉṟa-em pōlpavar tammaik kātta ḷippatē kaṭaṉeṉak koṇṭār uruviṉ niṉṟavar aru-eṉa niṉṟōr oṟṟi yūriṭai uṟṟaṉar avarkku maruviṉ niṉṟanaṉ maṇaṅkoḷum malarppū mālai cūṭṭutum varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: He has divine lotus feet where the Lord of Lakshmi offered his own eye to obtain the discus weapon for his hand. He took it as His duty to protect and save people like us caught in the womb. He stands with form and He stands as the formless. He has arrived in Otriyur. Let us crown Him with a flower garland bearing excellent fragrance. Come, my heart.
commentary: When Vishnu was short by one flower in his offering to Siva, he plucked out his own eye to complete the worship and was rewarded with his signature weapon. The Lord who commands such fierce devotion is both with physical form and formless. He takes it as his duty to protect fragile souls from the moment they enter the womb.

translit: karumpain nākaṇaik kaṭavuḷnāṉ mukaṉvāṉ kaṭavuḷ ātiyar kalakaṅkaḷ tavirppāṉ turumpai nāṭṭi-ōr viñcaiyaṉ pōlat tōṉṟi niṉṟavar turicaṟut tiṭṭōṉ tarumpaim pūmpoḻil oṟṟiyūr iṭattut talaṅkoṇ ṭāravar tamakkunām makiḻntu varumpaiñ cīrttamiḻ mālaiyō ṭaṇipū mālai cūṭṭutum varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: To stop the arrogant quarrels among the God on the serpent bed, the four-faced creator, the lord of the sky and others, He planted a single blade of grass and appeared as a mysterious spirit to destroy their pride. He has taken His seat in Otriyur, a place rich with lush flower groves. Let us joyfully adorn Him with a garland of beautiful flowers along with a fresh and glorious Tamil garland. Come, my heart.
commentary: When the other gods grew arrogant and quarrelled over who was supreme, a mysterious spirit planted a blade of grass before them. Because they could not move or destroy it, their pride was broken. Vallalar calls his heart to joyfully adorn the Lord who humbles the greatest gods, offering him fresh blossoms and Tamil verses.

translit: vataṉa nāṉkuṭai malaravaṉ cirattai vāṅki ōrkaiyil vaittanam perumāṉ nitaṉa neñcakark karuḷtarum karuṇā nitiya mākiya niṉmalap perumāṉ cutaṉa maṅkaiyar naṭamceyum oṟṟit tūya ṉālavar tuṇaittirut tōṭku mataṉa iṉtamiḻ mālaiyō ṭaṇupū mālai cūṭṭutum varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: Plucking a head from the lotus-born god who has four faces, our Lord held it in one hand. He is the pure Lord, the treasure of compassion who grants grace to steadfast hearts. He is the pure one of Otriyur where lovely women dance. Let us crown His two divine shoulders with a closely strung flower garland along with a sweet Tamil garland. Come, my heart.
commentary: The creator god Brahma once had five heads, until his arrogance caused the Lord to pluck one away. Beneath this fierce mythological power lies a pure treasure of compassion, granting grace to those whose hearts remain steady. Vallalar asks his heart to approach this Lord with sweet songs and closely strung flowers.

translit: kañcaṉ aṅkoru viñcaṉam ākik kālil pōntumuṉ kāṇaru muṭiyār añca ṉamkoḷum neṭuṅkaṇāḷ eṅkaḷ ammai kāṇaniṉ ṟāṭiya patattār ceñcoṉ mātavar pukaḻtiru voṟṟit tēvar kāṇavar tirumuṭik kāṭṭa mañca ṉaṅkoṭu varutumeṉ moḻiyai maṟātu nī-uṭaṉ varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: Brahma became a bird there and flew, yet could not see the Lord's crown. The Lord danced for our Mother, whose long eyes wear collyrium. He is the Lord of holy Otriyur, praised by great sages of flawless speech. Behold him. We shall bring sacred water to bathe his holy crown. Do not refuse my word. Come, my heart.
commentary: Serving God begins with acts of devotion, like bringing sacred water to bathe the deity's crown. Brahma once turned into a bird to find the top of the Lord's head and failed. While God's true heights cannot be measured by the greatest deities, he dances joyfully for his devotees and accepts humble offerings.

translit: cūḻu mālayaṉ peṇṇuru eṭuttut toḻumpu ceytiṭat tōṉṟiniṉ ṟavaṉaip pōḻum vaṇṇamē vaṭukaṉuk karuḷum pūta nātarnaṟ pūraṇā ṉantar tāḻum taṉmaiyōr uyarvuṟac ceyyum takaiyar oṟṟiyūrt talattiṉar avartām vāḻum kōyiṟkut tiruvala kiṭuvōm makiḻvu koṇṭuṭaṉ varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: Vishnu and Brahma took female forms and offered their service. He appeared and granted grace to Bhairava to cleave Brahma's head. He is the Lord of the elements and the perfect bliss. He holds the noble nature of uplifting the lowly. He dwells in the shrine of Otriyur. We shall sweep the holy temple where he lives. Joyfully, come, my heart.
commentary: God is the master of perfect bliss who constantly uplifts the lowly. Even the greatest creator deities take humble forms to serve him. True spiritual joy is found in the simplest tasks, which is why Vallalar asks his heart to come along and sweep the temple floors.

translit: vitiyum mālumuṉ vēṟuru eṭuttu mēlum kīḻumāy virumpuṟa niṉṟōr natiyum koṉṟaiyum nākamum piṟaiyum naṇṇi ōṅkiya puṇṇiyac caṭaiyār patiyu nāmaṅkaḷ aṉantamuṟ ṟuṭaiyār paṇaikoḷ oṟṟiyūrp paramarkā ṇavartām vatiyum kōyiṟkut tiruviḷak kiṭuvōm vāḻka nī-uṭaṉ varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: Brahma and Vishnu once took different forms and eagerly sought him above and below. He is the Lord with holy matted hair, soaring high with the river, kondrai flowers, a serpent, and the crescent moon. He owns endless names and abodes. Behold the supreme Lord of flourishing Otriyur. We shall light the holy lamps in the temple where he resides. May you prosper. Come, my heart.
commentary: The divine presence cannot be grasped by grand searches, even when the highest gods look everywhere for it. Yet this supreme being, adorned with the moon and a river in his hair, waits in the local temple. We can connect with that endless greatness by lighting the temple lamps.

translit: kuḷaṅkoḷ kaṇṇiṉār kuṟṟamē ceyiṉum kuṇameṉ ṟē-ataik koṇṭaruḷ purivōr uḷaṅkoḷ aṉpartam uḷḷakat tiruppōr oṟṟi yūriṭam paṟṟiya puṉitar kaḷaṅkoḷ kaṇṭareṇ tōḷarkaṅ kāḷar kallai vileṉak kaṇṭavar avartam vaḷaṅkoḷ kōyiṟkut tirumeḻuk kiṭuvōm vāḻka nī-uṭaṉ varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: Even if women with pond-like eyes commit faults, he accepts them as virtues and grants his grace. He dwells in the inner hearts of his loving devotees. He is the holy one who resides in Otriyur. He has a dark throat, eight shoulders, and wears a garland of bones. He took the great mountain as his bow. We shall purify the floors of his rich temple. May you prosper. Come, my heart.
commentary: God looks at the mistakes of his loving devotees and sees them as virtues. Because he dwells in the hearts of those who love him, he responds to their devotion rather than their flaws. In gratitude for this fierce and forgiving grace, Vallalar calls his heart to purify the temple floors.

translit: paṇikoḷ mārpiṉar pākaṉa moḻiyāḷ pākar kālaṉaip pāṟṟiya patattār tiṇikoḷ vaṉmata malai-uri pōrttōr tēvar nāyakar tiṅkaḷam caṭaiyār aṇikoḷ oṟṟiyūr amarntiṭum tiyākar aḻakar aṅkavar amaintuvīṟṟirukkum maṇikoḷ kōyiṟkut tiruppaṇi ceytum vāḻka nī-uṭaṉ varuti-eṉ maṉaṉē.
translation: He wears a snake on his chest. He shares his form with the Goddess of sweet speech. His feet destroyed Death. He draped himself in the thick skin of a wild elephant. He is the Lord of the gods. He wears the beautiful crescent moon on his matted hair. He is the beautiful Thyagar seated in adorned Otriyur. We shall perform holy service in the gem-studded temple where he sits in state. May you prosper. Come, my heart.
commentary: The Lord who conquered Death sits patiently in the local shrine. He wears fierce symbols like a wild elephant's skin, yet he shares his body with the goddess of sweet speech. We approach this supreme, death-conquering power through willing labor in his temple.

note: Editor's note: verse 3 recalls Thirukkural 1054: to ask of those who never hide what they have is as good as giving (irattalum ītalē pōlum, இரத்தலும் ஈதலே போலும்).
translit: ceṉṟu vañcartam puṟaṅkaṭai niṉṟu tikaikka eṇṇumeṉ tiṟaṉilā neñcē oṉṟum añcalai eṉṉuṭaṉ kūṭi oṟṟi yūrkkiṉṟu varutiyēl aṅku maṉṟuḷ mēviya vaḷḷalār makiḻntu vāḻkiṉ ṟāravar malaraṭi vaṇaṅki naṉṟu vēṇṭiya yāvaiyum vāṅki nalku vēṉeṉai namputi mikavē.
translation: O my incapable heart, you intend to go and stand bewildered at the back doors of deceitful people. Fear nothing. If you join me today and come to Otriyur, the benevolent Lord who abides in the Hall dwells there in joy. Bowing to His lotus feet, I will receive all the good things you desire and give them to you. Trust me completely.
commentary: The mind constantly seeks fulfillment from worldly people, often humiliating itself at the doors of the greedy or deceitful. Vallalar promises his heart that if it stops this futile begging and turns to the divine, God will provide everything it needs.

translit: tītu vēṇṭiya ciṟiyartam maṉaiyil ceṉṟu niṉṟunī tikaittiṭal neñcē yātu vēṇṭuti varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē yāṇar mēviya oṟṟiyūr akattu mātu vēṇṭiya naṭaṉanā yakaṉār vaḷḷa lāraṅku vāḻkiṉṟār kaṇṭāy ītu vēṇṭiya teṉṉumuṉ aḷippār ēṟṟu vāṅkināṉ īkuvaṉ uṉakkē.
translation: O heart, do not go and stand bewildered at the houses of petty people who desire evil. Whatever you desire, come with me. In Otriyur filled with fresh beauty dwells the Lord of the Dance, the benevolent Lord desired by the Goddess. See this! Before you even say you need a certain thing, He will grant it. I will receive it and give it to you.
commentary: God knows our needs before we even voice them. Instead of waiting on the unpredictable favors of petty people, the heart should seek the Lord of the Dance, a beloved form of Siva. Divine grace responds instantly to a genuine seeker.

translit: irakkiṉ ṟōrkaḷuk killai-eṉ ṉārpāl irattal ītalām eṉaluṇarn tilaiyō karakkiṉ ṟōrkaḷaik kaṉaviṉum niṉaiyēl karuti vantavar kaṭiyavar eṉiṉum purakkiṉ ṟōrmalarp puricaṭai uṭaiyār pūta nāyakar poṉmalaic cilaiyār urakkuṉ ṟōrtiru voṟṟiyūrk kēki uṉṉi ēṟkutum uṟuti-eṉ neñcē.
translation: Have you not realized that asking from those who never say no to beggars is itself a noble act of giving? Do not think, even in your dreams, of misers who hide their wealth. He protects even harsh people who come to Him with a purpose. He is the Lord with matted hair adorned with flowers. He is the Lord of the elements, holding the golden mountain as a bow, the Lord whose strength never fades. Let us go to holy Otriyur, meditate upon Him, and receive His gifts. This is a certainty, my heart.
commentary: Begging from misers only degrades the soul. True generosity belongs to God, who protects even harsh and flawed people when they turn to him for refuge. Depending on a giver this boundless is a noble act, never a cause for shame.

translit: kalliṉ neñcarpāl kalaṅkaleṉ neñcē karuti vēṇṭiya tiyātatu kēṇmō colliṉ ōṅkiya cuntarap perumāṉ cōlaicūḻ oṟṟit toṉṉakarp perumāṉ alliṉ ōṅkiya kaṇṭattem perumāṉ ayaṉum mālumniṉ ṟaṟivarum perumāṉ vallai īkuvāṉ īkuva tellām vāṅki īkuvēṉ varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē.
translation: O my heart, why do you suffer distress from those with hearts of stone? Listen to what you truly desire and seek. He is the beautiful Lord exalted in praise, the Lord of the ancient city of Otri surrounded by groves, our Lord with a throat dark as night, the Lord whom Brahma and Vishnu found hard to know. He will give to us swiftly. I will receive all that He gives and give it to you. Come with me.
commentary: Turning to people with hearts of stone brings nothing but distress. The Lord, whose nature is so vast that even the greatest gods cannot comprehend it, is intimately accessible to anyone who asks. Divine generosity is swift and certain.

translit: ilavu kākkiṉṟa kiḷḷaipōl uḻaṉṟāy eṉṉai niṉmati ēḻainī neñcē palavu vāḻaimāk kaṉikaṉin tiḻiyum paṇaikoḷ oṟṟiyūrk keṉṉuṭaṉ varuti nilavu veṇmatic caṭaiyuṭai aḻakar niṟaiya mēṉiyil nikaḻntanīṟ ṟaḻakar kulavu kiṉṟaṉar vēṇṭiya ellām koṭuppar vāṅkināṉ koṭuppaṉuṉ taṉakkē.
translation: You have wandered like a parrot waiting for the silk-cotton fruit to ripen, only to be disappointed. What has become of your wisdom, my poor heart? Come with me to fertile Otriyur, where jackfruits, plantains, and mangoes ripen and fall from the branches. The beautiful Lord wearing the radiant white moon in His matted hair, the beautiful Lord shining with holy ash smeared all over His body, rejoices there. He will give everything you desire. I will receive it and give it all to you.
commentary: A traditional Tamil proverb compares foolish hope to a parrot waiting for a silk-cotton pod to ripen, only to watch it burst into inedible fluff. Seeking joy from worldly patrons is exactly like this empty waiting. True abundance belongs to God, who gives real nourishment to all who approach.

translit: maṉṉu ruttirar vāḻvaivēṇ ṭiṉaiyō māla vaṉpeṟum vāḻvuvēṇ ṭiṉaiyō aṉṉa ūrtipōl ākavēṇ ṭiṉaiyō amaiyum intiraṉ ākavēṇ ṭiṉaiyō eṉṉa vēṇṭiṉum taṭaiyilai neñcē iṉṟu vāṅkināṉ īkuvaṉ uṉakkē vaṉṉi añcaṭai empirāṉ oṟṟi vaḷaṅkoḷ ūriṭai varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē.
translation: Do you desire the life of the eternal Rudras? Do you desire the life obtained by Vishnu? Do you desire to become the one whose vehicle is the swan? Do you desire to become Indra? Whatever you desire, there is no obstacle, O heart. Today I will receive it and give it to you. Come with me to the fertile town of Otriyur where our Lord with fiery matted hair resides.
commentary: The wandering mind is coaxed toward the divine with the promise of the highest prizes imaginable. If the heart desires the cosmic power of the greatest gods—Rudra, Vishnu, Brahma who rides a swan, or Indra—Vallalar promises to secure it. The Lord at Otriyur can easily grant even these supreme celestial ranks.

translit: maṟappi lācciva yōkamvēṇ ṭukiṉum vaḻutta rumperu vāḻvuvēṇ ṭukiṉum iṟappi lātiṉṉum irukkavēṇ ṭukiṉum yātu vēṇṭiṉum īkuvaṉ uṉakkē piṟappi lāṉeṅkaḷ paraciva perumāṉ pittaṉ eṉṟunī peyarntiṭal neñcē vaṟappi lāṉaruṭ kaṭalavaṉ amarntu vāḻum oṟṟiyiṉ varuti-eṉ ṉuṭaṉē.
translation: Even if you desire the unforgetting Siva Yoga, even if you desire the great life beyond praise, even if you desire to remain deathless forever, I will give you whatever you desire. Our supreme Lord Siva has no birth. Do not turn away calling him a madman, O heart. He is the unfailing ocean of grace. Come with me to Otriyur where he joyfully resides.
commentary: Spiritual liberation and physical immortality are offered next as rewards for the mind's cooperation. The heart is promised unbroken divine union (Siva Yoga) or the power to remain deathless. Vallalar warns his mind not to dismiss the Lord as a wild ascetic or a madman, as worldly people often do. He is an unfailing ocean of grace who grants eternal life.

translit: kālam celkiṉṟa taṟintilai pōlum kālaṉ vantiṭil kāriyam ilaikāṇ nīlam celkiṉṟa miṭaṟṟiṉār karattil nimirnta veṇnerup pēntiya nimalar ēlam celkiṉṟa kuḻali-ōr puṭaiyār irukkum oṟṟiyūrk keṉṉuṭaṉ varuti ñālam celkiṉṟa tuyarkeṭa varaṅkaḷ nalku vāravai nalkuvaṉ uṉakkē.
translation: It seems you do not realize that time is passing. If the God of Death arrives, nothing can be done. Come with me to Otriyur where the pure Lord dwells. He has a blue throat, he holds rising white fire in his hand, and he keeps the lady with fragrant tresses on one side. He grants boons to destroy the sorrow spreading through the world. I will get those boons and give them to you.
commentary: Time is running out, and once death arrives, opportunities for spiritual progress are lost. Vallalar reminds his heart that life is fragile. He describes the Lord in his classic form: a throat stained blue from swallowing poison to save the world, holding white fire, and sharing his form with the Goddess. This pure Lord has the power to destroy all worldly sorrow, and Vallalar promises to secure that grace if the heart follows.

translit: ceṉṟu nīpukum vaḻiyelām uṉṉait tēṭa eṉvacam alla-eṉ neñcē iṉṟa raikkaṇam eṅkumnērn tōṭā tiyalkoḷ oṟṟiyūrk keṉṉuṭaṉ varuti aṉṟu vāṉavar uyirpeṟa nañcam arunti niṉṟa-em aṇṇalār iṭattē niṉṟu vēṇṭiya yāvaiyum uṉakku nikaḻa vāṅkināṉ īkuvaṉ aṉṟē.
translation: It is beyond my power to search for you along every path you wander, my heart. Today, without running everywhere for even half a moment, come with me to illustrious Otriyur. Our great Lord consumed poison that day so the celestials could live. Standing before him, I will receive everything you need and give it to you right away.
commentary: The human mind is difficult to control, constantly wandering down distracting paths. Acknowledging that he cannot constantly chase his thoughts, Vallalar begs his heart to stop running for half a moment and accompany him. He invokes the Lord's supreme act of compassion in swallowing deadly poison to save the celestial beings. Standing before a God capable of such sacrifice, Vallalar guarantees his heart will receive everything it needs.

translit: keṭukkum vaṇṇamē palaruṉak kuṟuti kiḷattu vāravar keṭumoḻi kēḷēl aṭukkum vaṇṇamē colkiṉṟēṉ eṉainī ammai immaiyum akaṉṟiṭā maiyiṉāl taṭukkum vaṇṇamē ceytiṭēl oṟṟit talatti ṉukkiṉṟeṉ ṟaṉṉuṭaṉ varuti maṭukkum vaṇṇamē vēṇṭiya ellām vāṅki īkuvaṉ vāḻti-eṉ neñcē.
translation: Many will speak assurances to you only to ruin you. Do not listen to their destructive words. I tell you what is truly fitting. Since you do not part from me in this life or the next, do not act as an obstacle. Come with me today to the sacred place of Otriyur. I will receive and give you everything you desire in abundance. Prosper, my heart.
commentary: Worldly voices often offer false promises that lead the soul astray. Vallalar warns his mind to ignore these distractions and listen to the truth. Because the mind and the self are bound together through this life and the next, a resistant mind becomes the greatest obstacle to grace. By aligning with the soul's spiritual purpose, the heart is promised true prosperity and abundance.

translit: eṉṉa taṉṟukāṇ vāḻkkaiyuṭ cārnta iṉpa tuṉpaṅkaḷ iruviṉaip payaṉāl maṉṉum mummala maṭañceṟi maṉaṉē vāḻti yō-iṅku valviṉaik kiṭamāy uṉṉa nalamu tāmciva perumāṉ uṟṟu vāḻntiṭum oṟṟiyūrk kiṉṟē iṉṉal aṟṟiṭac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: See, the joys and sorrows attached to this life are not mine. They are the result of the two kinds of karma. O mind dense with the ignorance of the enduring three impurities! Will you live here as a dwelling place for hard karma? Lord Siva, who becomes sweet nectar when thought upon, resides in Otriyur. Today itself I am going there to end my sorrows. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Vallalar separates his true self from the ups and downs of life. He tells his mind that worldly joys and sorrows come from karma (the accumulated results of good and bad deeds) and the three impurities (ego, illusion, and past actions) that cloud human awareness. He leaves for the temple town of Otriyur to find God, offering the mind a choice to come or stay.

translit: tuṉpa vāḻviṉaic cukameṉa maṉaṉē cūḻntu māyaiyuḷ āḻntuniṟ kiṉṟāy vaṉpa tākiya nīyumeṉ ṉuṭaṉē varuti yō-aṉṟi niṟṟiyō aṟiyēṉ oṉpa tākiya uruvuṭaip perumāṉ oruvaṉ vāḻkiṉṟa oṟṟiyūrk kiṉṟē iṉpa vāḻvuṟac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: O mind, you consider this sorrowful life to be happiness. You surround yourself with illusion and stand immersed in it. I do not know if you, who are so stubborn, will come with me or stay behind. The one great Lord of nine forms lives in Otriyur. Today itself I am going there to attain a life of bliss. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: The mind is stubborn and mistakes the illusions of worldly life for happiness. Vallalar refuses to wait for it to change, announcing his departure to seek the Lord. By giving his mind formal notice, he clears himself of any blame if it chooses to remain stuck in its ways.

translit: āṭṭu kiṉṟataṟ kāka-am palattuḷ āṭu kiṉṟacē vaṭimalar niṉaiyāy vāṭṭu kiṉṟaṉai valviṉai maṉaṉē vāḻntu nīcuka māyiru kaṇṭāy kūṭṭu kiṉṟanam paracivaṉ makiḻvil kulavum oṟṟiyūrk kōyilcūḻn tiṉpam īṭṭu kiṉṟataṟ kēkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: You do not think of the red lotus feet dancing in the hall to make all things dance. You torment me, O mind of hard karma. Stay here and live happily, you see. Our supreme Siva, who unites us with himself, rejoices in Otriyur. I am going there to circle the temple and gather bliss. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: The divine dance of the Lord animates everything in the universe, but the distracted mind refuses to notice it. Frustrated by the mind's torment, Vallalar sarcastically tells it to stay behind and enjoy its worldly attachments while he goes to gather bliss at the temple.

translit: vañca vāḻkkaiyai viṭuttaṉaṉ nīyē vārik koṇṭiṅku vāḻntiru maṉaṉē nañcam āyiṉum uṇkuvai nītāṉ nāṉum aṅkatai nayappatu naṉṟō tañcam eṉṟavark karuḷtarum perumāṉ taṅkum oṟṟiyūrt talattiṉuk kiṉṟē eñcal iṉṟināṉ celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: I have abandoned this deceitful life. You scoop it up and live here, O mind. You would eat even poison. Is it right for me to desire it along with you? The great Lord who grants grace to those who seek refuge dwells in the sacred place of Otriyur. Today itself I am going there without hesitation. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: The human mind will eagerly consume toxic habits and worldly attachments as if they were nourishment. Recognizing this destructive appetite, Vallalar breaks with his thoughts, seeking refuge instead in divine grace.

translit: uṇmai ōtiṉum ōrntilai maṉaṉē uppi likkuvan tuṇṇukiṉ ṟavarpōl veṇmai vāḻkkaiyiṉ nukarviṉai virumpi veḷukkiṉ ṟāyuṉai veṟuppatil eṉṉē taṇmai mēviya caṭaiyuṭaip perumāṉ cārnta oṟṟiyan talattiṉuk kiṉṟē eṇmai nīṅkiṭac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: Even when the truth is spoken, you do not understand it, O mind. Like those who come and eat unsalted food, you desire the experiences of this empty life and grow pale. What is the use of hating you? The great Lord with cool matted locks resides in the sacred place of Otriyur. Today itself I am going there to cast off my insignificance. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Chasing worldly desires is as unsatisfying as eating unseasoned food. Realizing that hating the mind for its ignorance is useless, Vallalar walks away to seek a meaningful life in the divine presence.

translit: nīṭum aimpoṟi neṟinaṭan tulaka neṟiyil kūṭinī niṉaippoṭu maṟappum nāṭum māyaiyil kiṭantuḻaik kiṉṟāy naṉṟu niṉceyal niṉṟiṭu maṉaṉē āṭum ampalak kūttaṉem perumāṉ amarnta oṟṟiyūr ālayat tiṉṟē īṭu nīṅkiṭac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: You walk the path of the five extending senses, join the ways of the world, and toil in the illusion of remembering and forgetting. Do as you please and stay right here, O mind. Today I am going to the temple in Otriyur where our Lord, the dancer in the hall, resides, to shed my burdens. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Vallalar addresses his mind, declaring a final separation. Because the mind is trapped by the five senses and worldly distractions, Vallalar leaves it behind to seek God at the Otriyur temple.

translit: kūṟum ōrkaṇat teṇṇuṟum niṉaivu kōṭi kōṭiyāyk koṇṭatai maṟantu māṟu māyaiyāl mayaṅkiya maṉaṉē varuti aṉṟeṉil niṟṟi-iv vaḷavil āṟu mēviya vēṇi-em perumāṉ amarnta oṟṟiyūr ālayam ataṉpāl īṟil iṉpuṟac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: O mind deluded by shifting illusion, grasping millions of thoughts in a single moment and then forgetting them! Will you come? If not, stay right here. I am going to the temple in Otriyur, where our Lord with the river in his matted hair dwells, to experience endless joy. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: The mind is chaotic, generating millions of thoughts in a single moment only to lose them in a haze of illusion. Vallalar gives it a choice: come along to find joy in the divine, or be left behind. The imagery of the river in the Lord's matted hair refers to the traditional form of Siva holding the sacred Ganges river.

translit: yātu kaṇṭaṉai ataṉiṭat tellām aṇaikiṉ ṟāyava mākaniṟ kīnta pōtu pōkkiṉai yē-iṉi maṉaṉē pōti pōtinī pōmvaḻi ellām kōtu nīkkinal aruḷtarum perumāṉ kulavum oṟṟiyūrk kōyiluk kiṉṟē ētam ōṭanāṉ celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: O mind, you attach yourself to whatever you see. You squander the time given to you in vain. Now go wherever you wish to go. Today I am going to the temple in Otriyur where the Lord rejoices, who removes faults and grants good grace, so that my miseries flee. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Human awareness attaches itself to whatever crosses its path, wasting the precious time we are given. Vallalar dismisses this restless habit. Instead of following the mind on its wandering, Vallalar turns to the divine presence that clears away faults and grants grace.

translit: viccai vēṇṭiṉai viṉaiyuṭai maṉaṉē mēlai nāḷpaṭṭa vētaṉai aṟiyāy tuccai nīpaṭum tuyaruṉak kallāl colli ṟantanal cukampalit tiṭumō piccai emperu māṉeṉa niṉaiyēl piṟaṅkum oṟṟiyam peruntakai avaṉpāl iccai koṇṭunāṉ celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: O karma-bound mind, you desired illusions. You do not know the agony suffered in the past. You are wretched and only suffer sorrow. Will you ever attain the good joy beyond words? Do not think of our Lord as a mere beggar. I am going with immense longing to that great Lord of shining Otriyur. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Bound by karma, the mind chases illusions and forgets the pain those attachments cause. It even looks down on the divine, mistaking the Lord's traditional guise as a wandering beggar for poverty. Vallalar abandons this foolish mindset, moving toward a joy that words cannot describe.

translit: tūkkam uṟṟiṭum cōmpuṭai maṉaṉē colva teṉṉai-ōr cukamitu eṉṟē ākkam uṟṟunāṉ vāḻanī narakil āḻa nērntiṭum aṉṟukaṇ ṭaṟikāṇ nīkkam uṟṟiṭā niṉmalaṉ amarntu nikaḻum oṟṟiyūr niyamattiṟ kiṉṟē ēkkam aṟṟiṭac celkiṉṟēṉ uṉakkum iyampi ṉēṉpaḻi illai-eṉ mītē.
translation: O lazy mind consumed by sleep! What is there to say when you think this sluggishness is a pleasure? I will flourish and live, while you will end up sinking in hell. See and realize it on that day. Today I am going to the shrine in Otriyur where the flawless Lord eternally dwells, so that my anxieties vanish. I have told you too. There is no blame on me.
commentary: Spiritual growth requires alertness, but the mind often prefers the comfortable numbness of laziness and sleep. Vallalar warns that this sluggishness leads to ruin. By breaking away and turning to the flawless divine presence, Vallalar leaves all worldly anxiety behind to flourish in grace.

translit: vārkkoṇ maṅkaiyar mulaimalaik kēṟṟi maṟittum aṅkavar maṭuviṉil taḷḷap pārkkiṉ ṟāyeṉaik keṭuppatil uṉakkup pāva mē-alāl palaṉciṟi tuḷatō īrkkiṉ ṟāykaṭuṅ kāmamām pulaiyā iṉṟu ceṉṟunāṉ ērpeṟum oṟṟi ūrkkuḷ mēviya civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: You lift me onto the mountain-like breasts of women wearing tight bodices and then push me into their pool. You try to ruin me. Do you gain any benefit from this other than sin? You drag me around, you vile wretch of intense lust! Today I will go to beautiful Otriyur, and with the sword of grace from Lord Siva who dwells there, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Lust is a vicious enemy that drags the mind toward physical obsession and ruin. Vallalar vows to destroy this inner flaw using the grace of Lord Siva as a sword.

translit: koṭiya mātarkaḷ iṭaiyuṟum narakak kuḻiyil eṉtaṉaik koṇṭuceṉ ṟaḻuttik kaṭiya vañcaṉai yāleṉaik kalakkam kaṇṭa pāviyē kāmavēṭ ṭuvaṉē iṭiya neñcakam iṭaruḻan tiruntēṉ iṉṉum eṉṉainī ēṉiḻuk kiṉṟāy oṭivil oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: You dragged me and plunged me into the hellish pit among cruel women. You saw me bewildered by your severe deceit, you sinner, you hunter of lust! My heart breaks as I suffer in affliction. Why do you still pull at me? With the sword of grace from Lord Siva of endless Otriyur, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Lust acts like a deceitful hunter trapping the mind in pain and confusion. Vallalar warns the vice that divine grace will sever its hold.

translit: pētai mātartam maruṅkiṭai āḻnta pilattil eṉtaṉaip piṭittaḻa vīḻtti vātai uṟṟiṭa vaittaṉai aiyō matiyil kāmamām vañcaka muṟiyā ētam nīttaruḷ aṭiyartam cārvāl eḻukiṉ ṟēṉeṉai iṉṉumnī iḻukkil ōtum oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: You seized me and threw me weeping into the deep pit at the waists of foolish women. Alas, you made me suffer torment, you senseless and deceitful blockhead of lust! I am rising up now through the company of gracious devotees who have shed all flaws. If you drag me again, with the sword of grace from Lord Siva of renowned Otriyur, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Freedom from sensual torment comes through the right companions. Vallalar credits flawless devotees for helping him rise out of his obsession, warning lust that divine grace will finish it off if it returns.

translit: kōvam eṉṉumōr kolaippulait talaimaik koṭiya ṉē-eṉaik kūṭinī niṉṟa pāva vaṉmaiyāl pakai-aṭut tuyirmēl parivi lāmalē payaṉiḻan taṉaṉkāṇ cāva nīyila tēleṉai viṭuka calañcey vāyeṉil caturmaṟai muḻakkam ōvil oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O cruel chief of the murderous and vile clan called Anger! Because of the powerful sin of your union with me, I embraced enmity and lost my purpose, showing no compassion for life. Understand this. If you will not die, let me go. If you cause trouble, with the sword of grace from Lord Siva of Otriyur where the roar of the four Vedas never ceases, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Vallalar turns on anger next, calling it a murderer. He says that anger makes a person lose all compassion for living beings, destroying the very purpose of life. He orders this anger to leave or face destruction by the sword of grace.

translit: cārnta lōpamām tayaiyili ēṭā tāḻnti rappavar tamakkaṇu ataṉuḷ īrnta oṉṟiṉai īyavum oṭṭāy irakkiṉ ṟōrtariṉ atukoḷaṟ kicaivāy cōrnti ṭātunāṉ tuyppavum ceyyāy cukami lātanī tūranil iṉṟēl ōrnta oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O merciless fellow called Greed who has clung to me! You do not let me give even a fraction of an atom to those who humbly beg. Yet if those beggars offer something, you agree to take it. You do not even let me enjoy things without exhaustion. You joyless wretch, stand far away. If not, with the sword of grace from Lord Siva of esteemed Otriyur, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Greed refuses to give even a scrap to a beggar while eagerly taking whatever it can get, ruining both generosity and personal happiness. Vallalar banishes this joyless trait with the sword of grace.

translit: mōkam eṉṉumōr mūṭaril ciṟantōy muṭivi lāttuyar mūla-il oḻukkil pōkam eṉṉumōr aḷaṟṟiṭai viḻavum pōṟṟu makkaḷpeṇ ṭaṉṉaitan taiyarām cōka vāriyil aḻuntavum iyaṟṟic cūḻkiṉ ṟāyeṉait toṭarntiṭēl toṭaril ōkai oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O foremost among fools named Infatuation. You make me fall into the mire called sensual pleasure in this domestic life, the root of endless sorrow. You surround me, making me sink into the ocean of sorrow filled with cherished children, wife, mother, and father. Do not follow me. If you do, with the sword of grace from Lord Siva of joyful Otriyur, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Infatuation traps the soul in worldly life. Attachment to family, domestic routines, and physical pleasure creates an ocean of endless sorrow. To break free, divine grace must strike this delusion down.

translit: matame ṉumperu mattaṉē eṉainī varuttal ōtiṉāl vāyiṉuk kaṭaṅkā citame ṉumparaṉ ceyaliṉai aṟiyāy tīṅku ceytaṉar naṉmaiyām ceytōm itama ṟintaṉam emakkiṉi oppār yāvar eṉṟeṉai iḻicciṉai aṭiyārk kutavum oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O great madman named Pride. If I describe how you torment me, words cannot contain it. You do not know the workings of the Supreme Lord who is pure consciousness. You degraded me by making me proudly think, "They did harm. We did good. We know what is beneficial. Who is equal to us now?" With the sword of grace from Lord Siva of Otriyur, who helps his devotees, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Pride is a madness that tricks people into believing they are morally superior. It makes a person judge others and boast of their own good deeds, forgetting that the Supreme Lord orchestrates all things. Grace must destroy this false superiority.

translit: amaiva ṟintiṭā āṇavap payalē akila kōṭiyum āṭṭukiṉ ṟavaṉkāṇ emaina ṭattuvōṉ ītuṇa rāmal iṉṟu nāmparaṉ iṇaiyaṭi toḻutōm kamaiviṉ ēttiṉōm aṭiyarum āṉōm kaṉikiṉ ṟōmeṉak karutiṭa mayakkēl umaiyaṉ oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O arrogant wretch who knows no limits. The Lord who animates all the countless worlds is the very one who guides us. Do not delude me into ignoring this truth and proudly thinking, "Today we worshiped the Supreme Lord's twin feet. We praised him with devotion. We became devotees. We are spiritually maturing." With the sword of grace from Lord Siva of Otriyur, the consort of Uma, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Arrogance infects even spiritual life. The ego loves to claim credit for devotion, boasting of worship and spiritual maturity. This false pride ignores the absolute truth that the Lord animates and guides all actions.

translit: karumai yāmakaṅ kāramark kaṭavā kaṭaiya ṉē-uṉaik kalantata ṉālē arumai yākanām pāṭiṉōm kalvi aṟa-a ṟintaṉam aruḷaiyum aṭaintōm irumai iṉpamum peṟṟaṉam eṉṟē eṉaima tittunāṉ iḻivaṭain taṉaṉkāṇ orumai oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O dark monkey of Ego. O lowly one. By mingling with you, I esteemed myself and fell into degradation, thinking, "We sang beautifully. We mastered all learning. We attained grace. We gained the joys of both worlds." With the sword of grace from Lord Siva of unified Otriyur, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: The ego behaves like a restless monkey, ruining a person through self-congratulation. It turns talents like singing, scholarly learning, and even the experience of grace into fuel for vanity. Claiming these as personal victories leads to spiritual degradation.

translit: veṇmai cērakaṅ kāramām vīṇā viṭuvi ṭeṉṟaṉai vittakam uṇarāy taṇmai iṉṟitaṟ kitu-eṉat tuṇinteṉ taṉaiyum cāyppatu takaveṉa niṉaittāy aṇmai niṉṟiṭēl cēymaiceṉ ṟaḻinī aṉṟi niṟṟiyēl arimutal ēttum uṇmai oṟṟiyūrc civaṉaruḷ vāḷāl uṉṉai veṭṭuval uṇmai-eṉ ṟuṇarē.
translation: O vain Ego full of ignorance. Leave me, leave me. You do not understand divine wisdom. Lacking all calmness, you hastily jumped to conclusions and thought it right to ruin me. Do not stand near me. Go far away and perish. If you stay, with the sword of grace from Lord Siva of true Otriyur, praised by Vishnu and the other gods, I will cut you down. Know this as the truth.
commentary: Vain ego lacks divine wisdom and inner peace. Restless and prone to hasty conclusions, it threatens to ruin the soul. This ignorance must be driven far away, or else it will be cut down by divine grace.

tamil: வாணரை விடையூர் வரதனை ஒற்றி வாணனை மலிகடல் விடமாம்
ஊணனை அடியேம் உளத்தனை எல்லாம் உடையனை உள்கிநின் றேத்தா
வீணரை மடமை விழலரை மரட்ட வேடரை மூடரை நெஞ்சக்
கோணரைமுருட்டுக் குறும்பரைக் கண்டால் கூசுவ கூசுவ விழியே.
translit: vāṇarai viṭaiyūr varataṉai oṟṟi vāṇaṉai malikaṭal viṭamām ūṇaṉai aṭiyēm uḷattaṉai ellām uṭaiyaṉai uḷkiniṉ ṟēttā vīṇarai maṭamai viḻalarai maraṭṭa vēṭarai mūṭarai neñcak kōṇaraimuruṭṭuk kuṟumparaik kaṇṭāl kūcuva kūcuva viḻiyē.
translation: My eyes recoil, they recoil when they see the vain, the ignorant, the stubborn fools, the idiots, the crooked-hearted, and the rough ruffians who do not contemplate and praise the Lord of the heavens, the benefactor who rides the bull, the dweller of Otriyur, the one who consumed the overflowing ocean's poison as food, the one who dwells in the hearts of his devotees, the one who possesses everything.
commentary: True devotion means recognizing a God who sacrifices for others by swallowing the ocean's poison to save the world. People who ignore this compassionate Lord become trapped in vanity, stubbornness, and cruelty. Vallalar says his eyes physically shrink away from such crooked-hearted people.

tamil: மூவரை அளித்த முதல்வனை முக்கண் மூர்த்தியைத் தீர்த்தனைப் பெரிய
தேவரைக் காத்த செல்வனை ஒற்றித் தியாகனை நினைந்துநின் றேத்தாப்
பாவரை வரையாப் படிற்றரை வாதப் பதடரைச் சிதடரைப் பகைசேர்
கோவரைக் கொடிய குணத்தரைக் கண்டால் கூசுவ கூசுவ விழியே.
translit: mūvarai aḷitta mutalvaṉai mukkaṇ mūrttiyait tīrttaṉaip periya tēvaraik kātta celvaṉai oṟṟit tiyākaṉai niṉaintuniṉ ṟēttāp pāvarai varaiyāp paṭiṟṟarai vātap pataṭaraic citaṭaraip pakaicēr kōvaraik koṭiya kuṇattaraik kaṇṭāl kūcuva kūcuva viḻiyē.
translation: My eyes recoil, they recoil when they see the sinners, the boundless deceivers, the empty debaters, the ignorant, the spiteful, and the cruel-natured who do not remember and praise the primal one who created the three gods, the three-eyed Lord, the pure one, the wealthy one who protected the great gods, Lord Thyagar of Otriyur.
commentary: Forgetting the ultimate Creator goes hand in hand with becoming deceptive, cruel, and obsessed with empty arguments. Vallalar feels an instinctive physical disgust for those whose lives are consumed by malice instead of gratitude.

tamil: அண்டனை எண்தோள் அத்தனை ஒற்றி அப்பனை ஐயனை நீல
கண்டனை அடியர் கருத்தனைப் பூத கணத்தனைக் கருதிநின் றேத்தா
மிண்டரைப் பின்றா வெளிற்றரைவலிய வேற்றரைச் சீற்றரைப் பாபக்
குண்டரை வஞ்சக் குடியரைக் கண்டால் கூசுவ கூசுவ விழியே.
translit: aṇṭaṉai eṇtōḷ attaṉai oṟṟi appaṉai aiyaṉai nīla kaṇṭaṉai aṭiyar karuttaṉaip pūta kaṇattaṉaik karutiniṉ ṟēttā miṇṭaraip piṉṟā veḷiṟṟaraivaliya vēṟṟaraic cīṟṟaraip pāpak kuṇṭarai vañcak kuṭiyaraik kaṇṭāl kūcuva kūcuva viḻiyē.
translation: My eyes recoil, they recoil when they see the arrogant, the unrelentingly ignorant, the stubbornly hostile, the wrathful, the deep sinners, and the deceitful citizens who do not meditate upon and praise the Lord of the universe, the eight-shouldered father, the father of Otriyur, the Master, the blue-throated one, the one who dwells in the thoughts of his devotees, the Lord of the goblin hosts.
commentary: Arrogance and hostility are the natural outcomes of a life without spiritual focus. The Lord is a loving father and master who dwells in the thoughts of his devotees. When people close their minds to this presence, they fall into wrath and deceit, causing Vallalar to turn away in horror.

tamil: நாதனைப் பொதுவில் நடத்தனை எவர்க்கும் நல்லனை வல்லனைச் சாம
கீதனை ஒற்றிக் கிறைவனை எங்கள் கேள்வனைக் கிளர்ந்துநின் றேத்தாத்
தீதரை நரகச் செக்கரை வஞ்சத் திருட்டரை மருட்டரைத் தொலையாக்
கோதரைக் கொலைசெய் கோட்டரைக் கண்டால் கூசுவ கூசுவ விழியே.
translit: nātaṉaip potuvil naṭattaṉai evarkkum nallaṉai vallaṉaic cāma kītaṉai oṟṟik kiṟaivaṉai eṅkaḷ kēḷvaṉaik kiḷarntuniṉ ṟēttāt tītarai narakac cekkarai vañcat tiruṭṭarai maruṭṭarait tolaiyāk kōtaraik kolaicey kōṭṭaraik kaṇṭāl kūcuva kūcuva viḻiyē.
translation: My eyes recoil, they recoil when they see the wicked, those bound for the hellish oil press, the deceitful thieves, the deluded, the endlessly flawed, and the murderous tyrants who do not rise up and praise the Master, the dancer in the public hall, the one who is good to all, the omnipotent one, the lover of the Sama Veda, the Lord of Otriyur, our beloved.
commentary: The Divine is described as the dancer in the public hall, completely accessible and good to everyone. Those who reject this universal goodness end up committing violence, theft, and murder. Vallalar links a lack of spiritual love directly to real-world cruelty and oppression.

tamil: நம்பனை அழியா நலத்தனை எங்கள் நாதனை நீதனைக் கச்சிக்
கம்பனை ஒற்றிக் கங்கைவே ணியனைக் கருத்தனைக் கருதிநின் றேத்தா
வம்பரை ஊத்தை வாயரைக் கபட மாயரைப் பேயரை எட்டிக்
கொம்பரைப் பொல்லாக் கோளரைக் கண்டால் கூசுவ கூசுவ விழியே.
translit: nampaṉai aḻiyā nalattaṉai eṅkaḷ nātaṉai nītaṉaik kaccik kampaṉai oṟṟik kaṅkaivē ṇiyaṉaik karuttaṉaik karutiniṉ ṟēttā vamparai ūttai vāyaraik kapaṭa māyaraip pēyarai eṭṭik komparaip pollāk kōḷaraik kaṇṭāl kūcuva kūcuva viḻiyē.
translation: My eyes recoil, they recoil when they see the worthless, the foul-mouthed, the deceitful frauds, the demonic, the toxic branches, and the wicked slanderers who do not meditate upon and praise the trustworthy one, the one of imperishable goodness, our Master, the righteous one, Lord Kampan of Kanchi, the Lord of Otriyur who wears the Ganges in his braided hair, the supreme Lord of thought.
commentary: The Lord represents imperishable goodness and trustworthiness. People who turn their backs on this goodness become like toxic branches: full of deceit, foul language, and slander. Vallalar's recoiling eyes physically reject this harmful way of living.

tamil: சடையனை எவர்க்கும் தலைவனைக் கொன்றைத் தாரனைச் சராசர சடத்துள்
உடையனை ஒற்றி ஊரனை மூவர் உச்சனை உள்கிநின் றேத்தாக்
கடையரைப் பழைய கயவரைப் புரட்டுக் கடியரைக் கடியரைக் கலக
நடையரை உலக நசையரைக் கண்டால் நடுங்குவ நடுங்குவ மனமே.
translit: caṭaiyaṉai evarkkum talaivaṉaik koṉṟait tāraṉaic carācara caṭattuḷ uṭaiyaṉai oṟṟi ūraṉai mūvar uccaṉai uḷkiniṉ ṟēttāk kaṭaiyaraip paḻaiya kayavaraip puraṭṭuk kaṭiyaraik kaṭiyaraik kalaka naṭaiyarai ulaka nacaiyaraik kaṇṭāl naṭuṅkuva naṭuṅkuva maṉamē.
translation: If I see those who do not meditate on and praise the Lord with matted hair, the Lord of all, the one wearing the Konrai garland, the one holding the moving and unmoving universe within Himself, the Lord of Otriyur, the supreme one above the three gods, my mind trembles, it trembles. It trembles seeing such base people, habitual scoundrels, cruel deceivers, hard-hearted ones, those who walk the path of conflict, and those consumed by worldly desires.
commentary: Vallalar feels physical fear when he sees people consumed by greed, deceit, and conflict. They refuse to think of the divine, who wears the Konrai (a sacred golden flower) and holds the moving and unmoving universe within himself.

tamil: கஞ்சனைச் சிரங்கொய் கரத்தனை மூன்று கண்ணனைக் கண்ணனைக் காத்த
தஞ்சனை ஒற்றித் தலத்தனைச் சைவத் தலைவனைத் தாழ்ந்துநின் றேத்தா
வஞ்சரைக் கடைய மடையரைக் காம மனத்தரைச் சினத்தரை வலிய
நஞ்சரை இழிந்த நரகரைக் கண்டால் நடுங்குவ நடுங்குவ மனமே.
translit: kañcaṉaic ciraṅkoy karattaṉai mūṉṟu kaṇṇaṉaik kaṇṇaṉaik kātta tañcaṉai oṟṟit talattaṉaic caivat talaivaṉait tāḻntuniṉ ṟēttā vañcaraik kaṭaiya maṭaiyaraik kāma maṉattaraic ciṉattarai valiya nañcarai iḻinta narakaraik kaṇṭāl naṭuṅkuva naṭuṅkuva maṉamē.
translation: If I see those who do not bow down and praise the one whose hand plucked Brahma's head, the three-eyed one, the refuge who protected Vishnu, the Lord of Otriyur, the Lord of Saivam, my mind trembles, it trembles. It trembles seeing such deceitful people, the lowest fools, those with lustful minds, angry ones, those like potent poison, and those degraded beings of hell.
commentary: Anger, lust, and deceit are poisonous states of mind that drag down the soul. Vallalar feels terrified when he encounters people trapped in these states who refuse to seek divine refuge. God's power to offer this refuge is shown when Siva disciplines Brahma (the creator god) and shelters Vishnu (the preserver god).

tamil: தாமனை மழுமான் தரித்தசெங் கரனைத் தகையனைச் சங்கரன் தன்னைச்
சேமனை ஒற்றித் தியாகனைச் சிவனைத் தேவனைத் தேர்ந்துநின் றேத்தா
ஊமரைநீண்ட ஒதியரைப் புதிய ஒட்டரைத் துட்டரைப் பகைகொள்
நாமரை நரக நாடரைக் கண்டால் நடுங்குவ நடுங்குவ மனமே.
translit: tāmaṉai maḻumāṉ tarittaceṅ karaṉait takaiyaṉaic caṅkaraṉ taṉṉaic cēmaṉai oṟṟit tiyākaṉaic civaṉait tēvaṉait tērntuniṉ ṟēttā ūmarainīṇṭa otiyaraip putiya oṭṭarait tuṭṭaraip pakaikoḷ nāmarai naraka nāṭaraik kaṇṭāl naṭuṅkuva naṭuṅkuva maṉamē.
translation: If I see those who do not realize and praise the garlanded one, the one holding the battle-axe and the deer in his red hands, the great one, Sankara himself, the protector, Lord Tyagaraja of Otriyur, Siva, the supreme God, my mind trembles, it trembles. It trembles seeing such ignorant people, useless tall fools, strange schemers, wicked ones, terrifying instigators of enmity, and those seeking hell.
commentary: Living without the awareness of God turns people into ignorant and wicked schemers. Vallalar shrinks in fear from those who stir up enmity and ruin their own lives. He praises God as Thyagar (the presiding Lord at the Otriyur temple) and Sankara (the bringer of peace), the only protector from worldly ruin.

tamil: ஈசனைத் தாயில் இனியனை ஒற்றி இன்பனை அன்பனை அழியாத்
தேசனைத் தலைமைத் தேவனை ஞானச் சிறப்பனைச் சேர்ந்துநின் றேத்தா
நீசரை நாண்இல் நெட்டரை நரக நேயரைத் தீயரைத் தரும
நாசரை ஒழியா நட்டரைக் கண்டால் நடுங்குவ நடுங்குவ மனமே.
translit: īcaṉait tāyil iṉiyaṉai oṟṟi iṉpaṉai aṉpaṉai aḻiyāt tēcaṉait talaimait tēvaṉai ñāṉac ciṟappaṉaic cērntuniṉ ṟēttā nīcarai nāṇil neṭṭarai naraka nēyarait tīyarait taruma nācarai oḻiyā naṭṭaraik kaṇṭāl naṭuṅkuva naṭuṅkuva maṉamē.
translation: If I see those who do not gather and praise the Lord, the one sweeter than a mother, the blissful Lord of Otriyur, the loving one, the imperishable light, the supreme God, the one of excellent wisdom, my mind trembles, it trembles. It trembles seeing such base people, shameless empty vessels, lovers of hell, evil ones, destroyers of righteousness, and relentless bringers of ruin.
commentary: Vallalar describes God with affection as a loving presence sweeter than a mother. Those who reject this boundless love become empty, shameless, and destructive. They actively ruin righteousness instead of seeking the joy and wisdom of the divine.

tamil: நித்தனைத் தூய நிமலனைப் புலியூர் நிருத்தனை ஒருத்தனை வாய்மைச்
சுத்தனை ஒற்றித் தலம்வளர் ஞான சுகத்தனைச் சூழ்ந்துநின் றேத்தா
மத்தரைச் சமண வாதரைத் தேர வறியரை முறியரை வைண
நத்தரைச் சுணங்க நாவரைக் கண்டால் நடுங்குவ நடுங்குவ மனமே.
translit: nittaṉait tūya nimalaṉaip puliyūr niruttaṉai oruttaṉai vāymaic cuttaṉai oṟṟit talamvaḷar ñāṉa cukattaṉaic cūḻntuniṉ ṟēttā mattaraic camaṇa vātarait tēra vaṟiyarai muṟiyarai vaiṇa nattaraic cuṇaṅka nāvaraik kaṇṭāl naṭuṅkuva naṭuṅkuva maṉamē.
translation: If I see those who do not gather around and praise the eternal one, the pure flawless one, the cosmic dancer of Puliyur, the peerless one, the utterly truthful one, the blissful Lord of wisdom who prospers in Otriyur, my mind trembles, it trembles. It trembles seeing such madmen, argumentative Jains, impoverished Buddhists, broken ones, Vaishnava sectarians, and those with dog-like tongues.
commentary: Sectarian division and religious argument terrify Vallalar just as much as worldly greed. Vallalar plainly calls the argumentative Jains, Buddhists, and Vaishnavas (followers of Vishnu) madmen with dog-like tongues. He sees their rigid dogmas as a failure to recognize the pure, eternal divine truth, which he honors here as the cosmic dancer of Puliyur (the sacred town of Chidambaram).

tamil: தேவர் அறியார் மால்அறியான் திசைமா முகத்தோன் தான்அறியான்
யாவர் அறியார் திருஒற்றி யப்பா அடியேன் யாதறிவேன்
மூவர் திருப்பாட் டினுக்கிசைந்தே முதிர்தீம் பாலும் முக்கனியும்
காவல் அமுதும் நறுந்தேனும் கைப்ப இனிக்கும் நின்புகழே.
translit: tēvar aṟiyār mālaṟiyāṉ ticaimā mukattōṉ tāṉaṟiyāṉ yāvar aṟiyār tiru-oṟṟi yappā aṭiyēṉ yātaṟivēṉ mūvar tiruppāṭ ṭiṉukkicaintē mutirtīm pālum mukkaṉiyum kāval amutum naṟuntēṉum kaippa iṉikkum niṉpukaḻē.
translation: The celestial beings do not know. Vishnu does not know. The four-faced Brahma of the directions does not know. Everyone fails to know. Father of holy Otriyur, what can I, your servant, know? When sung in harmony with the sacred songs of the three saints, your praise tastes so sweet that rich sweet milk, the three fruits, the guarded nectar of the gods, and fragrant honey turn bitter in comparison.
commentary: Since the greatest gods cannot comprehend divine reality, an ordinary person naturally feels lost. Yet Vallalar finds that singing divine praise in the tradition of the ancient saints offers a sweetness surpassing honey, fruit, and the nectar of the gods.

tamil: புகழே விரும்பிப் புலன்இழந்தேன் போந்துன் பதத்தைப் போற்றுகிலேன்
இகழேன் எனைநான் ஒற்றியப்பா என்னை மதித்தேன் இருள்மனத்தேன்
திகழ்ஏழ் உலகில் எனைப்போல்ஓர் சிறியர் அறியேன் தீவினையை
translit: pukaḻē virumpip pulaṉiḻantēṉ pōntuṉ patattaip pōṟṟukilēṉ ikaḻēṉ eṉaināṉ oṟṟiyappā eṉṉai matittēṉ iruḷmaṉattēṉ tikaḻēḻ ulakil eṉaippōlōr ciṟiyar aṟiyēṉ tīviṉaiyai akaḻēṉeṉiṉum eṉaiyāḷā takaṟṟal aruḷuk kaḻakaṉṟē.
translation: Desiring worldly fame, I lost my senses. I do not come and praise your feet. I do not despise myself. Father of Otriyur, possessing a dark heart, I esteemed myself highly. In the radiant seven worlds, I know no one as petty as me. Even if I do not dig out my evil deeds, discarding me without taking me into your service does not befit your Grace.
commentary: A dark heart and swollen ego blind a person to spiritual life. Vallalar admits that chasing public approval leaves him feeling petty and disconnected from God. Unable to root out his own bad habits, he asks to be taken into divine service anyway, reasoning that grace exists to save those who cannot save themselves.

tamil: அன்றும் அறியார் மாதவரும் அயனும் மாலும் நின்நிலையை
இன்றும் அறியார் அன்றியவர் என்றும் அறியார் என்னில்ஒரு
ஒன்றும் நெறிஏ தொற்றியப்பா ஒப்பார் இல்லா உத்தமனே.
translit: aṉṟum aṟiyār mātavarum ayaṉum mālum niṉnilaiyai iṉṟum aṟiyār aṉṟiyavar eṉṟum aṟiyār eṉṉiloru naṉṟum aṟiyēṉ nāyaṭiyēṉ nāṉeppaṭitāṉ aṟivēṉō oṉṟum neṟi-ē toṟṟiyappā oppār illā uttamaṉē.
translation: Even in the past, the great sages, Brahma, and Vishnu did not know your state. Today too they do not know. Indeed, they will never know. If this is so, how can I possibly know, I who am a dog-like servant knowing no good at all? Father of Otriyur, peerless supreme one, what is the path to unite with you?
commentary: If powerful celestial beings remain forever ignorant of God's state, a humble servant stands no chance of grasping it through intellect. Acknowledging his ignorance, Vallalar stops trying to understand the divine mystery and instead asks the Lord to show him the direct path to unity.

tamil: ஒப்பார் இல்லா ஒற்றியப்பா உன்னை மறந்தேன் மாதர்கள்தம்
வெப்பார் குழியில் கண்மூடி விழுந்தேன் எழுந்தும் விரைகின்றேன்
இப்பார் நடையில் களித்தவரை ஈர்த்துக் கொடுபோய்ச் செக்கிலிடு
விப்பார் நமனார் என்பதைநான் நினையா தறிவை விடுத்தேனே.
translit: oppār illā oṟṟiyappā uṉṉai maṟantēṉ mātarkaḷtam veppār kuḻiyil kaṇmūṭi viḻuntēṉ eḻuntum viraikiṉṟēṉ ippār naṭaiyil kaḷittavarai īrttuk koṭupōyc cekkiliṭu vippār namaṉār eṉpataināṉ niṉaiyā taṟivai viṭuttēṉē.
translation: Peerless Father of Otriyur, I forgot you. I closed my eyes and fell into the hot pit of women. Even when I rise, I rush back to it. Lord Yama's agents drag away those who revel in worldly ways and crush them in an oil press. Without thinking of this, I abandoned my wisdom.
commentary: Sensual obsession pulls the mind repeatedly into a trap of its own making. Vallalar laments abandoning his wisdom for the heat of lust, rushing back to it even after trying to pull away. He recalls Yama, the god of death, whose messengers crush worldly souls in an oil press, yet he finds himself ignoring this inevitable end.

tamil: விடுத்தேன் தவத்தோர் நெறிதன்னை வியந்தேன் உலக வெந்நெறியை
மடுத்தேன் துன்ப வாரிதனை வஞ்ச மனத்தர் மாட்டுறவை
அடுத்தேன் ஒற்றி யப்பாஉன் அடியை நினையேன் அலமந்தேன்
படுத்தே நமன்செக் கிடும்போது படிறேன் யாது படுவேனோ.
translit: viṭuttēṉ tavattōr neṟitaṉṉai viyantēṉ ulaka venneṟiyai maṭuttēṉ tuṉpa vāritaṉai vañca maṉattar māṭṭuṟavai aṭuttēṉ oṟṟi yappā-uṉ aṭiyai niṉaiyēṉ alamantēṉ paṭuttē namaṉcek kiṭumpōtu paṭiṟēṉ yātu paṭuvēṉō.
translation: I abandoned the path of the ascetics. I admired the cruel path of the world. I drank from the ocean of sorrow. I associated with deceitful people. Father of Otriyur, I do not think of your feet. I reel in despair. When Yama lays me down and crushes me in his oil press, what suffering will I endure?
commentary: Choosing the cruel ways of the world over a disciplined spiritual life guarantees a harvest of sorrow. Deceitful company and forgotten devotion lead to despair as death approaches. Vallalar trembles at the thought of being crushed by the consequences of his worldly choices when his time runs out.

tamil: படுவேன் அல்லேன் நமன்தமரால் பரிவேன் அல்லேன் பரமநினை
விடுவேன் அல்லேன் என்னையும்நீ விடுவாய் அல்லை இனிச்சிறிதும்
கெடுவேன் அல்லேன் சிறியார்சொல் கேட்பேன் அல்லேன் தருமநெறி
அடுவேன் அல்லேன் திருஒற்றி யப்பா உன்றன் அருள்உண்டே.
translit: paṭuvēṉ allēṉ namaṉtamarāl parivēṉ allēṉ paramaniṉai viṭuvēṉ allēṉ eṉṉaiyumnī viṭuvāy allai iṉicciṟitum keṭuvēṉ allēṉ ciṟiyārcol kēṭpēṉ allēṉ tarumaneṟi aṭuvēṉ allēṉ tiru-oṟṟi yappā uṉṟaṉ aruḷuṇṭē.
translation: I will not suffer at the hands of death's messengers. I will not grieve. O Supreme Lord, I will not let you go, and you will not let me go. I will not face ruin even slightly hereafter. I will not listen to the words of petty people. I will not ruin the path of virtue. O Father of holy Otriyur, your grace is with me.
commentary: With the Lord's grace present, all fear of death, sorrow, and ruin vanishes. The soul holds fast to the divine, confident that God will never let go. This trust makes it easy to ignore petty distractions and remain steadily on the path of goodness.

tamil: உண்டோ எனைப்போல் மதிஇழந்தோர் ஒற்றி யப்பா உன்னுடைய
திண்டோள் இலங்கும் திருநீற்றைக் காண விரும்பேன் சேர்ந்தேத்தேன்
எண்தோள் உடையாய் என்றிரங்கேன் இறையும் திரும்பேன் இவ்வறிவைக்
கொண்டே உனைநான் கூடுவன்நின் குறிப்பே தொன்றும் அறியேனே.
translit: uṇṭō eṉaippōl mati-iḻantōr oṟṟi yappā uṉṉuṭaiya tiṇṭōḷ ilaṅkum tirunīṟṟaik kāṇa virumpēṉ cērntēttēṉ eṇtōḷ uṭaiyāy eṉṟiraṅkēṉ iṟaiyum tirumpēṉ ivvaṟivaik koṇṭē uṉaināṉ kūṭuvaṉniṉ kuṟippē toṉṟum aṟiyēṉē.
translation: Are there any who have lost their mind like me? O Father of Otriyur, I do not yearn to see the holy ash shining on your strong shoulders. I do not draw near to praise you. I do not melt crying out, "O Lord with eight shoulders!" I do not turn back from the world even slightly. Holding onto this ignorance, how will I unite with you? I do not know your intention at all.
commentary: A soul looks honestly at its own failings, wondering if anyone else is as foolish. Even while knowing the divine, a person often fails to offer sincere praise or turn away from worldly distractions. Vallalar asks how he can unite with God while still clinging to spiritual ignorance.

tamil: அறியேன் உன்தன் புகழ்ப்பெருமை அண்ணா ஒற்றி யப்பாநான்
சிறியேன் எனினும் நினைஅன்றித் தெளியேன் மற்றோர் தேவர்தமை
நெறியே தருதல் நின்கடன்காண் நின்னைப் பணிதல் என்கடனே.
translit: aṟiyēṉ uṉtaṉ pukaḻpperumai aṇṇā oṟṟi yappānāṉ ciṟiyēṉ eṉiṉum niṉai-aṉṟit teḷiyēṉ maṟṟōr tēvartamai veṟiyēṉ piḻaiyaik kuṟitteṉaikkai viṭṭāl eṉceyvēṉaṭiyēṉ neṟiyē tarutal niṉkaṭaṉkāṇ niṉṉaip paṇital eṉkaṭaṉē.
translation: I do not know the greatness of your glory. O Elder Brother, O Father of Otriyur, even though I am lowly, I seek no clarity in other gods besides you. If you mark the faults of this madman and abandon me, what will I, your servant, do? Granting the right path is your duty. Bowing to you is my duty.
commentary: Despite feeling small and foolish, Vallalar refuses to turn to any other gods for clarity. A binding agreement connects the soul and the divine: the devotee's only job is to surrender and bow down, while God's duty is to provide the right path.

tamil: கடனே அடியர் தமைக்காத்தல் என்றால் கடையேன் அடியன்அன்றோ
உடன்நேர் பிணியும் ஒழித்திலைஎன் உள்ளத் துயரும் தவிர்த்திலையே
விடன்நேர் கண்டத் தின்னமுதே வேத முடியில் விளங்கொளியே
அடன்ஏர் விடையாய் திருஒற்றி யப்பா உனைநான் அயர்ந்திலனே.
translit: kaṭaṉē aṭiyar tamaikkāttal eṉṟāl kaṭaiyēṉ aṭiyaṉaṉṟō uṭaṉnēr piṇiyum oḻittilai-eṉ uḷḷat tuyarum tavirttilaiyē viṭaṉnēr kaṇṭat tiṉṉamutē vēta muṭiyil viḷaṅkoḷiyē aṭaṉēr viṭaiyāy tiru-oṟṟi yappā uṉaināṉ ayarntilaṉē.
translation: If protecting devotees is your duty, am I, the lowest one, not your devotee? You have not cured the disease afflicting my body, and you have not dispelled the sorrow in my heart. O sweet nectar with a poison-stained throat, O shining light at the crown of the Vedas, O Lord of holy Otriyur who rides the strong bull, I have never forgotten you.
commentary: Vallalar holds God to the promise of protection. He points out that he has never forgotten the Lord, yet his physical illness and inner sorrow remain uncured. He asks why a God known as the guiding light of the Vedas (ancient sacred scriptures) would leave a devoted servant in pain.

tamil: இலனே மற்றோர் துணைசிறிதும் என்னே காமம் எனும்கடலில்
மலனேன் வருந்தக் கண்டிருத்தல் மணியே அருளின் மரபன்றே
நலனேர் தில்லை அம்பலத்தில் நடிக்கும் பதமே நாடினனே.
translit: ilaṉē maṟṟōr tuṇaiciṟitum eṉṉē kāmam eṉumkaṭalil malaṉēṉ varuntak kaṇṭiruttal maṇiyē aruḷiṉ marapaṉṟē alaṉē ayalāṉ aṭiyēṉnāṉ aiyā-oṟṟi yappānal nalaṉēr tillai ampalattil naṭikkum patamē nāṭiṉaṉē.
translation: I have no other support, not even the slightest. What is this? O Gem, watching this impure one suffer in the ocean of desire is not the way of grace. I am not a stranger; I am your servant. O Master, O Father of Otriyur, I sought your dancing feet in the supremely good hall of Thillai.
commentary: Grace cannot stand by and watch a soul drown in worldly desires. Vallalar reminds God that he is not a stranger but a dedicated servant who has always sought the divine dancing feet at Thillai (the sacred temple of Chidambaram). He argues that leaving a devotee to suffer goes against the nature of divine compassion.

tamil: நாடி அலுத்தேன் என்அளவோ நம்பா மன்றுள் நன்குநடம்
ஆடி மகிழும் திருஒற்றி அப்பா உன்தன் அருட்புகழைக்
கோடி அளவில் ஒருகூறும் குணித்தார் இன்றி ஆங்காங்கும்
தேடி அளந்தும் தெளிந்திலரே திருமால் முதலாம் தேவர்களே.
translit: nāṭi aluttēṉ eṉaḷavō nampā maṉṟuḷ naṉkunaṭam āṭi makiḻum tiru-oṟṟi appā uṉtaṉ aruṭpukaḻaik kōṭi aḷavil orukūṟum kuṇittār iṉṟi āṅkāṅkum tēṭi aḷantum teḷintilarē tirumāl mutalām tēvarkaḷē.
translation: I sought and grew weary. Does this happen only to me? O trustworthy Lord, O Father of sacred Otriyur who rejoices dancing beautifully in the hall, even the gods headed by Vishnu searched everywhere and tried to measure the glory of your grace. They could not calculate even one part in ten million, and they failed to understand it.
commentary: Vallalar's exhaustion in trying to comprehend God is shared by the highest deities. He finds comfort in realizing that his own weariness is natural. If the greatest gods like Vishnu search everywhere and cannot understand a fraction of this divine grace, a human seeker need not despair at their own limits. By calling out to the Father of Otriyur, Vallalar maintains a close, loving bond with the divine despite its unmeasurable vastness.

tamil: அணங்கனார் களபத் தனமலைக் கிவரும் அறிவிலேன் என்புகாத் துழலும்
சுணங்கனேன் தனக்குன் திருவருள் கிடைக்கும் சுகமும் உண் டாங்கொலோ அறியேன்
கணங்கள்நேர் காட்டில் எரிஉகந் தாடும் கடவுளே கடவுளர்க் கிறையே
உணங்குவெண் தலைத்தார் புனைதிருப் புயனே ஒற்றியூர் உத்தம தேவே.
translit: aṇaṅkaṉār kaḷapat taṉamalaik kivarum aṟivilēṉ eṉpukāt tuḻalum cuṇaṅkaṉēṉ taṉakkuṉ tiruvaruḷ kiṭaikkum cukamum uṇ ṭāṅkolō aṟiyēṉ kaṇaṅkaḷnēr kāṭṭil eri-ukan tāṭum kaṭavuḷē kaṭavuḷark kiṟaiyē uṇaṅkuveṇ talaittār puṉaitirup puyaṉē oṟṟiyūr uttama tēvē.
translation: I am a fool who scales the sandal-scented breast-mountains of beautiful women. I do not know if the bliss of attaining your sacred grace will ever happen to me, a dog that wanders guarding dry bones. O God who dances joyously in the fire of the cremation ground where ghostly hosts gather! O Lord of gods! O one whose sacred shoulders wear a garland of dried white skulls! O supreme God of Otriyur!
commentary: Vallalar compares his worldly desires to a dog guarding dry, fleshless bones. Consumed by lust, he wonders how a mind trapped by the senses could ever receive God's pure grace.

tamil: தேவரே அயனே திருநெடு மாலே சித்தரே முனிவரே முதலா
யாவரே எனினும் ஐயநின் தன்மை அறிந்திலர் யான்உனை அறிதல்
தாவில்வான் சுடரைக் கண்ணிலி அறியும் தன்மையன் றோபெருந்தவத்தோர்
ஓவில்மா தவம்செய் தோங்குசீர் ஒற்றியூர் அமர்ந் தருள்செயும் ஒன்றே.
translit: tēvarē ayaṉē tiruneṭu mālē cittarē muṉivarē mutalā yāvarē eṉiṉum aiyaniṉ taṉmai aṟintilar yāṉuṉai aṟital tāvilvāṉ cuṭaraik kaṇṇili aṟiyum taṉmaiyaṉ ṟōperuntavattōr ōvilmā tavamcey tōṅkucīr oṟṟiyūr amarn taruḷceyum oṉṟē.
translation: Whether they are the gods, Brahma, the sacred tall Vishnu, Siddhas, sages, or anyone else, they have not known your true nature, O Lord. My knowing you is like a blind man perceiving the flawless celestial light in the sky. O One who resides and grants grace in Otriyur of exalted glory, where great ascetics perform ceaseless great penance!
commentary: Even the highest gods and greatest sages cannot grasp the nature of the divine. For an ordinary person to claim to understand God is as impossible as a blind person trying to see the blazing sun in the sky.

tamil: ஒன்றுநின் தன்மை அறிந்தில மறைகள் உள்ளம்நொந் திளைக்கின்றதின்னும்
நன்றுநின் தன்மை நான் அறிந் தேத்தல் நாயர சாளல்போல் அன்றோ
சென்றுநின் றடியர் உள்ளகத் தூறும் தெள்ளிய அமுதத்தின் திரட்டே
மன்றுள்நின் றாடும் மாணிக்க மலையே வளங்கொளும் ஒற்றியூர் மணியே.
translit: oṉṟuniṉ taṉmai aṟintila maṟaikaḷ uḷḷamnon tiḷaikkiṉṟatiṉṉum naṉṟuniṉ taṉmai nāṉ aṟin tēttal nāyara cāḷalpōl aṉṟō ceṉṟuniṉ ṟaṭiyar uḷḷakat tūṟum teḷḷiya amutattiṉ tiraṭṭē maṉṟuḷniṉ ṟāṭum māṇikka malaiyē vaḷaṅkoḷum oṟṟiyūr maṇiyē.
translation: The Vedas do not know your nature in the slightest. Their hearts ache and they still grow weary. For me to know your nature well and praise you is like a dog ruling a kingdom. O mass of clear nectar that enters, stays, and flows in the inner hearts of devotees! O ruby mountain who dances in the Hall! O gem of fertile Otriyur!
commentary: The ancient scriptures try endlessly to define God, but they always fall short and grow exhausted. Vallalar feels so unworthy that he compares singing God's praises to a street dog being crowned king. Yet, he knows the divine flows like sweet nectar in the hearts of devotees.

tamil: மணித்தலை நாகம் அனையவெங் கொடியார் வஞ்சக விழியினால்மயங்கிப்
கணித்தலை அறியாப் பேர்ஒளிக்குன்றே கண்கள்மூன் றுடையஎன் கண்ணே
அணித்தலை அடியர்க் கருள்திரு வொற்றி அப்பனே செப்பரும்பொருளே.
translit: maṇittalai nākam aṉaiyaveṅ koṭiyār vañcaka viḻiyiṉālmayaṅkip piṇittalaik koṇṭu varuntiniṉ ṟuḻalumpētaiyēṟkuṉṉaruḷ uḷatō kaṇittalai aṟiyāp pēroḷikkuṉṟē kaṇkaḷmūṉ ṟuṭaiya-eṉ kaṇṇē aṇittalai aṭiyark karuḷtiru voṟṟi appaṉē cepparumporuḷē.
translation: Bewildered by the deceitful eyes of cruel women who resemble cobras bearing gems on their hoods, I suffer and wander, afflicted by disease. Is there grace for me, such a fool? O hill of immense light that defies calculation! O my eye who has three eyes! O Father of sacred Otriyur who grants grace to the devotees who draw near! O ineffable reality!
commentary: The distractions of the world are dangerously alluring. Vallalar feels poisoned by his own desires, wandering in confusion and sickness, yet he calls out to the supreme light in the hope of rescue.

tamil: ஒப்பிலாய் உனது திருவருள் பெறுவான் உன்னிநை கின்றனன் மனமோ
வெப்பில் ஆழ்ந்தெனது மொழிவழி அடையா வேதனைக் கிடங்கொடுத்துழன்ற
இப்பரி சானால் என்செய்வேன் எளியேன் எவ்வணம் நின் அருள்கிடைக்கும்
translit: oppilāy uṉatu tiruvaruḷ peṟuvāṉ uṉṉinai kiṉṟaṉaṉ maṉamō veppil āḻnteṉatu moḻivaḻi aṭaiyā vētaṉaik kiṭaṅkoṭuttuḻaṉṟa ippari cāṉāl eṉceyvēṉ eḷiyēṉ evvaṇam niṉ aruḷkiṭaikkum tuppura voḻintōr uḷḷakattōṅkum cōtiyē oṟṟiyūrttuṇaiyē.
translation: O peerless one! I think of attaining your sacred grace and pine away. But my mind is sunk in feverish heat and refuses to follow my words. It gives room to agony and wanders. If this is my state, what will I do, a poor wretch? How will I receive your grace? O Jothi who rises in the inner hearts of those who have completely renounced all attachments! O companion of Otriyur!
commentary: The desire for spiritual grace is strong, but the human mind is stubborn and refuses to cooperate. Vallalar feels trapped by a racing mind, realizing that the divine light only rises in hearts that have let go of worldly attachments.

tamil: துணையிலேன் நினது திருவடி அல்லால் துட்டனேன் எனினும் என் தன்னை
இணையிலாய் உனது தொண்டர்தம் தொண்டன் எனச்செயல் நின்அருள் இயல்பே
அணையிலா தன்பர் உள்ளகத் தோங்கும் ஆனந்த வெள்ளமே அரசே
பணையில்வா ளைகள்பாய் ஒற்றியம் பதியில் பரிந்தமர்ந் தருள்செயும் பரமே.
translit: tuṇaiyilēṉ niṉatu tiruvaṭi allāl tuṭṭaṉēṉ eṉiṉum eṉ taṉṉai iṇaiyilāy uṉatu toṇṭartam toṇṭaṉ eṉacceyal niṉaruḷ iyalpē aṇaiyilā taṉpar uḷḷakat tōṅkum āṉanta veḷḷamē aracē paṇaiyilvā ḷaikaḷpāy oṟṟiyam patiyil parintamarn taruḷceyum paramē.
translation: I have no companion other than your holy feet. Even though I am wicked, O peerless one, it is the nature of your grace to make me the servant of your servants. O King, the flood of bliss surging boundlessly within the hearts of devotees. O Supreme Lord who graciously abides with love in the city of Otriyur where scabbard fish leap in the fields.
commentary: Grace transforms even a flawed person into a humble servant of other devotees. Vallalar relies on this grace to elevate him, asking for no companion other than the divine. He describes this presence as an overflowing flood of inner joy experienced by those who love God.

tamil: பரிந்துநின் றுலக வாழ்க்கையில் உழலும் பரிசொழிந் தென்மலக் கங்குல்
இரிந்திட நினது திருவருள் புரியா திருத்தியேல் என்செய்வேன் எளியேன்
எரிந்திட எயில்மூன் றழற்றிய நுதற்கண் எந்தையே எனக்குறுந் துணையே
விரிந்தபூம் பொழில்சூழ் ஒற்றியம் பதியில் மேவிய வித்தக வாழ்வே.
translit: parintuniṉ ṟulaka vāḻkkaiyil uḻalum paricoḻin teṉmalak kaṅkul irintiṭa niṉatu tiruvaruḷ puriyā tiruttiyēl eṉceyvēṉ eḷiyēṉ erintiṭa eyilmūṉ ṟaḻaṟṟiya nutaṟkaṇ entaiyē eṉakkuṟun tuṇaiyē virintapūm poḻilcūḻ oṟṟiyam patiyil mēviya vittaka vāḻvē.
translation: If you do not grant your holy grace to banish the dark night of my impurities and end my wandering with attachment in worldly life, what will this poor one do? O Father whose forehead eye blazed to burn the three fortresses. O my close companion. O miraculous life residing in the city of Otriyur surrounded by expansive flower groves.
commentary: Without God's intervention, the soul remains trapped in the confusion and attachments of worldly life. Vallalar asks God to burn away his inner impurities, just as Lord Siva used the eye of fire on his forehead to burn down three demonic fortresses in ancient lore. God is seen here as both a fierce destroyer of illusion and a personal companion.

tamil: வாழ்வது நின்றன் அடியரோ டன்றி மற்றும் ஓர் வெற்றருள் வாழேன்
தாழ்வது நினது தாட்கலான் மற்றைத் தாட்கெலாம் சரண் எனத் தாழேன்
சூழ்வது நினது திருத்தளி அல்லால் சூழ்கிலேன் தொண்டனேன் தன்னை
ஆள்வது கருதின் அன்றிஎன் செய்கேன் ஐயனே ஒற்றியூர் அரசே.
translit: vāḻvatu niṉṟaṉ aṭiyarō ṭaṉṟi maṟṟum ōr veṟṟaruḷ vāḻēṉ tāḻvatu niṉatu tāṭkalāṉ maṟṟait tāṭkelām caraṇ eṉat tāḻēṉ cūḻvatu niṉatu tiruttaḷi allāl cūḻkilēṉ toṇṭaṉēṉ taṉṉai āḷvatu karutiṉ aṉṟi-eṉ ceykēṉ aiyaṉē oṟṟiyūr aracē.
translation: I will live only with your devotees, and I will never live an empty life with others. I bow down only to your feet, and I will never bow down in surrender to any other feet. I circumambulate only your holy shrine, and I circumambulate nothing else. What will I do if you do not intend to rule this servant? O Master, O King of Otriyur.
commentary: Total devotion means directing every action, reverence, and relationship toward God alone. Vallalar declares his life is bound to the divine, refusing to bow to any other authority or keep company with those who lack spiritual focus. He places the responsibility for his future in God's hands.

tamil: ஐயனே மாலும் அயனும்நின் றறியா அப்பனே ஒற்றியூர் அரசே
மெய்யனே நினது திருவருள் விழைந்தேன் விழைவினை முடிப்பையோ அன்றிப்
பொய்யனேன் தன்மைக் கடாதது கருதிப் பொன்அருள் செயாதிருப் பாயோ
கையனேன் ஒன்றும் அறிந்திலேன் என்னைக் காத்தருள் செய்வதுன் கடனே.
translit: aiyaṉē mālum ayaṉumniṉ ṟaṟiyā appaṉē oṟṟiyūr aracē meyyaṉē niṉatu tiruvaruḷ viḻaintēṉ viḻaiviṉai muṭippaiyō aṉṟip poyyaṉēṉ taṉmaik kaṭātatu karutip poṉaruḷ ceyātirup pāyō kaiyaṉēṉ oṉṟum aṟintilēṉ eṉṉaik kāttaruḷ ceyvatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: O Master, O Father whom Vishnu and Brahma stood and could not comprehend, O King of Otriyur. O Lord of Truth, I yearned for your holy grace. Will you fulfill my yearning, or will you withhold your golden grace by considering the unfit nature of this false one? I am ignorant and know nothing. It is your duty to protect and grace me.
commentary: God has a duty to protect the ignorant and the flawed. Even though the divine is so vast that the great deities Brahma and Vishnu could not comprehend it, the bond between God and the devotee remains personal. By admitting his lack of knowledge, Vallalar places the burden of his salvation on divine grace.

tamil: செய்வதுன் கடன்காண் சிவபெரு மானே திருவொற்றி யூர்வருந் தேனே
உய்வதென் கடன்காண் அன்றிஒன் றில்லை உலகெலாம் உடையநா யகனே
நைவதென் நெஞ்சம் என்செய்கேன் நினது நல்அருள் பெறாவிடில் என்னை
வைவதுன் அடியர் அன்றிஇவ் வுலக வாழ்க்கையில் வரும்பொலாஅணங்கே.
translit: ceyvatuṉ kaṭaṉkāṇ civaperu māṉē tiruvoṟṟi yūrvarun tēṉē uyvateṉ kaṭaṉkāṇ aṉṟi-oṉ ṟillai ulakelām uṭaiyanā yakaṉē naivateṉ neñcam eṉceykēṉ niṉatu nalaruḷ peṟāviṭil eṉṉai vaivatuṉ aṭiyar aṉṟi-iv vulaka vāḻkkaiyil varumpolā-aṇaṅkē.
translation: O Lord Siva, it is your duty to act. O sweet honey flowing in Otriyur. My only duty is to attain salvation, and there is nothing else. O Master who possesses all the worlds. My heart withers in sorrow. What will I do? If I do not receive your good grace, your devotees will reproach me. The evil afflictions of this worldly life will also torment me.
commentary: The soul has one purpose, and God has a corresponding duty: the individual must seek spiritual freedom, and God must grant the grace to achieve it. Vallalar's heart is withering under the harsh pressures of worldly life. He warns that if God fails to act, he will be left defenseless against the afflictions of the world.

tamil: இன்றிருந் தவரை நாளைஇவ் வுலகில் இருந்திடக் கண்டிலேம் ஆஆ
என்றிருந் தவத்தோர் அரற்றுகின் றனரால் ஏழையேன் உண்டுடுத் தவமே
சென்றிருந் துறங்கி விழிப்பதே அல்லால் செய்வன செய்கிலேன் அந்தோ
மன்றிருந் தோங்கும் மணிச்சுடர் ஒளியே வள்ளலே ஒற்றியூர் வாழ்வே.
translit: iṉṟirun tavarai nāḷai-iv vulakil iruntiṭak kaṇṭilēm ā-ā eṉṟirun tavattōr araṟṟukiṉ ṟaṉarāl ēḻaiyēṉ uṇṭuṭut tavamē ceṉṟirun tuṟaṅki viḻippatē allāl ceyvaṉa ceykilēṉ antō maṉṟirun tōṅkum maṇiccuṭar oḷiyē vaḷḷalē oṟṟiyūr vāḻvē.
translation: "Alas, those who were here today, we do not see them in this world tomorrow!" Great sages lament like this. Yet I, a poor wretch, merely eat, dress, wander, sit, sleep, and wake in vain. I do not do what ought to be done. Alas! O soaring radiant light of a jeweled flame in the Hall! O Munificent One! O life of Otriyur!
commentary: Sages warn of life's sudden end. Vallalar laments wasting his brief life on eating, sleeping, and wandering, missing the actual purpose of human birth.

tamil: தாவியே இயமன் தமர்வரும் அந்நாள் சம்புநின் திருவருள் அடையாப்
பாவியேன் செய்வ தென்என நெஞ்சம் பதைபதைத் துருகுகின் றனன்காண்
கூவியே எனக்குன் அருள்தரின் அல்லால் கொடியனேன் உய்வகை அறியேன்
வாவிஏர் பெறப்பூஞ் சோலைசூழ்ந் தோங்கி வளம்பெறும் ஒற்றியூர் வாழ்வே.
translit: tāviyē iyamaṉ tamarvarum annāḷ campuniṉ tiruvaruḷ aṭaiyāp pāviyēṉ ceyva teṉeṉa neñcam pataipatait turukukiṉ ṟaṉaṉkāṇ kūviyē eṉakkuṉ aruḷtariṉ allāl koṭiyaṉēṉ uyvakai aṟiyēṉ vāvi-ēr peṟappūñ cōlaicūḻn tōṅki vaḷampeṟum oṟṟiyūr vāḻvē.
translation: On that day when the messengers of death leap upon me, I, a sinner who has not attained your divine grace, O Shambu, will cry out asking what I shall do. See how my heart palpitates and melts in fear! Unless you call me and grant me your grace, I, a cruel wretch, know no way of salvation. O life of Otriyur, flourishing with beautiful ponds and soaring flower groves!
