commentary: The physical body is nothing more than a temporary leather bag. Stuffing it with food while ignoring the divine wastes the chance for liberation. True joy belongs to the peaceful devotees who keep the names of God constantly on their lips.

tamil: முறைப்படி நினது முன்புநின் றேத்தி முன்னிய பின்னர்உண் ணாமல்
சிறைப்படி வயிற்றில் பொறைப்பட ஒதிபோல் சென்றுநின் முன்னர்உற் றதனால்
கறைப்பட ஓங்கும் கண்டனே எவர்க்கும் கருத்தனே ஒருத்தனே மிகுசீர்
தறைப்படர்ந் தோங்கும் ஒற்றியில் உன்னால் தண்டிக்கப் பட்டனன் அன்றே.
translit: muṟaippaṭi niṉatu muṉpuniṉ ṟētti muṉṉiya piṉṉaruṇ ṇāmal ciṟaippaṭi vayiṟṟil poṟaippaṭa otipōl ceṉṟuniṉ muṉṉaruṟ ṟataṉāl kaṟaippaṭa ōṅkum kaṇṭaṉē evarkkum karuttaṉē oruttaṉē mikucīr taṟaippaṭarn tōṅkum oṟṟiyil uṉṉāl taṇṭikkap paṭṭaṉaṉ aṉṟē.
translation: Without properly standing before You, praising You, meditating upon You, and eating only afterward, I burdened my imprisoning stomach and came to stand before You like a chameleon. Because of this, O Lord with the dark throat, O creator of all, O peerless one, I was punished by you in highly renowned Otriyur which spreads its glory across the earth, was I not?
commentary: The proper sequence of daily life is to praise and meditate on God before taking a meal. Approaching the divine only after gorging oneself, weighed down by a heavy stomach, is a failure of devotion that separates the soul from grace.

note: Editor's note: sung at Otriyur and at Thillai (Chidambaram) (tiruvoṟṟiyūrum tiruttillaiyum, திருவொற்றியூரும் திருத்தில்லையும்).
translit: nīla ṉēṉkoṭum poyyala turaiyā nīcaṉ eṉpateṉ neñcaṟin tatukāṇ cāla āyiṉum niṉkaḻal aṭikkē caraṇpu kuntiṭil taḷḷutal vaḻakkō ālam uṇṭaniṉ taṉmaimā ṟuvatēl akila kōṭiyum aḻintiṭum aṉṟē cīla mēviya oṟṟiyam paraṉē tillai ampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: My heart knows I am a base person who speaks nothing but cruel lies. Even so, if I take refuge at your anklet-adorned feet, is it just to reject me? If your nature of consuming the poison changes, millions of worlds will perish. O Lord of virtuous Otriyur, O shining light in the Hall of Thillai.
commentary: Vallalar brings his worst self to God, confessing to a heart full of cruelty and lies. He reminds the divine of the ancient story where Siva swallowed cosmic poison to save the universe, asking for that same world-saving mercy now for a flawed soul seeking safety.

translit: kaṇṇuṉ māmaṇi yē-aruṭ karumpē kaṟṟa neñcakam kaṉintiṭum kaṉiyē eṇṇuḷ uṭpaṭā iṉpamē eṉṟeṉ ṟentai niṉṟaṉai ēttilaṉ eṉiṉum maṇṇuḷ maṟṟiyāṉ vaḻivaḻi aṭiyēṉ māya maṉṟituṉ maṉamaṟin tatuvē tiṇṇam īntaruḷ oṟṟiyūr aracē tillai ampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: O great gem in the eye, sugarcane of grace, fruit that ripens in the hearts of the learned, bliss that cannot be contained in thought. Even if I have not praised you in this way, my Father, I am your devotee on this earth through generations. This is no illusion. Your heart knows this truth. Bestow certainty and grace on me, O King of Otriyur, O shining light in the Hall of Thillai.
commentary: Devotion often feels inadequate when faced with the sweetness and majesty of the divine. Vallalar admits he has not praised God as well as the learned do. Instead, he relies on an inherited right to grace, coming from a long line of devoted servants.

translit: nallaṉ allaṉāṉ āyiṉum ciṟiyēṉ nāṉa ṟintatō nāṭaṟin tatukāṇ colla vāyilai āyiṉum eṉainī toḻumpu koṇṭiṭil tuyyaṉum āvēṉ valla uṉkarut taṟintilēṉ maṉamē mayaṅku kiṉṟatiyāṉ vāṭukiṉ ṟaṉaṉkāṇ cellal nīkkiya oṟṟiyūr aracē tillai ampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: I am not a good person. Even if I, a lowly one, do not know this, the world knows it well. I have no words to speak, but if you take me into your service, I will become pure. I do not know your powerful intention. My mind is bewildered and I wither away. O King of Otriyur who removes suffering, O shining light in the Hall of Thillai.
commentary: Admitting faults to the world leaves us vulnerable, but offering them to God brings purification. Vallalar knows his bad reputation and feels lost. Yet he trusts that being accepted into divine service is enough to wash away his impurities and heal his bewildered mind.

translit: irakkam eṉpateṉ ṉiṭattilai eṉanī ikaḻti yēlaḵti yalpumaṟ ṟaṭiyēṉ parakka niṉaruṭ kirakkamē aṭaintēṉ pārtti lāykolō pārttaṉai eṉilnī karappa tuṉṟaṉak kaḻakaṉṟu kaṇṭāy kāḷa kaṇṭaṉē kaṅkainā yakaṉē tirakkaṇ neṟṟiyāy oṟṟiyāyt tillait tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: If you despise me for lacking compassion, that is indeed my nature. Yet I have completely sought the compassion of your grace. Have you not seen this? If you have seen it, hiding yourself does not become you. O Lord with the dark throat, Lord of the Ganges, Lord with the steadfast eye on your forehead, Lord of Otriyur, O shining light in the Hall of Thillai.
commentary: Vallalar makes a striking admission that he lacks compassion. He teaches that compassion for all living beings (jīvakāruṇyam) is the absolute foundation of spiritual life. Unable to find this vital mercy in his own heart, he throws himself on divine grace, challenging God not to hide from someone in desperate need.

translit: yātu nāṉpiḻai ceyyiṉum poṟuppāṉ entai emmiṟai eṉṟuvan taṭaintēṉ tītu nōkkinī ceyirttiṭil aṭiyēṉ ceyva teṉṉainiṉ cittamiṅ kaṟiyēṉ pōtu pōkiṉṟa taṉṟi-eṉ māyap puṇarcci yātoṉṟum pōkiṉṟa tilaikāṇ cīta vārpoḻil oṟṟiyam paraṉē tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: Thinking that my Father and my Lord will forgive whatever wrongs I commit, I came and sought refuge in you. If you look at my faults and grow angry, what can this devotee do? I do not know your will here. Time passes, but none of my illusory attachments fade away. O Lord of Otriyur with cool flowing groves, O shining light in the Hall of Thillai.
commentary: Trusting in God as a forgiving parent is the only hope for a flawed soul. Vallalar worries about what will happen if God focuses on his mistakes instead of his potential. He watches time slip away while his destructive habits and worldly attachments remain as strong as ever.

translit: tāykkum tantaikkum nikarumniṉ irutāḷ cārnta mēlavar tamaittoḻu tēttā nāykkum nāyeṉum pāviyēṉ piḻaiyai nāṭi nallaruḷ nalkiṭā tiruntāl ēykkum mālniṟak kālaṉvan tiṭumpō teṉko lāminta eṇṇameṉ maṉattait tīykku teṉceyvēṉ oṟṟiyam civaṉē tillai ampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: I am a sinner worse than a dog. I do not worship and praise the exalted ones who have reached your two feet, which are like a mother and father. If you look at my faults and do not grant your good grace, what will happen when the deceiving, dark-hued god of death arrives? This thought burns my mind. What shall I do? O Siva of Otri! O shining light in the Thillai Ambalam!
commentary: The fear of facing death without divine protection burns the mind. Vallalar feels lower than a dog because he failed to honor the wise souls who have already reached God. He begs the divine, addressed here as Siva (the Supreme Divine) and the radiant Lamp of Thillai Ambalam (the sacred hall of consciousness), to grant grace before the dark god of death arrives. If God looks only at human faults, the soul is lost.

translit: āṭṭu kiṉṟanī aṟintilai pōlum aivar pakkamnāṉ āṭukiṉ ṟataṉaik kāṭṭu kiṉṟavāṉ kaṭaliṭai eḻunta kāḷa muṇṭa-ak karuṇaiyai ulakil nāṭṭu kiṉṟaṉai āyilik koṭiya nāykkum uṉṉaruḷ nalkiṭa vēṇṭum tīṭṭu kiṉṟanal pukaḻoṟṟi aracē tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: You who make me dance do not seem to know that I am dancing on the side of the five senses. You establish in the world that grace which consumed the dark poison rising from the vast manifesting ocean. If so, you must grant your grace even to this cruel dog. O King of Otri of well-written good fame! O shining light in Tiruchitrambalam!
commentary: Worldly life forces the soul to dance to the demands of the five senses. God's true nature is boundless compassion, which must now be directed at the struggling soul. If the divine directs the dance of life, it must step in and rescue those trapped by sensory illusions.

translit: uyya oṉṟilēṉ poyyaṉeṉ pataṉai oḷitti lēṉinta otiyaṉuk karuḷnī ceyya vēṇṭuva tiṉṟeṉil civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ tikaippatai aṉṟi maiyal neñciṉēṉ āyiṉum uṉṉai maṟanti lēṉitu vañcamum aṉṟē ceyya mēṉi-em oṟṟiyūr vāḻvē tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: I have nothing to save me. I do not hide that I am a liar. O Siva, if you do not grant your grace to this useless person today, what can I do but stand bewildered? Though I have a deluded heart, I have not forgotten you. This is no deception. O our Life in Otriyur of the red form! O shining light in Tiruchitrambalam!
commentary: Absolute honesty about personal flaws is sometimes the only offering a soul has left. Vallalar admits his heart is deluded and his life full of falsehood. Yet through this confusion, his inner memory of God remains constant and true. He stands bewildered, relying on divine grace to save a life he considers useless.

translit: vāṭu kiṉṟaṉaṉ eṉṟaṉai iṉṉum varunta vaikkiṉum maṟantiṭēṉ uṉṉaip pāṭu kiṉṟaṉaṉ pāviyēṉ eṉṉaip pātu kāppatuṉ paramatu kaṇṭāy tēṭu kiṉṟamāl nāṉmukaṉ mutalām tēvar yāvarum terivarum poruḷē cēṭu niṉṟanal oṟṟiyūr vāḻvē tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: I am withering. Even if you make me suffer further, I will not forget you. I, a sinner, sing of you. Know that protecting me is your burden. O Reality difficult to be known by seeking Vishnu, four-faced Brahma, and all the other gods! O good Life standing exalted in Otriyur! O shining light in Tiruchitrambalam!
commentary: True devotion remains steady even when the divine allows the devotee to suffer. Vallalar promises never to forget God, insisting that protecting a surrendered soul is entirely God's own burden to carry. This ultimate Reality cannot be grasped by seeking out the greatest figures of traditional religion, such as Vishnu (the preserver deity) or the four-faced Brahma (the creator god). The supreme divine light stands far above these conventional deities.

translit: ciṟiyar ceypiḻai periyavar poṟukkum cīla meṉpatuṉ tirumoḻi aṉṟē vaṟiya ṉēṉpiḻai yāvaiyum uṉatu maṉattil koḷḷutal vaḻakkala iṉinī iṟaiyum tāḻkkalai aṭiyaṉēṉ taṉṉai ēṉṟu koṇṭaruḷ īntiṭal vēṇṭum ceṟiya ōṅkiya oṟṟiyam paramē tirucciṟ ṟampalam tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: Is it not your divine word that the great bear the faults committed by the small? It is not customary for you to hold all the faults of this poor one in your mind. Now you must not delay even a little. You must accept me, your servant, and grant your grace. O Supreme of densely exalted Otri! O shining light in Tiruchitrambalam!
commentary: The defining quality of greatness is the willingness to forgive the mistakes of the small. The divine principle dictates that God should not keep a mental tally of a poor servant's errors. Because the divine nature is vast and forgiving, the soul begs to be accepted without delay. Grace is sought here not as a reward for perfection, but as the only cure for human weakness.

translit: iṉṟu niṉṟavar nāḷainiṉ ṟilarē eṉcey vōmitaṟ keṉṟuḷam pataittuc ceṉṟu niṉṟucōr kiṉṟaṉaṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ civaṉē naṉṟu niṉtuṇai nāṭaka malarttāḷ naṇṇa eṉṟunī nayantaruḷ vāyō poṉṟal iṉṟiya eḻiloṟṟi aracē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: Those who are here today are gone tomorrow. My heart trembles as I wonder what we will do about this. I go, stand, and grow weary, O Siva. What am I to do? I am lowly. Grant your grace, O Siva. When will you lovingly allow me to reach your good, comforting, dancing lotus feet? O King of beautiful Otriyur that knows no destruction. O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: The fragility of human life brings trembling anxiety. Realizing that time is running out, the only answer to this fear is to seek the safety of the divine. God stands in the "common space" (potu), meaning the divine presence is open and available to everyone.

translit: maṟumai immaiyum vaḷampeṟa vēṇṭēṉ maruvum niṉaruḷ vāḻvuṟa aṭaiyāc ciṟumai eṇṇiyē tikaikkiṉṟēṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ vaṟumai yāḷaṉēṉ vāṭṭamnī aṟiyā vaṇṇam uṇṭukol māṇikka malaiyē poṟumai yāḷaṉē oṟṟi-am paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: I do not ask to gain prosperity in this world and the next. I am bewildered as I think of my lowliness in not attaining the life of your fitting grace, O Siva. What am I to do? I am the lowest of the lowly. I am a poor man. Can my wilting remain unknown to you, O ruby mountain? O patient One! O beautiful Lord of Otriyur! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Most prayers ask for prosperity in this life or rewards in heaven, but Vallalar rejects these. He considers himself impoverished, lacking not money but divine grace. He asks how a patient God can watch him wither in this spiritual poverty without stepping in to help.

translit: uyya vallaṉēl uṉtiru aruḷām uṭaimai vēṇṭumav uṭaimaiyait tēṭal ceyya vallaṉō allakāṇ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ peyya vallaniṉ tiruvaruḷ nōkkam peṟavi ḻaintaṉaṉ piṟa-oṉṟum virumpēṉ poyyi talla-em oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: If I am to be saved, I need the wealth of your holy grace. Am I capable of seeking that wealth? Look, I am not, O Siva. What am I to do? I am the lowest of the lowly. I yearned to receive the glance of your holy grace that pours down. I desire nothing else. This is not a lie, O our beautiful Lord of Otriyur! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Spiritual effort often feels like a steep climb. Vallalar admits he lacks the strength to make it. He knows divine grace is his only salvation, but he cannot earn it through his own search. Helpless, he relies on God's compassion and asks only that grace be poured down.

translit: vellu kiṉṟaṉar viṉaippula vēṭar melikiṉ ṟēṉiṅku vīṇiṉil kālam cellu kiṉṟaṉa aiyavō civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ collu kiṉṟaṉaṉ kēṭkiṉṟāy kēṭṭum tūra niṉṟaṉai īramil lārpōl pullu kiṉṟacīr oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: The hunters of sensory karma conquer me. I languish here. Time passes in vain, alas, O Siva! What am I to do? I am the lowest of the lowly. I speak to you. You listen. Even after hearing me, you stand far away like those without compassion. O beautiful Lord of Otriyur embraced by greatness! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: The mind is dragged away by physical desires and distractions, which act like hunters capturing their prey. Losing this battle wastes precious time on earth. In despair, Vallalar's plea becomes an accusation: God is listening but standing far away, acting as if he lacks compassion for the struggle.

translit: ēṟu kiṉṟilēṉ iḻikilēṉ naṭuniṉ ṟeykkiṉ ṟēṉpavam eṉṉumak kuḻiyil tēṟu kiṉṟilēṉ cikkeṉac civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ kūṟu kiṉṟateṉ kaṭavuḷnī aṟiyāk koḷkai oṉṟilai kuṉṟavil lōṉē pūṟu vaṅkoḷum oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: I do not climb up and I do not climb down. Standing in the middle, I grow weary in this pit called worldly birth. I am not recovering firmly, O Siva. What am I to do? I am the lowest of the lowly. What is there to say? O God, there is nothing you do not know. O One who holds the mountain as a bow! O ancient, beautiful Lord of Otriyur! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Worldly existence feels like a deep pit where one is stuck in spiritual limbo. Unable to pull himself up to a higher state, yet unwilling to sink lower, Vallalar is left exhausted and paralyzed. He drops his defense: since God already knows everything, there is nothing left to explain.

translit: kanta mummala rumeṉa niṉṟāy kaṇṭu koṇṭilēṉ kāmavāḻ vataṉāl cintai nontayar kiṉṟaṉaṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ enta nalvaḻi yāluṉai aṭaivēṉ yātun tērntilēṉ pōtupō vatukāṇ punti iṉpamē oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: You stood like three fragrant flowers. I did not realize You because of my life of lust. My mind aches and I languish, O Siva. What can I do? I am the smallest of the small. By what good path will I reach You? I do not know anything, and time is passing by. O bliss of the intellect, Supreme Lord of Otri! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Worldly desires blind us to the divine presence that is already near. Vallalar laments wasting precious time on physical attachments, asking God for the right path to reach him before it is too late.

translit: allal eṉṉaiviṭ ṭakaṉṟiṭa oṟṟi aṭuttu niṟkavō aṉṟinaṟ puliyūrt tillai mēvavō aṟintilēṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ ollai iṅkuvā eṉṟaruḷ puriyā toḻiti yēluṉai uṟuvatev vaṇamō pullar mēviṭā oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: To make my sorrows leave me, should I stand near Otri, or should I reach Thillai in good Puliyur? I do not know, O Siva. What can I do? I am the smallest of the small. If You do not graciously tell me to come here quickly, how will I ever reach You? O Supreme Lord of Otri, unreached by the base! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: A spiritual seeker often wonders if one holy site is better than another, debating between sacred temple towns like Otri and Thillai. Acknowledging his own helplessness, Vallalar stops guessing and waits for a direct call from the divine.

translit: ñāla vāḻkkaiyai nampiniṉ ṟuḻalum nāyka ḷukkelām nāyara cāṉēṉ cīlam oṉṟilēṉ tikaikkiṉṟēṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ ēla niṉaruḷ ītiyēl uyvēṉ illai yēleṉak killai-uy tiṟamē pōla eṉṟurai yā-oṟṟi aracē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: I became the king of dogs among all the dogs that roam about trusting in worldly life. I have no virtue. I stand bewildered, O Siva. What can I do? I am the smallest of the small. If You bestow Your grace appropriately, I will be saved. If not, there is no way of salvation for me. O King of Otri who cannot be compared to anything! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: People absorbed in worldly survival roam without a higher purpose. Identifying with this lost state, Vallalar shows that spiritual rescue relies on God's grace, coming when a person admits they have no virtue of their own.

translit: cutta neñcaruḷ cērkkiṉum alatu cōmpal neñcaruḷ cērkkiṉum niṉatu cittam eṉṉaḷa vaṉṟatu civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ nittam niṉṉaṭi aṉṟi-oṉ ṟēttēṉ nitta ṉē-atu nī-aṟi yāyō putta runtamiḻ oṟṟiyūr aracē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: Whether You join me with those of pure hearts, or join me with those of lazy hearts, Your will is beyond my measure, O Siva. What can I do? I am the smallest of the small. Daily, I praise nothing other than Your feet. O Eternal One, do You not know that? O King of Otri where fresh Tamil flourishes! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Surrender means accepting whatever company or circumstances the divine provides. Despite feeling small and powerless, Vallalar holds onto one certainty: daily, steady devotion to God.

translit: tattu mattiṭait tayireṉa viṉaiyāl taḷarntu mūppiṉil taṇṭukoṇ ṭuḻaṉṟē cettu mīḷavum piṟappeṉil civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ tottu vēṇṭumniṉ tiruvaṭik keṉaiyē tuṭṭaṉ eṉṟiyēl tuṇaipiṟi taṟiyēṉ puttai nīkkiya oṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: Churned like curd by a plunging churning rod, weakened by karma, wandering with a walking stick in old age, what if I die and am born again, O Siva? What can I do? I am the smallest of the small. I must cling as a servant to Your holy feet. If You call me a wicked man, I know no other support. O Supreme Lord of Otri who removes ignorance! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: The cycle of aging, death, and rebirth churns the soul, like a rod beating milk into curd. Terrified of repeating this cycle, Vallalar clings to the divine as his only support, begging God not to turn him away.

translit: parinti lēṉaruṭ pāṅkuṟum poruṭṭāyp panta pācattaip paṟittiṭum vaḻiyait terinti lēṉtikaip puṇṭaṉaṉ civaṉē ceyva teṉṉaināṉ ciṟiyaruḷ ciṟiyēṉ virinta neñcamum kuvintila iṉṉum veyya māyaiyil kaiyaṟa vaṭaintē purintu cārkiṉṟa toṟṟiyam paraṉē pōṟṟum yāvarkkum potuvilniṉ ṟavaṉē.
translation: I have not strived with love to attain the state of grace. I do not know the way to uproot my worldly attachments. I am bewildered, O Siva. What am I to do? I am the lowest among the lowly. My wandering mind has still not found its focus. Feeling helpless in this cruel illusion, it willfully clings to it. O Supreme Lord of Otriyur! O You who stand in the common space for all who praise you.
commentary: Vallalar is trapped in a cruel illusion (māyai) and admits he has no idea how to break free. His mind wanders, clinging to the very worldly attachments that cause his confusion. Feeling helpless, he cries out to Siva, taking comfort in knowing God is accessible to anyone who offers praise.

tamil: அன்னையில் பெரிதும் இனியஎன் அரசே அம்பலத் தாடல்செய் அமுதே
பொன்னைஒத் தொளிரும் புரிசடைக் கனியே போதமே ஒற்றிஎம் பொருளே
உன்னைவிட் டயலார் உறவுகொண் டடையேன் உண்மைஎன் உள்ளம்நீ அறிவாய்
என்னைவிட் டிடில்நான் என்செய்வேன் ஒதிபோல் இருக்கின்ற இவ்வெளி யேனே.
translit: aṉṉaiyil peritum iṉiya-eṉ aracē ampalat tāṭalcey amutē poṉṉai-ot toḷirum puricaṭaik kaṉiyē pōtamē oṟṟi-em poruḷē uṉṉaiviṭ ṭayalār uṟavukoṇ ṭaṭaiyēṉ uṇmai-eṉ uḷḷamnī aṟivāy eṉṉaiviṭ ṭiṭilnāṉ eṉceyvēṉ otipōl irukkiṉṟa ivveḷi yēṉē.
translation: My King, far sweeter than a mother! Nectar who dances in the Hall! Fruit with twisted, golden shining matted hair! Pure consciousness! Our treasure of Otri! I will not leave you to seek the company of strangers. You know the truth of my heart. If you leave me, what will I do, a poor wretch as frail as an oti tree?
commentary: God's love is often compared to a mother's, but here it is called far sweeter. Vallalar promises absolute loyalty, refusing to seek help from worldly attachments or other deities, laying bare his vulnerability without divine support.

tamil: எளியனேன் மையல் மனத்தினால் உழன்றேன் என்செய்வேன் என்செய்வேன்பொல்லாக்
களியனேன் வாட்டம் கண்டனை இன்னும் கருணைசெய் திலைஅருட் கரும்பே
அளியனே திருச்சிற் றம்பலத் தொளியே அருமருந் தேவட வனத்துத்
தனியனே ஒற்றித் தலத்தமர் மணியே தயையிலி போல்இருந் தனையே.
translit: eḷiyaṉēṉ maiyal maṉattiṉāl uḻaṉṟēṉ eṉceyvēṉ eṉceyvēṉpollāk kaḷiyaṉēṉ vāṭṭam kaṇṭaṉai iṉṉum karuṇaicey tilai-aruṭ karumpē aḷiyaṉē tirucciṟ ṟampalat toḷiyē arumarun tēvaṭa vaṉattut taṉiyaṉē oṟṟit talattamar maṇiyē tayaiyili pōlirun taṉaiyē.
translation: I, a poor man, suffered with a deluded mind. What will I do? What will I do? You saw the withering of this wicked, intoxicated fool, yet you have not shown mercy, O sugarcane of grace! Compassionate one! Light of Thiruchitrambalam! Rare medicine! Solitary one of the banyan forest! Gem seated in the shrine of Otri! You remain like someone without mercy.
commentary: A painful contrast exists between God's nature of total grace and Vallalar's experience of being ignored. Admitting his flaws and confusion, he wonders why the divine medicine of Otri has not yet cured his suffering.

tamil: இருந்தனை எனது நெஞ்சினுள் எந்தாய் என்துயர் அறிந்திலை போலும்
முருந்தனை முறுவல் மங்கையர் மலைநேர் முலைத்தலை உருண்டன னேனும்
மருந்தனை யாய்உன் திருவடி மலரை மறந்திலேன் வழுத்துகின் றனன்காண்
வருந்தனை யேல்என் றுரைத்திலை ஐயா வஞ்சகம் உனக்கும்உண் டேயோ.
translit: iruntaṉai eṉatu neñciṉuḷ entāy eṉtuyar aṟintilai pōlum muruntaṉai muṟuval maṅkaiyar malainēr mulaittalai uruṇṭaṉa ṉēṉum maruntaṉai yāyuṉ tiruvaṭi malarai maṟantilēṉ vaḻuttukiṉ ṟaṉaṉkāṇ varuntaṉai yēleṉ ṟuraittilai aiyā vañcakam uṉakkumuṇ ṭēyō.
translation: You have been in my heart, my Father. It seems you have not known my sorrow. Even when I rolled on the mountain-like breasts of women with bright smiles, I did not forget the lotus of your sacred feet, O Medicine. See, I always praise them. You have not told me to stop suffering, O Lord. Is there deceit in you too?
commentary: Vallalar insists that even during times of intense worldly distraction and physical desire, he never forgot the divine. Since God lives right inside his heart, he asks how God could be unaware of his pain, playfully wondering if the divine is capable of deceit.

tamil: உண்டநஞ் சின்னும் கண்டம்விட் டகலா துறைந்தது நாடொறும் அடியேன்
கண்டனன் கருணைக் கடல்எனும் குறிப்பைக் கண்டுகண் டுளமது நெகவே
விண்டனன் என்னைக் கைவிடில் சிவனே விடத்தினும் கொடியன்நான் அன்றோ
அண்டர்கட் கரசே அம்பலத் தமுதே அலைகின்றேன் அறிந்திருந் தனையே.
translit: uṇṭanañ ciṉṉum kaṇṭamviṭ ṭakalā tuṟaintatu nāṭoṟum aṭiyēṉ kaṇṭaṉaṉ karuṇaik kaṭaleṉum kuṟippaik kaṇṭukaṇ ṭuḷamatu nekavē viṇṭaṉaṉ eṉṉaik kaiviṭil civaṉē viṭattiṉum koṭiyaṉnāṉ aṉṟō aṇṭarkaṭ karacē ampalat tamutē alaikiṉṟēṉ aṟintirun taṉaiyē.
translation: The poison you swallowed still remains in your throat without leaving. I, your servant, saw this every day. Seeing this clear sign of the ocean of mercy again and again, my heart melted and I spoke your praise. If you abandon me, O Siva, am I not more cruel than that poison? King of the celestials! Nectar of the Hall! You have known well that I am wandering in distress.
commentary: According to ancient tradition, Siva swallowed a deadly poison to save the universe, holding it forever in his throat as a visible mark of endless mercy. Vallalar reasons that if a God so merciful abandons him, his own flaws must be deadlier than that cosmic poison.

tamil: தனையர்செய் பிழையைத் தந்தையர் குறித்துத் தள்ளுதல் வழக்கல என்பார்
வினையனேன் பிழையை வினையிலி நீதான் விவகரித் தெண்ணுதல் அழகோ
உனையலா திறந்தும் பிறந்தும்இவ் வுலகில் உழன்றிடுந் தேவரை மதியேன்
எனையலா துனக்கிங் காளிலை யோஉண்டென்னினும் ஏன்றுகொண் டருளே.
translit: taṉaiyarcey piḻaiyait tantaiyar kuṟittut taḷḷutal vaḻakkala eṉpār viṉaiyaṉēṉ piḻaiyai viṉaiyili nītāṉ vivakarit teṇṇutal aḻakō uṉaiyalā tiṟantum piṟantumiv vulakil uḻaṉṟiṭun tēvarai matiyēṉ eṉaiyalā tuṉakkiṅ kāḷilai yō-uṇṭeṉṉiṉum ēṉṟukoṇ ṭaruḷē.
translation: People say it is not the custom for fathers to count their children's mistakes and cast them away. Is it proper for you, who are free from karma, to cross-examine and tally the faults of this karma-bound wretch? I do not revere any gods other than you, for they only wander in this world, dying and being born. Do you have no other servant here but me? Even if you do, please accept me and grant your grace.
commentary: A loving father does not keep a strict tally of his child's mistakes. Vallalar asks why the Supreme, free from karma (the binding cycle of action and consequence), should act like an accountant tallying the flaws of a struggling human. He rejects all lesser gods because they are trapped in the same cycle of birth and death.

tamil: ஏன்றுகொண் டருள வேண்டும்இவ் எளியேன் இருக்கினும் இறக்கினும் பொதுவுள்
ஊன்றுகொண் டருளும் நின்னடி யல்லால் உரைக்கும்மால் அயன்முதல் தேவர்
நான்றுகொண் டிடுவ ரேனும்மற் றவர்மேல் நாஎழா துண்மையீ திதற்குச்
சான்றுகொண் டருள நினைத்தியேல் என்னுள் சார்ந்தநின் சரண்இரண் டன்றே.
translit: ēṉṟukoṇ ṭaruḷa vēṇṭumiv eḷiyēṉ irukkiṉum iṟakkiṉum potuvuḷ ūṉṟukoṇ ṭaruḷum niṉṉaṭi yallāl uraikkummāl ayaṉmutal tēvar nāṉṟukoṇ ṭiṭuva rēṉummaṟ ṟavarmēl nā-eḻā tuṇmaiyī titaṟkuc cāṉṟukoṇ ṭaruḷa niṉaittiyēl eṉṉuḷ cārntaniṉ caraṇiraṇ ṭaṉṟē.
translation: You must accept and bestow your grace upon this poor one. Whether I live or die, except for your feet rooted firmly in the public hall, even if the celebrated Vishnu, Brahma, and other gods hang themselves in penance, my tongue will not rise to praise them. This is the truth. If you wish to seek proof for this, your two feet resting within me stand as the witness.
commentary: The soul's devotion belongs to the universal Divine, bypassing all traditional deities. Vallalar says he will not praise gods like Vishnu or Brahma, even if they performed extreme penance. His only refuge is the Divine whose presence fills the universal public hall of grace, and his own heart stands as the witness.

tamil: சரணவா ரிசம்என் தலைமிசை இன்னும் தரித்திலை தாழ்த்தனை அடியேன்
கரணவா தனையும் கந்தவா தனையும் கலங்கிடக் கபமிழுத் துந்தும்
மரணவா தனைக்கென் செய்குவம் என்றே வருந்துகின் றனன்மனம் மாழாந்
தரணமூன் றெரிய நகைத்தஎம் இறையே அடியனை ஆள்வதுன் கடனே.
translit: caraṇavā ricameṉ talaimicai iṉṉum tarittilai tāḻttaṉai aṭiyēṉ karaṇavā taṉaiyum kantavā taṉaiyum kalaṅkiṭak kapamiḻut tuntum maraṇavā taṉaikkeṉ ceykuvam eṉṟē varuntukiṉ ṟaṉaṉmaṉam māḻān taraṇamūṉ ṟeriya nakaitta-em iṟaiyē aṭiyaṉai āḷvatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: You have not yet placed your lotus feet on my head. You have delayed. What will I do during the agony of death, when the inner faculties and senses fail and choking phlegm pushes up? Thinking this, I suffer with a confused mind. O my Lord who laughed and burned the three fortresses, it is your duty to rule this devotee.
commentary: The physical agony of death brings a human fear of failing senses and a struggling body. Vallalar pleads for grace to be given before that final moment arrives, asking the Divine to step in and protect the devotee as a matter of sacred duty.

tamil: கடம்பொழி ஓங்கல் உரிஉடை உடுக்கும் கடவுளே கடவுளர் கோவே
மடம்பொழி மனத்தேன் மலஞ்செறிந் தூறும் வாயில்ஓர் ஒன்பதில் வரும்இவ்
நடம்பொழி பதத்தாய் நடுங்குகின் றனன்காண் நான்செயும் வகைஎது நவிலே.
translit: kaṭampoḻi ōṅkal uri-uṭai uṭukkum kaṭavuḷē kaṭavuḷar kōvē maṭampoḻi maṉattēṉ malañceṟin tūṟum vāyilōr oṉpatil varumiv uṭampoḻin tiṭumēl mīṇṭumīṇ ṭenta-uṭampukoṇ ṭuḻalvaṉō-eṉṟu naṭampoḻi patattāy naṭuṅkukiṉ ṟaṉaṉkāṇ nāṉceyum vakai-etu navilē.
translation: O God who wears the skin of the rut-showering elephant as a garment! O King of gods! My mind pours out ignorance. If this body with nine orifices oozing accumulated filth perishes, what bodies will I take again and again to wander? Thinking this, I tremble. O Lord whose feet shower the dance, tell me what I must do.
commentary: The dread of death is matched by the fear of being born again into flawed bodies. Looking honestly at the physical body's impurities, Vallalar worries about wandering endlessly through future births in ignorance. He addresses the Divine using the traditional imagery of Lord Siva, asking plainly for a way to break free.

tamil: வகைஎது தெரிந்தேன் ஏழையேன் உய்வான் வள்ளலே வலிந்தெனை ஆளும்
தகைஅது இன்றேல் என்செய்வேன் உலகர் சழக்குடைத் தமியன்நீ நின்ற
திகைஎது என்றால் சொலஅறி யாது திகைத்திடும் சிறியனேன் தன்னைப்
பகைஅது கருதா தாள்வதுன் பரங்காண் பவளமா நிறத்தகற் பகமே.
translit: vakai-etu terintēṉ ēḻaiyēṉ uyvāṉ vaḷḷalē valinteṉai āḷum takai-atu iṉṟēl eṉceyvēṉ ulakar caḻakkuṭait tamiyaṉnī niṉṟa tikai-etu eṉṟāl cola-aṟi yātu tikaittiṭum ciṟiyaṉēṉ taṉṉaip pakai-atu karutā tāḷvatuṉ paraṅkāṇ pavaḷamā niṟattakaṟ pakamē.
translation: What way do I know to be saved, poor as I am? O benevolent Lord, if you lack the nature to forcefully take and rule me, what will I do? I am a solitary one carrying the faults of worldly people. If asked which direction you stand in, I am a lowly one who stands bewildered, not knowing what to say. Taking charge of me without seeing me as an enemy is your burden, O wish-fulfilling tree of great coral hue.
commentary: True surrender means admitting helplessness. Feeling lost and carrying the ordinary faults of worldly life, Vallalar does not even know which direction to look for the Divine. He pleads for God to take charge forcefully out of sheer mercy, acting as a wish-fulfilling tree that shelters the one who has nowhere else to go.

tamil: கற்பன அறிந்து கற்கிலேன் சழக்குக் கல்விகற் றுழன்றனன் கருணை
சொற்பன மதிலும் காண்கிலேன் பொல்லாச் சூகரம் எனமலம் துய்த்தேன்
விற்பனன் எனவே நிற்பது விழைந்தேன் வீணனேன் விரகிலா வெறியேன்
அற்பனேன் தன்னை ஆண்டநின் அருளை ஆய்ந்திடில் அன்னையின் பெரிதே.
translit: kaṟpaṉa aṟintu kaṟkilēṉ caḻakkuk kalvikaṟ ṟuḻaṉṟaṉaṉ karuṇai coṟpaṉa matilum kāṇkilēṉ pollāc cūkaram eṉamalam tuyttēṉ viṟpaṉaṉ eṉavē niṟpatu viḻaintēṉ vīṇaṉēṉ virakilā veṟiyēṉ aṟpaṉēṉ taṉṉai āṇṭaniṉ aruḷai āyntiṭil aṉṉaiyiṉ peritē.
translation: I did not understand and learn what must be learned. I wandered learning flawed knowledge. I do not see grace even in my dreams. Like a wicked pig, I consumed filth. I desired to stand tall as a scholar. I am a useless one. I am a madman devoid of wisdom. When I examine your grace that claimed such a petty one, it is far greater than a mother's love.
commentary: God's grace pours out even when Vallalar feels unworthy. Looking back, he confesses to chasing worldly learning and the pride of being a scholar while missing the truth. Yet despite this foolishness and impurity, he finds that the Divine has claimed him anyway, showing a love far greater than a mother's.

translit: paṟṟu nōkkiya pāviyēṉ taṉakkup parintu nī-aruṭ patamaḷit tilaiyē maṟṟu nōkkiya valviṉai ataṉāl vañca māyaiyiṉ vāḻkkaiyiṉ maṉattiṉ aṟṟu nōkkiya nōykaḷiṉ mūppiṉ alaitan tivvula kampaṭum pāṭṭai uṟṟu nōkkiṉāl urukuteṉ uḷḷam oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur. You have not pitied me and granted your state of grace to this sinner driven by attachments. My heart melts when I look closely at the suffering this world undergoes as it wanders through a life of deceitful illusion, mental afflictions, disease, and old age caused by cruel karma.
commentary: The pain of living beings breaks Vallalar's heart. He sees people trapped in disease, old age, and the reactions of their past deeds (karma). Even as he confesses his own flaws, his primary grief is for the misery of the world.

translit: koṭiya neñciṉēṉ kōpamē aṭaintēṉ kōṭi kōṭiyām kuṇappaḻu tuṭaiyēṉ kaṭiya vañcakak kaḷvaṉēṉ taṉakkuṉ karuṇai īntiṭā tiruntiṭil kaṭaiyēṉ aṭiyaṉ ākuva tevvaṇam eṉṟē aiya aiyanāṉ alaṟiṭu kiṉṟēṉ oṭiya mummalam oruṅkaṟut tavarcēr oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur, a place reached by those who have entirely severed the three impurities. I have a cruel heart. I am consumed by anger and possess millions of flaws. I am a harsh, deceitful thief. If you do not grant me your compassion, how will a lowly person like me ever become your devotee? Thinking of this, O Lord, O Lord, I cry aloud in anguish.
commentary: Only divine compassion can save a flawed person. Vallalar lists his faults, calling himself a cruel, angry thief. He contrasts himself with the perfected saints who have destroyed the three impurities (mum-malam, the stains of ego, delusion, and past actions). Without God's pity, he has no hope of joining them.

translit: kāmam eṉpatōr urukkoṭiv vulakil kalaṅku kiṉṟa-ik kaṭaiyaṉēṉ taṉakkuc cēmam eṉpatām niṉaruḷ kiṭaiyāc ciṟumai yē-iṉṉum ceṟintiṭu māṉāl ēma neñciṉar eṉṟaṉai nōkki ēṭa nīkaṭai eṉṟiṭil avarmuṉ ūmaṉ ākuva taṉṟi-eṉ ceyvēṉ oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur. I am the lowest of men, suffering in this world as the very embodiment of lust. If the baseness of failing to receive your protective grace continues to persist in me, and if people with steadfast hearts look at me and call me a lowly wretch, what can I do but stand mute before them?
commentary: A life driven by worldly desire leaves a person spiritually ashamed. Vallalar feels he is the very image of lust, lacking the protective grace of the divine. If those with pure and steady hearts confront him about his baseness, he would have no defense.

translit: maṇṇil niṉṟavar vāḻvatum kaṇattil varunti māyvatum maṟṟivai ellām kaṇṇiṉ nērnitaṅ kaṇṭumiv vāḻvil kātal nīṅkilāk kalmaṉak koṭiyēṉ eṇṇi niṉṟa-ōr eṇṇamum muṭiyā teṉcey kēṉvarum iruviṉaik kayiṟṟāl uṇṇi rampaniṉ ṟāṭṭukiṉ ṟaṉainī oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur. I see people living on this earth and then dying in sorrow in an instant. Though I witness this directly every day, my desire for this worldly life never fades. I am a cruel person with a heart of stone. Not a single intention of mine is fulfilled. What can I do? You make me dance endlessly, pulled by the ropes of my two karmas.
commentary: We watch people die every day, yet still cling to worldly life. Vallalar calls his heart a stone because it remains bound to desires despite seeing death so clearly. He feels helpless, pulled like a puppet by the ropes of his good and bad past actions, unable to break free on his own.

translit: veruṭci yētarum mala-irā iṉṉum viṭiyak kaṇṭilēṉ viṉaiyiṉēṉ uḷḷam maruṭci mēviya teṉceykēṉ uṉpāl varuva taṟkoru vaḻiyumiṅ kaṟiyēṉ teruṭci yētarum niṉaruḷ oḷitāṉ cēril uykuvēṉ cērntila tāṉāl uruṭci āḻi-ot tuḻalvatu meykāṇ oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur. I have not yet seen the dawn break upon this terrifying night of impurity. My karmic heart is engulfed in delusion. What can I do? I know of no path to reach you. I will be saved only if the light of your grace, which brings true clarity, reaches me. If it does not reach me, I will surely spin endlessly like a rolling wheel.
commentary: The light of divine grace is the only way out of spiritual darkness. Vallalar compares his ignorance to a terrifying, unending night of delusion. Without the clarity brought by God's light, the soul will spin like a rolling wheel.

translit: yātum uṉceya lāmeṉa aṟintum aiya vaiyamēl avarivar oḻiyāt tītu ceytaṉar naṉmaicey taṉarnām terintu ceyvatē tiṟameṉa niṉaittuk kōtu ceymalak kōṭṭaiyaik kāval koṇṭu vāḻkiṟēṉ kaṇṭiṭa iṉinī ōtu ceyvatoṉ ṟeṉṉuyirt tuṇaiyē oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: Even knowing that everything is your doing, O Lord, I looked at people on this earth endlessly committing evil or good and believed that true skill lies in acting consciously. Holding this thought, I live guarding this flawed fortress of impurities. My soul's companion, tell me what you will do now. O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur!
commentary: The illusion of personal control is a common trap. Even when we know the divine is the doer, we still judge others for their deeds and rely on our own cleverness. Vallalar says this false sense of agency keeps us locked inside a flawed physical body, guarding our impurities instead of trusting God. He asks his divine companion to break this cycle and reveal what comes next.

translit: panta maṭṭiṉām pāvineñ cakattāl pavappe ruṅkaṭal paṭintuḻaṉ ṟayarntēṉ inta maṭṭilnāṉ uḻaṉṟatē amaiyum ēṟa vēṇṭumuṉ eṇṇamē taṟiyēṉ anta maṭṭiṉil iruttiyō aṉṟi aṭimai vēṇṭiniṉ aruṭperum puṇaiyai unta maṭṭiṉāl tarutiyō uraiyāy oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: Through my binding, sinful heart, I plunged into the vast ocean of birth, wandered, and grew weary. My wandering up to this point is enough. I must climb ashore. I do not know your intention. Will you leave me in that weary state? Or, claiming me as your servant, will you give me the great raft of your grace to steer across? Tell me. O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur!
commentary: The cycle of birth and death is an exhausting ocean. After wandering through countless lifetimes, the soul wants to reach the shore. Vallalar asks whether God will leave him in this weary state or offer the raft of divine grace. Only grace has the power to carry a person out of suffering and bring them safely across.

translit: ñāṉa meṉpatiṉ uṟuporuḷ aṟiyēṉ ñāṉi allaṉnāṉ āyiṉum kaṭaiyēṉ āṉa pōtilum eṉakkuniṉ aruḷōr aṇuvil pātiyē āyiṉum aṭaintāl vāṉa mēviya amararum ayaṉum mālum eṉmuṉam valiyilar aṉṟē ūṉam nīkkinal aruḷtarum poruḷē oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: I do not know the true meaning of wisdom. I am no sage. I am the lowest of the low. Even so, if I attain just half an atom of your grace, the heavenly celestials, Brahma, and Vishnu will stand powerless before me. O Reality who removes flaws and grants good grace! O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur!
commentary: Divine grace is more powerful than any heavenly god. Vallalar admits he lacks wisdom and feels unworthy, placing himself at the bottom. Yet he declares that even half an atom of God's grace makes a person stronger than deities like Brahma and Vishnu. Spiritual power comes from grace, never from personal merit or status.

translit: aḷiya neñcamōr aṟivuru vākum aṉpar tampuṭai aṇukiya aruḷpōl eḷiya neñciṉēṟ keytiṭā tēṉum eḷḷil pātimaṭ ṭīntaruḷ vāyēl kaḷiya māmayal kāṭaṟa eṟintāṅ kāra vēriṉaik kaḷaintumeyp pōta oḷiya vittiṉāl pōkamum viḷaippēṉ oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: True grace draws near to devotees whose tender hearts have become the very form of knowledge. Even if such grace does not reach my poor heart, if you grant me just half a sesame seed of it, I will chop down the forest of intoxicating delusion. I will pull up its deep roots and cultivate the supreme experience using the luminous seed of true wisdom. O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur!
commentary: A tiny fragment of grace is enough to destroy a lifetime of confusion. While complete grace naturally fills the tender hearts of devoted souls, Vallalar asks for just half a sesame seed of it for his own poor heart. With that amount, he promises to chop down the forest of delusion and tear out its roots. He can then plant the luminous seed of wisdom and harvest the spiritual experience.

translit: nāka nāṭṭatiṉ nalampeṟa vēṇṭēṉ narakil ēkeṉa naviliṉum amaivēṉ ākam nāṭṭiṭai viṭukeṉil viṭuvēṉ allal āmpavam aṭai-eṉil aṭaivēṉ tākam nāṭṭiya mayalaṟa aruḷnīr tarutal ileṉac cāṟṟiṭil tariyēṉ ōkai nāṭṭiya yōkiyar paravum oṟṟi mēviya ulakuṭai yōṉē.
translation: I do not desire the pleasures of the heavenly world. Even if you command me to go to hell, I will accept it. If you tell me to drop this body on earth, I will drop it. If you tell me to take on another sorrowful birth, I will take it. But if you declare that you will not give me the water of grace to destroy this thirsty delusion, I cannot endure it. O Lord praised by joy-filled yogis! O Lord of the world residing in Otriyur!
commentary: Devotion means accepting any condition God imposes, except separation from grace. Vallalar is ready to endure hell, the loss of his physical body, or another sorrowful birth without complaint. The one thing he cannot survive is being denied the water of divine grace. Worldly suffering and heavenly pleasures mean nothing to him, provided his spiritual thirst is quenched.

tamil: வஞ்சக வினைக்கோர் கொள்கலம் அனைய மனத்தினேன் அனைத்தினும் கொடியேன்
தஞ்சம்என் றடைந்தே நின்திருக் கோயில் சந்நிதி முன்னர்நிற் கின்றேன்
எஞ்சலில் அடங்காப் பாவிஎன் றெனைநீ இகழ்ந்திடில் என்செய்வேன் சிவனே
கஞ்சன்மால் புகழும் ஒற்றியங் கரும்பே கதிதரும் கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: vañcaka viṉaikkōr koḷkalam aṉaiya maṉattiṉēṉ aṉaittiṉum koṭiyēṉ tañcameṉ ṟaṭaintē niṉtiruk kōyil canniti muṉṉarniṟ kiṉṟēṉ eñcalil aṭaṅkāp pāvi-eṉ ṟeṉainī ikaḻntiṭil eṉceyvēṉ civaṉē kañcaṉmāl pukaḻum oṟṟiyaṅ karumpē katitarum karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: I have a mind like a receptacle for deceitful karma and am the cruelest of all. Seeking refuge, I have reached you and stand before the sanctum of your holy temple. If you reject me, calling me a boundless sinner, what will I do, O Siva? O sweet sugarcane of Otriyur praised by Brahma and Vishnu! O ocean of grace who grants liberation.
commentary: Vallalar feels burdened by karma. He asks what hope is left if God turns him away as a boundless sinner. Despite his unworthiness, he trusts the divine ocean of grace to grant freedom.

tamil: நிற்பது போன்று நிலைபடா உடலை நேசம்வைத் தோம்புறும் பொருட்டாய்ப்
பொற்பது தவிரும் புலையர்தம் மனைவாய்ப் புந்திநொந் தயர்ந்தழு திளைத்தேன்
சொற்பதங் கடந்த நின்திரு வடிக்குத் தொண்டுசெய் நாளும்ஒன் றுளதோ
கற்பது கற்றோர் புகழ்திரு வொற்றிக் காவல்கொள் கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: niṟpatu pōṉṟu nilaipaṭā uṭalai nēcamvait tōmpuṟum poruṭṭāyp poṟpatu tavirum pulaiyartam maṉaivāyp puntinon tayarntaḻu tiḷaittēṉ coṟpataṅ kaṭanta niṉtiru vaṭikkut toṇṭucey nāḷumoṉ ṟuḷatō kaṟpatu kaṟṟōr pukaḻtiru voṟṟik kāvalkoḷ karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: To lovingly protect this body which appears permanent but does not last, I waited at the doors of base people devoid of virtue, my mind hurting, exhausted, weeping, and weary. Is there a day when I will serve your holy feet that surpass the reach of words? O guardian of holy Otriyur praised by those who have learned what should be learned! O ocean of grace!
commentary: People mistake the physical body for something permanent and suffer to protect it. Vallalar laments wasting his life begging from cruel, worldly people merely to survive, longing instead to serve the divine directly.

tamil: முன்னைவல் வினையால் வஞ்சக மடவார் முழுப்புலைக் குழிவிழுந் திளைத்தேன்
என்னையோ கொடியேன் நின்திரு வருள்தான் எய்தில னேல்உயிர்க் குறுதிப்
பின்னைஎவ் வணந்தான் எய்துவ தறியேன் பேதையில் பேதைநான் அன்றோ
கன்னலே தேனே ஒற்றிஎம் அமுதே கடவுளே கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: muṉṉaival viṉaiyāl vañcaka maṭavār muḻuppulaik kuḻiviḻun tiḷaittēṉ eṉṉaiyō koṭiyēṉ niṉtiru varuḷtāṉ eytila ṉēluyirk kuṟutip piṉṉai-ev vaṇantāṉ eytuva taṟiyēṉ pētaiyil pētaināṉ aṉṟō kaṉṉalē tēṉē oṟṟi-em amutē kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: Because of cruel past karma, I fell into the utterly base pit of deceitful women and grew weary. Alas, if I, a cruel one, do not attain your holy grace as a firm anchor for my soul, I do not know how else I will ever attain it. Am I not the most ignorant of the ignorant? O sugarcane! O honey! Our nectar of Otriyur! O God! O ocean of grace!
commentary: Worldly desires pull the mind away from spiritual focus, leaving the soul exhausted. Vallalar confesses his ignorance in chasing physical distractions. Without divine grace acting as a firm anchor, his soul has no path forward.

tamil: மண்ணினுள் மயங்கி வஞ்சக வினையால் மனந்தளர்ந் தழுங்கிநாள் தோறும்
எண்ணினுள் அடங்காத் துயரொடும் புலையர் இல்லிடை மல்லிடு கின்றேன்
விண்ணினுள் இலங்கும் சுடர்நிகர் உனது மெல்அடிக் கடிமைசெய் வேனோ
கண்ணினுள் மணியே ஒற்றியங் கனியே கடவுளே கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: maṇṇiṉuḷ mayaṅki vañcaka viṉaiyāl maṉantaḷarn taḻuṅkināḷ tōṟum eṇṇiṉuḷ aṭaṅkāt tuyaroṭum pulaiyar illiṭai malliṭu kiṉṟēṉ viṇṇiṉuḷ ilaṅkum cuṭarnikar uṉatu melaṭik kaṭimaicey vēṉō kaṇṇiṉuḷ maṇiyē oṟṟiyaṅ kaṉiyē kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: Deluded in this world, my mind weakening and despairing every day because of deceitful karma, I struggle in the homes of base people with sorrow that defies measure. Will I ever serve your soft feet that resemble the radiant light shining in the sky? O pupil of my eye! O sweet fruit of Otriyur! O God! O ocean of grace!
commentary: Relying on worldly people for support brings endless sorrow. Vallalar contrasts the dark struggle of earthly survival with the radiant light of the divine, asking if his exhausted mind will ever find rest in that brightness.

tamil: அளவிலா உலகத் தனந்தகோ டிகளாம் ஆருயிர்த் தொகைக்குளும் எனைப்போல்
இளகிலா வஞ்ச நெஞ்சகப் பாவி ஏழைகள் உண்டுகொல் இலைகாண்
தளர்விலா துனது திருவடி எனும்பொற் றாமரைக் கணியனா குவனோ
களவிலார்க் கினிய ஒற்றிஎம் மருந்தே கனந்தரும் கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: aḷavilā ulakat taṉantakō ṭikaḷām āruyirt tokaikkuḷum eṉaippōl iḷakilā vañca neñcakap pāvi ēḻaikaḷ uṇṭukol ilaikāṇ taḷarvilā tuṉatu tiruvaṭi eṉumpoṟ ṟāmaraik kaṇiyaṉā kuvaṉō kaḷavilārk kiṉiya oṟṟi-em maruntē kaṉantarum karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: Among the countless millions of precious souls in this boundless world, are there any poor sinners with an unyielding deceitful heart like mine? There are none. Will I draw near to the golden lotuses of your holy feet without faltering? O our medicine of Otriyur, sweet to those free of deceit! O ocean of grace who grants greatness!
commentary: True devotion brings an awareness of one's own flaws. Vallalar looks at millions of souls and feels his heart is the hardest and most deceitful. Despite this heavy self-reproach, he begs to be cured by the divine grace he calls his medicine.

tamil: ஞானம்என் பதிலோர் அணுத்துணை யேனும் நண்ணிலேன் புண்ணியம் அறியேன்
ஈனம்என் பதனுக் கிறைஎனல் ஆனேன் எவ்வணம் உய்குவ தறியேன்
வானநா டவரும் பெறற்கரு நினது மலரடித் தொழும்புசெய் வேனோ
கானவேட் டுருவாம் ஒருவனே ஒற்றிக் கடவுளே கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: ñāṉameṉ patilōr aṇuttuṇai yēṉum naṇṇilēṉ puṇṇiyam aṟiyēṉ īṉameṉ pataṉuk kiṟai-eṉal āṉēṉ evvaṇam uykuva taṟiyēṉ vāṉanā ṭavarum peṟaṟkaru niṉatu malaraṭit toḻumpucey vēṉō kāṉavēṭ ṭuruvām oruvaṉē oṟṟik kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: I have not attained even an atom of wisdom. I know nothing of merit. I have become the very lord of baseness. I do not know how I will be saved. Will I ever perform service to your flower-like feet, which are difficult even for the heavenly beings to attain? O peerless one who took the form of a forest hunter. O God of Otriyur, O ocean of grace.
commentary: Confessing a total lack of wisdom and merit, Vallalar wonders if he will ever be worthy to serve the divine, a state even heavenly beings struggle to reach. He addresses God as the forest hunter, recalling the classic story where Siva takes a tribal form to test and bless his devotee.

tamil: ஞாலவாழ் வனைத்தும் கானல்நீர் எனவே நன்கறிந் துன்திரு அருளாம்
சீலவாழ் வடையும் செல்வம்இப் பொல்லாச் சிறியனும் பெறுகுவ தேயோ
நீலமா மிடற்றுப் பவளமா மலையே நின்மல ஆனந்த நிலையே
காலன்நாண் அவிழ்க்கும் காலனே ஒற்றிக் கடவுளே கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: ñālavāḻ vaṉaittum kāṉalnīr eṉavē naṉkaṟin tuṉtiru aruḷām cīlavāḻ vaṭaiyum celvamip pollāc ciṟiyaṉum peṟukuva tēyō nīlamā miṭaṟṟup pavaḷamā malaiyē niṉmala āṉanta nilaiyē kālaṉnāṇ aviḻkkum kālaṉē oṟṟik kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: Knowing well that all worldly life is a mirage, will this wicked and lowly one ever attain the wealth of a virtuous life guided by your holy grace? O great coral mountain with a blue throat. O state of pure bliss. O death to the god of death, unfastening his noose. O God of Otriyur, O ocean of grace.
commentary: Worldly life is an illusion, fading like a mirage. Vallalar asks if a lowly person can still attain the wealth of a life guided by divine grace. He addresses God as the blue-throated mountain who swallowed poison to save the world, and as the conqueror who unfastens the noose of the god of death.

tamil: மாலொடு நான்கு வதனனும் காணா மலரடிக் கடிமைசெய் தினிப்பாம்
பாலொடு கலந்த தேன்என உன்சீர் பாடும்நாள் எந்தநாள் அறியேன்
வேலொடு மயிலும் கொண்டிடுஞ் சுடரை விளைவித்த வித்தக விளக்கே
காலொடு பூதம் ஐந்துமாம் ஒற்றிக் கடவுளே கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: māloṭu nāṉku vataṉaṉum kāṇā malaraṭik kaṭimaicey tiṉippām pāloṭu kalanta tēṉeṉa uṉcīr pāṭumnāḷ entanāḷ aṟiyēṉ vēloṭu mayilum koṇṭiṭuñ cuṭarai viḷaivitta vittaka viḷakkē kāloṭu pūtam aintumām oṟṟik kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: I do not know the day when I will serve your flower-like feet, unseen by Vishnu and the four-faced Brahma, and sing your glory like sweet milk mixed with honey. O wise lamp who brought forth the radiant one wielding the spear and the peacock. O God of Otriyur who is the wind and all five elements, O ocean of grace.
commentary: The divine reality stands beyond the reach of traditional gods, unseen by Brahma and Vishnu. Vallalar longs to serve this truth and sing its glory. God is recognized here as the source of all physical elements and the creator of Murugan, the deity of the spear and peacock.

tamil: சற்றும்நற் குணந்தான் சார்ந்திடாக் கொடியார் தந்தலை வாயிலுள் குரைக்கும்
வெற்றுநாய் தனக்கும் வேறுநா யாக மெலிகின்றேன் ஐம்புலச் சேட்டை
அற்றுநின் றவர்க்கும் அரியநின் திருத்தாட் கடிமைசெய் தொழுகுவ னேயோ
கற்றுமுற் றுணர்ந்தோர்க் கருள்தரும் ஒற்றிக் கடவுளே கருணையங்கடலே.
translit: caṟṟumnaṟ kuṇantāṉ cārntiṭāk koṭiyār tantalai vāyiluḷ kuraikkum veṟṟunāy taṉakkum vēṟunā yāka melikiṉṟēṉ aimpulac cēṭṭai aṟṟuniṉ ṟavarkkum ariyaniṉ tiruttāṭ kaṭimaicey toḻukuva ṉēyō kaṟṟumuṟ ṟuṇarntōrk karuḷtarum oṟṟik kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅkaṭalē.
translation: I languish as a lesser dog to the stray dog barking at the gates of cruel people devoid of even a trace of good virtue. Will I ever serve and follow your holy feet, rare even for those who stand free from the mischief of the five senses? O God of Otriyur who grants grace to the fully learned and realized, O ocean of grace.
commentary: Vallalar places himself at the bottom of existence, lower than a stray dog begging at the doors of cruel people. He longs to serve the divine, a state rare even for ascetics who have mastered the mischief of the five senses. Divine grace alone bridges this gap between human weakness and spiritual attainment.

tamil: மறைகளும் இன்னும் தலைத்தலை மயங்க மறைந்துல குயிர்தொறும் ஒளித்த
இறைவநின் திருத்தாட் கன்பிலாக் கொடியன் என்னினும் ஏழையேன் தனக்கு
நிறைதரும் நினது திருவருள் அளிக்க நினைத்தலே நின்கடன் கண்டாய்
கறைமணி மிடற்றுத் தெய்வமே ஒற்றிக் காவல்கொள் கருணையங் கடலே.
translit: maṟaikaḷum iṉṉum talaittalai mayaṅka maṟaintula kuyirtoṟum oḷitta iṟaivaniṉ tiruttāṭ kaṉpilāk koṭiyaṉ eṉṉiṉum ēḻaiyēṉ taṉakku niṟaitarum niṉatu tiruvaruḷ aḷikka niṉaittalē niṉkaṭaṉ kaṇṭāy kaṟaimaṇi miṭaṟṟut teyvamē oṟṟik kāvalkoḷ karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē.
translation: O Lord hidden within every life in the world, concealed so completely that the Vedas still stand bewildered. Though I am a cruel person lacking love for your holy feet, it is your duty to think of bestowing your fulfilling holy grace upon this poor soul. O God with a dark-jeweled throat. O guarding ocean of grace in Otriyur.
commentary: God is hidden within every living being, concealed so thoroughly that even the ancient scriptures stand bewildered. Vallalar admits his heart lacks love, yet boldly claims it is God's innate duty to grant him grace. The divine is bound by compassion to save the helpless soul, regardless of the soul's flaws.

sections.title: The Petition to the Supreme Reality

translit: ulaka vāḻkkaiyiṉ uḻalumeṉ neñcam oṉṟu kōṭiyāyc ceṉṟuceṉ ṟulaintē kalaka māyaiyil kaviḻkkiṉṟa teḷiyēṉ kaluḻkiṉ ṟēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ ilakum aṉpartam eyppiṉil vaippē iṉpa veḷḷamē eṉṉuṭai uyirē tilaka mētiru oṟṟi-em uṟavē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: My mind wallows in worldly life. Multiplying one into ten million, it wanders, exhausts itself, and plunges into the turmoil of illusion. I am a poor simpleton. I weep. I know not what I must do. O treasure hoarded for your tired, radiant devotees! O flood of bliss! O my very life! O supreme ornament! O our kin in Otriyur! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The human mind turns a single thought into millions of distractions, losing itself in the illusion of worldly life. Vallalar confesses his helplessness against this mental chaos. Unable to fix the mind alone, he cries out to God as his only wealth and refuge.

translit: eṇṇi lāniṉaip puṟṟatiṉ vaḻiyē iṉpa tuṉpaṅkaḷ eyti-eṉ neñcam kaṇṇi lākkuraṅ keṉa-uḻaṉ ṟatukāṇ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ peṇni lāviya pākattem amutē piramaṉ ātiyar pēcarum tiṟaṉē teṇni lāmuṭi oṟṟiyaṅ kaṉiyē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Entertaining countless thoughts and following their paths, experiencing pleasure and pain, my mind wanders like a blind monkey. Look at this. I am the lowest of the low. I know not what I must do. O our nectar whose side shines with the Goddess! O greatness beyond the words of Brahma and the other gods! O beautiful fruit of Otriyur wearing the clear moon on your crown! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: An untrained mind reacts to every passing thought, swinging between pleasure and pain like a blind monkey. Vallalar feels at the mercy of this restless wandering. He asks for help from Para Siva (the ultimate reality), recognizing that divine grace is the only cure for a distracted mind.

translit: ūṇu ṟakkamē poruḷeṉa niṉaitta otiya ṉēṉmaṉam oṉṟiya tiṉṟāyk kāṇu ṟakkaruṅ kāmañcāṉ ṟatukāṇ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ māṇu ṟakkaḷaṅ kaṟuttacem maṇiyē vaḷḷa lē-eṉai vāḻvikkum maruntē cēṇu ṟattarum oṟṟinā yakamē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Thinking only of food and sleep as the ultimate goal, my useless mind remains completely unsteady and is visibly filled with dark lust. Look at this. I am the lowest of the low. I know not what I must do. O beautiful red gem with a blackened throat! O generous giver! O medicine that gives me life! O Lord of Otriyur who grants the heavenly realms! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: Physical survival and comfort become the mind's focus. When we think only of eating, sleeping, and sensual desires, the mind grows dark and unsteady. Vallalar admits to this failing and calls upon the Lord as the medicine to heal this obsession with the physical world.

translit: yātu colliṉum kēṭpatiṉ ṟantō yāṉcey tēṉeṉa teṉṉumiv iruḷil kātu kiṉṟateṉ vañcaka neñcam kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ ōtu māmaṟai upaniṭa tattiṉ ucci mēviya vaccira maṇiyē tītu nīkkiya oṟṟiyan tēṉē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Alas, whatever I tell it, my deceitful mind does not listen. It murders me in this darkness of ego and possession. I am the lowest of the low. I know not what I must do. O diamond resting at the peak of the great chanted Vedas and Upanishads! O honey of Otriyur who removes all evil! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The ego traps us in darkness by making us believe we are the doers of all actions and the owners of all things. A mind stuck in the illusion of "I" and "mine" refuses to listen to spiritual guidance. Vallalar prays to the divine light, the diamond at the peak of the sacred texts, to cut through this deceitful ego.

translit: collum collaḷa vaṉṟukāṇ neñcat tuṭukka ṉaittumiṅ koṭukkuva tevaṉō kallum piṟpaṭum irumpiṉum peritāl kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ allum ellumniṉ ṟakaṅkuḻain tēttum aṉparuḷ ūṟum āṉantap perukkē cellu lāmpoḻil oṟṟiyaṅ karumpē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: The arrogance of my mind cannot be measured by words. How will I ever suppress it? Stone falls behind it, and it is harder than iron. I am the lowest of the low. I know not what I must do. O flood of bliss welling up in the devotees who stand night and day with melting hearts to praise you! O beautiful sugarcane of Otriyur surrounded by groves where clouds wander! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The arrogance of the human mind is stubborn, feeling harder to break than stone or iron. Vallalar admits he cannot suppress this pride on his own. Instead of fighting the mind, he looks to the flood of divine bliss that wells up in the hearts of loving devotees, hoping that same grace will melt his hardened heart.

translit: immai iṉpamē vīṭeṉak karuti īṉar illiṭai iṭarmika uḻantē kaimmai neñcameṉ ṟaṉaivalip patukāṇ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ mummai yākiya tēvartam tēvē mukkaṇ mūrttiyē muttiyiṉ mutalē cemmai mēṉi-em oṟṟiyūr aracē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Considering worldly pleasure alone as liberation and suffering greatly in the homes of the base, see how this empty heart drags me away. I, the lowest one, do not know what I must do. O God of the trinity of gods! O three-eyed Lord! O source of liberation! O King of our Otriyur with the ruddy form! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The human heart errs when it settles for fleeting worldly pleasures and treats them as liberation. Empty and distracted, the mind drags the soul away from its real purpose. Vallalar calls out to the Supreme Reality, recognizing God as the source of freedom who rules over all other deities.

translit: niṉṉa ṭikkaṇōr kaṇappoḻu tēṉum niṟpa tiṉṟiyē nīcamaṅ kaiyartam kaṉṉa viltaṉam viḻaintatu maṉamkāṇ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ aṉṉa ūrtiyum mālumniṉ ṟalaṟa aṭiyar taṅkaḷuḷ amarntaruḷ amutē teṉi caippoḻil oṟṟi-em vāḻvē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Without standing at your feet for even a moment, see how my mind desires the rock-like breasts of base women. I, the lowest one, do not know what I must do. While Brahma on his swan mount and Vishnu stand crying out for you, O ambrosia of grace seated among your devotees! O our life in Otriyur surrounded by musical groves! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The mind wanders toward physical lust, unable to rest at God's feet for even a moment. This distracted state stands in contrast to the devotion of Brahma and Vishnu, who cry out to catch a glimpse of the Lord. Yet this same supreme God sits sweetly among devotees as the ambrosia of grace.

translit: pulaiya maṅkaiyar puṇarmulaik kuvaṭṭil pōntu ruṇṭeṉaip pulaṉvaḻip paṭuttik kalaiya niṉṟatik kalluṟaḻ maṉantāṉ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ vilaiyi lā-uyar māṇikka maṇiyē vēta ucciyil viḷaṅkoḷi viḷakkē cilaivi lākkoḷum oṟṟi-em maruntē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Going and rolling upon the hill-like breasts of degraded women, this stone-like mind drags me along the path of the senses and shatters me. I, the lowest one, do not know what I must do. O priceless supreme ruby! O shining lamp of light at the crown of the Vedas! O our medicine in Otriyur who wields the mountain as a bow! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The physical senses drag the mind down, leaving it shattered and hardened like a stone against spiritual feeling. Stripped of his own strength, Vallalar looks to the divine for a cure. He calls God the light that shines at the peak of the Vedas (the ancient scriptures) and the only medicine for a broken mind.

translit: tantai tāymaṉai makkaḷeṉ ṟulakac caḻakki lē-iṭar uḻakkumeṉ maṉantāṉ kanta vātaṉai iyaṟṟukiṉ ṟatukāṇ kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ entai yē-eṉai eḻumaiyum toṭarnta iṉpa veḷḷamē eṉuyirk kuyirē cintai ōṅkiya oṟṟi-en tēvē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Immersed in the worldly delusion of father, mother, wife, and children, see how my suffering mind acts out its sensory tendencies. I, the lowest one, do not know what I must do. O my Father! O flood of bliss that has followed me through all seven births! O life of my life! O our God in Otriyur exalted in the mind! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: Human beings lose themselves in the worldly roles of family life, bound by deep-rooted sensory habits. These attachments cause suffering and keep the mind trapped in delusion. In contrast to earthly ties, God is the soul's eternal companion, a flood of bliss that follows us through every birth as the life within all life.

translit: koṭiya vañcaka neñcakam eṉumōr kuraṅkiṟ keṉuṟu kuṟaipala uraittum kaṭiya tātaliṉ kacintila tiṉi-ik kaṭaiya ṉēṉceyak kaṭavatoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ aṭiya ṉēṉpiḻai uḷattiṭai niṉaiyēl aruḷal vēṇṭumeṉ āruyirt tuṇaiyē ceṭikaḷ nīkkiya oṟṟi-em uṟavē celva mēpara civaparam poruḷē.
translation: Even though I explained my many miseries to this monkey called the cruel and deceitful mind, it did not melt because it is so hardened. Now, I, the lowest one, do not know what I must do. Do not hold the faults of your servant in your heart. You must grant me your grace, O companion of my precious life! O our kin in Otriyur who clears away the thicket of sins! O wealth! O Para Siva, the ultimate reality!
commentary: The deceitful mind is like a stubborn monkey that refuses to listen or soften, no matter how much the soul complains of its suffering. Unable to control this hardened mind, Vallalar throws himself on divine mercy. He begs the Lord to overlook his faults and grant grace, trusting God to clear away the thicket of his past mistakes.

sections.title: The Petition to the Lord of the Bull Banner

translit: mālai oṉṟutōḷ cuntarap perumāṉ maṇattil ceṉṟavaṇ vaḻakkiṭṭa teṉavē ōlai oṉṟunīr kāṭṭutal vēṇṭām uvantu toṇṭaṉeṉ ṟuraippirēl eṉṉai vēlai oṉṟala mikappala eṉiṉum veṟuppi lātuḷam viyantucey kuvaṉkāṇ cōlai oṉṟucīr oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: You do not need to show a palm-leaf scroll, as you did when you went to the wedding of the beautiful lord Sundarar whose shoulder wears a garland and argued a case there. If you gladly declare me as your servant, I will do the work. Even if the tasks are extremely numerous instead of a single one, I will perform them with a marveling heart and without aversion. O Lord of Otriyur, rich in united groves! O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: According to Saiva tradition, the divine appeared at saint Sundarar's wedding with an ancient palm-leaf contract proving Sundarar was his bonded servant. Vallalar tells the Lord no such legal proof is needed to claim him. He offers himself, ready to perform any number of tasks with a joyful, willing heart.

translit: pūtam numpaṭai eṉiṉumnāṉ añcēṉ putiya pāmpiṉpūṇ pūṭṭavum veruvēṉ pētam iṉṟi-am palantaṉil tūkkum perumaic cēvaṭi piṭikkavum taḷarēṉ ētam eṇṇiṭā teṉṉaiyum toḻumpaṉ eṉṟu koḷvirēl eṉakkatu cālum cūta oṇpoḻil oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: Even if goblins form your army, I will not fear. I will not be terrified if you make me wear fresh snakes as ornaments. I will not grow weary of holding your glorious red foot that you raise without partiality in the Hall. If you accept even me as your servant without counting my faults, that is enough for me. O Lord of Otriyur, surrounded by bright mango groves! O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: The Lord is traditionally depicted as a wild ascetic, surrounded by fierce goblin armies and wearing live snakes for jewelry. Vallalar says these fearsome sights will never frighten him away from serving. He asks only to be accepted despite his flaws, content to hold the divine feet that offer grace to all beings equally.

translit: uppi ṭātakūḻ iṭukiṉum uṇpēṉ uvantiv vēlaiyai uṇarntucey eṉanīr ceppi ṭāmuṉam talaiyiṉāl naṭantu ceyya vallaṉyāṉ ceyyumap paṇikaḷ tappi ṭātatil tappirun teṉṉait taṇṭip pīreṉil calittuḷam veruvēṉ tuppi ṭā-eṉak karuḷoṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: Even if you serve me unsalted porridge, I will eat it. Even before you happily instruct me to understand and do a task, I am capable of walking on my head to get it done. If there are mistakes in the flawless work I do, and you punish me for them, I will not grow weary or afraid in my heart. O Lord of Otriyur who graciously grants me your support! O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: True devotion asks for no physical comforts. Vallalar will gladly eat the poorest unsalted food and eagerly rush to fulfill any command before it is fully spoken. He welcomes divine correction for his mistakes, seeing discipline as a part of his service.

translit: kūli eṉpatōr aṇuttuṇai yēṉum kuṟitti lēṉatu koṭukkiṉum koḷḷēṉ māli ṉōṭayaṉ mutaliyark kēval maṟantum ceytiṭēṉ maṉuyirp payirkkē āli aṉṉatām tēvarīr kaṭaikkaṇ aruḷai vēṇṭiṉēṉ aṭimaikoḷ kiṟpīr cūli ōrpuṭai makiḻoṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: I do not expect even an atom of a wage. Even if you give it, I will not take it. I will never perform tasks for Vishnu, Brahma, or the other gods, even in forgetfulness. I only requested your sideways glance of grace, which falls like rain upon the crop of enduring living beings. Please take me as your servant. O Lord of Otriyur, who rejoices with the Goddess holding the trident on one side! O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: Spiritual service is free of transactions or wages. Vallalar rejects payment and refuses to serve lesser deities, dedicating himself to the supreme truth. He asks only for divine grace, describing it as the rain that nourishes the crop of all living beings.

translit: tērntu tēṭiṉum tēvarpōl talaimait tēvar illai-at teḷivu koṇ ṭaṭiyēṉ ārntu numaṭik kaṭimaicey tiṭappēr ācai vaittumai aṭuttaṉaṉ aṭikēḷ ōrntiṅ keṉṟaṉait toḻumpukoḷ ḷīrēl uyki lēṉiḵ tumpatam kāṇka cōrnti ṭārpukaḻ oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: Even if one searches and investigates, there is no supreme God like you. With that clarity, I approached you with a great desire to fully serve your feet, O Lord! If you do not consider this and take me as your servant here, I will not survive. Witness this at your feet. O Lord of Otriyur, praised by the untiring! O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: Having searched and concluded there is no higher truth, Vallalar places his survival in the hands of the divine. Without the opportunity to serve this highest light, his life cannot endure.

translit: putiyaṉ eṉṟeṉaip pōkkuti rōnīr pūru vattiṉum poṉṉaṭik kaṭimaip patiya vaittaṉaṉ āyiṉum antap paḻaṅka ṇakkiṉaip pārppatil eṉṉē mutiyaṉ allaṉyāṉ eppaṇi viṭaiyum muyaṉṟu ceykuvēṉ mūrkkaṉum allēṉ tutiya tōṅkiya oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: Will you send me away, saying I am a newcomer? I registered myself as a slave to your golden feet long ago. What does it matter to look at that old account now? I am not an old man. I will strive to perform any service. I am not a stubborn fool. You possess Otriyur where praise rises high. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: Vallalar offers a playful defense of his fitness for divine service. He reminds God that his soul has belonged to him for a long time, yet he is physically young enough to work hard and willing to obey without stubbornness. There is no practical reason to turn him away.

translit: oḻukkam illavaṉ ōr iṭat taṭimaik kutavu vāṉkoleṉ ṟuṉṉukiṟ pīrēl puḻukka neñciṉēṉ ummuṭaic camukam pōntu niṟpaṉēl puṇṇiyak kaṉikaḷ paḻukka niṉṟiṭum kuṇattaru vāvēṉ pārtta pērumap pariciṉar āvar toḻukkaṉ eṉṉaiyāḷ vīroṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: You might wonder if a man without discipline will be of use as a slave anywhere. Yet if I, possessing a troubled heart, come and stand in your presence, I will become a tree of good character bearing ripe fruits of merit. Those who see me will also attain that state. Please rule over me, a base man. You possess Otriyur. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: A lack of personal discipline is no barrier to grace. Standing in the divine presence is enough to transform a troubled mind into a tree bearing good fruit. This grace is so powerful that it changes both the devotee and anyone who looks upon them.

translit: piccai ēṟṟuṇum pittareṉ ṟummaip pēcu kiṉṟavar pēcciṉaik kēṭṭum iccai niṟkiṉṟa tummaṭik kēval iyaṟṟu vāṉanta iccaiyai muṭippīr ceccai mēṉiyīr tiruvuḷam aṟiyēṉ ciṟiya ṉēṉmikat tiyaṅkukiṉ ṟaṉaṉkāṇ tuccai nīkkiṉōrk karuḷoṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: Even after hearing the words of those who call you a madman who begs for alms, my desire remains firm to serve your feet. Please fulfill that desire. You possess a coral-red body. I do not know your divine will. I am lowly, and I languish greatly. You grant grace to those who have eradicated all that is trivial. You possess Otriyur. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: The world often mocks the divine, calling God a mad beggar for wandering without worldly attachments. Hearing these insults only makes the desire to serve God stronger. True devotion pays no attention to the world's shallow opinions.

translit: ālam uṇṭanīr iṉṉumav vāṉōrk kamutu vēṇṭimā lakkaṭal kaṭaiya ōla vevviṭam varilatai nīyē uṇkeṉ ṟālumnum uraippaṭi uṇkēṉ cālam ceyvatu takai-aṉṟu tarumat taṉippoṟ kuṉṟaṉīr carācaram naṭattum cūla pāṇiyīr tiruvoṟṟi nakarīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: You consumed the poison. If those celestials churn the great ocean again for nectar and roaring fierce poison emerges, I will eat it myself if you tell me to do so according to your word. It is not fitting for you to play tricks. You are the peerless golden mountain of dharma. You direct the moving and unmoving worlds. You hold the trident. You possess the city of Otriyur. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: Traditional stories describe God swallowing deadly poison to save the world when the cosmic ocean was churned. If the ocean is churned again, Vallalar will drink the poison himself if God commands it. Service means trusting the divine will.

translit: mutti nērkilāt tēvarkaḷ tamaināṉ muntu ṟēṉavar muṟpaṭa variṉum cutti yākiya colluṭai aṇukkat toṇṭar tammuṭaṉ cūḻttiṭīr eṉiṉum putti cērpuṟat toṇṭartam muṭaṉē porunta vaikkiṉum pōtummaṟ ṟatuvē tutti yārpaṇi yīroṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: I will not approach the gods who cannot grant liberation. Even if they come forward, I will not follow them. Even if you do not gather me among your close devotees who speak pure words, it is enough if you place me appropriately with your outer devotees who possess good sense. You wear the spotted serpent. You possess Otriyur. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: True devotion demands a singular focus. Vallalar refuses to seek out lesser gods who do not have the power to grant liberation. He asks only to be kept near the highest truth, content to sit in the back row among the outer circle of devotees.

translit: eṉṉa nāṉaṭi yēṉpala palakāl iyampi niṟpatiṅ kemperu māṉīr iṉṉum eṉṉai-ōr toṇṭaṉeṉ ṟuḷattil ēṉṟu koḷḷirēl iruṅkaṭaṟ puviyōr paṉṉa eṉuyir numporuṭ ṭākap pāṟṟi nummicaip paḻicumat tuvalkāṇ tuṉṉu mātavar pukaḻoṟṟi uṭaiyīr tūya mālviṭait tuvacatti ṉīrē.
translation: O our Great Lord, why should I, your humble servant, stand here speaking again and again? If you still do not accept me in your heart as a servant, I will cast away my life for your sake. Watch me heap the blame on you, leaving the people of this sea-girt world to talk about it! You are the Lord of Otriyur, praised by gathering throngs of great ascetics. O Lord of the flag bearing the pure great bull!
commentary: Vallalar issues a desperate, loving threat to the divine. He warns that if he is not accepted as a servant, he will give up his life and leave the world to blame God for his death. This passionate demand reveals intimacy between the soul and the divine. Vallalar is dependent on grace and feels close enough to hold God accountable for withholding it. The banner of the great bull is a traditional mark of Siva, representing pure devotion and divine presence.

sections.title: The Petition to the Lord of the Drama of Wisdom

translit: maṭukkum nīruṭaip pāḻṅkiṇa ṟataṉuḷ vaḻukki vīḻntavaṉ varuntuṟā vaṇṇam eṭukkiṉ ṟōreṉa iṭaiyiṟkai viṭutal irakka muḷḷavark kiyalpaṉṟu kaṇṭīr taṭukki lāteṉaic cañcala vāḻvil tāḻttu kiṉṟatu tarumamaṉ ṟumakku naṭukki lārtoḻum oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: When someone slips and falls into a ruined well filled with water, compassionate people do not begin to lift him to ease his suffering and then let go of his hand halfway. It is not righteous of you to plunge me into this unsteady life without offering any support. Lord of Otriyur, worshipped by those free from fear, you perform a drama of wisdom.
commentary: Vallalar compares his spiritual struggle to falling into a ruined well. He asks how God can offer hope of rescue only to let go halfway, dropping him back into worldly suffering. God watches his desperate struggle from a distance, treating it like a theatrical performance.

translit: veṇmai neñciṉēṉ meyeṉpa taṟiyēṉ vimala nummiṭai vēṭkaiyum uṭaiyēṉ uṇmai ōtiṉēṉ vañcaka vāḻkkai uvari vīḻvaṉēl uṟutimaṟ ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṇmai uḷḷavar pāḻṅkuḻi vīḻak kaṇṭi ruppatu kaṟṟavark kaḻakō naṇmai oṟṟiyīr tirucciṟṟam palattuḷ ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: I have an ignorant heart. I do not know the truth. O pure Lord, I yearn for you. I speak the truth. If I fall into the ocean of this deceitful life, I know no other refuge. Is it beautiful for the wise to stand by and watch those dear to them fall into a ruined pit? Beloved Lord of Otriyur, you perform a drama of wisdom within the sacred hall.
commentary: Vallalar confesses his ignorance and yearning for the divine. He asks how the pure Lord can watch someone who loves him fall into a pit of deceit. God's silence feels like a play where the divine is merely an audience to human struggle.

translit: kuṟṟa mēpala iyaṟṟiṉum eṉainīr koṭiyaṉ eṉpatu kuṟippala umatu poṟṟai nērpuyat toḷirtiru nīṟṟaip pūcu kiṉṟaṉaṉ puṉitanum aṭikkaṇ uṟṟa tōrciṟi taṉpumiv vakaiyāl uṟuti īvatiṅ kumakkoru kaṭaṉkāṇ naṟṟa vattarvāḻ oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: Even though I commit many faults, you do not consider me a cruel person. I smear myself with the sacred ash that shines on your mountain-like shoulders. O pure Lord, I hold a little love for your feet. Because of this, it is your duty to grant me stability here. Lord of Otriyur where people of great penance live, you perform a drama of wisdom.
commentary: A devotee can claim God's protection even if full of flaws. Vallalar reminds the Lord that he wears the sacred ash and holds a little love in his heart. Because of this genuine connection, it is God's duty to grant him stability in a chaotic world.

translit: uḷḷa tōtiṉāl oṟukkilēm eṉpar ulaku ḷōrinta uṟutikoṇ ṭaṭiyēṉ kaḷḷam ōtilēṉ nummaṭi aṟiyak kāma vēṭkaiyil kaṭaliṉum periyēṉ vaḷḷa lē-uma taruḷpeṟac ciṟitu vaitta cintaiyēṉ mayakkaṟa aruḷvīr naḷḷal uṟṟavar vāḻoṟṟi uṭaiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: People of the world say they will not punish a person who speaks the truth. Holding onto this assurance, your servant speaks no lies. Before your feet I confess that I am vaster than the ocean in my lustful desires. O benevolent Lord, I have focused my mind just a little on attaining your grace. Bestow your grace to clear my delusion. Lord of Otriyur where loving devotees live, you perform a drama of wisdom.
commentary: Vallalar stakes his plea on honesty. He confesses his worldly desires are vaster than the ocean, trusting the old saying that a judge shows mercy to someone who tells the truth. He asks God to reward this transparency with the grace needed to clear his confusion.

translit: arantai yōṭoru vaḻiccelvōṉ taṉai-ōr āṟṟu veḷḷamīrt talaittiṭa avaṉum paranta nīriṭai niṉṟaḻu vāṉēl pakaivar āyiṉum pārttirup pārō karantai añcaṭai aṇṇalnīr aṭiyēṉ kalaṅkak kaṇṭiruk kiṉṟatu kaṭaṉō naranta mārpoḻil oṟṟiyūr uṭaiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: When a river flood drags away and batters a distressed person walking along a path, and he stands crying out in the spreading waters, would even his enemies stand by and simply watch? O Lord with beautiful matted hair adorned with Karanthai flowers, is it proper for you to just watch your servant suffer in confusion? Lord of Otriyur surrounded by fragrant orange groves, you perform a drama of wisdom.
commentary: Vallalar uses the image of a man swept away by a flash flood. He argues that even a bitter enemy would rush to help someone drowning. He asks how God, a loving master, can stand on the shore and watch his servant drown in the flood of worldly life.

translit: piṟavik kaṇṇilāṉ kaikkoḷum kōlaip piṭuṅki vīcutal periyavark kaṟamō maṟavik kaiyaṟai maṉattiṉēṉ ummēl vaikkum aṉpainīr māṟṟutal aḻakō uṟa-ik koḷkaiyai uḷḷirēl itaṉai ōtik koḷḷiṭam oṉṟilai kaṇṭīr naṟavik kōṅkiya oṟṟiyam patiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: Is it righteous for great people to snatch and throw away the walking stick held by a man blind from birth? I have an empty mind afflicted with forgetfulness. Is it fair for you to reject the love I place upon you? If you hold firmly to this principle, look, there is no other place for me to complain about it. O Lord of Otriyur filled with honey! You perform a drama of wisdom.
commentary: Snatching a walking stick from a blind man is a cruel act. Vallalar compares his weak and forgetful mind to this blindness. He relies on his love for the divine to guide him through life. If God rejects that love, it leaves him helpless with nowhere else to turn.

translit: valiya vantiṭu viruntiṉai oḻikkār vaṇkai uḷḷavar maṟṟatupōlak kaliya neñciṉēṉ vañcaka vāḻvil kalaṅki aiyanuṅ karuṇaiyām amutai maliya uṇṭiṭa varukiṉṟēṉ varumuṉ māṟṟu kiṟpirēl vaḷḷalnīr aṉṟō naliyal nīkkiṭum oṟṟiyam patiyīr ñāṉa nāṭakam naviṟṟukiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: Generous people do not turn away guests who come uninvited. Just like that, my heart is distressed and bewildered in this deceitful life. O Lord, I am coming to drink fully of your nectar of grace. If you turn me away before I even arrive, are you a true benefactor? O Lord of Otriyur who dispels distress! You perform a drama of wisdom.
