Because they are bewildered, he bypasses them to seek refuge in the perfect, eternal Lord. If the highest source of grace turns him away, he has no one else.

translit: tītumuṟṟum nāḷum ceyiṉum poṟuttaruḷum cātumuṟṟum cūḻnta tayānitinī eṉṟaṭaintēṉ kōtumuṟṟum tīrak kuṟiyāyēl naṉmai-eṉpa tētumaṟṟa pāvik kevartāṉ iraṅkuvarē.
translation: Knowing you are the treasure of compassion surrounded by sages, forgiving and granting grace even if one commits absolute evil every day, I came to you. If you do not intend to clear away all my faults, who will show mercy to this sinner utterly devoid of goodness?
commentary: Divine compassion forgives even the worst daily offenses. Vallalar describes himself as a sinner with no goodness, bringing his flaws directly to the source of mercy. A person with no merit relies on grace. If God does not clear away these faults, no one else has the power or patience to do so.

translit: tuṉṟiyamā pātakattōṉ cūḻviṉaiyai ōrkaṇattil aṉṟutavirt tāṇṭa aruṭkaṭalnī eṉṟaṭuttēṉ kaṉṟuṟumeṉ kaṇkalakkam kaṇṭum iraṅkāyēl eṉṟumuḷāy maṟṟiṅ kevartāṉ iraṅkuvarē.
translation: Knowing you are the ocean of grace who, in a single moment, dispelled the engulfing karma of a great sinner and ruled him that day, I approached you. If you do not show mercy even after seeing the sorrow in my suffering eyes, O eternal one, who else here will pity me?
commentary: The divine is an ocean of grace capable of wiping out a lifetime of karma in a single moment. Vallalar appeals to this history of instant forgiveness. Bringing his physical suffering directly to the eternal Lord, he asks how the divine can witness such pain and remain inactive, since no one else can offer salvation.

translit: kōṭāmē paṉṟitarum kuṭṭikaṭkut tāyāki vāṭā mulaikoṭutta vaḷḷaleṉa nāṉaṭuttēṉ vāṭā-eṉ ṟuṉaruḷil vāḻvāṉ aruḷilaiyēl īṭārum illāy eṉakkār iraṅkuvarē.
translation: Knowing you are the generous Lord who willingly became a mother to orphaned piglets and nursed them with unfailing milk, I approached you. If you do not bid me to come and live unwithering in your grace, O incomparable one, who will show me mercy?
commentary: Tradition holds that the Lord once took the form of a mother pig to nurse a litter of orphaned piglets. Vallalar uses this legend to show that divine grace reaches the lowliest creatures. He asks for that same motherly compassion. If the Lord can sustain orphaned animals, surely he can call a devoted soul to live forever in his grace.

translit: kallā naṭaiyēṉ karuṇaiyilēṉ āṉālum nallār pukaḻum namaccivā yappeyarē allātu paṟṟoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ aruḷāyēl ellām uṭaiyāy eṉakkār iraṅkuvarē.
translation: I follow ignorant ways and lack compassion. Even so, I know no refuge other than the name Namasivaya praised by the righteous. If you do not grant me grace, O Lord who possesses all things, who will show me mercy?
commentary: The foundation of spiritual life is Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings). Vallalar confesses that he lacks this compassion and follows ignorant ways. Despite this failure, he clings to the divine name as his refuge. He places his trust in the Lord who owns everything, knowing that without supreme grace, a soul without merit has no hope.

sections.title: The Sacred Decad of the Mind

translit: viṭai-ārkkum koṭi-uṭaiya vittaka-eṉ ṟuṉaṭiyiṉ iṭai-ārttu niṉṟaḻumiv ēḻaimukam pārāmē naṭai-ārkkum vāḻkkaiyilē nalkuravōrk kīyāta uṭaiyārkkō eṉṉai uṭaiyāy utavuvatē.
translation: O wise Lord bearing the banner of the roaring bull! I stand weeping, bound to Your feet. Without looking at the face of this poor one, do You extend Your help only to the wealthy who, in their bustling worldly life, give nothing to the destitute? O Lord who possesses me!
commentary: Vallalar boldly questions God's justice. Why does the divine favour the wealthy who ignore the poor, leaving a devoted soul to weep in despair?

translit: kaṟṟē aṟiyāk kaṭaippulaiyēṉ āṉālum uṟṟēniṉ taṉṉainiṉain tōtukiṉṟēṉ allāmē maṟṟētum tēṟēṉeṉ vaṉtuyartīrn tuḷkuḷirac caṟṟē iraṅkit tayavuceytāl ākātō.
translation: Though I am the lowest of the low, devoid of learning, I hold fast to You, thinking of You and chanting Your name. I know nothing else. Cannot You show a little pity and grant Your grace so my harsh sorrow ends and my heart cools?
commentary: True devotion requires no formal education or social standing. Vallalar calls himself the lowest of the low to show that worldly standing means nothing: his only qualification is his constant remembrance of the divine.

translit: kallā roṭumtirinteṉ kaṇṇēniṉ tāḷvaḻuttum nallār tamaikkāṇa nāṇukiṉṟēṉ āṉālum vallāyniṉ taṉṉai-aṉṟi maṟṟoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉnāṉ ellām aṟivāyk kitaṉai-iyam paleṉṉē.
translation: O my very eye! Having wandered with the ignorant, I am ashamed to face the good people who praise Your feet. Yet, O mighty Lord, I know nothing other than You. You know all things. What need is there to tell You this?
commentary: Guilt over past mistakes often makes a seeker feel unworthy to join the devout. Yet Vallalar finds comfort in God's total knowledge; there is no need to hide his flaws from a presence that already sees everything.

translit: kaḷḷaneṟi koḷḷum kaṭaināyēṉ eṉṉiṉumniṉ vaḷḷal malarttāḷē vaḻuttukiṉṟēṉ eṉṉuṭaiya uḷḷa melivō ṭuṭalmelivum kaṇṭumantō eḷḷaḷavum entāy iraṅkā tiruntaṉaiyē.
translation: Though I am the lowest dog taking a deceptive path, I praise only Your generous, flower-like feet. Alas, even seeing the wasting of my heart and the wasting of my body, O my Father, You show not even a sesame seed's worth of pity for me.
commentary: Spiritual longing takes a heavy physical and mental toll. Vallalar laments that his intense devotion is breaking his body and mind, yet he feels abandoned by a God who offers no pity.

translit: cīrtuṇaiyār tēṭum civaṉēniṉ taṉṉai-aṉṟi ōrtuṇaiyum illēṉniṉ oṇpoṟ patamaṟiya kārtuṇaiyā nāṭum kalāpi-eṉa nāṭukiṉṟēṉ ārtuṇai-eṉ ṟaiyā akala iruntaṉaiyē.
translation: O Siva, sought by those of excellent merit! I have no support other than You. I seek to know Your bright, golden feet, just as a peacock seeks the dark rain clouds. Leaving me to ask who will support me, O Lord, You stand far away.
commentary: In classical Tamil poetry, the peacock waiting for dark rain clouds is a traditional image of joyous expectation. Vallalar uses this comparison to describe his thirst for grace, feeling helpless while the divine remains distant.

translit: pēyaṉaiyā rōṭum piḻaipurintēṉ āṉālum nāyaṉaiyēṉ niṉṉuṭaiya nāmam naviṟṟukiṉṟēṉ tī-aṉaiya tuṉpil tikaikkiṉṟēṉ kaṇṭiruntum tāyaṉaiyāy caṟṟum tayavu purintilaiyē.
translation: I committed faults associating with those who are like demons. Even so, I who am like a dog chant your name. I stand bewildered in sorrow that burns like fire. Even seeing this, you who are like a mother have not shown me even the slightest compassion.
commentary: Even bad company and past mistakes cannot break the habit of devotion. Vallalar compares himself to a stray dog that still cries out for its master, wondering how a God with a mother's heart can watch his fiery suffering without intervening.

translit: veḷḷa maruvum viricaṭaiyāy eṉṉuṭaiya uḷḷa virivum uṭalmelivum kaṇṭiruntum taḷḷariya niṉṉaruḷōr caṟṟum puriyāmē kaḷḷaviṉaik keṉuḷattaik kaikāṭṭi niṉṟaṉaiyē.
translation: O Lord with spreading matted hair holding the flood, even seeing my mind's distress and my wasting body, you do not grant me even a fraction of your inescapable grace. Instead, you stand there pointing my heart out to deceitful karma.
commentary: The flood caught in matted hair is a classic description of Siva, who broke the fall of the river Ganges. Here, the Lord seems to withhold his grace, standing back and leaving the seeker to the mercy of deceitful karma (the accumulated consequences of past actions).

translit: eṉṉurimait tāykkum iṉiyāyniṉ ainteḻuttai uṉṉunilaik keṉṉai urittākka vēṇṭutiyēl maṉṉulakil poṉṉuṭaiyār vāyiltaṉaik kāttayarntēṉ taṉṉuṭaiya eṇṇan taṉaimuṭikka vēṇṭuvatē.
translation: O Lord who are sweeter to me than my own mother, if you wish to make me worthy to meditate on your five sacred syllables, you must fulfill the intention of this one who grew weary waiting at the doors of the wealthy in this enduring world.
commentary: The five sacred syllables refer to the fundamental mantra of Siva, Na-Ma-Si-Va-Ya. To give their whole heart to this meditation, a seeker must first be freed from the exhausting worldly struggle of begging for favor at the doors of the rich.

translit: kuṟṟamelām nalla kuṇamākak koṇṭaruḷum uṟṟatuṇai nīyēmaṟ ṟōrtuṇaiyum illai-eṉṟē naṟṟalaimai yāmuṉatu nāmam navilkiṉṟēṉ kaṟṟavaṉē eṉṟaṉainī kaiviṭileṉ ceyvēṉē.
translation: You are my close companion who accepts all my faults as good qualities, and I have no other companion. Knowing this, I chant your supremely exalted name. O omniscient one, if you abandon me, what will I do?
commentary: Total dependence on the divine means having no backup plan. God is the ultimate companion who transforms human flaws into virtues, leaving the seeker helpless if that grace is ever withdrawn.

translit: aṟiyāp paruvat taṟivuṟutti āṭkoṇṭa neṟiyāṉē niṉāṇai niṉāṇai niṉāṇai poṟiyārniṉ nāmam pukaluvatē aṉṟimaṟṟai veṟiyārvaṉ nāmamoṉṟum vēṇṭēṉnāṉ vēṇṭēṉē.
translation: O Lord of the true path who gave me knowledge and took dominion over me during my ignorant youth, I swear upon your command, upon your command, upon your command: other than chanting your glorious name, I do not desire, I do not desire any of the hollow names of others.
commentary: A triple oath marks absolute resolve. Vallalar recalls how the divine took hold of his life in his youth, swearing that he wants nothing to do with lesser gods or worldly titles; he desires only the ultimate name of the Lord.

translit: tiruvum cīrumci ṟappumti ṟalumcaṟ kuruvum kalviyum kuṟṟamil kēḷviyum poruvil aṉṉaiyum pōkkaṟu tantaiyum taruma veḷviṭaic cāminiṉ nāmamē.
translation: O Lord who rides the white bull of Dharma, Your name alone is my wealth, excellence, greatness, strength, true Guru, learning, flawless wisdom, incomparable mother, and steadfast father.
commentary: God's name takes the place of everything else in a devotee's life. The white bull of Dharma (righteousness or moral order) represents the foundation on which God is seated.

translit: poyya ṉēṉpiḻai yāvumpo ṟuttaruḷ ceyya vēṇṭumniṉ cempoṟpa tamalāl ayya ṉēmukka ṇā-iva ṭiyaṉēṟ kuyya vēṟupu kalilai uṇmaiyē.
translation: O Lord, O Three-eyed One, You must forgive all the faults of this false one and grant Your grace. Truly, for this devotee to be saved, there is no refuge other than Your pure golden feet.
commentary: The Three-eyed One is a traditional name for Siva. Acknowledging his falseness, Vallalar declares he has nowhere else to turn for safety.

translit: kaḷḷa neñcaka ṉēṉumka ṭaiyaṉēṉ vaḷḷal niṉmalar vārkaḻaṟ pātamē uḷḷu vēṉmaṟṟai ōrteyva nēyamum koḷḷa lēṉeṉku ṟippaṟin tāḷkavē.
translation: O Benefactor, though I have a deceitful heart and am the lowest of the low, I will think only of Your flower-like ankleted feet. I will not hold love for any other deity. Know my intention and rule over me.
commentary: Vallalar promises undivided loyalty to the divine. Confessing his deceitful nature, he vows never to seek help or offer love to any other god.

translit: vañca mātarma yakkamka ṉaviṉum eñcu ṟātitaṟ keṉceyku vēṉeṉṟaṉ neñcam ammayal nīṅkiṭa vanteṉait tañcam eṉṟuṉ caraṇtantu kākkavē.
translation: My infatuation with deceitful women does not diminish even in my dreams. What will I do about this? Come, free my heart from this delusion, grant me Your refuge, offer Your feet, and protect me.
commentary: Worldly desires and physical infatuations can haunt the mind so much that they remain even in dreams. Vallalar admits he is powerless to break this delusion on his own.

translit: paṟṟu neñcakap pātaka ṉēṉceyum kuṟṟam yāvumku ṇameṉak koṇṭaruḷ uṟṟa eḷtuṇai yēṉumu tavuvāy kaṟṟa naṟṟavar ēttummuk kaṇṇaṉē.
translation: O Three-eyed One praised by learned and virtuous ascetics, consider all the faults committed by this sinner with a grasping heart as virtues and grant me Your grace. Please help me, even to the measure of a sesame seed.
commentary: Surrendering his pride, Vallalar asks God to treat his faults as virtues. He begs for the tiniest drop of grace, knowing that even a sesame seed's worth is enough to save him.

translit: matiyum kalviyum vāymaiyum vaṇmaiyum patiyum īntempa cupati meynneṟik katiyiṉ vaippatu niṉkaṭaṉ vaṉkaṭal vatiyum nañcama ṇimaṇi kaṇṭaṉē.
translation: O Lord with a gem-like neck adorned with the poison from the fierce ocean, it is your duty to grant intelligence, learning, truthfulness, generosity, and a good abode, and to place me on the true path leading to the supreme state of the Lord of souls.
commentary: The divine swallowed ocean poison to save the universe. Virtues like intelligence and truthfulness are gifts that are God's duty to grant. Placing the soul on the true path is an act of divine grace rather than something achieved by human effort.

translit: nīṭu vāḻkkai neṟivaru tuṉpiṉāl vāṭum eṉṉaiva runtaleṉ ṟuṉpatam pāṭum vaṇṇamnaṟ pāṅkaruḷ vāymaṉṟuḷ āṭum mukkaṇa ruṭperu veḷḷamē.
translation: O great flood of grace with three eyes, dancing in the hall, tell me not to suffer as I wilt from the sorrows of this long worldly life, and grant me the right state to sing of your feet.
commentary: Worldly life brings exhaustion. The divine is pictured as a great flood of grace dancing in the hall. Vallalar asks for a simple reassurance: to be told not to suffer anymore. Singing God's praises becomes the cure for the sorrows of this long existence.

translit: cintai nonticci ṟiya-a ṭiyaṉēṉ entai eṉṟuṉai eṇṇiniṟ kiṉṟaṉaṉ intu cēkara ṉē-uṉṟaṉ iṉṉaruḷ tantu kāppatuṉ taṉkaṭaṉ ākumē.
translation: With an aching mind, I, this small servant, stand thinking of you as my father. O Lord wearing the moon, it is your duty to grant your sweet grace and protect me.
commentary: The relationship between the soul and God is personal. Vallalar approaches the divine as a child coming to a father with an aching mind. He reminds God that protecting the small and the suffering is the duty of a parent.

translit: uṉṉai nāṭumeṉ uḷḷam piṟariṭaip poṉṉai nāṭumpu tumai-i teṉkolō miṉṉai nāṭumnal vēṇippi rāṉiṅkē eṉṉai nāṭi-e ṉakkaruḷ ceykavē.
translation: My heart seeks you, yet it seeks gold from others. What strangeness is this? May the Lord with good matted hair flashing like lightning seek me here and grant me grace.
commentary: The human mind is full of contradiction. Vallalar wonders at his own behavior: his heart seeks God, yet he still runs after ordinary people for money. Since human effort is so easily distracted by material survival, he asks God to come seeking him instead.

translit: iḻaipo ṟuttamu laiyavark kēṟṟa-eṉ piḻaipo ṟuppatuṉ pēraruṭ kētakum maḻaipo ṟukkumva ṭivuṭai yōṉpukaḻ taḻaipo ṟukkumca ṭaimuṭit tantaiyē.
translation: O Father with a matted crown adorned with leaves, praised by the Lord whose form is like a raincloud, it is fitting for your great grace to forgive the faults I committed by pursuing women with jewel-adorned breasts.
commentary: Vallalar asks forgiveness for his past lust, appealing to a grace immense enough to pardon human weakness. God is praised by the raincloud-coloured Lord, a traditional reference to Vishnu.

translit: mūṭa ṉēṉpiḻai muṟṟum poṟuttuṉaip pāṭa vē-aruṭ pāṅkeṉak kītiyēl nāṭa vēṟuma ṉaiyiṭai naṇṇināṉ vāṭa vēṇṭuva teṉṉai-em vaḷḷalē.
translation: O our generous Lord! If you forgive all the faults of this fool and grant me the grace to sing of you, why should I wither, seeking out and visiting other houses?
commentary: If Vallalar receives the spiritual wealth of singing divine praise, he will never again have to suffer the humiliation of wandering to the doors of worldly people to seek favors. God's grace is the only support he needs.

translit: miṉṉop pāki viḷaṅkumvi ricaṭai eṉṉap pā-eṉak kiṉṉaruḷ īntuniṉ poṉṉop pāntuṇaip pūmpatam pōṟṟiyē uṉṉap pāṅkiṉu yarneṟi uykkavē.
translation: O my Father with spreading matted hair that shines like lightning! Grant me your sweet grace. Let me praise your golden, flower-like feet, and guide me to the high path of meditating upon them properly.
commentary: The spreading, lightning-like matted hair is a traditional image of Siva, picturing the divine as a source of spiritual power. The goal is to be led to the highest path, where the mind remains absorbed in praising and meditating on the golden feet of God.

tamil: குடிகொள் மலஞ்சூழ் நவவாயிற் கூட்டைக் காத்துக் குணமிலியாய்ப்
படிகொள் நடையில் பரதவிக்கும் பாவி யேனைப் பரிந்தருளிப்
பொடிகொள் வெள்ளைப் பூச்சணிந்த பொன்னே உன்னைப் போற்றிஒற்றிக்
கடிகொள் நகர்க்கு வரச்செய்தாய் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: kuṭikoḷ malañcūḻ navavāyiṟ kūṭṭaik kāttuk kuṇamiliyāyp paṭikoḷ naṭaiyil paratavikkum pāvi yēṉaip parintaruḷip poṭikoḷ veḷḷaip pūccaṇinta poṉṉē uṉṉaip pōṟṟi-oṟṟik kaṭikoḷ nakarkku varacceytāy kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: Guarding this nine-gated cage encompassed by impurities, I lacked all good qualities. I was a sinner struggling in worldly ways. You took pity on me and bestowed your grace. O Golden Lord adorned with a smear of white ash, you made me come to the fragrant city of Otri to praise you. I, the lowest, know no recompense.
commentary: Vallalar spent his life protecting his physical body—a fragile cage of impurities—and struggling in worldly ways until God rescued him. By bringing him to the sacred city of Otri to offer praise, the divine gave him a gift he feels he can never repay.

tamil: சாதல் பிறத்தல் எனும்கடலில் தாழ்ந்து கரைகா ணாதழுந்தி
ஈதல் இரக்கம் எள்அளவும் இல்லா தலையும் என்றனைநீ
ஓதல் அறிவித் துணர்வறிவித் தொற்றி யூர்ச்சென் றுனைப்பாடக்
காதல் அறிவித் தாண்டதற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: cātal piṟattal eṉumkaṭalil tāḻntu karaikā ṇātaḻunti ītal irakkam eḷaḷavum illā talaiyum eṉṟaṉainī ōtal aṟivit tuṇarvaṟivit toṟṟi yūrcceṉ ṟuṉaippāṭak kātal aṟivit tāṇṭataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: Sinking into the ocean of death and birth, I drowned without seeing a shore. I wandered without even a sesame seed's measure of charity or compassion. You taught me learning. You taught me awareness. You taught me the love to go to Otriyur and sing of you, and you took me under your rule. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this.
commentary: Life without compassion for living beings is a slow drowning in the endless cycle of birth and death. The divine intervened to teach Vallalar awareness, learning, and devotion, pulling him out of this ocean of suffering.

tamil: அற்ப அளவும் நிச்சயிக்கல் ஆகா உடம்பை அருமைசெய்து
நிற்ப தலதுன் பொன் அடியை நினையாக் கொடிய நீலன்எனைச்
சற்ப அணியாய் நின்றன்ஒற்றித் தலத்தைச் சார்ந்து நின்புகழைக்
கற்ப அருள்செய் தனைஅதற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: aṟpa aḷavum niccayikkal ākā uṭampai arumaiceytu niṟpa talatuṉ poṉ aṭiyai niṉaiyāk koṭiya nīlaṉeṉaic caṟpa aṇiyāy niṉṟaṉoṟṟit talattaic cārntu niṉpukaḻaik kaṟpa aruḷcey taṉai-ataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I cherished this body which cannot be guaranteed for even a brief moment. I did only that and never thought of your golden feet. I was a cruel, dark-hearted person. O Lord adorned with a serpent, you graced me to reach your sacred site of Otri and learn of your glory. I, the lowest, know no recompense for that.
commentary: Vallalar views his past self as dark-hearted for prioritizing his temporary physical survival over remembering the divine. He marvels that God overlooked this ignorance and brought him to the sacred site to learn spiritual glory.

tamil: உண்டு வறிய ஒதிபோல உடம்பை வளர்த்தூன் ஊதியமே
கொண்டு காக்கைக் கிரையாகக் கொடுக்க நினைக்கும் கொடியன் எனை
விண்டு அறியா நின்புகழை விரும்பி ஒற்றி யூரில்நினைக்
கண்டு வணங்கச் செய்ததற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: uṇṭu vaṟiya otipōla uṭampai vaḷarttūṉ ūtiyamē koṇṭu kākkaik kiraiyākak koṭukka niṉaikkum koṭiyaṉ eṉai viṇṭu aṟiyā niṉpukaḻai virumpi oṟṟi yūrilniṉaik kaṇṭu vaṇaṅkac ceytataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I ate and nurtured this body like a useless chameleon. I sought only the profit of flesh, intending to offer it as prey for crows. I was a cruel person. You gave me the desire for your indescribable glory. You made me see you and bow to you in Otriyur. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this.
commentary: Feeding the body for its own sake is pointless; the flesh only becomes food for scavenging crows. Vallalar expresses gratitude that God replaced his shallow, chameleon-like physical concerns with a thirst for divine truth.

tamil: நாய்க்கும் எனக்கும் ஒப்பாரி நாடி அதற்கு விருந்திடுவான்
வாய்க்கும் ஒதிபோல் பொய்உடலை வளர்க்க நினைக்கும் வஞ்சன்எனை
ஆய்க்கும் இனிய அப்பாஉன் ஒற்றி யூரை அடைந்திருளைக்
காய்க்கும் வண்ணம் செய்ததற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: nāykkum eṉakkum oppāri nāṭi ataṟku viruntiṭuvāṉ vāykkum otipōl poyuṭalai vaḷarkka niṉaikkum vañcaṉeṉai āykkum iṉiya appā-uṉ oṟṟi yūrai aṭaintiruḷaik kāykkum vaṇṇam ceytataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I sought equality between a dog and myself. I was a deceiver, thinking only of nurturing this false body like a thriving chameleon to provide a feast for that dog. O sweet Father who is kinder than a mother, you brought me to your Otriyur and caused the inner darkness to scorch away. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this.
commentary: A life devoted only to bodily comfort is false. Nurturing the flesh only prepares a future feast for wild dogs. The divine stepped in with a love sweeter than a mother's, bringing Vallalar to Otri to scorch away his inner spiritual darkness.

tamil: குருதி நிறைந்த குறுங்குடத்தைக் கொண்டோன் வழியில் சென்றிடவா
யெருதின் மனத்தேன் சுமந்துநலம் இழந்து திரியும் எய்ப்பொழிய
வருதி எனவே வழிஅருளி ஒற்றி யூர்க்கு வந்துன்னைக்
கருதி வணங்கச் செய்ததற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: kuruti niṟainta kuṟuṅkuṭattaik koṇṭōṉ vaḻiyil ceṉṟiṭavā yerutiṉ maṉattēṉ cumantunalam iḻantu tiriyum eyppoḻiya varuti eṉavē vaḻi-aruḷi oṟṟi yūrkku vantuṉṉaik karuti vaṇaṅkac ceytataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: Like one carrying a small pot filled with blood, I wandered with the mind of an ox. I bore this burden and lost all goodness. To end my weariness, you granted me the path and said, "Come." You made me reach Otriyur to think of you and worship you. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this.
commentary: God's grace reaches us even when we are worn out from mindless, animal-like living. The soul bears the worthless burden of the physical body like an ox until it is weary. Yet, in the midst of this exhaustion, God opens a clear path to the sacred city of Otriyur.

tamil: பாவம் எனும்ஓர் பெருஞ்சரக்குப் பையை எடுத்துப் பண்பறியாக்
கோவம் எனும்ஓர் குரங்காட்டும் கொடியேன் தன்னைப் பொருட்படுத்தித்
தேவர் அமுதே சிவனேநின் திருத்தாள் ஏத்த ஒற்றிஎனும்
காவல் நகரம் வரச்செய்தாய் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: pāvam eṉumōr peruñcarakkup paiyai eṭuttup paṇpaṟiyāk kōvam eṉumōr kuraṅkāṭṭum koṭiyēṉ taṉṉaip poruṭpaṭuttit tēvar amutē civaṉēniṉ tiruttāḷ ētta oṟṟi-eṉum kāval nakaram varacceytāy kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I carried a huge sack of goods called sin. I made the monkey called ignorant anger dance. Though I am so cruel, you took notice of me. O nectar of the gods. O Siva. You made me come to the guarded city of Otri to praise your holy feet. I, the lowest, know no recompense.
commentary: God values us even when we are weighed down by past mistakes and wild emotions. The burden of wrongdoings is a heavy sack, and uncontrolled anger is a dancing monkey that keeps the mind distracted. Vallalar marvels that divine perfection would invite someone so flawed to a holy sanctuary.

tamil: பொள்ளற் குடத்தின் புலால்உடம்பைப் போற்றி வளர்த்துப் புலன் இழந்தே
துள்ளற் கெழுந்த மனத்துடனே துள்ளி அலைந்த துட்டன் எனை
உள்ளற் கறிவு தந்துன்றன் ஒற்றி யூர்க்கு வந்துவினைக்
கள்ளப் பகைநீக் கிடச்செய்தாய் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: poḷḷaṟ kuṭattiṉ pulāluṭampaip pōṟṟi vaḷarttup pulaṉ iḻantē tuḷḷaṟ keḻunta maṉattuṭaṉē tuḷḷi alainta tuṭṭaṉ eṉai uḷḷaṟ kaṟivu tantuṉṟaṉ oṟṟi yūrkku vantuviṉaik kaḷḷap pakainīk kiṭacceytāy kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I cherished and nurtured this fleshly body that is nothing but a leaky pot. Losing my senses, I was a wicked man wandering wildly with a restless mind. You gave me the wisdom to reflect. You made me come to your Otriyur and banished the deceitful enemy of past karma. I, the lowest, know no recompense.
commentary: God gives the restless mind clarity to see past the illusion of the physical form, a leaking vessel that causes us to wander wildly. God intervenes by planting the wisdom to stop and reflect. This inner clarity, awakened in the sacred city, destroys the hidden enemy of past karma that traps the soul.

tamil: கூட்டும் எலும்பால் தசையதனால் கோலும் பொல்லாக் கூரைதனை
நாட்டும் பரம வீடெனவே நண்ணி மகிழ்ந்த நாயேனை
ஊட்டுந் தாய்போல் உவந்துன்றன் ஒற்றி யூர்வந் துறநினைவு
காட்டுங் கருணை செய்ததற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: kūṭṭum elumpāl tacaiyataṉāl kōlum pollāk kūraitaṉai nāṭṭum parama vīṭeṉavē naṇṇi makiḻnta nāyēṉai ūṭṭun tāypōl uvantuṉṟaṉ oṟṟi yūrvan tuṟaniṉaivu kāṭṭuṅ karuṇai ceytataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: This wicked hut is built of assembled bones and flesh. Like a dog, I rejoiced in it and treated it as my ultimate permanent home. Like a mother feeding her child, you gladly gave me the compassionate thought to come and reach your Otriyur. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this grace.
commentary: We mistake our temporary physical bodies for a permanent home, defending our fragile framework of bone and muscle like a dog guarding a worthless hut. Breaking this illusion takes tender grace. God provides this guidance with the loving eagerness of a mother feeding her child.

tamil: ஊணத் துணர்ந்த பழுமரம்போல் ஒதிபோல் துன்பைத் தாங்குகின்ற
தூணத் தலம்போல் சோரிமிகும் தோலை வளர்த்த சுணங்கன் எனை
மாணப் பரிவால் அருட்சிந்தா மணியே உன்றன் ஒற்றிநகர்
காணப் பணித்த அருளினுக்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: ūṇat tuṇarnta paḻumarampōl otipōl tuṉpait tāṅkukiṉṟa tūṇat talampōl cōrimikum tōlai vaḷartta cuṇaṅkaṉ eṉai māṇap parivāl aruṭcintā maṇiyē uṉṟaṉ oṟṟinakar kāṇap paṇitta aruḷiṉukkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I am like a flawed barren tree. I am like a useless tree. I am like a pillar bearing only sorrow. I am a dog who nurtured this blood-filled skin. With immense affection, O wish-fulfilling gem of grace, you commanded me to see your city of Otri. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this grace.
commentary: Divine affection reaches those who feel barren and useless. A life lived only to maintain the body eventually feels as lifeless as a dead tree or a pillar of sorrow. God responds to this despair with tenderness rather than judgment. Grace acts as a wish-fulfilling gem, giving meaning to a seemingly wasted life by calling the soul to witness the divine presence.

tamil: புண்ணும் வழும்பும் புலால்நீரும் புழுவும் பொதிந்த பொதிபோல
நண்ணுங் கொடிய நடைமனையை நான்என் றுளறும் நாயேனை
உண்ணும் அமுதே நீஅமர்ந்த ஒற்றி யூர்கண் டென்மனமும்
கண்ணுங் களிக்கச் செய்ததற்கோர் கைம்மா றறியேன் கடையேனே.
translit: puṇṇum vaḻumpum pulālnīrum puḻuvum potinta potipōla naṇṇuṅ koṭiya naṭaimaṉaiyai nāṉeṉ ṟuḷaṟum nāyēṉai uṇṇum amutē nī-amarnta oṟṟi yūrkaṇ ṭeṉmaṉamum kaṇṇuṅ kaḷikkac ceytataṟkōr kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: I am a dog who babbles "I" about this cruel moving house, which is like a packed sack of sores, slime, fleshy fluids, and worms. O sweet ambrosia, you made my mind and eyes rejoice by letting me see Otriyur where you abide. I, the lowest, know no recompense for this.
commentary: Pointing to a decaying sack of flesh and calling it the true self is a foolish mistake. Vallalar humbles himself for this ignorance, yet marvels at the grace he received. God allowed him to see the holy town of Otriyur, filling his eyes and mind with joy despite his unworthiness.

sections.title: The Decad on the Divine Form

translit: tiruvaṇṇa natiyumvaḷai oruvaṇṇa matiyumvaḷar cevvaṇṇam naṇṇucaṭaiyum teruḷvaṇṇa nutalviḻiyum aruḷvaṇṇa vataṉamum tikaḻvaṇṇa veṇṇakaiyumōr maruvaṇṇa maṇikuvaḷai malarvaṇṇa miṭaṟummalai makaḷvaṇṇa maruvumiṭamum maṉvaṇṇa mikutuṇaip poṉvaṇṇa aṭimalarum māṇikka vaṇṇavaṭivum iruvaṇṇa māmeṉmaṉa toruvaṇṇam ākiyē iṭaiyaṟā teṇṇumvaṇṇam evvaṇṇam avvaṇṇam ivvaṇṇam eṉṟivaṇ iyampaluṉ karuṇaivaṇṇam karuvaṇṇam aṟa-uḷam peruvaṇṇam uṟaniṉṟu kaṭalvaṇṇaṉ eṇṇumamutē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: The sacred river and the curved crescent moon, the glowing red matted hair, the wisdom-filled frontal eye, the grace-filled face, the shining white smile, the fragrant sapphire-like blue water-lily throat, the left side united with the mountain's daughter, the glorious beautiful golden lotus feet, and the ruby-like form: to make my dual-natured mind become single-minded, to meditate on these without break, and to speak of them here in whichever way possible: this is the nature of Your grace! O Nectar meditated upon by the sea-colored Vishnu, standing so that the nature of birth ceases and the mind attains a great state! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The mind is restless, pulled in different directions. By focusing on the traditional imagery of the divine form, the soul finds a single anchor. The ability to concentrate on God and speak of this beauty is an act of divine grace.

translit: eṇṇuṟuvi ruppāti valvilaṅ kiṉamelām iṭaiviṭā tuḻala-oḷi-ōr eḷaḷavum iṉṟi-añ ñāṉa-iruḷ mūṭiṭa iruṇṭuyir maruṇṭumāḻka naṇṇumaṉa māyaiyām kāṭṭaik kaṭantuniṉ ñāṉa-aruḷ nāṭṭai-aṭaiyum nāḷenta nāḷanta nāḷinta nāḷeṉṟu nāyiṉēṟ karuḷceykaṇṭāy viṇṇuṟucu ṭarkkelām cuṭaraḷit toruperu veḷikkuḷvaḷar kiṉṟacuṭarē vittoṉṟum iṉṟiyē viḷaivelām tarukiṉṟa viññāṉa maḻaiceymukilē kaṇṇuṟunu taṟperuṅ kaṭavuḷē maṉṟiṉil karuṇainaṭam iṭuteyvamē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: Desire and other fierce beasts roam endlessly without a break. Without even a sesame-seed measure of light, the darkness of ignorance covers all. In this darkness, the soul is bewildered and perishes. When is the day I will cross this approaching forest of mental illusion and reach the country of Your graceful wisdom? Tell me, "That day is this day," and bestow Your grace upon me, a dog! O Flame who grows in the one vast space, giving light to all the lights in the sky! O Cloud of wisdom who showers rain that yields all harvest without any seed! O Great God with the frontal eye! O Deity who dances with compassion in the hall! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The worldly mind is a dark forest where desires roam like wild animals. Lost in this darkness without a spark of spiritual light, the soul is bewildered. Vallalar asks for liberation right now, urging the divine to declare that the day of rescue is today.

translit: pūtaneṟi yātivaru nātaneṟi varaiyumāp pukalumū vulakunīttup puraiyuṟṟa mūṭameṉum iruḷnilama kaṉṟumēl pōyaruḷo ḷittuṇaiyiṉāl vētaneṟi pukalcakala kēvalami lātapara veḷikaṇṭu koṇṭukaṇṭa viḷaiviṉṟi nāṉiṉṟi veḷi-iṉṟi veḷiyāy viḷaṅkunāḷ eṉṟaruḷuvāy vātaneṟi naṭavāta pōtaneṟi yāḷarniṟai matineṟi-u lāvummatiyē maṇimiṭaṟ ṟaracē-em vāḻviṉmuta lē-aru maruntēpe runteyvamē kātaneṟi maṇamvīcu kaṉitarupo ḻiṟkulavu kaṭimatiṟ ṟillainakarvāḻ kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: Transcending the three vast worlds spoken of, from the path of the elements up to the path of sound, leaving the dark ground of flawed ignorance and going above by the aid of the light of grace, seeing the supreme space free of the embodied and disembodied states spoken of by the Vedic path, when is the day I will shine as that very space, without the resulting experience of seeing, without myself, and without space? Please grant me this grace! O Moon who wanders in the path of the full moon of the wise who do not walk the path of argument! O King with the sapphire throat! O First Cause of our life! O Rare Medicine! O Great Deity! O Lord who lives in the city of Thillai with guarded walls, surrounded by fruit-bearing groves spreading fragrance for leagues! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: True liberation requires moving past physical elements, cosmic worlds, and spiritual stages described in traditional scriptures. Guided by grace, the soul reaches a supreme space beyond form and formlessness. In that state, the separation between the seer, the act of seeing, and the space itself dissolves.

translit: kūrkoṇṭa vāḷkoṇṭu kolaikoṇṭa vēṭṭuvak kuṭikoṇṭa cērinaṭuvil kuvaikoṇṭa orucelvaṉ arumaikoṇ ṭīṉṟiṭu kulaṅkoṇṭa ciṟuvaṉoruvaṉ nērkoṇṭu ceṉṟavarkaḷ kaikoṇ ṭuṟakkaṇkaḷ nīrkoṇṭu vāṭaleṉavē nilaikoṇṭa nī-aruṭ kalaikoṇ ṭaḷittayāṉ neṟikoṇṭa kuṟitavaṟiyē pōrkoṇṭa poṟimutal pulaikoṇṭa tattuvap puraikoṇṭa maṟavarkuṭiyām poykoṇṭa meyeṉṉum maikoṇṭa cēriyil pōntuniṉ ṟavaralaikkak kārkoṇṭa iṭi-olik kaṇkoṇṭa pārppil kalaṅkiṉēṉ aruḷpurikuvāy kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: Like a boy born to an immensely wealthy man, captured by hunters armed with sharp, murderous swords, taken into the midst of their settlement, withered with eyes full of tears as they surrounded and grabbed him; I, who was graciously given the art of grace by You, the steadfast one, missed the mark of the path, entered the dark settlement of this false body, a settlement of murderous hunters, the senses that wage war and the base principles, and as they stood and tormented me, I was bewildered like a fledgling bird hearing the sound of dark thunderclouds. Please bestow Your grace on me! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The soul is compared to the child of a wealthy family kidnapped by ruthless hunters. These hunters are the physical senses and worldly principles, and their dark settlement is the physical body. Trapped and tormented by these forces, the soul feels as terrified as a baby bird hearing a crash of thunder.

translit: paṭameṭut tāṭumoru pāmpāka eṉmaṉam pāmpāṭṭi yākamāyaip pārttuk kaḷittutavu paricuṭaiyar viṭayam paṭarntapira pañcamākat tiṭamaṭut tuṟupāmpiṉ āṭṭamatu kaṇṭañcu ciṟuvaṉyā ṉākaniṉṟēṉ tīrattu rantanta accanta virttiṭu tiṟattaṉnī ākalvēṇṭum viṭamaṭut taṇikoṇṭa maṇikaṇṭa ṉēvimala viññāṉa māmakaṇṭa vīṭaḷit taruḷkaruṇai veṟpaṉē aṟputa virāṭṭuruva vētārttaṉē kaṭamaṭut tiṭukaḷiṟ ṟurikoṇṭa ṇintameyk kaṭavuḷē caṭaikoḷaracē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: My mind acts as a dancing cobra with a spread hood. Illusion acts as the snake-charmer. The expansive world acts as the sense objects offering gifts to those who watch and enjoy. I stand as a little boy who watches the dance of this strong snake and is terrified. You must be the capable one to swiftly drive it away and remove that fear! O Lord with the sapphire throat adorned with poison! O Mountain of compassion who grants the vast liberation of pure wisdom! O Wonder whose universal form is the meaning of the Vedas! O True God who wears the skin stripped from a rutting elephant! O King with matted hair! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The mind is a dangerous force, swaying like a hooded cobra under the spell of a snake-charmer called illusion. The surrounding world feeds this performance with endless distractions. Left powerless, the soul stands by like a frightened child watching the dance, depending on God to drive the danger away.

translit: eḻuvakaip piṟavikaḷuḷ eppiṟavi eytukiṉum eytukapi ṟappiliṉināṉ eytāmai eytukiṉum eytiṭuka irumaiyiṉum iṉpamey tiṉumeytuka vaḻuvakait tuṉpamē vantiṭiṉum varukamiku vāḻvuvan tiṭiṉumvaruka vaṟumaivaru kiṉumvaruka mativariṉum varuka-ava mativariṉum varuka-uyarvō ṭiḻivakait tulakiṉmaṟ ṟetuvariṉum varuka-ala tetupō kiṉumpōkaniṉ iṇaiyaṭikaḷ maṟavāta maṉamoṉṟu māttiram eṉakkaṭaital vēṇṭumaracē kaḻivakaip pavarōka nīkkumnal laruḷeṉum katimarun tutavunitiyē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: Whatever birth among the seven kinds of births I may take, let it happen. If I attain the state of no future births, let it be so. Whether I attain joy in both worlds, let it be. If flawed sorrow comes, let it come. If great prosperity comes, let it come. If poverty comes, let it come. If honor comes, let it come. If dishonor comes, let it come. High or low, whatever comes in this world, let it come. Or whatever goes, let it go. O King, I need to attain only one thing: a mind that never forgets your twin feet. O treasure offering the medicine of good grace to cure the severe disease of worldly birth! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The only thing that matters is remembering the divine, no matter what happens in the physical world. Vallalar welcomes poverty or wealth, honor or disgrace, rebirth or liberation, asking only for a mind that never forgets God. He calls this constant connection to grace the medicine for the disease of endless worldly births.

translit: paṟṟuvatu pantamap paṟṟaṟutal vīṭiḵtu paramavē tārttameṉavē paṇpuḷōr naṇpiṉoṭu pakaruvatu kēṭṭumeṉ pāvimaṉam viṭayanaṭaiyē eṟṟuvatu ceyyāmal eḻuvatoṭu viḻuvatum iṟaṅkuvatum ēṟuvatumvīṇ eṇṇuvatum naṇṇuvatum ippuvaṉa pōkaṅkaḷ yāviṉum ceṉṟuceṉṟē cuṟṟuvatum āki-ōr caṟṟumaṟi villātu cuḻalkiṉṟa teṉceykuvēṉ tūyaniṉ tiruvaruḷiṉ aṉṟi-iv vēḻai-ac cuḻalmaṉama ṭakkavarumō kaṟṟuvaḻu vaṟṟavar karuttamar karuttaṉē kaṇṇutaṟ kaṭavuḷmaṇiyē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: Good people declare with friendship that attachment is bondage and cutting that attachment is liberation, stating this as the supreme meaning of the Vedas. Even after hearing this, my sinful mind continues to walk the path of sensory objects. Without giving them up, it rises and falls, descends and ascends, vainly thinking and approaching, wandering after all the pleasures of this world. What will I do as it spins around with absolutely no understanding? Without your pure divine grace, can this poor wretch control this spinning mind? O Lord seated in the minds of the learned who are free from flaws! O jewel of a God with an eye on your forehead! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: Knowing the truth intellectually is not enough to stop the mind from chasing worldly pleasures. Vallalar notes that people can learn from the Vedas that attachment causes suffering, yet still wander after sensory distractions. His own mind spins out of control despite knowing better. Human effort alone cannot tame a restless mind; only divine grace can bring it to stillness.

translit: eḷiyaṉēṉ ciṟiyaṉyāṉ ceypiḻaikaḷ ciṟiyavō eḻukaṭali ṉumperiyavē eṉceykēṉ eṉceykēṉ iṉi-āyi ṉumceyā tentainiṉai ētta-eṉṟāl vaḷiyiṉvāṉ cuḻalkiṉṟa pañcāka neñcāl mayaṅkukiṉ ṟēṉaṭiyaṉēṉ maṉameṉatu vacamāka niṉatuvacam nāṉāka vantaṟivu tantaruḷuvāy oḷiyiṉoḷi yēnāta veḷiyiṉ veḷiyēviṭaya uruviṉuru vē-uruviṉām uyiriṉuyi rē-uyarkoḷ uṇarviṉuṇar vē-uṇarviṉ uṟaviṉuṟa vē-emiṟaiyē kaḷiyiṉniṟai vē-aḷikoḷ karuṇainiti yēmaṇikoḷ kaṇṭa-eṇ tōḷkaṭavuḷē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: I am simple and small. Are the mistakes I make small? They are larger than the seven oceans. What will I do? What will I do? Even if I resolve not to commit them anymore and try to praise you, my Father, I am bewildered in my heart like cotton spinning in the wind. Please come and grant me wisdom so that my mind comes under my control and I come under your control. O Light within light! O Space within the supreme space! O Form within the forms of the sensory world! O Life within the life of embodied beings! O Awareness within high awareness! O Bond within the bonds of awareness! O our Lord! O Fullness of joy! O Treasure of abundant compassion! O God with a jewel-like neck and eight shoulders! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The human heart is easily blown around by worldly distractions like cotton in the wind. Vallalar confesses his mistakes feel vast and overwhelming, leaving him confused and unable to focus. He asks for the wisdom to master his own mind so he can belong to the divine. He describes God not as a distant figure, but as the inner reality hiding inside everything.

translit: cantatame ṉakkumakiḻ tantainī uṇṭuniṉ taṉṉiṭat tēmavalli tāyuṇṭu niṉaṭiyar eṉṉumnal tamaruṇṭu cāntameṉum nēyaruṇṭu puntikoḷni rācaiyām maṉaivi-uṇ ṭaṟiveṉum putalvaṉuṇ ṭiravupakalum pōṉaviṭa muṇṭaruṭ poruḷumuṇ ṭāṉanta pōkapōk kiyamumuṇṭu vantaṉaicey nīṟeṉum kavacamuṇ ṭakkamā maṇiyumuṇ ṭañceḻuttām mantirap paṭai-uṇṭu civakati-e ṉumperiya vāḻvuṇṭu tāḻvumuṇṭō kantamiku koṉṟaiyoṭu kaṅkaivaḷar ceñcaṭaik kaṭavuḷē karuṇaimalaiyē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: You are always my joyful Father. I have Mother Hemavalli by your side. I have your devotees as my good relatives. I have peace as my friend. I have desirelessness as my intelligent wife. I have wisdom as my son. I have a place that transcends day and night. I have the wealth of grace. I have the bliss and the objects of blissful enjoyment. I have the revered holy ash as my armor. I have the rudraksha beads. I have the five-lettered mantra as my weapon. I have the great life of liberation in Siva. Can there be any downfall for me? O God with red matted hair adorned with fragrant konrai flowers and the flourishing river Ganges! O Mountain of compassion! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: True spiritual life provides a complete family and protection. Vallalar replaces a worldly household with divine relationships: God and Hemavalli are his parents, devotees his relatives, peace his friend, desirelessness his wife, and wisdom his son. Armed with holy ash, sacred rudraksha beads, and the five-letter mantra of Siva, he feels secure. A person supported by this spiritual wealth can never experience a downfall.

translit: nāṉmukaṉum mālumaṭi muṭiyumaṟi variyapara nātamicai ōṅkumalaiyē ñāṉamaya māṉa-oru vāṉanaṭu āṉanta naṭaṉamiṭu kiṉṟa-oḷiyē māṉmukamvi ṭātuḻalum eṉaiyumuyar neṟimaruva vaittavaṇva ḷarttapatiyē maṟaimuṭivil niṟaiparap piramamē ākama matikkummuṭi vuṟṟacivamē ūṇmukac ceyalviṭut tuṇmukap pārvaiyiṉ uṟuntavarpe ṟuñcelvamē oḻiyāta uvakaiyē aḻiyāta iṉpamē oṉṟiraṇ ṭaṟṟanilaiyē kāṉmukak kaṭakaḷiṟ ṟurikoṇṭa kaṭavuḷē kaṇkoṇṭa nutalaṇṇalē kaṉaka-am palanāta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇapōta kamalakuñ citapātaṉē.
translation: O Mountain towering above the supreme sound, whose base and summit even Brahma and Vishnu found impossible to know! O Light dancing in bliss at the center of the sky of pure wisdom! O Lord who placed even me, wandering endlessly after worldly illusions, on the high path and nurtured me there! O perfect Supreme Brahman at the culmination of the Vedas! O ultimate Siva revered by the Agamas! O wealth attained by ascetics who abandon outward physical actions and hold an inward vision! O unceasing joy! O imperishable bliss! O state devoid of one or two! O God wearing the skin of the fierce forest elephant! O Lord with an eye on your forehead! O Lord of the Golden Hall! O Source of compassionate, beautiful eyes! O Lord with the raised lotus foot!
commentary: The divine reality is beyond the reach of traditional gods, physical rituals, and ordinary logic. Vallalar refers to a classic story where the creator god Brahma and the preserver god Vishnu could not find the top or bottom of Siva, showing that the supreme is boundless. He calls this divine presence the final truth of both the Vedas and the Agamas. However, this truth is not found in outward actions. It is a state of undivided bliss attained only by those who turn their vision inward.

translit: aruḷtaral vēṇṭum pōṟṟi-eṉ aracē aṭiyaṉēṉ maṉattakat teḻunta iruḷkeṭal vēṇṭum pōṟṟi-en tāyē ēḻaiyēṉ niṉṟaṉaip pāṭum teruḷuṟal vēṇṭum pōṟṟi-eṉ aṟivē cintainain tulakiṭai mayaṅkum maruḷaṟal vēṇṭum pōṟṟi-eṉ kuruvē matinati vaḷarcaṭai maṇiyē.
translation: Grant me Grace, praise be to You, my King! The darkness that has risen in the heart of this humble devotee must be destroyed, praise be to You, my Mother! This poor one must attain the clarity to sing of You, praise be to You, my Wisdom! The delusion of languishing in mind and being confused in this world must cease, praise be to You, my Guru! O Gem with the crescent moon and river on Your matted hair!
commentary: Vallalar asks the divine to destroy inner darkness and worldly confusion. He addresses God in four intimate roles: a ruling king, a nurturing mother, the source of wisdom, and a guiding guru. The imagery of the crescent moon and river on matted hair points to Siva, but the focus is on the direct, personal rescue of the soul.

translit: maṇimiṭaṟ ṟamutē pōṟṟi-eṉ taṉṉai vāḻvikka vēṇṭuval pōṟṟi aṇimati muṭiyōy pōṟṟi-iv vēḻaik karuḷamu taruḷuka pōṟṟi paṇi-aṇi puyattōy pōṟṟiniṉ cīrē pāṭutal vēṇṭumnāṉ pōṟṟi taṇivilpē roḷiyē pōṟṟi-eṉ taṉṉait tāṅkuka pōṟṟiniṉ patamē.
translation: O Nectar with the blue throat, praise be! I pray that You make me live, praise be! O You who wear the beautiful crescent moon on Your crown, praise be! Grant the nectar of Grace to this poor one, praise be! O You whose shoulders are adorned with serpents, praise be! I must sing of Your greatness, praise be! O great unquenchable Light, praise be! Sustain me, praise be to Your feet!
commentary: The soul begs for the nectar of divine grace to sustain its spiritual life. Classic forms of Siva appear, such as his blue throat and serpent ornaments. Yet the core request is for the great, unquenchable light of God to uphold the devotee and inspire their song.

translit: niṉpatam pāṭal vēṇṭumnāṉ pōṟṟi nīṟupūt toḷirkuḷir neruppē niṉpukaḻ kēṭṭal vēṇṭumnāṉ pōṟṟi neṟṟiyaṅ kaṇkoḷum niṟaivē niṉvaca mātal vēṇṭumnāṉ pōṟṟi neṭiyamāl pukaḻtaṉi nilaiyē niṉpaṇi purital vēṇṭumnāṉ pōṟṟi neṭuñcaṭai muṭittayā nitiyē.
translation: I must sing of Your feet, praise be! O cool Fire shining with smeared ash! I must hear Your praise, praise be! O Complete One with the beautiful eye on the forehead! I must become entirely Yours, praise be! O singular State praised by tall Vishnu! I must perform Your service, praise be! O Treasure of compassion with a long matted crown!
commentary: True devotion means wanting to belong to God through singing, listening, and serving. The divine is a cool fire shining with sacred ash, a paradox showing God's presence as both purifying and soothing. Calling God a treasure of compassion shows that divine grace is rooted in pure mercy.

translit: nititaru niṟaivē pōṟṟi-eṉ uyirkkōr neṟitaru nimalamē pōṟṟi matimuṭik kaṉiyē pōṟṟi-eṉ taṉṉai vāḻvitta vaḷḷalē pōṟṟi vitimutaṟ kiṟaiyē pōṟṟimeyñ ñāṉa viyaṉneṟi viḷakkamē pōṟṟi patipacu patiyē pōṟṟi niṉpātam pāṭa-eṟ karuḷuka pōṟṟi.
translation: O Complete One who grants true wealth, praise be! O pure One who gives a path to my life, praise be! O Fruit with the crescent moon on the crown, praise be! O Benefactor who made me live, praise be! O Lord of Brahma and the other gods, praise be! O Light of the vast path of true wisdom, praise be! O Lord of all souls, praise be! Grant me Grace to sing of Your feet, praise be!
commentary: God is the benefactor who grants the wealth of spiritual wisdom. The Supreme Lord is the master over all other gods, including creator deities like Brahma. The highest gift the soul asks for is the grace to stay on the path of wisdom and sing the Lord's praises.

translit: pōṟṟi-eṉ uyirkkōr iṉpamē aṉpar puritavak kāṭciyē pōṟṟi pōṟṟi-eṉ aṉpām teyvamē caivam pukalciva pōkamē pōṟṟi pōṟṟi-eṉ peritāñ celvamē karuṇaip pūraṇa veḷḷamē pōṟṟi pōṟṟi-eṉ vāḻvuk koruperu mutalē pōṟṟiniṉ cēvaṭip pōtē.
translation: Praise be, O joy of my life! Praise be, O Vision attained by the penance of loving devotees! Praise be, O God who is my love! Praise be, O supreme bliss proclaimed by Saivism! Praise be, my great wealth! Praise be, O perfect flood of compassion! Praise be, O one great source of my life! Praise be to the lotus of Your reddened feet!
commentary: God is pure joy, love, and a flood of compassion. The highest spiritual state is not an abstract idea but a direct experience of divine love. Vallalar calls this loving God his greatest wealth and the source of his life.

translit: pōta-ā ṉanta pōkamē eṉṉaip puṟampiṭa niṉaittiṭēl pōṟṟi cītavāṉ piṟaicēr ceñcaṭai yāyeṉ ciṟumaitīrt taruḷuka pōṟṟi pētamoṉ ṟillā aruṭkaṭa lē-eṉ piḻai-elām poṟuttaruḷ pōṟṟi vētameyp poruḷē pōṟṟiniṉ allāl vēṟeṉak kilai-aruḷ pōṟṟi.
translation: O experience of the bliss of awareness, do not think of casting me away. Praise to you. O Lord with red matted hair wearing the cool crescent moon, clear away my baseness and bestow your grace. Praise to you. O ocean of grace without a single division, forgive all my faults. Praise to you. O true essence of the Vedas, praise to you. Other than you, I have no one. Bestow your grace. Praise to you.
commentary: Vallalar cries out to God as an undivided ocean of grace and the bliss of awareness. Beneath familiar forms, he seeks the essence of spiritual knowledge, begging not to be cast away because he has no other refuge.

translit: pōṟṟuvār uḷḷam pukuntoḷir oḷiyē pōṟṟiniṉ pūmpatam pōṟṟi āṟṟuvār caṭai-eṉ appaṉē pōṟṟi amalaniṉ aṭimalar pōṟṟi ēṟṟuvār koṭikoḷ entaiyē pōṟṟi iṟaivaniṉ iruṅkaḻal pōṟṟi cāṟṟumā ṟariya perumaiyē pōṟṟi talaivaniṉ tāṭṭuṇai pōṟṟi.
translation: O light that enters and shines in the hearts of those who praise you. Praise to your flower-like feet. O my father with the river flowing in your matted hair, praise to you. O pure one, praise to your lotus feet. O my father holding the banner of the bull, praise to you. O Lord, praise to your great ankleted feet. O greatness impossible to describe in words, praise to you. O master, praise to your paired feet.
commentary: God is a living light that enters and shines in the hearts of those who offer praise. Vallalar pairs this intimate inner presence with vivid traditional forms, such as the Lord holding a bull banner. The divine is both a felt light within the heart and a majestic power that words cannot capture.

translit: tuṇaimulai maṭantai emperu māṭṭi tuṇaivaniṉ tuṇaiyaṭi pōṟṟi puṇai-eṉa iṭariṉ kaṭaliṉiṉ ṟēṟṟum puṉitaniṉ poṉṉaṭi pōṟṟi iṇaiyilpē riṉpa amutaruḷ karuṇai iṟaivaniṉ iṇaiyaṭi pōṟṟi kaṇai-eṉak kaṇṇaṉ taṉaikkoḷum orumuk kaṇṇaniṉ kaḻalaṭi pōṟṟi.
translation: O consort of our great lady, the young woman with lovely breasts, praise to your paired feet. O pure one whose golden feet lift me from the ocean of sorrow like a raft, praise to your golden feet. O compassionate Lord who grants the nectar of peerless supreme bliss, praise to your paired feet. O unique three-eyed Lord who took Vishnu as your arrow, praise to your ankleted feet.
commentary: The divine offers a raft to carry the soul out of the ocean of worldly sorrow. To express this saving power, Vallalar calls upon ancient myths of Siva, referencing his three eyes, his heavenly consort, and the story where he used the god Vishnu as his arrow. These traditional stories act as poetic expressions of the Lord's absolute power to grant bliss and rescue those who suffer.

translit: aṭiyaṉēṉ piḻaikaḷ poṟuttaruḷ pōṟṟi ayaleṉai viṭṭiṭēl pōṟṟi koṭiyaṉēṟ kiṉpan tantaruḷ pōṟṟi kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟamē pōṟṟi neṭiya-eṉ tuṉpan tuṭaittaruḷ pōṟṟi niṉai-alāl piṟitilēṉ pōṟṟi paṭimicaip piṟarpāl celuttiṭēl eṅkaḷ paramaniṉ aṭaikkalam nāṉē.
translation: Forgive the faults of this servant. Praise to you. Do not abandon me to strangers. Praise to you. Grant bliss to this cruel one. Praise to you. O great mountain of virtues, praise to you. Wipe away my endless sorrow. Praise to you. I have no one other than you. Praise to you. Do not send me to anyone else on this earth. O our Supreme Lord, I seek refuge in you.
commentary: True surrender means having nowhere else to turn. Vallalar asks God to forgive his flaws and wipe away endless sorrow, pleading not to be abandoned or handed over to anyone else in the world. He places his trust in the divine as his only refuge and source of peace.

translit: nāṉceyum piḻaikaḷ palavumnī poṟuttu nalantaral vēṇṭuvaṉ pōṟṟi ēṉceytāy eṉpār illaimaṟ ṟeṉakkuṉ iṉṉaruḷ nōkkañcey pōṟṟi ūṉceynā vāluṉ ainteḻut teḷiyēṉ ōtanī uvantaruḷ pōṟṟi māṉceyum neṭuṅkaṇ malaimakaḷ iṭaṅkoḷ vaḷḷalē pōṟṟiniṉ aruḷē.
translation: I pray that you forgive the many faults I commit and grant me goodness. Praise to you. I have no one else to ask me, "Why did you do this?" Bestow the gaze of your sweet grace upon me. Praise to you. Rejoice and grant that this lowly one may chant your five syllables with this fleshy tongue. Praise to you. O benevolent Lord who keeps the mountain daughter with large deer-like eyes on your left side. Praise to your grace.
commentary: The bond between the soul and God is personal. Vallalar has no one else who will correct his mistakes or care enough to ask why he went astray. He asks for the joy of chanting the five sacred syllables of Siva (Na-ma-shi-va-ya) with his physical tongue, seeking grace from the Lord who holds the goddess on his left side.

tamil: தண்ணார் மதிபோல் சீதளவெண் தரளக் கவிகைத் தனிநிழற்கீழ்க்
கண்ணார் செல்வச் செருக்கினர்தம் களிப்பில் சிறிய கடைநாயேன்
பெண்ணார் பாகப் பெருந்தகைதன் பெரிய கருணைக் குரியம்என்றே
எண்ணா நின்று களிக்கின்றேன் ஆரூர் எந்தாய் இரங்காயே.
translit: taṇṇār matipōl cītaḷaveṇ taraḷak kavikait taṉiniḻaṟkīḻk kaṇṇār celvac cerukkiṉartam kaḷippil ciṟiya kaṭaināyēṉ peṇṇār pākap peruntakaitaṉ periya karuṇaik kuriyameṉṟē eṇṇā niṉṟu kaḷikkiṉṟēṉ ārūr entāy iraṅkāyē.
translation: Under the unique shade of the cool white pearl umbrella resembling the moon, those arrogant with worldly wealth rejoice. Yet my joy surpasses theirs, for though I am a small and lowly dog, I constantly rejoice thinking I am worthy of the great grace of the noble Lord who shares his form with the Goddess. O my Father in Arur, have mercy!
commentary: The joy of awaiting divine grace is far greater than the pride of wealthy kings. Though Vallalar feels like a lowly street dog, he finds greater happiness believing he is worthy of God's compassion.

tamil: இரங்கா திருந்தால் சிறியேனை யாரே மதிப்பார் இழிந்தமனக்
குரங்கால் அலைப்புண் டலைகின்ற கொடிய பாவி இவன்என்றே
உரங்கா தலித்தோர் சிரிப்பார்நான் உலகத் துயரம் நடிக்கின்ற
அரங்காக் கிடப்பேன் என்செய்வேன் ஆரூர் அமர்ந்த அருமணியே.
translit: iraṅkā tiruntāl ciṟiyēṉai yārē matippār iḻintamaṉak kuraṅkāl alaippuṇ ṭalaikiṉṟa koṭiya pāvi ivaṉeṉṟē uraṅkā talittōr cirippārnāṉ ulakat tuyaram naṭikkiṉṟa araṅkāk kiṭappēṉ eṉceyvēṉ ārūr amarnta arumaṇiyē.
translation: If you remain without mercy, who will respect this small one? Those of firm wisdom will laugh, calling me a cruel sinner tossed and driven by the monkey of a degraded mind. I will lie here as a stage where worldly sorrow enacts its play. What will I do? O rare gem seated in Arur!
commentary: A mind left to itself behaves like a wild monkey, dragging a person into confusion. Without divine mercy, life becomes a stage where worldly sorrow plays out. Vallalar fears wise people will laugh at his restless mind unless he receives God's grace.

tamil: மணியார் கண்டத் தெண்டோள்செவ் வண்ணப் பவள மாமலையே
அணியால் விளங்கும் திருஆரூர் ஆரா அமுதே அடிச்சிறியேன்
தணியா உலகச் சழக்கிடையே தளர்ந்து கிடந்து தவிக்கின்றேன்
திணியார் முருட்டுக் கடைமனத்தேன் செய்வ தொன்றும் தெரியேனே.
translit: maṇiyār kaṇṭat teṇṭōḷcev vaṇṇap pavaḷa māmalaiyē aṇiyāl viḷaṅkum tiru-ārūr ārā amutē aṭicciṟiyēṉ taṇiyā ulakac caḻakkiṭaiyē taḷarntu kiṭantu tavikkiṉṟēṉ tiṇiyār muruṭṭuk kaṭaimaṉattēṉ ceyva toṉṟum teriyēṉē.
translation: O great mountain of red coral with eight shoulders and a throat dark as a sapphire! O insatiable nectar of beautiful holy Arur! I, your lowly devotee, lie exhausted and suffering amidst the unceasing deceit of the world. With my dense, stubborn, and base mind, I do not know what to do.
commentary: Worldly life is filled with unceasing deceit that exhausts the soul. Vallalar confesses his mind feels dense and stubborn, leaving him lost. He turns to the Lord of Arur for rescue from his own confusion.

tamil: தெரியத் தெரியும் தெரிவுடையார் சிவாநு பவத்தில் சிறக்கின்றார்
பிரியப் பிரியும் பெரும்பாவி அடியேன் பிழையில் பிழைக்கின்றேன்
துரியப் பொருளே அணிஆரூர்ச் சோதி மணிநீ தூயஅருள்
புரியப் பெறுவேன் எனில்அவர்போல் யானும் சுகத்திற் பொலிவேனே.
translit: teriyat teriyum terivuṭaiyār civānu pavattil ciṟakkiṉṟār piriyap piriyum perumpāvi aṭiyēṉ piḻaiyil piḻaikkiṉṟēṉ turiyap poruḷē aṇi-ārūrc cōti maṇinī tūya-aruḷ puriyap peṟuvēṉ eṉilavarpōl yāṉum cukattiṟ polivēṉē.
translation: Those of clear understanding who know what must be known excel in the experience of Siva. I am a great sinner who breaks away through attachments, and I merely survive amidst my faults. O supreme reality of the transcendent state! O radiant gem of beautiful Arur! If I receive your pure grace, I too will shine in bliss like them.
commentary: People with spiritual clarity live in the blissful experience of Siva. Vallalar contrasts their peace with his own struggle, admitting his worldly attachments pull him away from the truth. He knows only a pure gift of grace can elevate him to that same lasting joy.

tamil: பொலிவேன் கருணை புரிந்தாயேல் போதா னந்தக் கடல்ஆடி
மலிவேன் இன்ப மயமாவேன் ஆரூர் மணிநீ வழங்காயேல்
மெலிவேன் துன்பக் கடல்மூழ்கி மேவி எடுப்பார் இல்லாமல்
நலிவேன் அந்தோ அந்தோநின் நல்ல கருணைக் கழகன்றே.
translit: polivēṉ karuṇai purintāyēl pōtā ṉantak kaṭalāṭi malivēṉ iṉpa mayamāvēṉ ārūr maṇinī vaḻaṅkāyēl melivēṉ tuṉpak kaṭalmūḻki mēvi eṭuppār illāmal nalivēṉ antō antōniṉ nalla karuṇaik kaḻakaṉṟē.
translation: If you grant your grace, I will shine. I will bathe in the ocean of blissful awareness, flourish, and become the very embodiment of joy. O gem of Arur, if you do not grant it, I will waste away, sinking into the ocean of sorrow. With no one to reach out and lift me, I will perish. Alas, alas, this does not befit the beauty of your good grace.
commentary: Divine grace makes the difference between flourishing in joy and drowning in sorrow. If the Lord grants his mercy, the soul bathes in blissful awareness. Without it, the soul sinks into suffering with no one to pull it to safety.

tamil: கருணைக் கடலே திருஆரூர்க் கடவுட் சுடரே நின்னுடைய
அருணக் கமல மலரடிக்கே அடிமை விழைந்தேன் அருளாயேல்
வருணக் கொலைமா பாதகனாம் மறையோன் தனக்கு மகிழ்ந்தன்று
தருணக் கருணை அளித்தபுகழ் என்னாம் இந்நாள் சாற்றுகவே.
translit: karuṇaik kaṭalē tiru-ārūrk kaṭavuṭ cuṭarē niṉṉuṭaiya aruṇak kamala malaraṭikkē aṭimai viḻaintēṉ aruḷāyēl varuṇak kolaimā pātakaṉām maṟaiyōṉ taṉakku makiḻntaṉṟu taruṇak karuṇai aḷittapukaḻ eṉṉām innāḷ cāṟṟukavē.
translation: Ocean of compassion, divine flame of Thiruvarur, I longed to serve your red lotus feet. If you do not grant me grace, tell me, what will happen today to the fame you gained long ago when you joyfully showed timely compassion to that Brahmin who committed the great sin of murder?
commentary: Vallalar challenges the divine, asking how God can maintain His reputation for mercy if He ignores a devoted servant. He reminds the Lord of Thiruvarur, a sacred temple town in Tamil Nadu, of an ancient story where God forgave a priest guilty of a terrible murder. If God could save such a severe wrongdoer in the past, He surely must have compassion for someone whose only fault is human weakness. This bold, intimate way of demanding grace by questioning God's consistency is a traditional feature of Tamil devotional poetry.

tamil: இந்நாள் அடியேன் பிழைத்தபிழை எண்ணி இரங்காய் எனில்அந்தோ
அந்நாள் அடிமை கொண்டனையே பிழையா தொன்றும் அறிந்திலையோ
பொன்னார் கருணைக் கடல்இன்று புதிதோ பிறர்பால் போயிற்றோ
என்நா யகனே திருஆரூர் எந்தாய் உள்ளம் இரங்கிலையே.
translit: innāḷ aṭiyēṉ piḻaittapiḻai eṇṇi iraṅkāy eṉilantō annāḷ aṭimai koṇṭaṉaiyē piḻaiyā toṉṟum aṟintilaiyō poṉṉār karuṇaik kaṭaliṉṟu putitō piṟarpāl pōyiṟṟō eṉnā yakaṉē tiru-ārūr entāy uḷḷam iraṅkilaiyē.
translation: Alas, if you do not take pity on me today as you count the faults I have committed, did you not know when you took me into your service back then that I would commit faults? Is the beautiful ocean of compassion newly formed today? Or has it flowed away to others? My Lord, my father of Thiruvarur, your heart shows no pity.
commentary: God knew of all human flaws when He first accepted Vallalar's devotion, so it makes no sense to withhold grace now because of those faults. Vallalar asks if God's ocean of compassion has dried up or been given to others. He appeals to God as a father who must naturally accept his child's imperfections. This intimacy removes any distance between the worshipper and the divine.

tamil: உள்ளக் கவலை ஒருசிறிதும் ஒருநா ளேனும் ஒழிந்திடவும்
வெள்ளக் கருணை இறையேனும் மேவி யிடவும் பெற்றறியேன்
கள்ளக் குரங்காய் உழல்கின்ற மனத்தேன் எனினும் கடையேனைத்
தள்ளத் தகுமோ திருஆரூர் எந்தாய் எந்தாய் தமியேனே.
translit: uḷḷak kavalai oruciṟitum orunā ḷēṉum oḻintiṭavum veḷḷak karuṇai iṟaiyēṉum mēvi yiṭavum peṟṟaṟiyēṉ kaḷḷak kuraṅkāy uḻalkiṉṟa maṉattēṉ eṉiṉum kaṭaiyēṉait taḷḷat takumō tiru-ārūr entāy entāy tamiyēṉē.
translation: I have never known the sorrow in my heart to cease even a little for a single day, nor have I received even a drop of your flooding compassion. Even though I have a mind that wanders like a thieving monkey, is it right to cast me away, the lowest of the low? My father of Thiruvarur, my father, I stand entirely alone.
commentary: Vallalar begs God not to abandon him despite his restless mind. Feeling alone with this inner turmoil, he argues that he is the kind of helpless person who needs divine grace the most. God, acting as a father, has a duty to comfort even the most distracted of His children.

tamil: எந்தாய் ஒருநாள் அருள்வடிவின் எளியேன் கண்டு களிப்படைய
வந்தாய் அந்தோ கடைநாயேன் மறந்து விடுத்தேன் மதிகெட்டேன்
செந்தா மரைத்தாள் இணைஅன்றே சிக்கென் றிறுகப் பிடித்தேனேல்
translit: entāy orunāḷ aruḷvaṭiviṉ eḷiyēṉ kaṇṭu kaḷippaṭaiya vantāy antō kaṭaināyēṉ maṟantu viṭuttēṉ matikeṭṭēṉ centā maraittāḷ iṇai-aṉṟē cikkeṉ ṟiṟukap piṭittēṉēl intār caṭaiyāy tiru-ārūriṟaivā tuyaraṟ ṟiruppēṉē.
translation: My father, one day you came in a form of grace so that I, a poor wretch, could see you and rejoice. Alas, I, the lowest dog, forgot it and lost my senses. If only I had tightly grasped your two red lotus feet that very day, O Lord of Thiruvarur with the moon in your matted hair, I would be entirely free from sorrow.
commentary: Vallalar regrets failing to hold onto a brief, past experience of God's direct presence. He recalls a specific moment when grace appeared and brought joy. Because he became distracted and let that connection slip away, he now suffers from spiritual sorrow. He wishes he had anchored his mind to the divine in that fleeting instant of clarity.

tamil: இருப்பு மனத்துக் கடைநாயேன் என்செய் வேன்நின் திருவருளாம்
பொருப்பில் அமர்ந்தார் அடியர்எலாம் அந்தோ உலகப் புலைஒழுக்காம்
திருப்பில் சுழன்று நான்ஒருவன் திகைக்கின் றேன்ஓர் துணைகாணேன்
விருப்பில் கருணை புரிவாயோ ஆரூர் தண்ணார் வியன்அமுதே.
translit: iruppu maṉattuk kaṭaināyēṉ eṉcey vēṉniṉ tiruvaruḷām poruppil amarntār aṭiyarelām antō ulakap pulai-oḻukkām tiruppil cuḻaṉṟu nāṉoruvaṉ tikaikkiṉ ṟēṉōr tuṇaikāṇēṉ viruppil karuṇai purivāyō ārūr taṇṇār viyaṉamutē.
translation: What shall I do, this lowest dog with a heart of iron? All your devotees have settled upon the mountain of your holy grace. Alas, I alone am bewildered as I spin in the whirlpool of base worldly conduct. I see no companion. Will you lovingly show me compassion, O cool and vast nectar of Thiruvarur?
commentary: Vallalar feels isolated in his worldly struggles while other devotees have achieved spiritual peace. He sees them resting on the mountain of divine grace, while he feels caught in a dizzying whirlpool of ordinary life without a companion to guide him. He asks the divine to act as a cooling nectar to soften his hardened heart.

note: Editor's note: sung at Chidambaram, which Saiva tradition calls simply “the Temple” (kōyil, கோயில்).
tamil: திருவார் பொன்னம் பலநடுவே தெள்ளார் அமுதத் திரள்அனைய
உருவார் அறிவா னந்தநடம் உடையார் அடியார்க் குவகைநிலை
தருவார் அவர்தம் திருமுகத்தே ததும்பும் இளவெண் ணகைகண்டேன்
இருவா தனைஅற் றந்தோநான் இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: tiruvār poṉṉam palanaṭuvē teḷḷār amutat tiraḷaṉaiya uruvār aṟivā ṉantanaṭam uṭaiyār aṭiyārk kuvakainilai taruvār avartam tirumukattē tatumpum iḷaveṇ ṇakaikaṇṭēṉ iruvā taṉai-aṟ ṟantōnāṉ iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: In the center of the holy Golden Hall, He whose form is like a mass of clear nectar performs the dance of conscious bliss. He grants the state of joy to His devotees. I saw the gentle white smile overflowing on His holy face. Freed from the two afflictions, alas, will I see it once again?
commentary: A vision of the divine smile frees the soul from its burdens. The two afflictions are the binding cycles of good and bad karma that keep a person tied to worldly birth. Having tasted this state of conscious bliss, Vallalar aches to experience it again.

tamil: பொன்நா யகனும் புரந்தரனும் பூவாழ் பவனும் புகழ்ந்தேத்த
மின்னார் பொன்னம் பலநடுவே விளங்கும் கருணை விழிவழங்கும்
அன்னார் அறிவா னந்தநடம் ஆடும் கழல்கண் டகங்குளிர்ந்தேன்
என்நா யகனார் அவர்கழலை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: poṉnā yakaṉum purantaraṉum pūvāḻ pavaṉum pukaḻntētta miṉṉār poṉṉam palanaṭuvē viḷaṅkum karuṇai viḻivaḻaṅkum aṉṉār aṟivā ṉantanaṭam āṭum kaḻalkaṇ ṭakaṅkuḷirntēṉ eṉnā yakaṉār avarkaḻalai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: As Vishnu, Indra, and Brahma praise Him, He bestows His shining gaze of grace in the center of the radiant Golden Hall. Seeing the ankleted feet that dance the dance of conscious bliss, my heart cooled with joy. Will I see those ankleted feet of my Lord once again?
commentary: The supreme divine light commands the reverence of gods like Vishnu, Indra, and Brahma. The Lord's dancing feet are a symbol of refuge and liberating grace. Beholding this dance brings a spiritual relief that cools a heart weary from worldly struggles.

tamil: தாயிற் பெரிய கருணையினார் தலைமா லையினார் தாழ்சடையார்
வாயிற் கினிய புகழுடைய வள்ளல் அவர்தந் திருஅழகைக்
கோயிற் கருகே சென்றுமனம் குளிரக் கண்டேன் பிரிவுற்றேன்
ஈயில் சிறியேன் அவர் அழகை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: tāyiṟ periya karuṇaiyiṉār talaimā laiyiṉār tāḻcaṭaiyār vāyiṟ kiṉiya pukaḻuṭaiya vaḷḷal avartan tiru-aḻakaik kōyiṟ karukē ceṉṟumaṉam kuḷirak kaṇṭēṉ pirivuṟṟēṉ īyil ciṟiyēṉ avar aḻakai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: He possesses compassion greater than a mother's. He wears a garland of skulls and long matted hair. He is the supreme benefactor whose praise is sweet to speak. Going near the temple, I saw His holy beauty and my heart cooled with joy. I am smaller than a fly and I have parted from Him. Will I see His beauty once again?
commentary: The divine appears wearing the ascetic features of Siva: a skull garland and long matted hair. Beneath this fierce imagery lies a compassion that exceeds a mother's love. Struck by his own smallness, Vallalar expresses the sharp pain of separation from a benefactor of such boundless grace.

tamil: புன்கண் அகற்றும் மெய்யடியார் போற்றும் பொன்னம் பலநடுவே
வன்கண் அறியார் திருநடஞ்செய் வரதர் அமுதத் திருமுகத்தை
முன்கண் உலகில் சிறியேன்செய் முழுமா தவத்தால் கண்டேன்நான்
என்கண் அனையார் அவர்முகத்தை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: puṉkaṇ akaṟṟum meyyaṭiyār pōṟṟum poṉṉam palanaṭuvē vaṉkaṇ aṟiyār tirunaṭañcey varatar amutat tirumukattai muṉkaṇ ulakil ciṟiyēṉcey muḻumā tavattāl kaṇṭēṉnāṉ eṉkaṇ aṉaiyār avarmukattai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: In the center of the Golden Hall praised by true devotees whose sorrows are dispelled, the boon-granting Lord who knows no harshness performs His holy dance. Through the great penance I, a lowly one, performed earlier in the world, I saw His nectar-like holy face. He is like my very eye. Will I see His face once again?
commentary: The divine nature is pure gentleness, devoid of any harshness. This past vision of grace is the fruit of spiritual penance performed long ago. The Lord has become as essential to Vallalar as his own eyesight, making the current absence feel painful.

tamil: அன்புற் றடியார் தொழுதேத்த அணியார் மணிப்பொன் அம்பலத்தே
வன்புற் றழியாப் பெருங்கருணை மலையார் தலையார் மாலையினார்
மன்புற் றரவார் கச்சிடையின் வயங்க நடஞ்செய் வதுகண்டேன்
இன்புற் றடியேன் அவர்நடத்தை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: aṉpuṟ ṟaṭiyār toḻutētta aṇiyār maṇippoṉ ampalattē vaṉpuṟ ṟaḻiyāp peruṅkaruṇai malaiyār talaiyār mālaiyiṉār maṉpuṟ ṟaravār kacciṭaiyiṉ vayaṅka naṭañcey vatukaṇṭēṉ iṉpuṟ ṟaṭiyēṉ avarnaṭattai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: As devotees worship and praise Him with love in the beautiful, jeweled Golden Hall, He who is a mountain of imperishable great grace wearing a garland of skulls dances brightly with a snake wrapped firmly around His waist. I saw this and rejoiced. Will I, a humble devotee, see His dance once again?
commentary: Wild imagery of a coiled snake and skulls contrasts with the sheltering presence of an indestructible mountain of grace. True worship takes place among a community of devotees offering their love in the Golden Hall. Having shared this joy, Vallalar pleads to witness it one more time.

tamil: இம்மா நிலத்தில் சிவபதமீ தென்னும் பொன்னம் பலநடுவே
அம்மால் அறியா அடிகள்அடி அசைய நடஞ்செய் வதுகண்டேன்
எம்மால் அறியப் படுவதல என்என் றுரைப்பேன் ஏழையன்யான்
எம்மான் அவர்தந் திருநடத்தை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: immā nilattil civapatamī teṉṉum poṉṉam palanaṭuvē ammāl aṟiyā aṭikaḷaṭi acaiya naṭañcey vatukaṇṭēṉ emmāl aṟiyap paṭuvatala eṉeṉ ṟuraippēṉ ēḻaiyaṉyāṉ emmāṉ avartan tirunaṭattai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: In the center of the Golden Hall, celebrated as the realm of Siva on this vast earth, I saw the Lord perform his dance, his feet moving, feet unknown even to Vishnu. It cannot be known by us. What can I, a poor wretch, say? Will I see my Lord's sacred dance once again?
commentary: Vallalar is overwhelmed by a glimpse of the divine dance in the Golden Hall. Even great gods like Vishnu cannot comprehend this sacred movement. Feeling small and incapable of capturing the experience in words, he longs to witness that grace one more time.

tamil: சிறியேன் தவமோ எனைஈன்றாள் செய்த தவமோ யான்அறியேன்
மறியேர் கரத்தார் அம்பலத்தே வாழும் சிவனார் தமைக்கண்டேன்
பிறியேன் எனினும் பிரிந்தேன்நான் பேயேன் அந்தப் பிரிவினைக்கீழ்
எறியேன் அந்தோ அவர்தம்மை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: ciṟiyēṉ tavamō eṉai-īṉṟāḷ ceyta tavamō yāṉaṟiyēṉ maṟiyēr karattār ampalattē vāḻum civaṉār tamaikkaṇṭēṉ piṟiyēṉ eṉiṉum pirintēṉnāṉ pēyēṉ antap piriviṉaikkīḻ eṟiyēṉ antō avartammai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: Was it my own small penance or the penance of the mother who bore me? I do not know. I saw Lord Siva who dwells in the Hall, holding a young deer in his hand. Though I resolved never to part, I parted from him. I am a wretched fool. I did not cast down that separation. Alas, will I see him once again?
commentary: Vallalar wonders if he earned this rare vision through his own spiritual efforts or his mother's quiet merit. He briefly beheld the Lord, but despite a resolve to stay united with the divine, he allowed himself to drift away. Feeling foolish and broken by the separation, he cries out to return to that presence.

tamil: அருளே வடிவாய் அம்பலத்தே ஆடும் பெருமான் அடிகள்தமைத்
தெருளே வடிவாம் அடியவர்போல் சிறியேன் கண்டேன் சீர்உற்றேன்
மருளே வடிவேன் ஆதலினால் மறந்தே பிரிந்தே மதிகெட்டேன்
இருளேர் மனத்தேன் அவர்தமைநான் இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: aruḷē vaṭivāy ampalattē āṭum perumāṉ aṭikaḷtamait teruḷē vaṭivām aṭiyavarpōl ciṟiyēṉ kaṇṭēṉ cīruṟṟēṉ maruḷē vaṭivēṉ ātaliṉāl maṟantē pirintē matikeṭṭēṉ iruḷēr maṉattēṉ avartamaināṉ iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: I, a lowly one, saw the feet of the great Lord who dances in the Hall as the very form of grace, just as devotees of pure clarity see him, and I attained excellence. But since I am the very form of delusion, I forgot him, parted from him, and lost my mind. My heart is filled with darkness. Will I see him once again?
commentary: For a brief moment, Vallalar experienced the divine as the clearest saints do, seeing the Lord's dancing feet as pure grace. However, his own mind quickly clouded over with worldly confusion and delusion. Having forgotten that perfect clarity, he feels plunged back into inner darkness. He begs to return to the light of that initial vision.

tamil: அன்னோ திருஅம் பலத்தேஎம் ஐயர் உருக்கண் டேன்அதுதான்
பொன்னோ பவளப் பொருப்பதுவோ புதுமா ணிக்க மணித்திரளோ
மின்னோ விளக்கோ விரிசுடரோ மேலை ஒளியோ என் உரைப்பேன்
என்னோ அவர்தந் திருஉருவை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: aṉṉō tiru-am palattē-em aiyar urukkaṇ ṭēṉatutāṉ poṉṉō pavaḷap poruppatuvō putumā ṇikka maṇittiraḷō miṉṉō viḷakkō viricuṭarō mēlai oḷiyō eṉ uraippēṉ eṉṉō avartan tiru-uruvai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: Ah, I saw our Lord's form in the sacred Hall. Is it gold, or a mountain of coral, or a cluster of fresh rubies? Is it lightning, or a lamp, or a spreading flame, or the supreme light? What can I say? What is this? Will I see his sacred form once again?
commentary: The divine form is an unearthly radiance that leaves Vallalar struggling for words. He compares the vision to the brightest and most precious things in the physical world: gold, red coral, fresh rubies, lightning, and a spreading flame. Worldly language fails to capture this supreme light. He is left in awe, wishing to see it again.

tamil: பொன்என் றுரைக்கும் அம்பலத்தே புனித னார்தம் அழகியலை
உன்என் றுரைப்பேன் என்னேஎன் உள்ளம் சிறிதும் உணர்ந்ததிலை
மின்என் றுரைக்கும் படிமூன்று விளக்கும் மழுங்கும் எனில்அடியேன்
என்என் றுரைப்பேன் அவர்அழகை இன்னும் ஒருகால் காண்பேனோ.
translit: poṉeṉ ṟuraikkum ampalattē puṉita ṉārtam aḻakiyalai uṉeṉ ṟuraippēṉ eṉṉē-eṉ uḷḷam ciṟitum uṇarntatilai miṉeṉ ṟuraikkum paṭimūṉṟu viḷakkum maḻuṅkum eṉilaṭiyēṉ eṉeṉ ṟuraippēṉ avaraḻakai iṉṉum orukāl kāṇpēṉō.
translation: How can I describe the beauty of the pure Lord in the Golden Hall? What is this? My heart has not comprehended it in the slightest. If the three luminaries that shine like lightning grow dim before him, what can this humble devotee say? Will I see his beauty once again?
commentary: The beauty of the divine is beyond human understanding. Vallalar admits his mind cannot grasp even a fraction of what he saw in the Golden Hall. Before this pure presence, even the three great luminaries of the world (the sun, the moon, and fire) appear dim and faded. Humbled by this overpowering radiance, he prays for a second glimpse.

tamil: உலகம் பரவும் பொருளேஎன் உறவே என்றன் உயிர்க்குயிரே
இலகம் பரத்தே பரம்பரமாய் இன்ப நடஞ்செய் எம்இறையே
கலகம் பரவும் மனத்தேனைக் கைவிட் டிடநீ கருதுதியோ
திலகம் பரவும் நுதற்பாகன் என்ப தருளின் திறத்தன்றே.
translit: ulakam paravum poruḷē-eṉ uṟavē eṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirē ilakam parattē paramparamāy iṉpa naṭañcey emiṟaiyē kalakam paravum maṉattēṉaik kaiviṭ ṭiṭanī karututiyō tilakam paravum nutaṟpākaṉ eṉpa taruḷiṉ tiṟattaṉṟē.
translation: O Reality pervading the world. O my relation. O life of my life. O our Lord who performs the blissful dance as the supreme of the supreme in the shining supreme space. Do you intend to abandon me, a person whose mind is filled with turmoil? Such abandonment is not the nature of your grace, you who share half your form with the goddess wearing a tilaka on her forehead.
commentary: The Divine is both the supreme reality dancing in space and the soul's closest kin. Abandoning a struggling soul whose mind is in turmoil contradicts the very nature of divine grace.

tamil: அன்றோர் பொருளாய் அடியேனை ஆட்கொண் டருளி அறிவளித்தாய்
இன்றோ சிறியேன் பிழைகருதி இரங்கா தகற்ற எண்ணுதியோ
குன்றோர் அனைய குறைசெயினும் கொண்டு குலம்பே சுதல்எந்தாய்
நன்றோ கருணைப் பெருங்கடலே ஆளாய் இந்த நாயினையே.
translit: aṉṟōr poruḷāy aṭiyēṉai āṭkoṇ ṭaruḷi aṟivaḷittāy iṉṟō ciṟiyēṉ piḻaikaruti iraṅkā takaṟṟa eṇṇutiyō kuṉṟōr aṉaiya kuṟaiceyiṉum koṇṭu kulampē cutalentāy naṉṟō karuṇaip peruṅkaṭalē āḷāy inta nāyiṉaiyē.
translation: On that day, you considered me a worthy entity, took me into your service, and granted me knowledge. Today, considering the faults of this lowly one, do you intend to cast me away without pity? O my Father, even if one commits faults as huge as a mountain, is it proper to hold onto them and criticize their lineage? O great ocean of compassion, rule over this dog.
commentary: God originally chose this soul and granted it knowledge freely. A loving father does not obsess over a child's mountain-sized mistakes or mock their origins. The ocean of divine compassion must not cast the soul away for its human flaws.

tamil: நாய்க்குங் கடையேன் பிழைஅனைத்தும் நாடில் தவத்தால் நல்கியநல்
தாய்க்கும் கோபம் உறும்என்னில் யாரே யென்பால் சலியாதார்
வாய்க்கும் கருணைக் கடல்உடையாய் உன்பால் அடுத்தேன் வலிந்தெளிய
பேய்க்கும் தயவு புரிகின்றோய் ஆள வேண்டும் பேதையையே.
translit: nāykkuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ piḻai-aṉaittum nāṭil tavattāl nalkiyanal tāykkum kōpam uṟumeṉṉil yārē yeṉpāl caliyātār vāykkum karuṇaik kaṭaluṭaiyāy uṉpāl aṭuttēṉ valinteḷiya pēykkum tayavu purikiṉṟōy āḷa vēṇṭum pētaiyaiyē.
translation: I am lower than a dog. If one examines all my faults, even the good mother who bore me through arduous penance will grow angry. If so, who will not be disgusted with me? O Lord who possesses an ocean of abundant compassion, I have approached you. You willingly show mercy even to a lowly ghost. You must rule over this ignorant one.
commentary: Human patience has limits, and even a devoted mother will eventually grow angry at constant faults. Divine patience is different. Since God willingly shows mercy to the lowliest spirits, that same vast compassion must be given to the suffering soul.

tamil: பேதைப் பருவத் தெனைவலியப் பிடித்தாட் கொண்ட பெருமானே
போதைக் கழிப்பான் வீண்புரியும் புலையேன் பிழையைப் பொறுக்கிலையேல்
வாதைப் படும்என் உயிரைஉன்றன் மலர்த்தாள் முன்னர் மடிவித்தே
ஓதைக் கடல்சூழ் உலகத்தே பழிசூழ் விப்பேன் உரைத்தேனே.
translit: pētaip paruvat teṉaivaliyap piṭittāṭ koṇṭa perumāṉē pōtaik kaḻippāṉ vīṇpuriyum pulaiyēṉ piḻaiyaip poṟukkilaiyēl vātaip paṭumeṉ uyirai-uṉṟaṉ malarttāḷ muṉṉar maṭivittē ōtaik kaṭalcūḻ ulakattē paḻicūḻ vippēṉ uraittēṉē.
translation: O Lord who forcefully grasped me and took me into your service during my childhood years of ignorance. I am a base person who commits useless acts merely to pass the time. If you do not bear with my faults, I will end my suffering life right before your flower-like feet. I will bring blame upon you in this world surrounded by the roaring ocean. I have declared this.
commentary: Devotion here takes the form of a passionate threat. If God does not forgive Vallalar's wasted time, he promises to end his life right at the Lord's feet. This would make the entire world blame the Divine for failing to save a trusting devotee.

tamil: உரைத்தார் சிலர்சின் னாள்கழிய உறுவேம் என்ன உரைத்தவரே
நரைத்தார் இறந்தார் அவர்தம்மை நான்கண் டிருந்தும் நாணாமே
விரைத்தாள் மலரைப் பெறலாம்என் றெண்ணி வீணே இளைக்கின்றேன்
திரைத்தாழ் கடலிற் பெரும்பிழையே செய்தேன் என்ன செய்வேனே.
translit: uraittār cilarciṉ ṉāḷkaḻiya uṟuvēm eṉṉa uraittavarē naraittār iṟantār avartammai nāṉkaṇ ṭiruntum nāṇāmē viraittāḷ malaraip peṟalāmeṉ ṟeṇṇi vīṇē iḷaikkiṉṟēṉ tiraittāḻ kaṭaliṟ perumpiḻaiyē ceytēṉ eṉṉa ceyvēṉē.
translation: Some people said they would attain the goal after a few days passed. Those very people grew gray and died. Even though I have seen them, I feel no shame. Thinking I can attain your fragrant flower-like feet later, I grow weary in vain. I have committed faults vaster than the ocean with its crashing waves. What shall I do?
commentary: Delaying the spiritual life is a fatal error. People often promise to seek grace later, only to grow old and die without taking action. Assuming there is always more time to reach God is a fault vaster than the ocean.

tamil: செய்வேன் தீமை நலம்ஒன்றும் தெரியேன் தெரிந்து தெளிந்தோரை
வைவேன் அன்றி வாழ்த்தேன்என் வண்ணம் இந்த வண்ணம்எனில்
உய்வேன் என்ப தெவ்வாறென் உடையாய் உய்வேன் உய்வித்தால்
நைவேன் அலதிங் கென்செய்வேன் அந்தோ எண்ணி நலிவேனே.
