translit: ceyvēṉ tīmai nalamoṉṟum teriyēṉ terintu teḷintōrai vaivēṉ aṉṟi vāḻttēṉeṉ vaṇṇam inta vaṇṇameṉil uyvēṉ eṉpa tevvāṟeṉ uṭaiyāy uyvēṉ uyvittāl naivēṉ alatiṅ keṉceyvēṉ antō eṇṇi nalivēṉē.
translation: I commit evil. I know no good at all. I insult those who have attained clear spiritual vision, instead of praising them. If my nature is like this, my Lord, how can I ever find redemption? I will be saved only if you save me. Otherwise, I will simply languish. What else can I do here? Alas, I suffer just thinking about this.
commentary: Vallalar confesses to a life of wrongdoing and a habit of mocking those who have found spiritual clarity. Bound by these flaws, he realises that human effort alone cannot change his nature. His only hope for redemption is direct rescue by the divine. True spiritual progress begins with an admission of one's own shortcomings and a surrender to grace.

tamil: எண்ணி நலிவேன் நின்பாதம் எந்நாள் அடைவோம் எனஎன்பால்
நண்ணி நலிவைத் தவிராயேல் என்செய் திடுவேன் நாயகனே
கண்ணி நலியப் படும்பறவைக் கால்போல் மனக்கால் கட்டுண்ணப்
பண்ணி நலஞ்சேர் திருக்கூட்டம் புகுத எனினும் பரிந்தருளே.
translit: eṇṇi nalivēṉ niṉpātam ennāḷ aṭaivōm eṉa-eṉpāl naṇṇi nalivait tavirāyēl eṉcey tiṭuvēṉ nāyakaṉē kaṇṇi naliyap paṭumpaṟavaik kālpōl maṉakkāl kaṭṭuṇṇap paṇṇi nalañcēr tirukkūṭṭam pukuta eṉiṉum parintaruḷē.
translation: I suffer, constantly wondering when I will reach your feet. If you do not draw near and dispel my affliction, what will I do, my Master? Like the leg of a bird trapped and struggling in a snare, my wandering mind must be tightly bound. Bestow your grace with compassion, so that I may enter your auspicious holy gathering.
commentary: The longing to reach God brings its own suffering when the goal feels far away. Vallalar compares his restless mind to a bird caught in a snare. He asks the divine to step in and bind this wandering attention securely. Only when the mind is stilled by grace can a person join the gathering of the devout.

tamil: பரியும் மனத்தால் கருணைநடம் பரவுந் தொண்டர் பதப்பணியே
புரியும் இனத்தா ரொடுங்கூடிப் புனித னாக வேண்டும்எனத்
திரியும் அடிமைச் சிறியேனுக் கிரங்கா திருந்தால் சின்னாட்பின்
எரியுங் கொடுவாய் நரகத்துக் கென்செய் வேன்என் செய்வேனே.
translit: pariyum maṉattāl karuṇainaṭam paravun toṇṭar patappaṇiyē puriyum iṉattā roṭuṅkūṭip puṉita ṉāka vēṇṭumeṉat tiriyum aṭimaic ciṟiyēṉuk kiraṅkā tiruntāl ciṉṉāṭpiṉ eriyuṅ koṭuvāy narakattuk keṉcey vēṉeṉ ceyvēṉē.
translation: With a loving heart, I long to join the company of those who serve the feet of the devotees praising your dance of grace. I wander around as a lowly servant, wishing to become pure. If you do not show me mercy, what will I do when I face the fiercely burning hell in a few days? What will I do?
commentary: True devotion often takes the form of wanting to serve those who are already devoted. Vallalar longs for the purity that comes from keeping company with those who praise God's compassionate dance. Without divine mercy and the shelter of good company, he fears the harsh consequences of his unresolved karma. Community and humble service are essential protections against spiritual ruin.

tamil: என்செய் திடுவேன் புலைநாயேன் இயற்றும் பிழைகள் எல்லாம்நின்
பொன்செய் மலர்த்தாள் துணைஅந்தோ பொறுத்துக் கருணை புரியாதேல்
புன்செய் விளவிப் பயனிலியாய்ப் புறத்திற் கிடத்தி எனஅடியார்
வன்செய் உரையில் சிரிப்பார்மற் றதுகண் டெங்ஙன் வாழ்வேனே.
translit: eṉcey tiṭuvēṉ pulaināyēṉ iyaṟṟum piḻaikaḷ ellāmniṉ poṉcey malarttāḷ tuṇai-antō poṟuttuk karuṇai puriyātēl puṉcey viḷavip payaṉiliyāyp puṟattiṟ kiṭatti eṉa-aṭiyār vaṉcey uraiyil cirippārmaṟ ṟatukaṇ ṭeṅṅaṉ vāḻvēṉē.
translation: What will I do? I am a lowly dog. If your golden flower-like feet do not pardon all my faults and bestow mercy, your devotees will mock me with harsh words. They will say to cast me out as useless, like an unripe wood-apple from arid land. Seeing their ridicule, how will I endure?
commentary: There is a fear of being found unworthy by those who have already walked the spiritual path. Vallalar worries that without God's direct pardon, the devotees will see right through him and cast him aside. He compares himself to an unripe, useless fruit grown on barren land. Divine forgiveness is what gives a person value and a rightful place among the faithful.

tamil: வாழா மனத்தின் வழிசென்று வாளா நாளைக் கழிக்கின்ற
பாழாம் உலகச் சிறுநடையில் பாவி யேனைப் பதிவித்தாய்
ஊழாம் எனில்எம் பெருமானே இன்னும் வினையால் ஒதிஅனையேன்
ஏழாம் நரகுக் காளாவேன் அல்லால் புகல்என் எளியேற்கே.
translit: vāḻā maṉattiṉ vaḻiceṉṟu vāḷā nāḷaik kaḻikkiṉṟa pāḻām ulakac ciṟunaṭaiyil pāvi yēṉaip pativittāy ūḻām eṉilem perumāṉē iṉṉum viṉaiyāl oti-aṉaiyēṉ ēḻām narakuk kāḷāvēṉ allāl pukaleṉ eḷiyēṟkē.
translation: I follow the path of an unredeemed mind and waste my days in vain. You have embedded me, a sinner, in the petty and ruinous ways of this world. If this is my fate, my Lord, I will be driven further by my karma and subjected to the seventh hell. What other refuge exists for this poor soul?
commentary: Worldly distractions can consume a person's life and leave their mind unredeemed. Vallalar feels trapped in petty, ruinous habits, fearing his past actions are dragging him toward despair. He questions why the divine has placed him in such a difficult world, yet knows God remains his only refuge.

tamil: எளியேன் கருணைத் திருநடஞ்செய் இணைத்தாள் மலர்கண் டிதயமெலாம்
களியேன் கருங்கற் பாறைஎனக் கிடக்கின் றேன்இக் கடையேனை
அளியே பெருக ஆளுதியோ ஆள்கி லாயோ யாதொன்றும்
தெளியேன் அந்தோ அந்தோஎன் செய்வேன் விலங்கிற் சிறியேனே.
translit: eḷiyēṉ karuṇait tirunaṭañcey iṇaittāḷ malarkaṇ ṭitayamelām kaḷiyēṉ karuṅkaṟ pāṟai-eṉak kiṭakkiṉ ṟēṉik kaṭaiyēṉai aḷiyē peruka āḷutiyō āḷki lāyō yātoṉṟum teḷiyēṉ antō antō-eṉ ceyvēṉ vilaṅkiṟ ciṟiyēṉē.
translation: I am lowly. Even after seeing your paired flower-feet perform the sacred dance of grace, my heart does not rejoice. I lie here like a black rock. Will you accept this lowest of the low with abounding love, or will you refuse to rule me? I have no clarity on anything at all. Alas, alas, what shall I do? I am lower than an animal.
commentary: Vallalar laments his spiritual numbness. Even when witnessing the divine dance of grace, his heart remains as cold and heavy as a black rock. He feels dependent on God's mercy, uncertain if he will be accepted or abandoned to his own lifelessness.

tamil: சிறியேன் பிழையைத் திருவுளத்தே தேர்ந்திங் கென்னைச் சீறுதியோ
எறியேம் எனக்கொண் டிரங்குதியோ இவ்வா றவ்வா றெனஒன்றும்
அறியேன் அவலக் கடல்அழுந்தி அந்தோ அழுங்கி அயர்கின்றேன்
பிறியேன் என்னைப் பிரிக்கினும்பின் துணையும் காணேன் பெருமானே.
translit: ciṟiyēṉ piḻaiyait tiruvuḷattē tērntiṅ keṉṉaic cīṟutiyō eṟiyēm eṉakkoṇ ṭiraṅkutiyō ivvā ṟavvā ṟeṉa-oṉṟum aṟiyēṉ avalak kaṭalaḻunti antō aḻuṅki ayarkiṉṟēṉ piṟiyēṉ eṉṉaip pirikkiṉumpiṉ tuṇaiyum kāṇēṉ perumāṉē.
translation: Will you examine my faults in your divine mind and direct your anger at me? Or will you take pity and declare you will never cast me away? I do not know if it will be this way or that. Sinking in the sea of sorrow, alas, I suffer and grow faint. I will never separate from you. Even if you push me away, I will find no other companion, O Lord.
commentary: Fear of rejection wrestles with surrender. Vallalar does not know if God will punish his flaws or show pity, yet he declares he has no other refuge. Even if pushed away, he cannot leave.

tamil: காணேன் நினது திருவருளைக் கண்டார் தமது கழல்தலைமேல்
பூணேன் உலகச் சிறுநடையில் போந்து பொய்யே புகன்றந்தோ
வீணே சுழன்று மெலிகின்றேன் என்னே இன்னல் மிகச்சுமக்கும்
தூணே எனஇங் கெனைவிதித்தாய் எந்தாய் யாது சூழ்வேனே.
translit: kāṇēṉ niṉatu tiruvaruḷaik kaṇṭār tamatu kaḻaltalaimēl pūṇēṉ ulakac ciṟunaṭaiyil pōntu poyyē pukaṉṟantō vīṇē cuḻaṉṟu melikiṉṟēṉ eṉṉē iṉṉal mikaccumakkum tūṇē eṉa-iṅ keṉaivitittāy entāy yātu cūḻvēṉē.
translation: I do not see your sacred grace. I do not wear upon my head the feet of those who have seen it. Entering the petty paths of the world and speaking only lies, alas, I wander in vain and waste away. What is this? You have ordained me to stand here like a pillar bearing immense sorrow. My father, what am I to do?
commentary: A life spent chasing worldly things leaves the soul exhausted and empty. Having neither seen divine grace nor served the saints who have, Vallalar feels stuck in place. He compares himself to a stone pillar, built only to bear an immense weight of sorrow.

tamil: சூழ்வேன் நினது கருணைநடம் சூழும் பெரியார் தமைச்சூழ்ந்து
வாழ்வேன் எளியேன் குறிப்பிந்த வண்ணம் எனது மனக்குரங்கோ
தாழ்வேன் நினையும் தாழ்விப்பேன் அவலக் கடலில் சலியாமே
வீழ்வேன் என்றால் எம்பெருமான் இதற்கென் செய்கேன் வினையேனே.
translit: cūḻvēṉ niṉatu karuṇainaṭam cūḻum periyār tamaiccūḻntu vāḻvēṉ eḷiyēṉ kuṟippinta vaṇṇam eṉatu maṉakkuraṅkō tāḻvēṉ niṉaiyum tāḻvippēṉ avalak kaṭalil caliyāmē vīḻvēṉ eṉṟāl emperumāṉ itaṟkeṉ ceykēṉ viṉaiyēṉē.
translation: I intend to gather around your dance of grace and live among the great ones who gather there. Such is the wish of this lowly one. But my monkey mind declares, "I will sink, and I will drag you down too. I will plunge unhesitatingly into the sea of sorrow." My Lord, if it acts this way, what can I do, burdened as I am by my karma?
commentary: The soul's intentions are undermined by the restless mind. Vallalar wants to join the saints in the presence of grace, but his mind acts like a wild monkey threatening to drag him down into suffering. Burdened by his karma (the momentum of past actions), he cries out to God for help against his own destructive thoughts.

tamil: வினையே பெருக்கிக் கடைநாயேன் விடயச் செருக்கால் மிகநீண்ட
பனையே எனநின் றுலர்கின்றேன் பாவி யேனுக் கருளுதியோ
நினையே நினையாப் பிழைகருதி நெகிழ விடவே நினைதியோ
அனையே அனையாய் திருக்குறிப்பை அறியேன் ஈதென் றடியேனே.
translit: viṉaiyē perukkik kaṭaināyēṉ viṭayac cerukkāl mikanīṇṭa paṉaiyē eṉaniṉ ṟularkiṉṟēṉ pāvi yēṉuk karuḷutiyō niṉaiyē niṉaiyāp piḻaikaruti nekiḻa viṭavē niṉaitiyō aṉaiyē aṉaiyāy tirukkuṟippai aṟiyēṉ īteṉ ṟaṭiyēṉē.
translation: Multiplying my karma, I, a lowly dog, stand parched like a very tall palmyra tree due to my infatuation with worldly pleasures. Will you grant grace to this sinner? Or, considering my fault of failing to think of you, do you intend to let me slip away? O Lord who is like a mother! Your servant does not know the nature of your divine will.
commentary: Worldly obsession leaves a person spiritually hollow. Vallalar compares himself to a tall palmyra tree standing parched in the sun. He begs the Lord to act as a mother and grant him grace, fearing his habit of forgetting the divine will cause him to be cast aside.

tamil: அடியேன் முடுகிச் செயும்பிழைகள் அனந்தம் அவற்றை அந்தோஇக்
செடியேன் மனமோ வினையோநின் செயலோ செய்கை தெரியேன்வெண்
பொடியே திகழும் வடிவுடையாய் யாது புரிவேன் புலையேனே.
translit: aṭiyēṉ muṭukic ceyumpiḻaikaḷ aṉantam avaṟṟai antō-ik koṭiyēṉ niṉakkuntoṟumuḷḷam kumaintu naṭuṅkik kulaikiṉṟēṉ ceṭiyēṉ maṉamō viṉaiyōniṉ ceyalō ceykai teriyēṉveṇ poṭiyē tikaḻum vaṭivuṭaiyāy yātu purivēṉ pulaiyēṉē.
translation: The mistakes I commit in haste are endless. Alas, whenever this cruel person thinks of them, my heart breaks, trembles, and falls apart. Is it the mind of this sinful one, or karma, or your doing? I do not understand the cause. O One whose form shines with white ash! What will I do, a base wretch?
commentary: Vallalar looks at his endless, hasty mistakes and feels his heart break with regret. He asks a timeless question: are our failings the result of our own mind, the weight of our karma, or the will of God? Faced with his flaws, he asks the divine what a person like him is supposed to do.

tamil: புலையே புரியும் மனம்போன போக்கே அல்லால் புண்ணியநல்
நிலையே அறியேன் சிறியேனுக் கருளல் அழகோ நிறைந்தகுண
மலையே மணியே மருந்தேஎன் வாழ்வே எல்லாம் வல்லோனே
கலையே கருதும் கழலுடையாய் அருளா மையும்நின் கடன்அன்றே.
translit: pulaiyē puriyum maṉampōṉa pōkkē allāl puṇṇiyanal nilaiyē aṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṉuk karuḷal aḻakō niṟaintakuṇa malaiyē maṇiyē maruntē-eṉ vāḻvē ellām vallōṉē kalaiyē karutum kaḻaluṭaiyāy aruḷā maiyumniṉ kaṭaṉaṉṟē.
translation: I only follow the wandering path of a mind that commits base acts, and I do not know the good state of merit. Is it fitting to bestow grace upon this lowly one? O mountain of perfect qualities! O gem! O medicine! O my life! O omnipotent One! O Lord whose feet are revered by the scriptures! Yet, withholding your grace is not your duty.
commentary: Vallalar admits he follows wherever his wandering mind leads him, ignorant of goodness or spiritual merit. He wonders if it is even fitting for the divine to bless someone so lowly. He praises God as a perfect mountain, a precious gem, and the medicine for his life. Yet he concludes with confidence that withholding grace is not in God's nature.

tamil: கடந்தாழ் கயம்போல் செருக்கிமயற் கடலில் அழுத்திக் கடுவினையேன்
மடந்தாழ் மனத்தோ டுலைகின்றேன் கரைகண் டேறும் வகைஅறியேன்
தொடர்ந்தார் எடுப்பார் எனையெடுக்கும் துணைநின் மலர்த்தாள் துணைகண்டாய்
அடர்ந்தார் தமக்கும் அருள்கின்றோய் ஆணை ஆணை அடியேனே.
translit: kaṭantāḻ kayampōl cerukkimayaṟ kaṭalil aḻuttik kaṭuviṉaiyēṉ maṭantāḻ maṉattō ṭulaikiṉṟēṉ karaikaṇ ṭēṟum vakai-aṟiyēṉ toṭarntār eṭuppār eṉaiyeṭukkum tuṇainiṉ malarttāḷ tuṇaikaṇṭāy aṭarntār tamakkum aruḷkiṉṟōy āṇai āṇai aṭiyēṉē.
translation: Swelling with pride like a rutting elephant, I press myself into the ocean of delusion. Burdened by harsh karma, I suffer with an ignorant mind. I do not know how to find the shore and climb out. Those who hold fast to you will be rescued. The only support to lift me is the support of your lotus feet. O One who grants grace even to fierce enemies! This is my solemn vow, a vow made by your servant.
commentary: Pride can trap a person like a wild elephant sinking into an ocean of delusion. Burdened by karma and an ignorant mind, Vallalar cannot find the shore on his own. He declares that only the support of the divine can pull him out. He rests his hope on the fact that God grants grace even to fierce enemies, let alone a struggling servant.

tamil: அடியார் இன்பம் அடைகின்றார் அடியேன் ஒருவன் அயர்கின்றேன்
படியார் பலரும் பலபேசிச் சிரியா நின்றார் பரந்திரவும்
விடியா நின்ற தென்புரிவேன் இன்னுங் கருணை விளைத்திலையே
கொடியார் பிழையும் குணமாகக் கொண்டு மகிழும் குணக்குன்றே.
translit: aṭiyār iṉpam aṭaikiṉṟār aṭiyēṉ oruvaṉ ayarkiṉṟēṉ paṭiyār palarum palapēcic ciriyā niṉṟār parantiravum viṭiyā niṉṟa teṉpurivēṉ iṉṉuṅ karuṇai viḷaittilaiyē koṭiyār piḻaiyum kuṇamākak koṇṭu makiḻum kuṇakkuṉṟē.
translation: Your devotees attain bliss, while I alone languish. Many people in this world speak of this and laugh at me. The long night has passed and the day has dawned. What will I do? You have still not shown your compassion. O mountain of virtues who rejoices by taking even the faults of cruel people as merits!
commentary: It is painful to watch others find spiritual peace while feeling left behind in the dark. Vallalar says the world laughs at him as he waits for divine compassion to arrive. He appeals to a quality of the divine: the ability to look at our faults and choose to see them as merits.

tamil: குன்றா நிலைநின் றருள்அடைந்தார் அன்பர் எல்லாம் கொடியேன்நான்
நன்றாம் நெறிசென் றறியாதே மனஞ்செல் வழியே நடக்கின்றேன்
பொன்றா மணியே அவர்க்கருளி என்னை விடுத்தல் புகழன்றே
என்றால் எனக்கே நகைதோன்றும் எந்தாய் உளத்துக் கென்னாமே.
translit: kuṉṟā nilainiṉ ṟaruḷaṭaintār aṉpar ellām koṭiyēṉnāṉ naṉṟām neṟiceṉ ṟaṟiyātē maṉañcel vaḻiyē naṭakkiṉṟēṉ poṉṟā maṇiyē avarkkaruḷi eṉṉai viṭuttal pukaḻaṉṟē eṉṟāl eṉakkē nakaitōṉṟum entāy uḷattuk keṉṉāmē.
translation: All your loving devotees stood firm in the unfailing state and attained your grace. I am a cruel person who never learned to walk the good path. I merely wander wherever my mind leads. O imperishable gem! If I say that granting them grace while abandoning me brings you no glory, I laugh at my own words. O my father, how much more laughable must it be to your heart!
commentary: Vallalar contrasts the steady dedication of true seekers with his own habit of wandering wherever his mind leads. He tries to argue that leaving him behind would be a stain on God's reputation. He realizes how ridiculous this sounds, laughing at his own logic and imagining how much more it must amuse the divine.

tamil: என்ஆ ருயிருக் குயிர்அனையாய் என்னைப் பொருளாய் எண்ணிமகிழ்ந்
தந்நாள் அடிமை கொண்டளித்தாய் யார்க்கோ வந்த விருந்தெனவே
இந்நாள் இரங்கா திருக்கின்றாய் எங்கே புகுவேன் என்புரிவேன்
நின்னால் அன்றிப் பிறர்தம்மால் வேண்டேன் ஒன்றும் நின்மலனே.
translit: eṉā ruyiruk kuyiraṉaiyāy eṉṉaip poruḷāy eṇṇimakiḻn tannāḷ aṭimai koṇṭaḷittāy yārkkō vanta virunteṉavē innāḷ iraṅkā tirukkiṉṟāy eṅkē pukuvēṉ eṉpurivēṉ niṉṉāl aṉṟip piṟartammāl vēṇṭēṉ oṉṟum niṉmalaṉē.
translation: O pure one, you are the life of my precious life. On that day, you considered me worthy, rejoiced, took me as your servant, and granted your grace. Today, you show no pity, treating me like a guest meant for someone else. Where will I seek refuge? What will I do? I desire nothing from others, only from you.
commentary: Vallalar feels abandoned by God. He remembers when the Divine accepted him, but today he feels ignored, treated like a stranger who arrived at the wrong house. Having known that connection, he has nowhere else to turn.

tamil: நின்பால் அடைந்தார் அன்பாலே அடியார் எல்லாம் நெடுவினையேன்
வன்பால் மனப்பேய் தன்பாலே வருந்திச் சுழன்று மயர்கின்றேன்
தென்பால் நோக்கி இன்பநடம் செய்யும் இறைவா சிறுவனுக்கா
முன்பால் அமுதக் கடல்அளித்த முதல்வா என்னை முன்னுதியே.
translit: niṉpāl aṭaintār aṉpālē aṭiyār ellām neṭuviṉaiyēṉ vaṉpāl maṉappēy taṉpālē varuntic cuḻaṉṟu mayarkiṉṟēṉ teṉpāl nōkki iṉpanaṭam ceyyum iṟaivā ciṟuvaṉukkā muṉpāl amutak kaṭalaḷitta mutalvā eṉṉai muṉṉutiyē.
translation: Through love, all devotees have reached you. I am bound by vast karma. Caught by the cruel demon of my mind, I suffer, spin around, and grow bewildered. O Lord who dances in bliss facing south! O primal Lord who long ago granted the ocean of nectar-like milk for a little boy! Please hold me in your thoughts.
commentary: Devotees reach the Divine through love, but Vallalar feels trapped by a restless mind and the burden of past actions (karma). He calls upon the Lord who dances in bliss at Chidambaram. He reminds God of a sacred story where a crying child was fed an ocean of divine milk, asking for that same grace now.

translit: ceṟiyāta neñcaka vañcaka ṉēṉic ciṟutalattē aṟiyā taṟintavaṉ pōṟcila ceytiṭal aiyaniṉtāḷ kuṟiyā tarittala tāṇaimaṟ ṟillai-eṅ koṟṟavaṉē muṟiyā taruḷceyti yōteri yēṉentai muṉṉiyatē.
translation: I am a deceitful person whose heart lacks focus. In this small world, though I know nothing, I act like someone who possesses knowledge. O Lord, I swear on Your feet, my aim is to bear Your mark and nothing else, O my King. I do not know if You will grant me unbroken grace or what my Father has intended for me.
commentary: An ordinary person often gets caught in spiritual pride, pretending to have wisdom while knowing very little. Beneath this pretense is a sincere vow to belong to God alone. Vallalar places himself at the mercy of the divine will, waiting to see what grace will unfold.

translit: tītoṉṟu mēkaṇ ṭaṟintatal lālpalaṉ cēranalam yātoṉṟum nāṉkaṇ ṭaṟiyēṉ aṟintavaṉ eṉṉa-iṅkē pōtoṉṟu pōkkukiṉ ṟēṉpiḻai yāvum poṟuttaruḷvāy mātoṉṟu pākat tuṇai-aṉṟi naṟṟuṇai maṟṟilaiyē.
translation: I have seen and known only evil. I have known absolutely no beneficial good. Passing the time here, I act like someone who possesses knowledge. Please forgive all my faults and grant me grace. I have no true companion other than You, who share half Your form with the Goddess.
commentary: It is easy to spend a lifetime posturing as a spiritual expert while failing to do any genuine good. Vallalar asks for forgiveness for this wasted time. He directs this plea to Siva as Ardhanarishvara, the deity who shares half of his physical form with the divine feminine.

translit: ellām terinta iṟaivāniṉ taṇṇaruḷ eytukilāp pollāta pāvip pulaiyēṉ piḻaiyaip poṟuttaruḷvāy kallā maṉakkaṭai yālē kaṭaivaittuk kaṇṭatutuṉ pallāl aṇuttuṇai yumaṟi yēṉiṉpam āvatuvē.
translation: O all-knowing Lord, please forgive the faults of this wicked, sinful, and lowly person who has not attained Your cool grace. Because of the baseness of my ignorant mind, I placed myself at the very bottom and experienced only sorrow. I do not know even an atom of joy.
commentary: Our ignorant minds drag us into sorrow. By placing worldly concerns first, the mind creates a state of baseness where genuine joy becomes impossible. Vallalar begs the all-knowing Lord to look past these flaws and offer the relief of cool grace.

translit: maṇṇuṭai yāriṭai vāḷā maṉañcela vaittatalāl eṇṇuṭai yāriṭai eytiniṉ tāṇmalar ēttukilēṉ puṇṇuṭai yāriṟ pulampukiṉ ṟēṉaip poṟuttaruḷmuk kaṇṇuṭai yāykaḻaṟ kāluṭai yāymaṇi kaṇṭattaṉē.
translation: Because I uselessly let my mind chase after those who possess worldly lands, I did not join the wise to praise Your lotus feet. Please forgive me as I lament like someone covered in wounds. O three-eyed Lord, O wearer of anklets, O Lord with the jewel-colored neck!
commentary: Chasing wealthy, powerful people is a painful waste of time compared to the true work of gathering with wise devotees. The regret of this misdirected effort feels like physical wounds. Vallalar asks for healing from the divine, described here with classic attributes of Siva, including three eyes and a throat stained blue by cosmic poison.

translit: tāḻāta tuṉpac camuttirat tē-it taṉi-aṭiyēṉ vīḻāta vaṇṇam karuṇaicey vāyeṉṉai vēṇṭi-annāḷ ūḻām viṉaitavirt tāṇṭaṉai yē-eṉ uṭaiyavaṉē vāḻā vakai-eṉai innāḷ viṭuttal vaḻakkalavē.
translation: Show mercy so that this lonely devotee does not fall into the bottomless ocean of sorrow. You sought me out that day, removed my destined karma, and claimed me as Your own, O my Master. It is not just for You to abandon me today, leaving me unable to live.
commentary: Vallalar makes an intimate, direct claim on God's protection. He reminds the divine of a past intervention, noting that God already stepped in to clear away his accumulated past actions (karma). Having been claimed by grace once, he argues it would be unjust for God to let him drown in worldly sorrow now.

translit: ūṉceyta vempulaik kūṭṭiṉ poruṭṭiṅ kuṉaimaṟantu nāṉceyta tīmaiyai nāṉē niṉaikka naṭuṅkukiṉṟēṉ ēṉcey taṉai-eṉak kēḷātu mēlum iraṅkukiṉṟāy vāṉceyta nātaniṉ taṇṇaruḷ vaṇṇameṉ vāḻttuvaṉē.
translation: For the sake of this cruel cage of flesh, I forgot You here. I tremble just thinking of the evil I have done. Yet, without asking why I did this, You show me even more compassion. O Lord who created the heavens, how can I praise the nature of Your cool grace?
commentary: The demands of the physical body often make people forget God and commit wrongs. Vallalar looks back at his own actions and trembles at his mistakes. Yet he finds that God does not interrogate or judge him. Instead, the divine response is unconditional compassion.

translit: āyātu nāṉceyum kuṟṟaṅ kaḷaikkaṇ ṭaṟiyilpeṟṟa tāyāyi ṉumpoṟup pāḷala āṅkavai caṟṟalavē ōyātu ceyyun toṟumpoṟut tāḷum uṉai-eḷiyēṉ vāyāl uraikkavum māṭṭēṉan tō-eṉṉa vaṉmai-itē.
translation: Even the mother who bore me would not forgive the reckless faults I commit if she saw them, for they are not small in number. Every time I ceaselessly commit them, You forgive me and take me as Your own. I, a poor wretch, cannot even speak of You with my mouth. Alas, what hardness of heart is this!
commentary: We usually think of a mother's love as the highest standard of forgiveness. Vallalar says God's grace goes far beyond human limits. Even a mother would eventually lose patience with endless reckless mistakes, but God forgives every single one. He is struck by his inability to praise a love so vast.

translit: oṉṟun terintiṭa māṭṭāp paruvat tuṇarvutantāy iṉṟun tarutaṟ kiṟaivā niṉuḷḷam iyaitikolō kaṉṟuṅ karuttoṭu māḻkukiṉ ṟēṉuṉ kaḻalaṭikkē tuṉṟuṅ karuttaṟi yēṉciṟi yēṉeṉ tuṇivatuvē.
translation: At an age when I could understand nothing, You gave me awareness. O Lord, will Your heart consent to give it to me today as well? I languish with a grieving mind. I do not know how to fix my thoughts firmly upon Your ankleted feet. What resolve can this small one truly have?
commentary: Spiritual awakening is a gift of divine grace, given independent of human effort. Vallalar remembers that God gave him awareness when he was only an infant unable to understand anything. Now, struggling to keep his mind focused, he pleads for God to grant him that same unearned clarity today.

translit: āvā eṉa-eṉai āṭkoḷa vēṇṭum aṭimaikoṇṭa tēvā-eṉ kuṟṟam tiruvuḷat teṇṇileṉ ceytiṭuvēṉ vāvā eṉa-aḻaip pārpiṟar illai maṟantumeṉṟaṉ nāvāl uraikkavum māṭṭēṉ ciṟuteyva nāmaṅkaḷē.
translation: You must cry out in pity and take me as Your own. O God who made me Your servant, what will I do if You count my faults in Your divine heart? There is no one else to call out and invite me to come. Even in forgetfulness, I will never utter the names of petty deities with my tongue.
commentary: Vallalar throws himself on the mercy of the supreme God, knowing he cannot survive a strict accounting of his faults. He declares he will never speak the names of lesser deities, even in a moment of forgetfulness. He relies solely on the highest divine grace for his salvation.

translit: paḷḷatti lēcelum nīrpōleṉ uḷḷam parappatalāl eḷḷatti lēciṟi tāyiṉum nāṉcelva tillai-entāy kaḷḷatti lēcollu kiṉṟēṉ alaniṉ kaḻaliṇai-eṉ uḷḷatti lēniṉṟa āṅkavai kāṇka uṭaiyavaṉē.
translation: My mind only spreads outward like water flowing into a low valley. I do not advance forward even the size of a sesame seed, O my Father! I do not say this in deceit. Your twin ankleted feet stand within my heart. See them there, O Lord who possesses me!
commentary: The human mind naturally scatters and sinks into worldly distractions, just as water flows downhill into a valley. Vallalar admits he cannot make even a tiny bit of spiritual progress on his own. Yet he finds comfort in a single truth: despite his wandering mind, God is already seated within his heart.

tamil: நல்லார்க் கெல்லாம் நல்லவன்நீ ஒருவன் யாண்டும் நாயடியேன்
பொல்லார்க் கெல்லாம் பொல்லவன்நான் ஒருவன் இந்தப் புணர்ப்பதனால்
எல்லாம் உடையாய் நினக்கெதிரென் றெண்ணேல் உறவென் றெண்ணுகஈ
தல்லால் வழக்கென் இருமைக்கும் பொதுமை அன்றோ அருளிடமே.
translit: nallārk kellām nallavaṉnī oruvaṉ yāṇṭum nāyaṭiyēṉ pollārk kellām pollavaṉnāṉ oruvaṉ intap puṇarppataṉāl ellām uṭaiyāy niṉakketireṉ ṟeṇṇēl uṟaveṉ ṟeṇṇuka-ī tallāl vaḻakkeṉ irumaikkum potumai aṉṟō aruḷiṭamē.
translation: You are the single greatest good among all good people. I, your dog-like servant, am the single worst among all wicked people everywhere. By this pairing, O Lord who possesses everything, do not consider me your opposite. Consider this a relationship. What other rule is there? Is not the realm of grace common to both extremes?
commentary: Vallalar claims his wickedness and God's absolute goodness are a perfect match. A realm of grace must have room for both extremes, binding the highest and the lowest together in a natural relationship.

tamil: இடமே பொருளே ஏவலே என்றென் றெண்ணி இடர்ப்படுமோர்
மடமே உடையேன் தனக்கருள்நீ வழங்கல் அழகோ ஆநந்த
நடமே உடையோய் நினைஅன்றி வேற்றுத் தெய்வம் நயவேற்குத்
திடமே அருள்தான் வழங்காது தீர்த்தல் அழகோ தெரிப்பாயே.
translit: iṭamē poruḷē ēvalē eṉṟeṉ ṟeṇṇi iṭarppaṭumōr maṭamē uṭaiyēṉ taṉakkaruḷnī vaḻaṅkal aḻakō ānanta naṭamē uṭaiyōy niṉai-aṉṟi vēṟṟut teyvam nayavēṟkut tiṭamē aruḷtāṉ vaḻaṅkātu tīrttal aḻakō terippāyē.
translation: I possess the foolishness of suffering in constant worry over place, wealth, and power. Is it fitting for You to grant me your grace? O Lord of the blissful dance, I desire no other god but You. Is it fitting to turn me away without firmly granting your grace? Tell me.
commentary: Confessing his worldly anxieties about property, money, and influence, Vallalar wonders if someone so flawed deserves grace. Yet, because he worships no one else, he asks if God can turn away such single-minded devotion.

tamil: தெரித்தால் அன்றிச் சிறிதேனும் தெரிவொன் றில்லாச் சிறியேனைப்
பிரித்தாய் கூடும் வகைஅறியும் பெற்றி என்னே பிறைமுடிமேல்
தரித்தாய் அடியேன் பிழைபொறுக்கத் தகுங்காண் துன்பம் தமியேனை
அரித்தால் கண்டிங் கிரங்காமை அந்தோ அருளுக் கழகேயோ.
translit: terittāl aṉṟic ciṟitēṉum terivoṉ ṟillāc ciṟiyēṉaip pirittāy kūṭum vakai-aṟiyum peṟṟi eṉṉē piṟaimuṭimēl tarittāy aṭiyēṉ piḻaipoṟukkat takuṅkāṇ tuṉpam tamiyēṉai arittāl kaṇṭiṅ kiraṅkāmai antō aruḷuk kaḻakēyō.
translation: I am a lowly one who understands absolutely nothing unless You make it known. You separated me. How will I ever know the way to reunite with You? O Lord who wears the crescent moon on your crown, it is fitting for You to forgive my faults. Alas, when sorrow gnaws at my lonely self, is it beautiful for your grace to watch without showing pity?
commentary: The soul knows nothing unless the divine reveals it. Since God placed him in this separate, worldly existence, Vallalar argues that God must also show him the way back to unity. A compassionate divine presence cannot watch a lonely soul suffer.

tamil: அருள்ஓர் சிறிதும் உதவுகிலாய் அதனைப் பெறுதற் கடியேன்பால்
தெருள்ஓர் சிறிதும் இலையேஎன் செய்கேன் எங்கள் சிவனேயோ
மருளோர் எனினும் தமைநோக்கி வந்தார்க் களித்தல் வழக்கன்றோ
பொருளோர் இடத்தே மிடிகொண்டோர் புகுதல் இன்று புதிதன்றே.
translit: aruḷōr ciṟitum utavukilāy ataṉaip peṟutaṟ kaṭiyēṉpāl teruḷōr ciṟitum ilaiyē-eṉ ceykēṉ eṅkaḷ civaṉēyō maruḷōr eṉiṉum tamainōkki vantārk kaḷittal vaḻakkaṉṟō poruḷōr iṭattē miṭikoṇṭōr pukutal iṉṟu putitaṉṟē.
translation: You do not offer even a little grace. I lack even the slightest wisdom to attain it. What shall I do, O our Siva! Even if they are steeped in delusion, is it not the custom to grant gifts to those who come seeking You? It is nothing new today for the destitute to seek refuge at the doors of the wealthy.
commentary: Lacking both grace and the wisdom to find it, Vallalar is helpless. He points to a basic rule of charity in the human world. Just as a destitute beggar seeks refuge at the door of the wealthy, a struggling soul comes to God, and the one with infinite wealth is obliged to give.

tamil: புதியேன் அல்லேன் நின்அடிமைப் பொருத்தம் இல்லேன் அல்லேன்யான்
மதியேன் வேற்றுத் தேவர்தமை வந்தங் கவர்தாம் எதிர்ப்படினும்
துதியேன் நின்னை விடுவேனோ தொண்ட னேனை விடல்அழகோ
நதியேர் சடையோய் இன்னருள்நீ நல்கல் வேண்டும் நாயேற்கே.
translit: putiyēṉ allēṉ niṉaṭimaip poruttam illēṉ allēṉyāṉ matiyēṉ vēṟṟut tēvartamai vantaṅ kavartām etirppaṭiṉum tutiyēṉ niṉṉai viṭuvēṉō toṇṭa ṉēṉai viṭalaḻakō natiyēr caṭaiyōy iṉṉaruḷnī nalkal vēṇṭum nāyēṟkē.
translation: I am no newcomer. I am not unfit to be your servant. I do not respect other gods. Even if they stand before me, I will not praise them. Will I ever abandon You? Is it fitting to abandon me, your devotee? O Lord with the river adorning your matted hair, You must grant your sweet grace to this dog.
commentary: Vallalar insists he is a rightful, long-standing servant who would ignore other gods even if they stood right in front of him. Having given himself to one master, he asks how he could be abandoned.

tamil: நாயேன் துன்பக் கடல்வீழ்ந்து நலிதல் அழகோ நல்லோர்க்கிங்
கீயேன் ஒன்றும் இல்லேன்நான் என்செய் கேனோ என்னுடைய
தாயே அனையாய் சிறிதென்மேல் தயவு புரிந்தால் ஆகாதோ
சேயேன் தன்னை விடுப்பாயோ விடுத்தால் உலகஞ் சிரியாதோ.
translit: nāyēṉ tuṉpak kaṭalvīḻntu nalital aḻakō nallōrkkiṅ kīyēṉ oṉṟum illēṉnāṉ eṉcey kēṉō eṉṉuṭaiya tāyē aṉaiyāy ciṟiteṉmēl tayavu purintāl ākātō cēyēṉ taṉṉai viṭuppāyō viṭuttāl ulakañ ciriyātō.
translation: Is it right for a dog like me to fall into the sea of sorrow and suffer? I give nothing to the good people here. I possess nothing. What shall I do? You who are like my mother, can you not show a little compassion toward me? Will you abandon this child? If you abandon me, will the world not laugh?
commentary: Comparing the bond between God and the soul to a mother and child, Vallalar feels helpless. He possesses nothing of value to give. He asks how a divine mother could abandon her child to a sea of sorrow; if she did, the world would mock such a parent.

tamil: சிரிப்பார் நின்பேர் அருள்பெற்றோர் சிவனே சிவனே சிவனேயோ
விரிப்பார் பழிச்சொல் அன்றிஎனை விட்டால் வெள்ளை விடையோனே
தரிப்பாய் இவனை அருளிடத்தே என்று நின்று தகும்வண்ணம்
தெரிப்பார் நினக்கும் எவர்கண்டாய் தேவர் தேடற் கரியானே.
translit: cirippār niṉpēr aruḷpeṟṟōr civaṉē civaṉē civaṉēyō virippār paḻiccol aṉṟi-eṉai viṭṭāl veḷḷai viṭaiyōṉē tarippāy ivaṉai aruḷiṭattē eṉṟu niṉṟu takumvaṇṇam terippār niṉakkum evarkaṇṭāy tēvar tēṭaṟ kariyāṉē.
translation: Those who have received your great grace will laugh. O Siva, Siva, Siva! If you abandon me, they will spread words of blame, O Rider of the white bull! Who is there to stand and properly advise you, 'Hold him in the state of grace'? O Lord who is difficult for the gods to find!
commentary: Vallalar appeals to God's reputation among the saints. If the Lord abandons him now, those who have received grace will spread words of blame. Because God is beyond even the highest celestial beings, no equal can step in to advise the Lord to be merciful. God must choose to grant this grace on his own.

tamil: அரிய பெருமான் எளியோமை ஆளும் பெருமான் யாவர்கட்கும்
பெரிய பெருமான் சிவபெருமான் பித்தப் பெருமான் என்றுன்னை
உரிய பெருமா தவர்பழிச்சல் உண்மை எனில்என் உடையானே
கரிய பெருமால் உடையேற்கும் அருளல் உன்றன் கடன்அன்றே.
translit: ariya perumāṉ eḷiyōmai āḷum perumāṉ yāvarkaṭkum periya perumāṉ civaperumāṉ pittap perumāṉ eṉṟuṉṉai uriya perumā tavarpaḻiccal uṇmai eṉileṉ uṭaiyāṉē kariya perumāl uṭaiyēṟkum aruḷal uṉṟaṉ kaṭaṉaṉṟē.
translation: The rare Lord, the Lord who rules us simple ones, the great Lord of all, Lord Siva, the Lord of madness. If it is true that the rightful great sages praise you in this way, O my Master, is it not your duty to grant grace even to me who possesses great dark delusion?
commentary: The great sages call God the 'Lord of madness' because divine grace flows freely and defies ordinary human calculation. If this praise is true, Vallalar argues, it is God's duty to save him. The depth of Vallalar's darkness and delusion makes him the perfect candidate for this unpredictable grace.

tamil: அன்றும் சிறியேன் அறிவறியேன் அதுநீ அறிந்தும் அருள்செய்தாய்
இன்றும் சிறியேன் அறிவறியேன் இதுநீ அறிந்தும் அருளாயேல்
என்றும் ஒருதன் மையன்எங்கள் இறைவன் எனமா மறைகள்எலாம்
தொன்று மொழிந்த தூமொழிதான் சூது மொழியோ சொல்லாயே.
translit: aṉṟum ciṟiyēṉ aṟivaṟiyēṉ atunī aṟintum aruḷceytāy iṉṟum ciṟiyēṉ aṟivaṟiyēṉ itunī aṟintum aruḷāyēl eṉṟum orutaṉ maiyaṉeṅkaḷ iṟaivaṉ eṉamā maṟaikaḷelām toṉṟu moḻinta tūmoḻitāṉ cūtu moḻiyō collāyē.
translation: Even in the past, I was a lowly one who lacked wisdom; knowing that, you granted me grace. Even today, I am a lowly one who lacks wisdom. If you know this and do not grant me grace, tell me, is the pure word spoken since ancient times by all the great Vedas stating 'Our Lord is forever unchanging in nature' a deceitful word?
commentary: The ancient scriptures declare God's nature is eternal and unchanging. Vallalar uses this teaching to make a direct demand. Since God showed him mercy in the past when he was ignorant, God must do the same today. If the Lord refuses to help him now, it would mean the sacred texts are lying about God's steady nature.

tamil: சொல்லற் கரிய பெரியபரஞ் சுடரே முக்கட் சுடர்க்கொழுந்தே
மல்லற் கருமால் அயன்முதலோர் வழுத்தும் பெருஞ்சீர் மணிக்குன்றே
புல்லற் கரிதாம் எளியேன்றன் பிழைகள் யாவும் பொறுத்திந்த
அல்லற் கடல்நின் றெனைஎடுத்தே அருள்வாய் உன்றன் அருள்நலமே.
translit: collaṟ kariya periyaparañ cuṭarē mukkaṭ cuṭarkkoḻuntē mallaṟ karumāl ayaṉmutalōr vaḻuttum peruñcīr maṇikkuṉṟē pullaṟ karitām eḷiyēṉṟaṉ piḻaikaḷ yāvum poṟuttinta allaṟ kaṭalniṉ ṟeṉai-eṭuttē aruḷvāy uṉṟaṉ aruḷnalamē.
translation: O great supreme Light that defies description! O flame of the three-eyed Light! O mountain of gems possessing great glory, praised by the dark-hued Vishnu, Brahma, and others! Forgive all the faults of this simple one who is hard to accept, lift me from this sea of sorrow, and grant me the goodness of your grace.
commentary: God is the supreme, indescribable light that even the greatest traditional deities worship. Recognizing his flaws, Vallalar surrenders and asks for forgiveness. He pleads to be lifted out of worldly suffering and drawn into the goodness of divine grace.

translit: āḷviṉaiyāl payaṉuṟuvār acati yāṭa antō ip pulaināyēṉ aṉpāl niṉpāl vēḷviceyum peruntavarkkē vēḷvi ceyya vēṇṭumitaṟ kemperumāṉ karuṇai ceyyum nāḷviḷaivil ciṉṉāḷē itutāṉ uṇmai nampumeṉa naviṉṟuṉaiyē nampi niṉṟēṉ kēḷviyilāt turaittaṉamō alatu nāyēṉ kiḷakkumuṟai kiḷakkilaṉō kēṭṭi lāyē.
translation: While those who profit from worldly efforts mock me, alas, this lowly dog must lovingly serve the great ascetics who worship You. Our Lord will grant His grace for this in just a few days, and this is the truth. Telling myself to believe this, I stood placing my trust only in You. Is Your rule one that does not grant a hearing? Or did I, a dog, fail to voice my appeal properly? You have not listened.
commentary: Vallalar questions if the Divine has ignored him or if his prayers were inadequate, capturing the vulnerable doubt of a sincere seeker waiting for grace amidst worldly mockery.

translit: kēṭṭilāy aṭiyēṉcey muṟaiyai antō kēṭilāk kuṇattavarpāl kiṭṭu kiṉṟōy ēṭṭilā yiraṅkōṭi eṉiṉum caṟṟum eḻutamuṭi yākkuṟaikoṇ ṭiḷaikkiṉ ṟēṉnāṉ cēṭṭiyā viṭiṉumeṉaic cēṭṭit tīrkkum ciṟumaṉattāl ceypiḻaiyait tērti yāyil nāṭṭilār kākkavallār eṉṉai entāy nāḷkaḻiyā vaṇṇamiṉi nalkalvēṇṭum.
translation: Alas, You have not listened to my appeal! You draw near to those of flawless character. Even if I had ten billion palm leaves, I grow exhausted with flaws that cannot be completely written down. Even if You do not trouble me, my petty mind torments and drains me. If You examine the wrongs committed by this petty mind, who in this world can save me, my Father? You must grant Your grace now without letting another day pass.
commentary: Vallalar contrasts the perfection of the Divine with his own endless flaws. If judged strictly on these faults, no one else in the world can save him.

translit: vēṇṭāmai vēṇṭukiṉṟōr niṟka maṟṟai vēṇṭuvār vēṇṭuvaṉa virumpi nalkum tūṇṭāta maṇiviḷakkē potuvi lāṭum cuṭarkkoḻuntē eṉṉuyirkkut tuṇaiyē eṉṉai āṇṭāṟu mūṉṟāṇṭil āṇṭu koṇṭa aruṭkaṭalē eṉuḷḷat tamarnta tēvē īṇṭāva eṉacciṟiya aṭiyēṉ uḷḷat teṇṇamaṟin taruḷāyēl eṉcey kēṉē.
translation: Let those who seek desirelessness stand aside. You gladly grant whatever is desired by those who ask. O radiant lamp that burns without being lit! O leaping flame that dances in the public hall! O companion to my life! O ocean of grace who claimed me in my ninth year! O God seated in my heart! If You do not know the thoughts in the heart of this lowly servant and grant Your grace by calling me near, what shall I do?
commentary: Recalling the intimate bond formed when God claimed him at age nine, Vallalar contrasts himself with seekers who pray for desirelessness. He plainly asks God to fulfill his one desperate longing for grace.

translit: eṉṉai-aṟiyāpparuvat tāṇṭukoṇṭa eṉkuruvē eṉakkuriya iṉpa mē-eṉ taṉṉai-iṉṟu viṭattuṇintāy pōlum antō takumōniṉ peruṅkaruṇait takavuk kentāy uṉṉai-alā toruvartampāl cellēṉ eṉṉai uṭaiyāṉē eṉṉuḷḷat tuḷḷē niṉṟu muṉṉaiviṉaip payaṉūṭṭa niṉaippik kiṉṟāy muṭippikkat tuṇintilaiyēl moḻiva teṉṉē.
translation: O my Guru who claimed me at an age when I did not even know myself! O my rightful bliss! It seems You have decided to abandon me today. Alas, is this fitting for the nature of Your vast grace, my Father? I will not go to anyone but You. O Lord who owns me! Standing within my heart, You make me experience the fruits of my past karma. If You do not resolve to end this, what can I say?
commentary: Belonging wholly to God, Vallalar refuses to seek help elsewhere. He asks the Divine to end the painful cycle of his past actions (karma), pleading that abandoning him now violates the nature of supreme compassion.

translit: eṉnāṇai aṟintumeṉṉai antō antō ivvakaicey tiṭattuṇintāy eṉṉē entāy niṉāṇai niṉṉaiyalā toṉṟum vēṇṭēṉ nī-itaṉai aṟintilaiyō niṉaippik kiṉṟa maṉṉā-eṉ āruyirkku vāḻvē eṉkaṇ maṇiyē-eṉ kuruvē-eṉ maruntē iṉṉum uṉṉāliṅ kuyirtarittu vāḻkiṉ ṟēṉeṉ uḷḷamaṟin tutavutiyō uṇarki lēṉē.
translation: Even knowing my modesty, alas, You have decided to treat me this way. What is this, my Father? I swear upon You, I desire nothing but You. Do You not know this? O King who directs my thoughts! O life of my precious soul! O pupil of my eye! O my Guru! O my medicine! Even now, I sustain my life and live here only because of You. I do not know if You will understand my heart and help me.
commentary: Stripped of all other attachments, Vallalar declares that God is the medicine sustaining his life. His survival depends on the hope that the Divine will recognize his single-minded devotion and answer his call.

translit: uḷḷamaṟin tutavuvaṉnam uṭaiyāṉ ellām uṭaiyāṉmaṟ ṟorukuṟai-iṅ kuṇṭō eṉṉak kaḷḷamaṉat tēṉantō kaḷitti runtēṉ kaiviṭuvār pōliruntāy karuṇaik kuṉṟē eḷḷaluṟap paṭuvēṉiṅ kētu ceyvēṉ eṅkeḻukēṉ yārkkuraippēṉ iṉṉum uṉṟaṉ vaḷḷalaruḷ tiṟanōkki niṟkiṉ ṟēṉeṉ maṉattuyarpōm vakai-aruḷa matitti ṭāyē.
translation: Thinking, "Our Lord who owns all things knows my heart and will help. Is there any other lack here?", I rejoiced, alas, with a deceitful mind. O mountain of grace, you appeared as though you would abandon me. I face ridicule. What will I do here? Where will I rise up? To whom will I tell this? Still, I stand looking toward the power of your bountiful grace. Please resolve to grant me the means to banish my mental sorrow.
commentary: Relying on the thought that God will handle everything without personal effort is a trap. Vallalar confesses his early confidence was complacency. Terrified the Divine might abandon him to public ridicule, he realizes he must actively plead for grace to clear his sorrow.

translit: vakai-aṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṉcaṉ mārkka mēvum māṇpuṭaiya peruntavattōr makiḻa vāḻum takai-aṟiyēṉ nalamoṉṟum aṟiyēṉ poymmai tāṉaṟivēṉ nallōraic calañcey kiṉṟa mikai-aṟivēṉ tīṅkeṉpa ellām iṅkē mika-aṟivēṉ eṉiṉumeṉai viṭuti yāyil pakai-aṟivēṉ niṉmītil paḻivait tintap pāvi-uyir viṭattuṇivēṉ pakarntiṭ ṭēṉē.
translation: I am small and know no methods. I do not know the nature of the great and dignified ascetics who live joyfully having attained Sanmarkkam. I know no good at all. I know only falsehood. I know the excessive harm inflicted upon good people. I know very well everything called evil here. Yet, if you abandon me, I will know hostility. Blaming you, this sinner will resolve to give up my life. I declare this now.
commentary: Desperation drives Vallalar to an extreme ultimatum. Confessing he knows nothing of Sanmarkkam (the path of pure truth and goodness) and is entangled in worldly faults, he threatens God directly. If grace is withheld, he vows to take his own life and lay the blame on the Divine, showing how raw and demanding the intimacy between soul and God can become.

translit: iṭṭavakai vāḻkiṉṟēṉ entāy nāṉē eṇṇukilēṉ eṇṇuvittāl eṉcey vēṉniṉ maṭṭalarcē vaṭi-āṇai niṉaitta vaṇṇam vāḻvikka vēṇṭuminta vaṇṇam allāl tuṭṭaṉeṉa viṭattuṇiti yāyil antō cūṟaiyuṟu turumpeṉavum cuḻaṉṟu vāṉil viṭṭacilai eṉappavattil viḻuvēṉ aṉṟi vēṟetucey vēṉinta viḻala ṉēṉē.
translation: O my father, I live entirely according to how you place me. I do not think on my own. If you make me think, what can I do? I swear upon your fragrant blossoming red feet: you must make me live exactly as you intended. If instead you resolve to abandon me as a wicked person, alas, I will fall back into worldly birth like a straw spinning in a whirlwind or a stone thrown into the sky. What else can I, this worthless person, do?
commentary: The soul has no independent will; it lives and thinks only as God directs. Since every thought comes from the Divine, the responsibility to save the soul rests on God. Without that saving grace, Vallalar will be thrown back into the endless cycle of worldly birth, as helpless as a falling stone.

translit: viḻaṟkiṟaittu melikiṉṟa vīṇa ṉēṉiv viyaṉulakil viḷaittiṭṭa mikaikaḷ ellām aḻaṟkiṟaitta pañceṉavē ākki nīyē āṭkoṇṭāl taṭuppavariṅ kārē aiyā kaḻaṟkaṭimai eṉa-ulakam aṟiya oṉṟum karutaṟiyāc ciṟuparuvatteṉṉai āṇṭu niḻaṟkaruṇai aḷittāyē innāḷ nīkai nekiḻaviṭṭāl eṉceyvēṉ nilaiyi lēṉē.
translation: I am a vain person who weakens himself by pouring water on barren land. I have caused all these offenses in this vast world. If you turn them to ashes like cotton thrown into a fire and take me as your own, who is here to stop it, O Lord? In my tender youth when my mind knew nothing, you claimed me and gave me the shade of your grace so the world would know I am a slave to your ankleted feet. If you let me slip from your hand today, what will I do? I have no other standing.
commentary: Divine grace can erase a lifetime of mistakes in an instant. Vallalar leans on an old, intimate bond, reminding God he was claimed in early childhood before he had any understanding. Having been sheltered by that grace for his whole life, being dropped now would leave him destroyed.

translit: nilai-aṟiyēṉ nilai-aṟintu peṟṟa nallōr neṟi-aṟiyēṉ eṉiṉumuṉṟaṉ nēca maṉṟi ilai-aṟiyēṉ maṟṟavaraik kaṉavi lēṉum eṭṭuṇai-ōr tuṇai-eṉavum eṇṇu ṟēṉnal kalai-aṟiyēṉ karuttilirun taṟivit tāynāṉ kaṇṭaṟintēṉ eṉiṉumavai kāṭṭa vēṇṭum alai-aṟiyā aruṭkaṭalē amutē tēṉē ampalatteṉ kuruvēnāṉ aṭimai āḷē.
translation: I do not know stability. I do not know the path of the good people who understood the true state and attained it. Yet I know nothing but your love. Even in my dreams, I do not consider others as even the tiniest fraction of support. I know no good arts. Residing in my mind, you granted me knowledge. Though I have seen and understood, you must reveal those things to me. O ocean of grace free of waves! O nectar! O honey! O my Guru in the Ambalam! I am your slave. Rule over me.
commentary: True devotion means relying on God's love without seeking help elsewhere, even in a dream. Though he lacks formal knowledge, Vallalar trusts the inner guidance God has taught him. He begs his Guru in the Ambalam (the open space of supreme grace) to bring that inner understanding out into full revelation.

note: Editor's note: a general poem (potu, பொது), not tied to one temple.
translit: nīrār caṭaiyatu nīṇmāl viṭaiyatu nērkoḷkoṉṟait tārār muṭiyatu cīrār aṭiyatu tāḻvakaṟṟum pērā yirattatu pērā varattatu pērulakam ōrā vaḷattatoṉ ṟuṇṭēmuk kaṇṇoṭeṉ uḷḷakattē.
translation: It has matted hair bearing the waters. It rides the tall great bull. It has a crown adorned with a garland of cassia flowers. It has glorious feet. It has a thousand names that banish sorrow. It grants unfailing boons. It holds an abundance the great world cannot fathom. There is One with three eyes within my heart.
commentary: Vallalar describes the divine using the familiar imagery of Lord Siva, with rivers in His matted hair and a crown of cassia flowers. He teaches that this immense, sorrow-destroying God dwells intimately within the human heart.

translit: maṭṭup paṭātatu māmaṟai yālum malappakaiyāl kaṭṭup paṭātatu mālā tiyartam karuttiṉukkum taṭṭup paṭātatu pārmutal pūtat taṭaikaḷiṉāl oṭṭup paṭātatoṉ ṟuṇṭēmuk kaṇṇoṭeṉ uḷḷakattē.
translation: It is unmeasured even by the great Vedas. It is unbound by the hostility of impurities. It remains ungrasped even by the minds of Vishnu and the other gods. It does not attach to the obstacles of the physical elements beginning with the earth. There is One with three eyes within my heart.
commentary: The divine presence is entirely beyond the reach of ancient scriptures and the minds of other gods. It remains completely free from physical elements and worldly impurities. This boundless and uncontainable reality makes its home directly in the innermost heart.

translit: pētap paṭātatu paṟpala kaṟpaṅkaḷ pērntiṭiṉum cētap paṭātatu naṉṟitu tīteṉac ceykaikaḷāl ētap paṭātatuḷ eṭṭap paṭātatiṅ kiyāvarkaṭkum ōtap paṭātatoṉ ṟuṇṭēmuk kaṇṇoṭeṉ uḷḷakattē.
translation: It is undivided. It remains indestructible even if countless eons pass away. It is untouched by the flaws of actions deemed good or bad. It cannot be grasped within. It cannot be described to anyone here. There is One with three eyes within my heart.
commentary: God exists outside time and remains untouched by karma—human ideas of good and bad. Though it defies all attempts to grasp or describe it, this presence is a silent resident within the devotee.

translit: taṇṇār aḷiyatu viṇṇēr oḷiyatu cāṟṟumaṟaip paṇṇār muṭivatu peṇṇār vaṭivatu paṇpuyartīk kaṇṇār nutalatu kaṇṇār maṇiyatu kaṇṭukoḷḷa oṇṇā nilaiyatoṉ ṟuṇṭēmuk kaṇṇoṭeṉ uḷḷakattē.
translation: It holds cool compassion. It shines with a light like the heavens. It is the culmination of the chanted Vedas. It shares its form with a woman. It bears a majestic eye of fire on its forehead. It is the precious gem of the eye. It exists in a state impossible to behold. There is One with three eyes within my heart.
commentary: Vallalar unites the fiery third eye with the cooling grace of compassion. The traditional form of God sharing half His body with the Goddess symbolizes a perfect balance of forces. This supreme light is the treasure hidden within our own eyes and hearts.

translit: piṟavā neṟiyatu pēcā nilaiyatu pēcileṉṟum iṟavā uruvatuḷ ēṟṟāl varuva tiruḷakaṉṟōr maṟavā tuṭaiyatu mātōr puṭaiyatu vāḻttukiṉṟōr uṟavāy iruppatoṉ ṟuṇṭēmuk kaṇṇoṭeṉ uḷḷakattē.
translation: It is the path of birthlessness. It is a state beyond speech. If spoken of, it is an immortal form. It manifests when accepted within. It is held unforgotten by those who have banished darkness. It holds a woman on one side. It stands as loving kin to those who praise it. There is One with three eyes within my heart.
commentary: Vallalar teaches that when a person clears away inner darkness and accepts this presence, it frees them from the cycle of rebirth. The divine acts as loving family, forging an intimate relationship built on constant remembrance and devotion.

translit: mativār caṭaimā maṇiyē aruḷvaḷ ḷalēnaṉ nitiyē tiru-am palattā ṭalceynit taṉēniṉ tutiyēṉ eṉiṉum uṉai-aṉ ṟittuṇaiyi lēṉeṉ patiyē eṉateṇ ṇampa likkumpaṭik karuḷē.
translation: O great gem with the crescent moon on your flowing matted hair, O benevolent Lord of grace, my good treasure, O eternal one who dances in the holy hall. Even if I do not sing your praise, I have no refuge other than you. O my Lord, bestow your grace so my intention is fulfilled.
commentary: Total surrender is the only requirement for divine grace. Vallalar admits he fails even to sing God's praises, yet claims the divine as his only refuge. This absolute reliance becomes his primary qualification for mercy.

translit: paṭimēl aṭiyēṉ uṉai-aṉ ṟi-ōrpaṟṟi lēṉeṉ muṭimēl aṭivait taruḷcey tiṭamuṉṉu kaṇṭāy koṭimēl viṭaināṭ ṭiya-eṇku ṇakkuṉ ṟamē poṭimēl viḷaṅkun tirumē ṉi-empuṇ ṇiyaṉē.
translation: On this earth, I, your servant, have no refuge other than you. Resolve to place your feet upon my head and bestow your grace. O mountain of eight attributes who raised the bull upon your banner, O our virtuous Lord whose holy body shines with sacred ash.
commentary: Placing the divine feet upon the devotee's head is an act of supreme grace and protection. God is described as possessing eight core attributes (eṇkuṇam), which traditionally include purity, infinite knowledge, and boundless grace. Vallalar insists he has nowhere else to turn.

translit: puṇṇām maṉamcañ calittuḷ ḷampularntu niṉṟēṉ aṇṇā eṉai-āṭ koḷavēṇ ṭumakaṟṟu vāyēl kaṇṇār kaḷaikaṇ piṟitoṉ ṟilaikaḷḷa ṉēṉai eṇṇā viṉai-eṉ ceyumō itaṟkeṉcey vēṉē.
translation: I stand with a withered heart and a wounded, wavering mind. O Lord, you must take me as your own. If you cast me away, I have no other true refuge. What will incalculable karma do to me, a deceitful person? What can I do about this?
commentary: The human mind is easily broken by worldly struggles and the heavy burden of past actions, known as karma. Vallalar fears that without divine protection, his past misdeeds will overwhelm him. He throws himself on God's mercy, knowing human effort alone cannot erase the weight of deceit and failure.

translit: ceyvēṉ avamaṉ ṟittavam oṉṟumcey taṟiyēṉ naivēṉ piḻaiyā vumpoṟut taruḷnalku vāyēl uyvēṉ alatuy vakai-iṉ ṟumaṉṟōṅku kiṉṟāy vaivēṉ tutippēṉ uṉai-eṉ ṟummaṟanti lēṉē.
translation: I perform only worthless deeds and know nothing of doing penance. I languish in suffering. If you forgive all my faults and grant your grace, I will be saved. Otherwise, I have no way to find salvation. O Lord who stands supreme in the hall, whether I abuse or praise you, I never forget you.
commentary: True devotion survives intense frustration. Vallalar confesses his lack of spiritual discipline and admits he sometimes lashes out in despair. Yet whether praising God or angrily blaming him, his mind never stops focusing on the divine presence.

tamil: உறவா கியநின் பதம்அன் றிஒன் றோர்கி லேன்நான்
பிறவா நெறிதந் தருள்என் பதென் பேசி டாயே.
translit: maṟavā tuṉaivāḻt tumeyaṉ paraimāni lattē iṟavā vakai-āṭ koṇṭaru ḷiya-īca ṉēmey uṟavā kiyaniṉ patamaṉ ṟi-oṉ ṟōrki lēṉnāṉ piṟavā neṟitan taruḷeṉ pateṉ pēci ṭāyē.
translation: O Lord who bestows grace upon your true devotees who praise you unceasingly, taking them as your own so they never die on this great earth. I know nothing other than your feet, which are my true kinship. Why must I ask you to grant me the path of no rebirth? Please speak.
commentary: The highest reward of spiritual life is freedom from death and the endless cycle of rebirth. Vallalar observes that God already grants this immortal state to those who love him. Since God is his only true family and knows his heart, he asks why he should even need to speak his request aloud.

translit: eṉṉē iṉumniṉ aruḷey tilaṉēḻai yēṉai muṉṉē valintāṭ koṇṭatiṉ ṟumuṉinta tēyō poṉṉēr aṇi-am palattā ṭiyapuṇṇi yā-eṉ aṉṉē aracē amutē aruḷāṇṭa vaṉē.
translation: What is this? Even now I have not attained your grace. You forcefully claimed me, a poor wretch, in the past. Are you angry with me today? O virtuous one who dances in the beautiful golden hall! My mother, my king, my nectar, Lord of grace!
commentary: Vallalar questions why he feels distant from God's grace, reminding the Divine who first reached out to claim him. Addressing God with intimacy as mother and king, he wonders if he has done something to cause this separation.

translit: āṇṭāy eṉai-ēḻ piṟappum uṉai-aṉṟi oṉṟum tīṇṭā teṉatuḷ ḷameṉṟāl eṉciṟumai tīrkka vēṇṭā tayalār eṉakkāṇ pateṉmeyya ṉēpoṉ āṇṭāṉ tiru-ey tanañcaik kaḷamnāṭṭi ṉōyē.
translation: You have ruled me through all seven births. Nothing touches my heart except you. Since this is true, why do you see me as a stranger and refuse to end my misery, O truthful one? You held poison in your throat so the golden lord could attain prosperity.
commentary: Vallalar asserts his steady devotion across multiple lifetimes, asking why he is now ignored as a stranger. He reminds God of His compassion, recalling the story where Siva drank the ocean's poison to save the world and the other gods. He pleads for that same mercy to end his own misery.

translit: nāṭṭār nakaicey vareṉṟō aruḷnalki lāynī vīṭṭār niṉai-eṉ ṉiṉaippār eṉaimēvi lāyēl tāṭṭā marai-aṉ ṟittuṇai oṉṟumcārn tilēṉeṉ māṭṭā mai-aṟin taruḷvāy maṇimaṉṟu ḷāṉē.
translation: Do you refuse to grant grace thinking the people of the world will laugh? If you do not unite with me, what will the people of your home think of you? I rely on no support other than your lotus feet. Knowing my helplessness, grant me your grace, O Lord of the gem-studded hall.
commentary: Vallalar playfully asks if God is withholding grace out of worry that ordinary people will laugh at Him for blessing such a lowly person. He notes that God's true family of saints will be surprised if He abandons someone who relies on His feet for support.

translit: maṉṟā ṭiyamā maṇiyē taṉivāṉa vā-ōr miṉṟāḻ caṭaivē tiyaṉē niṉaivēṇṭu kiṉṟēṉ poṉṟā tameyaṉ parukkaṉ puḷampūṇṭu niṉṟu naṉṟāy iravum pakalum uṉaināṭu māṟē.
translation: O great gem who dances in the hall! O peerless heavenly Lord! O Lord of the Vedas with flashing matted hair! I beg you to plant love in my heart for your true devotees of undying love, so that I may seek you steadfastly night and day.
commentary: Vallalar asks for a specific blessing: the ability to love God's true devotees. Grounding himself in the company of seekers and sharing their devotion is the best way to keep his mind focused on God day and night.

translit: māṟā maṉamā yaiyiṉāl matimāḻki māḻki ēṟā maliṟaṅ kukiṉṟēṉ itaṟkeṉ ceyvēṉ tēṟā vuḷattēṉ ṟaṉai-ē ṟiṭacceyti kaṇṭāy pēṟā maṇi-am palamē viyapeṟṟi yāṉē.
translation: Thoroughly bewildered by the unceasing illusion of the mind, I descend instead of ascending. What shall I do about this? Cause me, a person whose heart lacks clarity, to ascend. O Lord of great nature dwelling in the blessed gem-studded hall!
commentary: The mind constantly creates illusions that drag a person down into confusion and despair. Vallalar admits his helplessness against his own restless thoughts, asking God to lift him up and bring clarity to his heart.

translit: āṉē ṟivantaṉ parai-āṭ koḷumaiya ṉē-em māṉē maṇimaṉ ṟilnaṭam purivaḷḷa lēcen tēṉē amutē mutalā kiyateyva mēnī tāṉē eṉai-āṇ ṭaruḷvāy niṉcaraṇ caraṇē.
translation: O Lord who comes riding the bull to claim Your devotees! Our Master! O benevolent Lord who dances in the hall of gems! O pure honey! O ambrosia! O primal God! You alone must claim me and bestow Your grace. Your feet are my refuge.
commentary: Vallalar asks the divine to step in and take charge of the soul. God is pictured arriving on a sacred bull to save devotees and dancing in a radiant hall of gems. Yet this primal Lord is also intimately close, experienced as pure honey and sweet nectar. Total surrender means placing absolute trust at the feet of this loving master.

note: Editor's note: verse 3 is also known as a separate song, made about a wedding invitation from the house of Sabapathi Mudaliar of Chennai; the early editions (and the 1896 edition) do not include it in this poem.
translit: cīrtaru vārpukaḻp pērtaru vāraruḷ tēṉtaruvār ūrtaru vārmati yuntaru vārkati yuntaruvār ērtaru vārtaru vāroṟṟi yūrem iṟaivaraṉṟi yārtaru vārneñca mē-iṅkum aṅkum iyampukavē.
translation: He gives the name of excellent fame. He gives the honey of grace. He gives a place to live. He gives wisdom. He gives liberation. He gives beauty and eloquence. Other than our Lord of Otriyur, who else will give these, O heart? Speak of this here and there.
commentary: The Lord of Otriyur (God at the Otriyur temple) is the source of all lasting gifts. He alone grants grace, wisdom, and liberation, while the world offers nothing of real value.

translit: vāṭakkaṟ ṟāyiḵ teṉṉaineñ cēyicai vāyntacintu pāṭakkaṟ ṟāyilai poyvēṭam kaṭṭip paṭimicaikkūt tāṭakkaṟ ṟāyilai antō poruḷuṉak kārtaruvār nīṭakkaṟ ṟārpukaḻ oṟṟi-em māṉai niṉai-iṉiyē.
translation: O heart, you have only learned to wither. What is this? You have not learned to sing sweet songs. You have not learned to wear false costumes and dance on this earth. Alas, who will give you wealth? Think now of our Lord of Otriyur, praised by the deeply learned.
commentary: Worldly success often requires people to put on an act, flatter others, and play false roles. Because the sincere heart cannot do these things and suffers in poverty, it must turn to God as its only refuge.

translit: cōṭillai mēlveḷḷaic cokkāy ilainalla cōmaṉillai pāṭillai kaiyiṟ paṇamillai tēkap parumaṉillai vīṭillai yātoru vīṟāppum illai vivākamatu nāṭillai nīneñca mē-enta āṟṟiṉil naṇṇiṉaiyē.
translation: You have no companion. You have no white upper shirt and no good lower garment. You have no greatness. You have no money in hand. You have no physical strength. You have no house. You have no pride of any sort. You do not seek marriage. O heart, what path have you chosen?
commentary: Society measures a person by wealth, fine clothes, property, and family. Stripped of these worldly markers of success, Vallalar asks his heart where its unconventional path is leading.

translit: nērā aḻukkut tuṇiyākil uṉṟaṉai nērilkaṇṭum pārā tavareṉa niṟpār uṭuttatu paṭṭeṉilō vārā tiruppateṉ vārumeṉ pārinta vañcakarpāl cērātu naṉṉeñca mē-oṟṟi yūraṉaic cērviraintē.
translation: If you wear a dirty cloth, people will see you right in front of them and stand as if they did not notice you. If you wear silk, they will ask why you keep away and invite you in. Do not associate with such deceitful people. O good heart, swiftly join the Lord of Otriyur.
commentary: People judge others by outward appearance and wealth, ignoring the poor and flattering the rich. Spiritual life requires leaving behind this hypocrisy and seeking God.

translit: poyvirip pārkkup poruḷvirip pārnaṟ poruṭpayaṉām meyvirip pārkkiru kaivirip pārpeṭṭi mēvupaṇap paivirip pāralkuṟ paivirip pārkkavar pāṟparavi maivirip pāymaṉa mē-eṉko lōniṉ matiyiṉmaiyē.
translation: People give wealth to those who spread lies. They show empty hands to those who speak the truth, which is the ultimate good. They open their money boxes for women who offer their bodies. O mind, you go to such worldly men and spread your darkness. What is this foolishness of yours?
commentary: The worldly system is backward, rewarding lies and lust while turning its back on truth. It is foolish to seek help or validation from a society that values corruption over spiritual reality.

translit: vāḻaik kaṉi-uṇa māṭṭātu vāṉiṉ vaḷarntuyarnta tāḻaik kaṉi-uṇat tāvukiṉ ṟōril cayilampeṟṟa māḻaik kaṉitikaḻ vāmattem māṉtoṇṭar māṭṭakaṉṟē ēḻaik kaṉikar uḷattiṉar pāṟceṉṟa teṉṉaineñcē.
translation: O heart, why did you depart from the devotees of our Lord, who has on His left side the shining, golden-hued Lady born of the mountain? Why did you go to those with impoverished hearts, like someone who, refusing to eat the readily available plantain fruit, leaps to grasp the fruit of the tall screwpine tree that grows high into the sky?
commentary: The mind makes spiritual life harder than it needs to be. Instead of staying with sincere devotees, the heart chases worldly people who have nothing of value to offer. The sweet fruit of grace is close at hand, yet the mind leaps after things out of reach.

translit: kāyār carikaik kaliṅkamuṇ ṭēlik kaliṅkaṅkaṇṭāl nīyārniṉ pēretu niṉūr etuniṉ nilaiyetuniṉ tāyārniṉ tantai evaṉkulam ēteṉpar cāṟṟumavval vāyār iṭañcelal neñcē viṭaitara vallai-aṉṟē.
translation: O heart, if you wear garments adorned with bright gold threads, upon seeing those clothes, they will ask: "Who are you? What is your name? What is your town? What is your station in life? Who is your mother? Who is your father? What is your caste?" Do not go near those with such harsh mouths, for you do not have the ability to answer them.
commentary: Worldly society obsesses over outward appearance and social identity. If you approach people dressed in finery, they immediately demand to know your caste, your parents, and your station in life. The text warns the mind to stay completely away from those who speak with such harsh, dividing words. A sincere heart has no answer for a society that measures a person by their social status.

tamil: துட்ட வஞ்சக நெஞ்சக மேஒன்று சொல்லக் கேள்கடல் சூழ்உல கத்திலே
இட்டம் என்கொல் இறையள வேனும்ஓர் இன்பம் இல்லை இடைக்கிடை இன்னலால்
நட்ட மிக்குறல் கண்டுகண் டேங்கினை நாணு கின்றிலை நாய்க்குங் கடையைநீ
பட்ட வன்மைகள் எண்ணில் எனக்குடல் பதைக்கும் உள்ளம் பகீல்என ஏங்குமே.
translit: tuṭṭa vañcaka neñcaka mē-oṉṟu collak kēḷkaṭal cūḻula kattilē iṭṭam eṉkol iṟaiyaḷa vēṉumōr iṉpam illai iṭaikkiṭai iṉṉalāl naṭṭa mikkuṟal kaṇṭukaṇ ṭēṅkiṉai nāṇu kiṉṟilai nāykkuṅ kaṭaiyainī paṭṭa vaṉmaikaḷ eṇṇil eṉakkuṭal pataikkum uḷḷam pakīleṉa ēṅkumē.
translation: O wicked and deceitful heart, listen to what I say. Why do you have such attachment to this world surrounded by the ocean? There is not even a trace of true joy here. Seeing the immense losses brought by recurring sorrows, you grieve, yet you feel no shame. You are lower than a dog. If I recount the cruelties you have endured, my body trembles and my mind shudders in fear.
commentary: Worldly attachments bring sorrow, yet the mind continually runs back to them. There is no joy in chasing earthly desires. The heart repeatedly suffers losses and cruelties, failing to learn from its own grief. Realizing how much needless pain the mind invites upon itself causes the body to tremble in fear.

tamil: துரியநிலை அநுபவத்தைச் சுகமயமாய் எங்குமுள்ள தொன்மை தன்னை
அரியபரம் பரமான சிதம்பரத்தே நடம்புரியும் அமுதை அந்தோ
உரியபர கதிஅடைதற் குன்னினையேன் மனனேநீ உய்கு வாயே.
translit: periyaporuḷ evaikkummutaṟ perumporuḷām arumporuḷaip pēcaṟkoṇṇāt turiyanilai anupavattaic cukamayamāy eṅkumuḷḷa toṉmai taṉṉai ariyaparam paramāṉa citamparattē naṭampuriyum amutai antō uriyapara kati-aṭaitaṟ kuṉṉiṉaiyēṉ maṉaṉēnī uyku vāyē.
translation: O mind, to attain the rightful supreme state of liberation, you did not think of the rare Reality that is the primal great Substance for all great entities. You did not think of the experience of the inexpressible state of Turiya. You did not think of the ancient One who exists everywhere as pure bliss, the nectar who dances in the supreme space of Chidambaram. Alas, how will you find salvation?
commentary: Liberation requires turning toward ultimate reality. Instead of remembering the divine presence that fills everything with bliss, the mind forgets its true purpose. It ignores the stillness of Turiya (the state of spiritual consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep). Without focusing on this ancient source of grace, the heart cannot find freedom.

tamil: சொன்னிலைக்கும் பொருணிலைக்கும் தூரியதாய் ஆனந்தச் சுடராய் அன்பர்
தன்னிலைக்கும் சென்னிலைக்கும் அண்மையதாய் அருள்பழுக்கும் தருவாய் என்றும்
முன்னிலைக்கும் நின்னிலைக்கும் காண்பதரிதாய் மூவாத முதலாய்ச் சுத்த
நன்னிலைக்கும் நிலையாய பசுபதியை மனனேநீ நவின்றி டாயே.
translit: coṉṉilaikkum poruṇilaikkum tūriyatāy āṉantac cuṭarāy aṉpar taṉṉilaikkum ceṉṉilaikkum aṇmaiyatāy aruḷpaḻukkum taruvāy eṉṟum muṉṉilaikkum niṉṉilaikkum kāṇpataritāy mūvāta mutalāyc cutta naṉṉilaikkum nilaiyāya pacupatiyai maṉaṉēnī naviṉṟi ṭāyē.
translation: O mind, speak the name of Pasupati, the Lord of souls. He transcends all states of word and meaning. He is the flame of bliss. He stands close to the true nature of devotees and their righteous path. He is the tree that ripens with the fruit of grace. He remains difficult to perceive from any outward stance or from your own state. He is the ageless primal source and the firm foundation of the pure and perfect state.
commentary: True grace is beyond the reach of human language or intellectual understanding. The mind must invoke Pasupati (the Lord of all souls). While God remains hidden from those who look outward, this ageless flame of bliss stands close to anyone who walks the path of devotion. He is the foundation of reality and the living tree that yields the fruit of grace.

tamil: மண்முகத்தில் பல்விடய வாதனையால் மனனேநீ வருந்தி அந்தோ
புண்முகத்தில் சுவைவிரும்பும் எறும்பெனவா ளாநாளைப் போக்கு கின்றாய்
சண்முகத்தெம் பெருமானை ஐங்கரனை நடராஜத் தம்பி ரானை
உண்முகத்தில் கருதிஅநு பவமயமாய் இருக்கிலைநின் உணர்ச்சி என்னே.
translit: maṇmukattil palviṭaya vātaṉaiyāl maṉaṉēnī varunti antō puṇmukattil cuvaivirumpum eṟumpeṉavā ḷānāḷaip pōkku kiṉṟāy caṇmukattem perumāṉai aiṅkaraṉai naṭarājat tampi rāṉai uṇmukattil karuti-anu pavamayamāy irukkilainiṉ uṇarcci eṉṉē.
translation: O mind, you suffer from the impressions of many worldly objects on this earthly plane. Alas, you waste your days in vain like an ant seeking the taste of an open wound. You do not meditate inwardly on our six-faced Lord, the five-handed Lord, and the supreme Lord Nataraja to remain absorbed in that experience. What kind of awareness is yours?
commentary: The mind chases worldly distractions that cause suffering. Vallalar compares this to an ant drawn to an open wound, mistaking a painful injury for something sweet. Instead of wasting time on illusions, the mind must turn inward and meditate on the divine presence, seen here as Murugan (the six-faced Lord), Vinayakar (the five-handed Lord), and Nataraja (the dancing Lord).

tamil: மால்எடுத்துக் கொண்டுகரு மால்ஆகித் திரிந்தும்உளம் மாலாய்ப் பின்னும்
வால்எடுத்துக் கொண்டுநடந் தணிவிடையாய்ச் சுமக்கின்றான் மனனே நீஅக்
கால்எடுத்துக் கொண்டுசுமந் திடவிரும்பு கிலைஅந்தோ கருதும் வேதம்
நால்எடுத்துக் கொண்டுமுடி சுமப்பதையும் அறிகிலைநின் நலந்தான் என்னே.
translit: māleṭuttuk koṇṭukaru mālākit tirintumuḷam mālāyp piṉṉum vāleṭuttuk koṇṭunaṭan taṇiviṭaiyāyc cumakkiṉṟāṉ maṉaṉē nī-ak kāleṭuttuk koṇṭucuman tiṭavirumpu kilai-antō karutum vētam nāleṭuttuk koṇṭumuṭi cumappataiyum aṟikilainiṉ nalantāṉ eṉṉē.
translation: Vishnu took the form of a black boar and wandered in search of the Lord's feet. Then, his heart filled with devotion, he took on a tail and walked as a beautiful bull to carry Him. O mind, you do not desire to lift and carry those feet. Alas, you do not even realize that the four esteemed Vedas carry them upon their crowns. What is the nature of your virtue?
commentary: Even the greatest divine beings and sacred texts humble themselves to serve God. Vishnu once became a boar to search for the Creator's feet, and later became a bull to carry them. The four Vedas (ancient sacred scriptures) also hold those divine feet upon their crowns. The human mind shows foolish pride when it refuses to bow to the presence that the highest forces revere.

tamil: உலகம் ஏத்திநின் றோங்க ஓங்கிய ஒளிகொள் மன்றிடை அளிகொள்மாநடம்
இலகு சேவடிக்கே அன்பு கூர்ந்திலை ஏழை நெஞ்சே
திலக வாணுத லார்க்கு ழன்றனை தீமை யேபுரிந் தாய்வி ரிந்தனை
கலக மேகனிந்தாய் என்னை காண்நின் கடைக்க ருத்தே.
translit: ulakam ēttiniṉ ṟōṅka ōṅkiya oḷikoḷ maṉṟiṭai aḷikoḷmānaṭam ilaku cēvaṭikkē aṉpu kūrntilai ēḻai neñcē tilaka vāṇuta lārkku ḻaṉṟaṉai tīmai yēpurin tāyvi rintaṉai kalaka mēkaṉintāy eṉṉai kāṇniṉ kaṭaikka ruttē.
translation: O poor heart, you have not deepened your love for the radiant red feet performing the great dance of grace in the supreme hall of light, praised by the flourishing world. You wandered after women with bright foreheads. You committed only evil deeds and scattered your focus. You ripened only in discord. Show me your ultimate intention.
commentary: The heart scatters its energy on physical desires and harmful actions instead of focusing on the light. Grace is found in the supreme hall of light, where the divine performs a cosmic dance. By chasing passing infatuations and discord, the mind wastes its potential for love. It is time for the inner self to ask what purpose such a wandering life is meant to serve.

note: Editor's note: verses 9 and 10 are word puzzles. Verse 9: the middle letters of pakuti, takuti, vikuti (three ku) doubled make six ku, aṟuku (அறுகு, the sacred grass); their first letters give patavi (rank) and their last letters mutti (liberation): worship the Lord of the Chit Sabhai with aṟuku grass and gain the rank of liberation. Verse 10: “tā” seven times reads eḻutā (“not written”): what can we do about what was not written on our heads?
translit: vantikkum meyyaṭiyār mālaṟṟa ōrmaṉattil cantikkum eṅkaḷ cayampuvē - pantikkum vaṉmalakkaṭ ṭellām valikeṭ ṭaṟaniṉatu niṉmalakkaṇ taṇṇaruḷtāṉ nēr.
translation: Our self-manifest Lord, you appear in the singular, delusion-free minds of the true devotees who worship you. Grant the cool grace of your pure eyes so all the binding strong fetters of impurity lose their power and break away.
commentary: God reveals himself only to minds free of confusion. This cool grace alone can dissolve the hard fetters of worldly impurity trapping the soul.

translit: caṅkarā mukkaṭ cayampuvē tāḻcaṭaimēl poṅkarāt tiṅkaḷ polintōṉē - veṅkarā vāyniṉṟu piḷḷai varappāṭum vaṉtoṇṭark kāyniṉṟu canturaitta tār.
translation: O Sankara, three-eyed self-manifest Lord! You shine with a hissing serpent and the moon on your hanging matted hair. Who stood and acted as a messenger for the fierce devotee Sundarar, who sang to bring a child back from the mouth of a cruel crocodile?
commentary: Vallalar addresses Siva as Sankara (the bringer of peace) and recalls a miracle from Tamil tradition where the saint Sundarar rescued a swallowed child from a crocodile. The rhetorical question is a joyful reminder that the supreme Lord personally serves his devoted followers.

translit: nīlak kaḷaṅkoṇṭa nīṭoḷiyē nīḷkaṅkai kōlac caṭaikkaṇinta kōmaḷamē - ñālattil antō ciṟiyēṉ aruḷiṉṟi vāṭuvatu cantōṭa mōniṉ ṟaṉakku.
translation: O boundless light with a blue throat! O beautiful Lord who wears the long river Ganges on your handsome matted hair! Alas, does it bring you joy that I, a lowly one, wither in this world without your grace?
commentary: Vallalar recalls the Lord's blue throat, a mark left when Siva drank deadly cosmic poison to save the universe. By invoking this extreme act of compassion, Vallalar gently challenges God to show that same mercy to him rather than letting him wither without grace.

translit: nāṉciṟiyēṉ eṉṉiṉumin nāṉilattil nāṉceypiḻai tāṉciṟitō aṉṟulakil tāṉperitē - māṉkarattōy aṅṅaṉamē ṉumuṉ aruṭperumaik kipperumai eṅṅaṉameṉ ṟuḷḷam eḻum.
translation: Though I am a small being, the wrongs I commit in this vast world are not small. Indeed they are huge. O Lord holding a deer in your hand, even so, my heart rises to ask how this great pile of sins measures against the immense greatness of your grace.
commentary: Acknowledging his worldly faults, Vallalar measures his burden of wrongdoings against the infinite scale of divine grace. His vast pile of sins is dwarfed by God's boundless mercy. The Lord holds a deer in his hand, a traditional symbol of a restless mind that God brings to peace. Vallalar trusts his own restless heart will be saved by this grace.

translit: āvit tuṇaiyē-eṉ āramutē niṉvaṭivaip pāvittuḷ naiyēṉip pāviyēṉ - cēvittu vāḻttēṉniṉ poṉṉaṭiyil vanteṉ talaikuṉittut tāḻttēṉeṉ ceytēṉ tavam.
translation: O companion of my soul, my rare ambrosia! I am a sinner who does not meditate on your form and melt within. I do not worship and praise you. I do not come to your golden feet and bow my head low. What penance have I done?
commentary: Vallalar grieves over his failure to actively engage in worship. He lists everything he has not done: he has not meditated, praised God, or bowed his head at the golden feet of the divine. Calling God the companion of his soul, he wonders aloud if he has done any true penance at all to deserve salvation.

translit: uṉṉainiṉain tiṅkē ulāvukiṉṟēṉ aṉṟi-entāy piṉṉai niṉaippoṉṟum peṟṟilēṉ - eṉṉai viṭātēniṉ poṉṉaṭiyai mēvārcēr tuṉpam koṭātē eṉai-ēṉṟu koḷ.
translation: My Father, I wander here thinking only of you. I hold no other thought. Do not abandon me. Do not inflict on me the sorrow that falls upon those who do not reach your golden feet. Accept me.
commentary: A mind turned to God holds no room for anything else. Vallalar wanders the world with this single-minded focus, holding no thought but the divine. The only sorrow is being separated from God's presence, pictured here as the golden feet. He pleads to be spared from that pain and taken in.

translit: eṉṉaracē niṉṉaṭikkīḻ eṉṉiṭarai nīkkeṉanāṉ coṉṉatalāl tāyuṭaṉum coṉṉēṉō - iṉṉumintat tuṉpac cumaiyaic cumakkamuṭi yāteṉṉāl aṉpark karuḷvōy aruḷ.
translation: My King, I fell at your feet and asked you to remove my affliction. Did I mention this even to my mother? I can no longer bear this burden of sorrow. O Lord who grants grace to devotees, grant me your grace.
commentary: God is closer to the soul than a mother is to her child. Vallalar takes his afflictions straight to the divine feet, keeping them secret even from his family. The burden of worldly life has become too heavy to carry alone. He asks for grace, the only remedy for this exhaustion.

translit: aṉṉē-eṉ appā-eṉ āruyirkkōr ātaravē eṉṉēniṉ uḷḷam iraṅkilaiyē - poṉṉē uṭaiyā riṭai-eṉ uḷanontu vāṭik kaṭaiyēṉ paṭuntuyaraik kaṇṭu.
translation: My Mother, my Father, the sole support of my precious life, why does your heart not show pity? O golden Lord, you see the sorrow I suffer as the lowest of men, my heart aching and withering among the wealthy.
commentary: Seeking spiritual truth in a society obsessed with material wealth is isolating. Living among the wealthy who do not share his longing, Vallalar has nowhere else to turn. He cries out to God as his father and mother, begging for pity to relieve the pain of this alienation.

translit: pakuti takuti vikuti-eṉum pāṭṭil ikalil iṭaiyai iraṭṭit - takaviṉ aruccittāl muṉṉām atukaṭaiyām kaṇṭīr tirucciṟ capaiyāṉait tērntu.
translation: In the sequence of root, fitness, and suffix, if you double the middle without conflict and worship worthily, the first becomes the last. Understand this by seeking the Lord of the holy hall of wisdom.
commentary: A mystical riddle built on Tamil grammatical terms for root words, middle elements, and suffixes. Vallalar suggests that by rearranging these syllables in worthy worship, a hidden truth is revealed. He does not spell out the answer directly, stating the meaning can only be understood by seeking the Lord in the holy hall of wisdom.

translit: tātātā tātātā tākkuṟaikkeṉ ceykutumyām tātātā eṉṟulakil tāṉalaintōm - pōtātā nantā maṇiyē namaccivā yapporuḷē entāy eṉappukaḻa vē.
translation: "Give, give, give, give, give, give!" What shall we do about this poverty? We wandered the world begging others, "Give, give, give!" Is it not enough simply to praise you, calling out, "O unextinguished gem, O essence of Namashivaya, my Father"?
commentary: The world forces people into an endless cycle of begging others for survival and favors. Vallalar captures the exhaustion of constantly crying out for help from mortals. Realizing relief cannot come from worldly patrons, he finds sufficiency in praising God, calling upon the sacred mantra Namashivaya (adoration to Siva) and recognizing the divine as his provider.

translit: poykaṇṭāy kāmap putumayakkiṟ pōyuḻalak kaikaṇṭāy eṉṉapalaṉ kaṇṭāyē - meykaṇṭa poṉṉē aṉaiyārpāl pōyvaṇaṅkak kaṟṟilaiyō eṉṉēniṉ taṉmaimaṉa mē.
translation: O mind, you saw only falsehood. What benefit did you gain by wandering lost in the strange delusion of lust? You experienced it firsthand. Have you not learned to go and bow before the pure, golden ones who have realized the truth? What is this nature of yours, O mind?
commentary: Sensual desires lead the mind only to falsehood and empty results. Vallalar asks his mind why it chases physical delusions instead of seeking the company of realized saints who know the truth, reminding it that worldly lust offers no benefit.

translit: ivvaḻiyil cellātē eṉṉuṭaiyāṉ taṉṉaṭicēr avvaḻiyil celeṉ ṟaṭikkaṭikkuc - cevvaḻiyil coṉṉālum kēṭkilainī tuṭṭamaṉa mē-uṉakkiṅ keṉṉāl uṟavē tiṉi.
translation: "Do not go down this path. Walk the path that reaches the feet of my Lord." Even when I tell you this repeatedly and clearly, you do not listen, O wicked mind. What relationship do I have with you anymore?
commentary: The human mind is often a stubborn, unruly companion that refuses to listen to reason. Because his mind repeatedly ignores instructions to turn toward God and refuses the spiritual path, Vallalar declares he is severing his relationship with it.

translit: kālvāṅ kiya-uṭ katavam koḷumakattiṉ pālvāṅ kiyakāl paramparaṉē - mālvāṅ karitāram ūṇāti yāmmayalkoṇ ṭēḻaip peritāra ōrmoḻiyaip pēcu.
translation: O Supreme Lord! This poor soul is caught in the deep delusion of desiring a wife, food, and worldly things. Speak a supreme word of grace to comfort me when the breath withdraws and the inner door of this body closes.
commentary: Worldly attachments like family and food create a delusion that distracts the soul from its purpose. Vallalar asks the Supreme Lord for a final word of grace to comfort him at the critical moment of death, when breath stops and the body shuts down.

translit: āṟṟuk kēpiṟaik kīṟṟuk kēcaṭai ākkic cēvaṭi tūkki āruyirp pēṟṟukkē naṭippāy maṇimaṉṟil peruntakaiyē cōṟṟuk kē-itañ collip pētaiyar cūḻal vāyttuyar cūḻntu mēṟṟicaik kāṟṟukkē kaṟaṅkāyc cuḻaṉṟēṉaik karututiyō.
