translation: O Great One in the ruby hall, you fashioned your matted hair to hold the river and the crescent moon. You lift your red foot and dance for the salvation of precious souls. Will you think of me? I spoke pleasing words just for food, fell into the company of fools, became engulfed in sorrow, and spun like a pinwheel caught in the west wind.
commentary: Vallalar contrasts God's vast, saving grace with his own worldly distractions. Having chased his next meal by flattering fools, he feels out of control, spinning like a pinwheel in the wind. He wonders if God will still notice him in this scattered state.

translit: ñālat tārtamaip pōlat tāmiṅku naṇṇu vārniṉṉai eṇṇu vārmiku cīlattār civamē evaiyumeṉat tērntaṉarāl cālat tāṉkoṭuñ cālat tālattait tāvi nāṉperum pāvi āyiṉaṉ ēlattār kuḻalā ḷiṭattāyeṉai eṇṇutiyō.
translation: People of great virtue approach you and meditate on you here, living just like ordinary people of the world. They have realized that Sivam is everything. I have become a great sinner, embracing the cruel poison of grand illusion. O Lord who holds the lady with fragrant hair on your left side, will you think of me?
commentary: True spiritual masters often live quietly among ordinary people, carrying the realization that Sivam (the supreme reality of divine grace) is everything. Vallalar feels he is the exact opposite. Swallowing the poison of worldly illusion, he asks if the Lord will still hold him in thought.

translit: aṇṇa lēniṉṉai eṇṇa lēṉeṉṉai āṇṭu koṇṭaṉai mīṇṭum viṇṭaṉaṉ naṇṇalē aṟiyēṉ kaṭaiyēṉciṟu nāyaṉaiyēṉ peṇṇa lēṉiyal āṇa lēṉalip pēya ṉēṉkoṭum pētai yēṉpiḻai kaṇṇalē puriyā tiṉummīṭkak karututiyō.
translation: O Lord, I did not think of you. You took me under your rule, but I parted from you again. I do not know how to draw near to you. I am the lowest, like a little dog. I am not a woman. I am not a true man. I am a fiend of neither nature. I am a severe fool. Will you overlook my faults and still think to redeem me?
commentary: Vallalar begs for a second chance after turning away from the grace that once saved him. Stripping away all claims to status, dignity, or pride, he calls himself a stray dog who does not know how to approach God. Will God look past these failures and choose to redeem him anyway?

translit: valli āṉanta valli cērmaṇa vāḷa ṉē-aru ḷāḷa ṉēmalai villiyāy nakaittē puramvīḻtta viṭaiyavaṉē pulli yāṉpulaip pōkam vēṭṭuniṉ poṉṉa ṭittuṇaip pōkam pōkkiṉēṉ illi-ār kaṭampō liruntēṉeṉai eṇṇutiyō.
translation: O bridegroom united with Ananda Valli! O Lord of grace! O rider of the bull, who made the mountain your bow and burned the three cities with a laugh! I am a base person. I desired foul fleshly pleasures and lost the bliss of your twin golden feet. I sit here like a pot riddled with holes. Will you think of me?
commentary: Chasing physical pleasures leaves a person unable to hold onto grace. Vallalar traded divine bliss for base desires, comparing himself to a clay pot riddled with holes that leaks away any goodness poured in. Addressing the Lord united with Ananda Valli (the divine mother of bliss) who destroyed the mythical three cities of the demons, he asks to be remembered even as a broken vessel.

tamil: திங்கள் விளங்கும் சடைத்தருவைத் தீம்பாற் சுவையைச் செந்தேனைச்
செங்கை மருவும் செழுங்கனியைச் சீரார் முக்கட் செங்கரும்பை
மங்கை மலையாள் மணந்தபெரு வாழ்வைப் பவள மலைதன்னை
எங்கள் பெருமான் தனைஅந்தோ என்னே எண்ணா திருந்தேனே.
translit: tiṅkaḷ viḷaṅkum caṭaittaruvait tīmpāṟ cuvaiyaic centēṉaic ceṅkai maruvum ceḻuṅkaṉiyaic cīrār mukkaṭ ceṅkarumpai maṅkai malaiyāḷ maṇantaperu vāḻvaip pavaḷa malaitaṉṉai eṅkaḷ perumāṉ taṉai-antō eṉṉē eṇṇā tiruntēṉē.
translation: The tree of matted hair where the moon shines, the taste of sweet milk, the pure honey, the rich fruit held in the red hands, the excellent three-eyed red sugarcane, the great life wedded to the mountain's daughter, the coral mountain, our great Lord. Alas, why did I remain without thinking of Him?
commentary: Vallalar describes the divine presence in terms of pure sweetness, calling God milk, honey, rich fruit, and sugarcane. He pairs these sweet tastes with familiar images of Siva, such as the moon in his matted hair and his marriage to the mountain goddess Parvati. Vallalar asks himself how he could have possibly forgotten a Lord who offers such rich spiritual nourishment.

tamil: அன்பர் இதய மலர்க்கோயில் அமர்ந்த பரமா னந்தத்தைத்
துன்பம் அகலச் சுகமளிக்கும் தூய துணையைச் சுயஞ்சுடரை
வன்ப ரிடத்தின் மருவாத மணியை மணியார் மிடற்றானை
இன்ப நிறைவை இறையோனை என்னே எண்ணா திருந்தேனே.
translit: aṉpar itaya malarkkōyil amarnta paramā ṉantattait tuṉpam akalac cukamaḷikkum tūya tuṇaiyaic cuyañcuṭarai vaṉpa riṭattiṉ maruvāta maṇiyai maṇiyār miṭaṟṟāṉai iṉpa niṟaivai iṟaiyōṉai eṉṉē eṇṇā tiruntēṉē.
translation: The supreme bliss seated in the flower temple of the devotees' hearts, the pure companion who dispels sorrow and grants comfort, the self-luminous light, the gem who does not approach the hard-hearted, the one with a gem-like throat, the fullness of joy, the sovereign. Why did I remain without thinking of Him?
commentary: God dwells within the loving hearts of devotees, acting as a pure companion who removes sorrow and brings perfect bliss. Vallalar notes that this divine light avoids the hard-hearted entirely. True connection requires a tender, compassionate heart, and Vallalar laments ever losing sight of this joyful inner presence.

tamil: ஒருமைப் பயனை ஒருமைநெறி உணர்ந்தார் உணர்வின் உள்ளுணர்வைப்
பெருமைக் கதியைப் பசுபதியைப் பெரியோர் எவர்க்கும் பெரியோனை
அருமைக் களத்தில் கருமைஅணி அம்மான் தன்னை எம்மானை
இருமைப் பயனுந் தருவானை என்னே எண்ணா திருந்தேனே.
translit: orumaip payaṉai orumaineṟi uṇarntār uṇarviṉ uḷḷuṇarvaip perumaik katiyaip pacupatiyaip periyōr evarkkum periyōṉai arumaik kaḷattil karumai-aṇi ammāṉ taṉṉai emmāṉai irumaip payaṉun taruvāṉai eṉṉē eṇṇā tiruntēṉē.
translation: The fruit of unity, the inner awareness within the awareness of those who know the path of unity, the exalted refuge, the Lord of souls, the one greater than all the great ones, the father who wears blackness on his precious throat, my Lord, the one who grants the fruits of both worlds. Why did I remain without thinking of Him?
commentary: God is discovered through the path of unity, revealing himself as deep inner awareness. The dark mark on Siva's throat refers to the classic story of him swallowing poison to save the world, a symbol of supreme compassion.

tamil: கறையோர் கண்டத் தணிந்தருளும் கருணா நிதியைக் கண்ணுதலை
மறையோன் நெடுமாற் கரியசிவ மலையை அலையில் வாரிதியைப்
பொறையோர் உள்ளம் புகுந்தொளிரும் புனித ஒளியைப் பூரணனாம்
இறையோன் தன்னை அந்தோநான் என்னே எண்ணா திருந்தேனே.
translit: kaṟaiyōr kaṇṭat taṇintaruḷum karuṇā nitiyaik kaṇṇutalai maṟaiyōṉ neṭumāṟ kariyaciva malaiyai alaiyil vāritiyaip poṟaiyōr uḷḷam pukuntoḷirum puṉita oḷiyaip pūraṇaṉām iṟaiyōṉ taṉṉai antōnāṉ eṉṉē eṇṇā tiruntēṉē.
translation: The treasure of compassion who gracefully wears the dark stain on his throat, the one with a forehead eye, the Siva mountain difficult for Brahma and tall Vishnu to comprehend, the waveless ocean, the pure light that enters and shines in the hearts of the patient, the perfect sovereign. Alas, why did I remain without thinking of Him?
commentary: God is a pure light that makes its home only in patient, compassionate hearts. This presence is beyond the understanding of even the great gods Brahma and Vishnu. Vallalar likens the divine to a still, waveless ocean, wondering how anyone could forget such a vast truth.

translit: viti-e lāmvilak keṉavilak kiṭuvēṉ vilakke lāṅkoṇṭu viti-eṉa vitippēṉ niti-e lāmpeṟa niṉaitteḻu kiṉṟēṉ nilame lāṅkoḷum niṉaippuṟu kiṉṟēṉ eti-e lāmveṟut tiṭṭaciṟ ṟūḻai iṉpe lāṅkoḷa eṇṇiniṉ ṟayarvēṉ pati-e lāṅkaṭan tevvaṇam uyvēṉ parama rāciyap paramparap poruḷē.
translation: I reject all prescribed rules as prohibitions. I take all prohibitions and establish them as rules. I rise up with the thought of acquiring all wealth. I harbor thoughts of possessing all lands. I stand exhausted, hoping to reap every pleasure from this petty worldly life that ascetics have completely rejected. How will I cross all realms and find salvation, O Supreme Reality of the ultimate secret?
commentary: Vallalar confesses to a mind in rebellion against spiritual discipline. Reversing rules and prohibitions, he is exhausted from squeezing pleasure out of the worldly life that ascetics have abandoned. He asks the divine reality how someone so trapped by greed can ever reach spiritual freedom.

translit: ceṭiya ṉēṉkaṭun tīmaiyē purivēṉ teḷivi lēṉmaṉac ceṟiveṉpa taṟiyēṉ koṭiya ṉēṉkoṭuṅ kolaipayil iṉattēṉ kōḷa ṉēṉneṭu nīḷavañ cakaṉēṉ aṭiya ṉēṉpiḻai aṉaittaiyum poṟuttuṉ aṉpar taṅkaḷō ṭiṉpuṟa aruḷvāy paṭi-a ṉēkamuṅ kaṭantaciṟ capaiyil parama rāciyap paramparap poruḷē.
translation: I am a sinner. I commit only harsh evil. I lack clarity. I do not know mental focus. I am cruel. I am of those who practise cruel murder. I am treacherous. I am an endless deceiver. Forgive all the faults of this devotee. Grant your grace so I may rejoice in the company of your lovers, O Supreme Reality of the ultimate secret in the Chit Sabhai that transcends countless worlds.
commentary: Vallalar lists his deepest faults, calling himself cruel, deceitful, and entirely lacking in mental focus. He counts himself among those who practise cruel murder (kolai). This points directly to Vallalar's core teaching of Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings): the murder of any living being bars the way to God. He begs the divine in the Chit Sabhai (the Hall of Consciousness) to forgive these terrible sins and grant him a place among true devotees.

translit: tiruvuḷan teriyēṉ tikaippuṟu kiṉṟēṉ ciṟiyariṟ ciṟiyaṉēṉ vañcak karuvuḷak kaṭaiyēṉ pāviyēṉ koṭiya kaṉmaṉak kuraṅkaṉēṉ antō veruvuṟu kiṉṟēṉ añcaleṉ ṟiṉṉē virumpi-āṭ koḷḷutal vēṇṭum maruvumā karuṇaip peruṅkaṭal amutē vaḷḷalē eṉperu vāḻvē.
translation: I do not know Your divine will. I stand bewildered. I am the smallest of the small. I am the lowest of the low with a deceitful core. I am a sinner. I am a monkey with a cruel, stony heart. Alas, I am terrified. You must willingly take me under Your rule right now, saying, "Do not fear." O nectar of the great, vast ocean of grace! O Benefactor! O my great life!
commentary: Vallalar confesses feeling unworthy. Stripped of pride, he stands terrified by his own flaws and asks for immediate rescue, pleading for the divine reassurance of "Do not fear."

translit: tāyum tantaiyum teyvamum kuruvum tāṅku kiṉṟatōr talaivaṉum poruḷum āyum iṉpamum aṉpummey aṟivum aṉaittum nī-eṉa ātarit tiruntēṉ ēyum eṉṉaḷa virakkamoṉ ṟilaiyēl eṉcey vēṉitai yārkkeṭut turaippēṉ cēyum niṉṉaruḷ nacai-uṟuṅ kaṇṭāy tillai maṉṟiṭait tikaḻoḷi viḷakkē.
translation: Mother, father, God, Guru, the Lord who sustains me, wealth, exquisite joy, love, and true knowledge: I sought refuge in You, knowing You are all these things. If You have no compassion for me, what will I do? To whom will I tell this? Look, this child longs for Your grace. O shining lamp of light in the hall of Thillai!
commentary: God is the single source of every relationship and comfort we seek in the world. Having placed all his trust in this divine presence, Vallalar asks where a child could go if denied compassion. His devotion leaves no backup plan if grace is withheld. Thillai is the ancient name for the sacred town of Chidambaram, representing the core of cosmic awareness.

translit: aruḷpaḻut tōṅkum kaṟpakat taruvē aruṇmarun toḷirkuṇak kuṉṟē aruḷeṉum amutan tarumoru kaṭalē aruṭkira ṇaṅkoḷum cuṭarē aruḷoḷi vīcum arumpeṟaṉ maṇiyē aruṭcuvai kaṉintacem pākē aruḷmaṇam vīcum orutaṉi malarē aruṇmaya māmpara civamē.
translation: O wish-fulfilling tree that grows tall and ripens with grace! O shining mountain of virtues, the medicine of grace! O unique ocean that yields the nectar of grace! O flame possessing rays of grace! O rare, precious gem radiating the light of grace! O perfect syrup ripened with the sweet taste of grace! O incomparable solitary flower radiating the fragrance of grace! O transcendent Supreme Being entirely filled with grace!
commentary: Every image is saturated with divine grace, known in Tamil as arul. The supreme being is made of this grace. The repetition creates a cascading feeling of abundance, showing that at the highest level of spiritual vision, there is nothing left to experience except grace itself.

note: Editor's note: this poem mixes metres; a new metre is named above the verse it begins. Verses 48 to 57 are not in the 1896 edition. Verse 57 is a puzzle on āvi (ஆவி) and īraintu (ஈரைந்து, “ten”): chanting with ya (the soul’s letter) placed after Si removes calamities, ends the five impurities and brings devotion.
translit: nīrpūtta vēṇiyum āṉantam pūttu niṟaimatiyiṉ cīrpūt tamuta iḷanakai pūtta tirumukamum pārpūtta paccaip pacuṅkoṭi pūttacem pākamumōr kārpūtta kaṇṭamum kaṇpūtta kālumeṉ kaṇviruntē.
translation: The matted hair blooming with the river, the divine face blooming with bliss and the radiance of the full moon alongside a nectar-like tender smile, the red half blooming with the green creeper of the Goddess who brought forth the earth, the neck blooming with dark cloud-like poison, and the feet blooming with eyes of grace constitute a feast for my eyes.
commentary: The divine form is a vivid, blooming vision of grace. Every traditional feature of Siva, from the river flowing through his hair to the green form of the Goddess sharing his body, becomes a visual feast.

translit: vīḻāka ñāṉṟacev vēṇip pirāṉeṉ viṉai-iraṇṭum kīḻāka nāṉataṉ mēlāka neñcak kilēcamellām pāḻāka iṉpam payirāka vāykkilap pāṟpiṟavi ēḻāka aṉṟimaṟ ṟeṭṭāka iṅkeṉṉai eṉceyumē.
translation: If the Lord with red matted hair hanging down like aerial roots causes my two karmas to stay beneath me and places me above them, destroying all the afflictions of my heart and cultivating joy as a crop, then what does it matter if my subsequent births number seven or eight? What harm can they do to me here?
commentary: When divine grace lifts a person above the burden of past actions, the fear of future lifetimes vanishes. The two karmas are the accumulated results of good and bad deeds, which usually bind the soul to endless rebirths. If the heart is filled with spiritual joy, the cycle of birth and death loses its power to harm.

translit: āyiraṅ kārmukil nīrviḻi nīrtara aiyaniṉpāl cēyiraṅ kāreṉak keṉṟēniṉ poṟpatam cintikkiṉṟēṉ nī-iraṅ kāyeṉil eṉceyku vēṉin nilattiṟpeṟṟa tāyiraṅ kāḷeṉpa tuṇṭōtaṉ piḷḷai taḷarccikaṇṭē.
translation: With eyes shedding tears like a thousand dark rain clouds, O Lord, I meditate on Your golden feet, realizing that others will not pity this child. If You do not show mercy, what will I do? Is it ever said in this world that a mother who bore a child refuses to show mercy when she sees her child's distress?
commentary: The relationship between the soul and God is compared to a child crying for its mother. Recognizing that the world offers no real comfort, Vallalar sheds tears like heavy rain, trusting that a true mother can never ignore her child's distress.

translit: cempavaḷat taṉikkuṉṟē aruḷā ṉantac ceḻuṅkaṉiyē mukkaṇuṭait tēvē mūvā ampuvinīr aṉalvaḷivāṉ āti yāya aracē-eṉ āruyirkkōr araṇa mākum campuciva cayampuvē caṅka rāveṇ cailamvaḷar teyvatavāṉ taruvē mikka vampaviḻmeṉ kuḻalorupāl viḷaṅka ōṅkum maḻaviṭaimēl varuṅkāṭci vaḻaṅku vāyē.
translation: O unique mountain of red coral! O lush fruit of blissful grace! O three-eyed God! O King who became the primal elements of eternal earth, water, fire, wind, and sky! O Sambhu, Siva, Svayambhu, and Sankara who stands as a fortress for my precious life! O divine celestial tree growing on the white mountain! Grant me the vision of You arriving on the lofty young bull, with the Goddess whose soft fragrant hair blossoms shining on one side.
commentary: God is addressed as the origin of all physical elements and the protector of life. Sambhu, Siva, Svayambhu, and Sankara are traditional titles praising the divine as the self-created source of peace and goodness. Vallalar begs for a direct vision of this supreme reality, asking to see the Lord and Goddess arriving together.

tamil: நீடுகின்ற மாமறையும் நெடுமாலும் திசைமுகனும் நிமல வாழ்க்கை
நாடுகின்ற முனிவரரும் உருத்திரரும் தேடஅருள் நாட்டங் கொண்டு
பாடுகின்ற மெய்யடியர் உளம்விரும்பி ஆநந்தப் படிவ மாகி
ஆடுகின்ற மாமணியை ஆரமுதை நினைந்துநினைந் தன்பு செய்வாம்.
translit: nīṭukiṉṟa māmaṟaiyum neṭumālum ticaimukaṉum nimala vāḻkkai nāṭukiṉṟa muṉivararum uruttirarum tēṭa-aruḷ nāṭṭaṅ koṇṭu pāṭukiṉṟa meyyaṭiyar uḷamvirumpi ānantap paṭiva māki āṭukiṉṟa māmaṇiyai āramutai niṉaintuniṉain taṉpu ceyvām.
translation: While the enduring great Vedas, the great Vishnu, the four-faced Brahma, the Rudras, and the sages seeking a pure life all search for Him, He fixes His gaze of grace upon the true devotees who sing His praise. Desiring their hearts, He takes a form of bliss. Let us constantly think of that dancing great gem, that rare nectar, and shower our love upon Him.
commentary: The highest gods and the oldest scriptures search endlessly for the supreme truth without finding it. Yet the divine freely reveals itself to devotees who sing with pure love. True connection to God is found through affection and a devoted heart, rather than through grand spiritual quests.

tamil: மறைமுடி விளக்கே போற்றி மாணிக்க மலையே போற்றி
கறைமணி கண்ட போற்றி கண்ணுதற் கரும்பே போற்றி
பிறைமுடிச் சடைகொண் டோங்கும் பேரருட் குன்றே போற்றி
சிறைதவிர்த் தெனையாட் கொண்ட சிவசிவ போற்றி போற்றி.
translit: maṟaimuṭi viḷakkē pōṟṟi māṇikka malaiyē pōṟṟi kaṟaimaṇi kaṇṭa pōṟṟi kaṇṇutaṟ karumpē pōṟṟi piṟaimuṭic caṭaikoṇ ṭōṅkum pēraruṭ kuṉṟē pōṟṟi ciṟaitavirt teṉaiyāṭ koṇṭa civaciva pōṟṟi pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the lamp at the crown of the Vedas! Praise to the mountain of rubies! Praise to the Lord with the dark-gem throat! Praise to the sweet sugarcane with an eye on the forehead! Praise to the hill of great grace rising with matted locks bearing the crescent moon! Praise, praise to Siva Siva, who dispelled my imprisonment and took me as his own!
commentary: God is addressed as the final truth of the ancient scriptures (the Vedas) and praised for classic attributes: the throat darkened by swallowing poison to save the world, the crescent moon in his matted hair, and the third eye of wisdom. Through these familiar forms, Vallalar expresses gratitude for the grace that freed him from the prison of worldly illusion.

translit: ceyvakai aṟiyēṉ maṉṟuṇmā maṇiniṉ tiruvuḷak kuṟippaiyun teriyēṉ uyvakai aṟiyēṉ uṇarvilēṉ antō uṟukaṇmēl uṟuṅkoleṉ ṟulaintēṉ meyvakai aṭaiyēṉ vēṟevark kuraippēṉ viṉaiyaṉēṉ eṉceya viraikēṉ poyvakai uṭaiyēṉ eṅṅaṉam pukukēṉ pulaiyaṉēṉ pukalaṟi yēṉē.
translation: I do not know what to do. O great gem in the Hall, I do not understand the intention of your divine will. I do not know the way to salvation. I have no awareness. Alas, I tremble wondering if suffering will pile upon suffering. I do not attain the state of truth. To whom else shall I speak? I am bound by karma. What shall I rush to do? I possess a false nature. How will I enter? I am lowly and know no refuge.
commentary: Total surrender often begins with an honest admission of helplessness. Stripped of confidence, Vallalar confesses his ignorance, his fears of endless suffering, and the heavy burden of his past actions (karma). He stands before divine grace feeling false and unworthy, yet brings this exact brokenness directly to God. True refuge is found when we realize we have nowhere else to go.

tamil: நிதியைநினைந் துனைமறந்த மதியைநினைந் தழுகேனோ நிமலா னந்தக்
கதியைஇகழ்ந் திருள்விழைந்த விதியைநினைந் தழுகேனோ கண்போல் வாய்ந்த
பதியைஉனைப் பாடாத பாட்டைநினைந் தழுகேனோ படிற்று நெஞ்சச்
சதியைநினைந் தழுகேனோ யாதுகுறித் தழுகேன்இத் தமிய னேனே.
translit: nitiyainiṉain tuṉaimaṟanta matiyainiṉain taḻukēṉō nimalā ṉantak katiyai-ikaḻn tiruḷviḻainta vitiyainiṉain taḻukēṉō kaṇpōl vāynta patiyai-uṉaip pāṭāta pāṭṭainiṉain taḻukēṉō paṭiṟṟu neñcac catiyainiṉain taḻukēṉō yātukuṟit taḻukēṉit tamiya ṉēṉē.
translation: Shall I weep thinking of the mind that forgot you while thinking of wealth? Shall I weep thinking of the fate that despised the path of pure bliss and desired darkness? Shall I weep thinking of the poetry that fails to sing of you, the Lord who is as precious as an eye? Shall I weep thinking of the treachery of my deceitful heart? Over what shall I weep, a lonely wretch?
commentary: The regret here is raw and directed inward. Looking back, Vallalar sees how his mind chased wealth instead of divine truth, how his choices favored the darkness of ignorance over pure joy, and how even his poetry failed to praise God. He realizes his own heart has betrayed him at every turn. He mourns the inner habits that keep the soul separated from grace.

tamil: தாய்தடை என்றேன் பின்னர்த் தாரமே தடைஎன் றேன்நான்
சேய்தடை என்றேன் இந்தச் சிறுதடை எல்லாந் தீர்ந்தும்
தோய்தடைச் சிறியேன் இன்னுந் துறந்திலேன் எனைத் தடுக்க
ஏய்தடை யாதோ எந்தாய் என்செய்கேன் என்செய் கேனே.
translit: tāytaṭai eṉṟēṉ piṉṉart tāramē taṭai-eṉ ṟēṉnāṉ cēytaṭai eṉṟēṉ intac ciṟutaṭai ellān tīrntum tōytaṭaic ciṟiyēṉ iṉṉun tuṟantilēṉ eṉait taṭukka ēytaṭai yātō entāy eṉceykēṉ eṉcey kēṉē.
translation: I said my mother was a hindrance. Then I said my wife was a hindrance. I said my children were a hindrance. Even after all these small hindrances ended, I, a lowly one bound by attachments, have still not renounced the world. What is the hindrance that stops me now? O my Father, what will I do? What will I do?
commentary: It is a common human habit to blame family obligations for our lack of spiritual progress. Vallalar admits he used his mother, wife, and children as excuses for remaining tangled in the material world. Now that those external ties are gone, he realizes he is still bound by his inner attachments. The real obstacle was never the people around him; it was his own mind.

translit: eṇkaṭanta uyirkaḷtoṟum oḷiyāy mēvi iruntaruḷum peruvāḻvē iṟaiyē niṉṟaṉ viṇkaṭanta perumpatattai virumpēṉ tūymai virumpukilēṉ niṉaruḷai viḻainti lēṉnāṉ peṇkaṭanta mayaleṉumōr muruṭṭup pēyāṟ piṭi-uṇṭēṉ aṭi-uṇṭa piñcu pōṉṟēṉ kaṇkaṭanta kuruṭṭūmar kataipōl niṉcīr kaṇṭuraippal eṉkēṉō kaṭaiya ṉēṉē.
translation: O great life, O Lord who gracefully abides as the light in countless souls! I do not desire the great realm beyond the heavens. I do not desire purity. I have not longed for your grace. I am seized by a crude demon of extreme delusion over women. I am like a bruised tender fruit. Will I, the lowliest wretch, claim to have seen and spoken of your glory like the tale of a blind and mute person?
commentary: God is present as a guiding light within every living soul, yet Vallalar feels disconnected from this inner truth. He confesses to being consumed by worldly desires, comparing himself to a delicate fruit that has been bruised and ruined. Because his life is dominated by delusion rather than a longing for grace, he feels fraudulent speaking of God's glory. He asks how someone who is spiritually blind and mute can claim to witness the divine.

translit: miṉṉaip pōliṭai meliya lāreṉṟē viṭattaip pōlvarum vemmaṉap pēykaḷaip poṉṉaip pōlmikap pōṟṟi iṭainaṭup puḻaiyi lēviral pōtappu kutti-īt taṉṉaip pōlmuṭai nāṟṟacca lattaiyē canta ṉaccalan tāṉeṉak koḷkiṉṟēṉ eṉṉaip pōlvatu nāykkulam taṉṉilum illai alla tevaṟṟiṉum illaiyē.
translation: Believing them to be gentle women with waists like lightning, I praise those cruel-minded demons, who come like poison, as though they were fine gold. Inserting my fingers into the central hole, I treat that foul-smelling fluid, which stinks of dead flies, as if it were sandalwood water. There is no one like me even among the race of dogs or in any other species.
commentary: Lust is a delusion that mistakes physical foulness for sweet fragrance. Vallalar looks back in intense disgust at his past desires. He describes physical attraction as a trap that makes a person behave worse than a wandering dog. He uses shocking imagery to break the illusion of physical beauty and expose the reality of the flesh.

tamil: கள்உருகும் மலர்மணம்போல் கலந்தெங்கும் நிறைந்தோய்நின் கருணைக் கந்தோ
முள்உருகும் வலியபராய் முருடுருகும் உருகாத முறைசேர் கல்லும்
வள்உருகும் மலைஉருகும் மண்உருகும் மரம்உருகும் மதியி லேன்றன்
உள்உருகும் வகையிலைஎன் செய்கேன்நான் ஏன்பிறந்தேன் ஒதிய னேனே.
translit: kaḷurukum malarmaṇampōl kalanteṅkum niṟaintōyniṉ karuṇaik kantō muḷurukum valiyaparāy muruṭurukum urukāta muṟaicēr kallum vaḷurukum malai-urukum maṇurukum maramurukum matiyi lēṉṟaṉ uḷurukum vakaiyilai-eṉ ceykēṉnāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ otiya ṉēṉē.
translation: O Lord who pervades everywhere, mingling like the fragrance of a honey-dripping flower. Alas, by your grace, a thorn melts. Hard wood melts. Unmelting stone melts. Sharp iron melts. A mountain melts. Earth melts. A tree melts. But there is no way for the inner heart of this senseless person to melt. What will I do? Why was I born as such an ignorant fool?
commentary: God's grace is powerful enough to melt solid stone, sharp iron, and entire mountains. Yet Vallalar feels sorrow because his own heart remains unyielding to that same divine presence. He wonders why he was born if he cannot feel the softening power of grace that transforms the hardest things in nature.

tamil: மன்உயிர்க்குத் தாய்தந்தை குருதெய்வம் உறவுமுதல் மற்றும் நீயே
மின்உடற்குத் தாய்தந்தை யாதியரை மதித்தேனோ விரும்பி னேனோ
என்உயிர்க்குத் துணைவாநின் ஆணைஒன்றும் அறியேன்நான் இரங்கி டாயே.
translit: maṉuyirkkut tāytantai kuruteyvam uṟavumutal maṟṟum nīyē piṉuyirkkōr tuṇaivēṟu piṟitilai-eṉ ṟiyāṉaṟinta piṉpoyyāṉa miṉuṭaṟkut tāytantai yātiyarai matittēṉō virumpi ṉēṉō eṉuyirkkut tuṇaivāniṉ āṇai-oṉṟum aṟiyēṉnāṉ iraṅki ṭāyē.
translation: For the eternal soul, You alone are mother, father, guru, God, relative, and all else. After I realized there is no other companion for the soul, did I respect or desire the mother, father, and others connected to this false body that flashes like lightning? O companion of my soul, I swear by Your command, I know nothing else. Please show me mercy.
commentary: God is the soul's only true family, teacher, and companion. Earthly parents and relatives belong only to the physical body, which vanishes as quickly as a flash of lightning. Having realized this truth, Vallalar swears he no longer places his hope in human relationships. He asks only for divine mercy, knowing God is the only bond that lasts forever.

tamil: மாற்றரிய பசும்பொன்னே மணியேஎன் கண்ணேகண் மணியே யார்க்குந்
தோற்றரிய சுயஞ்சுடரே ஆனந்தச் செழுந்தேனே சோதி யேநீ
போற்றரிய சிறியேனைப் புறம்விடினும் வேற்றவர்பாற் போகேன் வேதம்
தேற்றரிய திருவடிக்கண் பழிவிளைப்பேன் நின்ஆணைச் சிறிய னேனே.
translit: māṟṟariya pacumpoṉṉē maṇiyē-eṉ kaṇṇēkaṇ maṇiyē yārkkun tōṟṟariya cuyañcuṭarē āṉantac ceḻuntēṉē cōti yēnī pōṟṟariya ciṟiyēṉaip puṟamviṭiṉum vēṟṟavarpāṟ pōkēṉ vētam tēṟṟariya tiruvaṭikkaṇ paḻiviḷaippēṉ niṉāṇaic ciṟiya ṉēṉē.
translation: O pure gold of unchangeable quality, O gem, O my eye, O pupil of my eye. O self-effulgent flame hard for anyone to perceive, O rich honey of bliss, O Jothi. Even if You cast away this low person who cannot adequately praise You, I will not go to others. I will bring blame upon Your holy feet, which even the Vedas struggle to understand. I swear by Your command, I am only a lowly person.
commentary: True devotion means refusing to seek comfort elsewhere, even if God seems to reject you. Vallalar addresses the divine light directly as Jothi, calling it his very eyesight and greatest treasure. He warns God that if he is cast aside, he will never turn to another deity. Instead, he will stay and lay the blame for his ruin at God's own feet.

tamil: உள்உணர்வோர் உளத்துநிறைந் தூற்றெழுந்த தெள்ளமுதே உடையாய் வஞ்ச
நள்உணர்வேன் சிறிதேனும் நலமறியேன் வெறித்துழலும் நாயிற் பொல்லேன்
வெள்உணர்வேன் எனினும்என்னை விடுதியோ விடுதியேல் வேறென் செய்கேன்
தள்உணர்வோன் எனினும்மகன் தனைஈன்றோர் புறம்பாகத் தள்ளார் அன்றே.
translit: uḷuṇarvōr uḷattuniṟain tūṟṟeḻunta teḷḷamutē uṭaiyāy vañca naḷuṇarvēṉ ciṟitēṉum nalamaṟiyēṉ veṟittuḻalum nāyiṟ pollēṉ veḷuṇarvēṉ eṉiṉumeṉṉai viṭutiyō viṭutiyēl vēṟeṉ ceykēṉ taḷuṇarvōṉ eṉiṉummakaṉ taṉai-īṉṟōr puṟampākat taḷḷār aṉṟē.
translation: O clear nectar springing up and filling the hearts of those who realize You within. O Master. I harbor deceitful thoughts. I know not the slightest good. I am worse than a dog wandering aimlessly. I possess only shallow understanding. Even so, will You abandon me? If You abandon me, what else will I do? Even if a son has a rejecting mind, the parents who bore him will never cast him away.
commentary: God will never abandon a soul, just as loving parents will never throw away a difficult child. Vallalar confesses his flaws, admitting his mind is deceitful, wandering, and shallow. Despite feeling unworthy, he claims his right to divine protection based on this eternal family bond. He knows no matter how stubbornly a child behaves, true parents will always provide a home.

tamil: கலைபயின்று நெறிஒழுகும் கருத்துடையேன் அலன்நின்னைக் கனவி லேனும்
மலைபயின்ற பெருங்குணத்தெம் வள்ளலே எனத்துதியேன் வஞ்ச மில்லா
நிலைபயின்ற நல்லோர்தம் நேசமிலேன் கைதவமே நினைப்பேன் அந்தோ
உலைபயின்ற அரக்கெனநெஞ் சுருகேன்நான் ஏன்பிறந்தேன் ஒதிய னேனே.
translit: kalaipayiṉṟu neṟi-oḻukum karuttuṭaiyēṉ alaṉniṉṉaik kaṉavi lēṉum malaipayiṉṟa peruṅkuṇattem vaḷḷalē eṉattutiyēṉ vañca millā nilaipayiṉṟa nallōrtam nēcamilēṉ kaitavamē niṉaippēṉ antō ulaipayiṉṟa arakkeṉaneñ curukēṉnāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ otiya ṉēṉē.
translation: I do not have the intention to study the arts and walk the righteous path. Even in a dream, I do not praise you or cry out to our Lord of great mountain-like virtues. I lack the friendship of good people established in a guileless state. I think only of deceit. Alas, I do not melt in heart like lac in a forge. Why was I born, an ignorant fool?
commentary: Vallalar laments feeling empty of spiritual merit. He confesses he lacks knowledge, righteous behavior, and the company of good people. Worst of all, he feels his heart is too hard to melt with love for the divine, leaving him to wonder why he was born.

tamil: இரும்புன்னை மலர்ச்சடையாய் இவ்வுலகில் சிலர்தங்கட் கென்று வாய்த்த
அரும்பின்னை மார்பகத்தோன் அயனாதி சிறுதெய்வ மரபென் றோதும்
கரும்பொன்னைச் செம்பொன்னில் கைவிடா திருக்கின்றார் கடைய னேற்கே
தரும்பொன்னை மாற்றழிக்கும் அரும்பொன்நீ கிடைத்தும்உனைத் தழுவி லேனே.
translit: irumpuṉṉai malarccaṭaiyāy ivvulakil cilartaṅkaṭ keṉṟu vāytta arumpiṉṉai mārpakattōṉ ayaṉāti ciṟuteyva marapeṉ ṟōtum karumpoṉṉaic cempoṉṉil kaiviṭā tirukkiṉṟār kaṭaiya ṉēṟkē tarumpoṉṉai māṟṟaḻikkum arumpoṉnī kiṭaittumuṉait taḻuvi lēṉē.
translation: O Lord with matted hair adorned with dark punnai flowers! In this world, some people hold onto the lineage of minor deities like Brahma and Vishnu who keeps Pinnai on his chest. They never let go of that lesser brass for pure gold. For me, the lowest one, you are the rare gold that surpasses all given gold in purity. Yet even after finding you, I do not embrace you.
commentary: Vallalar explicitly calls traditional gods like Brahma and Vishnu minor deities, comparing their worship to holding onto cheap brass when pure gold is available. He teaches that the supreme divine is the only true gold. Yet he mourns his own spiritual weakness, asking how he can know this highest truth and still fail to embrace it.

tamil: கஞ்சமலர்த் தவிசிருந்த நான்முகனும் நெடுமாலும் கருதிப் போற்ற
அஞ்சநடை அம்மைகண்டு களிக்கப்பொன் அம்பலத்தில் ஆடு கின்ற
எஞ்சல்இலாப் பரம்பொருளே என்குருவே ஏழையினே னிடத்து நீயும்
வஞ்சம்நினைத் தனையாயில் என்செய்வேன் என்செய்வேன் மதியி லேனே.
translit: kañcamalart tavicirunta nāṉmukaṉum neṭumālum karutip pōṟṟa añcanaṭai ammaikaṇṭu kaḷikkappoṉ ampalattil āṭu kiṉṟa eñcalilāp paramporuḷē eṉkuruvē ēḻaiyiṉē ṉiṭattu nīyum vañcamniṉait taṉaiyāyil eṉceyvēṉ eṉceyvēṉ matiyi lēṉē.
translation: The four-faced Brahma seated on the lotus and tall Vishnu mindfully praise you. As the Goddess with a swan-like gait watches and rejoices, you dance in the golden hall. O flawless Supreme Reality! My Guru! If you harbor deceitful intentions toward me, this poor soul, what will I do? What will I do, I the mindless one?
commentary: The supreme Lord is so great that even the major gods of tradition worship him as he dances in the golden hall. Facing this reality, Vallalar feels helpless. He pleads for grace, crying out that if his guide and master turns away, a poor soul like him will have nowhere else to go.

translit: vēmpukkum taṇṇiya nīrviṭu kiṉṟaṉar vevviṭañcēr pāmpukkum pāluṇa vīkiṉ ṟaṉarip paṭimicaiyāṉ vīmpukkum tīmpukkum āṉēṉ eṉiṉum viṭēleṉainī tēmpukkum vārcaṭait tēvē karuṇaic civakkoḻuntē.
translation: They pour cool water even for the bitter neem tree. On this earth, they feed milk even to the snake bearing harsh poison. I am bound to stubborn pride and evil ways. Even so, do not abandon me. O God with long matted hair dripping with honey! O tender flame of compassionate Siva!
commentary: People in this world care for things that are bitter or dangerous, watering the harsh neem tree and feeding milk to venomous snakes. Vallalar asks God to show him the same unearned mercy. Even though he is full of stubborn pride and harmful ways, he begs the compassionate divine to treat him with protective care and never let him go.

translit: aṭamuṭi yātupal āṟṟālum ēḻaik kaṭuttatuṉpam paṭamuṭi yāteṉṉai ceykēṉeṉ taṉmukam pārttiraṅkāy tiṭamuṭi yālayaṉ mālvaṇaṅ kuntuṇaic cēvaṭiyāy taṭamuṭi yāyceñ caṭaimuṭi yāynan tayānitiyē.
translation: The sorrow afflicting this poor soul cannot be contained by any means. It cannot be endured. What will I do? Look at my face and show mercy. You have the paired red feet that Brahma and Vishnu worship with their firm heads. O Lord with a broad crown! O Lord with a crown of red matted hair! Our treasure of compassion!
commentary: The pain of spiritual separation has become too heavy to carry. Vallalar begs the Lord, whom all other gods bow down to, to look at his face and give him mercy. He calls out to God as a treasure of compassion, desperate for relief from a sorrow that can no longer be endured.

tamil: பொல்லா வாழ்க்கைத் துயரம்எனும் புணரிப் பெருக்கில் வீழ்ந்தழுந்திப்
பல்லார் நகைக்கப் பாவிபடும் பாட்டை முழுதும் பார்த்திருந்தும்
கல்லால் அமர்ந்தீர் என்னிரண்டு கண்கள் அனையீர் கறைமிடற்றீர்
எல்லாம் உடையீர் மால்விடையீர் என்னே இரங்கி அருளீரே.
translit: pollā vāḻkkait tuyarameṉum puṇarip perukkil vīḻntaḻuntip pallār nakaikkap pāvipaṭum pāṭṭai muḻutum pārttiruntum kallāl amarntīr eṉṉiraṇṭu kaṇkaḷ aṉaiyīr kaṟaimiṭaṟṟīr ellām uṭaiyīr mālviṭaiyīr eṉṉē iraṅki aruḷīrē.
translation: I have fallen and sunk into the swelling ocean of sorrow in this wretched life. You have completely watched the suffering of this sinner while many people mock me. You sit beneath the banyan tree. You are like my two eyes. You have a dark-stained throat. You possess everything. You ride the great bull. Why do You not take pity and bestow grace?
commentary: Vallalar feels abandoned in worldly sorrow, mocked by others while God watches. He addresses traditional forms of Lord Siva: the teacher under a banyan tree, the savior with a throat stained dark from swallowing poison, and the rider of a sacred bull. Since God possesses everything and is as precious to him as his own eyes, Vallalar cries out to know why divine grace is withheld.

tamil: பொன்னை உடையார் மிகுங்கல்விப் பொருளை உடையார் இவர்முன்னே
இன்னல் எனும்ஓர் கடல்வீழ்ந்திவ் வேழை படும்பா டறிந்திருந்தும்
மின்னை நிகரும் சடைமுடியீர் விடங்கொள் மிடற்றீர் வினைதவிர்ப்பீர்
என்னை உடையீர் வெள்விடையீர் என்னே இரங்கி அருளீரே.
translit: poṉṉai uṭaiyār mikuṅkalvip poruḷai uṭaiyār ivarmuṉṉē iṉṉal eṉumōr kaṭalvīḻntiv vēḻai paṭumpā ṭaṟintiruntum miṉṉai nikarum caṭaimuṭiyīr viṭaṅkoḷ miṭaṟṟīr viṉaitavirppīr eṉṉai uṭaiyīr veḷviṭaiyīr eṉṉē iraṅki aruḷīrē.
translation: I stand before those who possess gold and those who possess the great wealth of education. I, this poor wretch, have fallen into an ocean of misery and suffer. You know my suffering. You have matted hair shining like lightning. You hold poison in your throat. You dispel karma. You own me. You ride the white bull. Why do You not take pity and bestow grace?
commentary: Earthly wealth and education offer no comfort to a soul drowning in despair. Standing before people with worldly success, Vallalar feels poor and broken. He cries out to the Lord who has the power to wipe away the accumulated burden of past actions (karma), asking how a God so powerful can watch a devotee suffer and hold back compassion.

translit: āyum vañcaka neñcaṉiv aṭiyaṉēṉ aiyā nīyum vañcaka neñcaṉeṉ ṟālinta nilattē ēyum iṅkitaṟ keṉceyvēṉ eṉceyvēṉ evaikkum tāyum tantaiyum āki-uḷ niṟkiṉṟōy cāṟṟāy.
translation: Lord, I am a devotee with a deceitful heart when examined. If You too have a deceitful heart, what will I do here in this world? What will I do? You stand within everything as mother and father. Tell me.
commentary: In a moment of intimacy, Vallalar accuses God of playing tricks. He admits his own heart is full of flaws, but warns that if the divine mother and father of all creation acts the same way, there is no hope left in the world. This plea is born of desperate love, demanding that God step forward and act with the grace that is his nature.

translit: nāṉum poyyaṉniṉ aṭiyaṉēṉ taṇṇaruḷ nitinī tāṉum poyyaṉeṉ ṟālitaṟ keṉceyvēṉ talaivā tēṉum pāluntīṅ kaṭṭiyum ākiniṟ ṟeḷintōr ūṉum uḷḷamum uyirumaṇ ṇikkiṉṟa uravōy.
translation: I, Your devotee, am a liar. You are the treasure of cool grace. If You Yourself are a liar, what will I do about this, my Lord? You become honey, milk, and sweet rock candy. You sweeten the flesh, mind, and soul of those who have realized You, O mighty Lord.
commentary: Vallalar continues questioning God. He knows his own faults, but if the Lord of grace also breaks his promises, he has nowhere else to turn. Yet even in frustration, he remembers how sweet the divine presence is to those who have realized it, knowing God's grace fills the flesh, mind, and soul with joy.

translit: nēcaṉumnī cuṟṟamumnī nērniṉ ṟaḷittuvarum īcaṉumnī īṉṟāḷum entaiyumnī eṉṟēniṉ tēcuṟucīr ainteḻuttum ceppukiṉṟa nāyēṉai ācakalum vaṇṇam aruḷpurintāl ākātō.
translation: You are my friend. You are my kin. You are the Lord who stands before me and protects me. You are the mother who bore me, and You are my father. Saying this, I, a dog, recite Your radiant five letters. Will You not bestow Your grace so that my flaws depart?
commentary: True devotion recognizes God as the only family a person has. Vallalar calls the divine his friend, mother, and father. He repeats the sacred five-syllable mantra of Lord Siva, hoping this constant remembrance will wash away his worldly flaws and bring down the grace he needs.

translit: āṟṟāl viḷaṅkum caṭaiyōyiv vēḻai aṭiyaṉumpal āṟṟāl varuntum varuttamel lāmmuṟ ṟaṟintumiṉṉam āṟṟā tiruttalniṉ pēraruḷ āṟṟuk kaḻakukolō āṟṟāmai mēṟkoṇ ṭaḻutāl evareṉai āṟṟuvarē.
translation: O Lord whose matted hair shines with the river! You know completely all the sorrows that afflict this poor devotee in so many ways. Is it fitting for the river of your great grace to leave me uncomforted still? If I weep in my overwhelming helplessness, who else will comfort me?
commentary: The soul's comfort can only come from divine grace. Vallalar invokes the traditional image of Siva wearing the river Ganges in his matted hair, but asks for a different kind of water. He pleads for the river of God's grace. Since the divine already knows every sorrow the soul suffers, only God can provide the solace no earthly source can offer.

tamil: அருளார் அமுதே அரசேநின் அடியேன் கொடியேன் முறையேயோ
இருள்சேர் மனனோ டிடர்உழந்தேன் எந்தாய் இதுதான் முறையேயோ
மருள்சேர் மடவார் மயலாலே மாழ்கின் றேன்நான் முறையேயோ
தெருளோர் சிறிதும் அறியாதே திகையா நின்றேன் முறையேயோ.
translit: aruḷār amutē aracēniṉ aṭiyēṉ koṭiyēṉ muṟaiyēyō iruḷcēr maṉaṉō ṭiṭaruḻantēṉ entāy itutāṉ muṟaiyēyō maruḷcēr maṭavār mayalālē māḻkiṉ ṟēṉnāṉ muṟaiyēyō teruḷōr ciṟitum aṟiyātē tikaiyā niṉṟēṉ muṟaiyēyō.
translation: O nectar full of grace! O King! I am your cruel devotee. I cry out to you! I suffer afflictions with a mind full of darkness. O my Father, is this fair? I perish in my infatuation with deluding women. I cry out to you! I stand bewildered, knowing nothing of the wise ones. I cry out to you!
commentary: Vallalar makes a traditional appeal for justice, begging the divine sovereign to rescue a soul trapped in its own ignorance. Drawn into worldly delusions and physical desires, the mind remains cut off from the wisdom of enlightened beings. Vallalar confesses this spiritual darkness and throws himself on the mercy of God, asking if it is fair for a divine father to leave his child lost in such confusion.

tamil: ஒழியாக் கவலை உறுகின்றேன் உடையாய் முறையோ முறையேயோ
அழியாக் கருணைக் கடலேஎன் அரசே முறையோ முறையேயோ
பொழியாப் புயலே அனையார்பால் புகுவித் தனையே முறையேயோ
இழியாத் திரிதந் துழல்கின்றேன் இறைவா முறையோ முறையேயோ.
translit: oḻiyāk kavalai uṟukiṉṟēṉ uṭaiyāy muṟaiyō muṟaiyēyō aḻiyāk karuṇaik kaṭalē-eṉ aracē muṟaiyō muṟaiyēyō poḻiyāp puyalē aṉaiyārpāl pukuvit taṉaiyē muṟaiyēyō iḻiyāt tiritan tuḻalkiṉṟēṉ iṟaivā muṟaiyō muṟaiyēyō.
translation: I suffer unending sorrow. O Master, I cry out to you! O imperishable ocean of compassion! O my King, I cry out to you! You have made me enter the company of people who are like unyielding rainclouds. I cry out to you! I wander and roam aimlessly in degradation. O Lord, I cry out to you!
commentary: The greatest hardship for a spiritual seeker is living among people who lack compassion. God is praised as an endless ocean of mercy, while worldly people are compared to dry rainclouds that refuse to drop rain. Wandering among those who withhold their help and hoard what they have brings sorrow. Vallalar cries out to be rescued from this barren and ungiving company.

tamil: மதிஒளிர் கங்கைச் சடைப்பெருங் கருணை வள்ளலே தெள்ளிய அமுதே
நிதிஒளிர் வாழ்க்கை இந்திரன் முதலோர்நிலைத்தவான் செல்வமும் மண்ணில்
பதிஒளிர் வாழ்க்கை மணிமுடி அரசர் படைத்திடும் செல்வமும் வேண்டேன்
கதிஒளிர் நினது திருவருட் செல்வக் களிப்பையே கருதுகின் றனனே.
translit: mati-oḷir kaṅkaic caṭaipperuṅ karuṇai vaḷḷalē teḷḷiya amutē niti-oḷir vāḻkkai intiraṉ mutalōrnilaittavāṉ celvamum maṇṇil pati-oḷir vāḻkkai maṇimuṭi aracar paṭaittiṭum celvamum vēṇṭēṉ kati-oḷir niṉatu tiruvaruṭ celvak kaḷippaiyē karutukiṉ ṟaṉaṉē.
translation: O patron of great compassion whose matted hair shines with the moon and the river Ganges! O clear nectar! I do not desire the lasting celestial wealth of Indra and other gods whose lives shine with treasure. Nor do I desire the wealth amassed by bejeweled kings who live glorious lives ruling the earth. I seek only the joy of the wealth of your divine grace that shines as my ultimate refuge.
commentary: True spiritual wealth has nothing to do with earthly power or heavenly rewards. Many religious traditions promise their followers a place in celestial realms, such as the heaven ruled by the god Indra, or great prosperity on earth. The poem rejects both completely. It declares that divine grace is the only treasure worth seeking, and that the pure joy of receiving God's compassion far outweighs the highest pleasures of this world or the next.

translit: veḷḷaṅkoṇ ṭōṅkum viricaṭai yāymiku mēṭṭiṉiṉṟum paḷḷaṅkoṇ ṭōṅkum puṉalpōlniṉ taṇṇaruṭ paṇpunallōr uḷḷaṅkoṇ ṭōṅkum avamē parutta oti-aṉaiyēṉ kaḷḷaṅkoṇ ṭōṅkum maṉattuṟu mō-uṟiṟ kāṇkuvaṉē.
translation: O Lord with spreading matted hair that holds the mighty flood! Like water rushing from a high peak down into a deep valley, the nature of your cool grace swells and fills the hearts of the good. I am puffed up in vain. Will your grace enter my mind that swells with deceit? If it enters, I shall truly perceive it.
commentary: Divine grace flows naturally toward the humble, just as water rushes from a mountain peak into a deep valley. The hearts of the good are like low valleys, shaped to catch the flood of God's compassion. Vallalar worries his mind is swollen with pride and deceit, making it too high and puffed up to catch the water. Yet he knows that if grace enters his heart, spiritual vision will open.

translit: aiyāmuk kaṇkoṇṭa āramu tē-aru ḷārpavaḷa meyyāmeyñ ñāṉa viḷakkē karuṇai viḷaṅkavaitta maiyār miṭaṟṟu maṇiyē-aṉ ṟeṉṉai makiḻntatantō poyyā-eṉ ceyval aruḷā yeṉileṅkup pōtuvaṉē.
translation: O Lord, rare ambrosia with three eyes. O grace-filled coral body. O true lamp of wisdom. O jewel with a dark throat that makes compassion shine. Was it a lie that you rejoiced in me back then? Alas, what shall I do? If you do not grant grace, where will I go?
commentary: Past moments of divine intimacy feel like an illusion when grace seems withdrawn. Vallalar addresses God using traditional forms of Siva, mentioning his dark throat. With nowhere else to turn, he begs this compassionate God not to abandon him.

translit: nārā yaṇaṉticai nāṉmukaṉ ātiyar naṇṇiniṉṟu pārā yaṇañceyap paṭṭaniṉ cēvaṭip paṅkayamēl cīrā yaṇampeṟap pāṭun tiṟamōr ciṟitumilēṉ ārā yaṇaṅkuṟa niṉṟēṉpoṉ maṉṟat tamarntavaṉē.
translation: Narayana, the four-faced Brahma, and other gods approach and recite praises upon your red lotus feet. I lack even the slightest skill to sing your praises and attain excellent refuge. I stand suffering unendurable pain, O Lord seated in the Golden Hall.
commentary: Even the highest gods of the Hindu pantheon, like Narayana (Vishnu) and the four-faced creator Brahma, must stand and sing praises to reach the supreme divine. Vallalar contrasts their heavenly devotion with his own desperate state. He feels he lacks the basic skill to sing praise, leaving him standing in unendurable pain before the Golden Hall where the Lord resides.

translit: pēykoṇṭa neñcakap pāḻāl varumeṉ peruntuyarai vāykoṇ ṭaṉantar aṉantarkkum colla varāteṉilin nāykoṇ ṭuraikka varumō-eṉ ceykuvaṉ naccumarak kāykoṇṭu vāḻaik kaṉiyaikkai viṭṭa kaṭaiyavaṉē.
translation: My great sorrow arises from this ruinous heart possessed by demons. If this sorrow cannot be described by the mouths of countless thousands, can it be spoken by this dog? What will I do? I am the lowest wretch who took the fruit of a poison tree and threw away the sweet plantain fruit.
commentary: The unbearable sorrow of a troubled heart is too immense for thousands to describe, let alone one person. Throwing away a sweet, nourishing plantain to eat the fruit of a poison tree illustrates the foolishness of turning from divine truth to chase worldly illusions that destroy a person.

tamil: வன்மானங் கரத்தேந்தும் மாமணியே மணிகண்ட மணியே அன்பர்
நன்மானங் காத்தருளும் அருட்கடலே ஆனந்த நடஞ்செய் வாழ்வே
பொன்மானம் பினைப்பொருந்தும் அம்பினைவைத் தாண்டருளும் பொருளேநீ இங்
translit: vaṉmāṉaṅ karattēntum māmaṇiyē maṇikaṇṭa maṇiyē aṉpar naṉmāṉaṅ kāttaruḷum aruṭkaṭalē āṉanta naṭañcey vāḻvē poṉmāṉam piṉaipporuntum ampiṉaivait tāṇṭaruḷum poruḷēnī iṅ keṉmāṉaṅ kāttaruḷa vēṇṭutiyō vēṇṭāyēl eṉceyvēṉē.
translation: O great jewel holding the leaping deer in your hand. O jewel with a blue throat. O ocean of grace who protects the good honor of devotees. O life performing the joyful dance. O Supreme Reality who rules, keeping beside you the Mother who resembles a golden female deer. Do you wish to protect my honor here? If you do not, what will I do?
commentary: True devotees rely on the ocean of divine grace to protect their dignity and honor in the world. Vallalar calls out using classic images of Siva performing a joyful cosmic dance, holding a leaping deer, and standing beside the divine Mother. Having given his life to this Supreme Reality, he asks what he is supposed to do if God chooses not to protect him.

translit: vaiva meṉṟeḻu kiṉṟavar tamakkumnal vāḻvu ceyvam eṉṟeḻu kiṉṟameyt tiruvaruṭ ceyalum caiva meṉpatum caivattiṟ cāṟṟiṭun talaimait teyva meṉpatum eṉṉaḷa villai-eṉ ceyvēṉ.
translation: The action of true divine grace rises up to declare, "We will grant a good life even to those who rise up to abuse us." The path called Saivam and the supreme God proclaimed in Saivam are beyond my measure. What will I do?
commentary: Divine grace is so absolute that it promises to bless and uplift even those who rise up to hurl abuse at it. Faced with this overwhelming compassion, Vallalar feels entirely inadequate. He states that the vastness of the religious path of Saivam (Shaivism) and its supreme God remain completely beyond his human ability to measure or comprehend.

tamil: ஐய ரேஉம தடியன்நான் ஆகில் அடிகள் நீர்என தாண்டவர் ஆகில்
தைய லோர்புறம் நின்றுளங் களிப்பச் சச்சி தானந்தத் தனிநடம் புரியும்
மெய்ய ரேமிகு துய்யரே தரும விடைய ரேஎன்றன் விழிஅமர்ந் தவரே.
translit: aiya rē-uma taṭiyaṉnāṉ ākil aṭikaḷ nīreṉa tāṇṭavar ākil poyya ṉēṉuḷat tavalamum payamumpuṉkaṇumtavirt taruḷutalvēṇṭum taiya lōrpuṟam niṉṟuḷaṅ kaḷippac cacci tāṉantat taṉinaṭam puriyum meyya rēmiku tuyyarē taruma viṭaiya rē-eṉṟaṉ viḻi-amarn tavarē.
translation: O Lord, if I am your devotee and you are the Master who governs me, you must grant your grace to dispel the sorrow, fear, and misery from the heart of this false one. O truthful One, O supremely pure One, O rider of the bull of dharma, O One seated in my eyes. You perform the peerless dance of existence, consciousness, and bliss while the Lady stands at your side with a rejoicing heart.
commentary: Vallalar claims his right to grace by pointing to the bond between a master and a servant. He says that if God is his guiding master, then God owes it to him to clear the sorrow and fear from his heart. The divine dancer of existence, consciousness, and bliss is not distant, as Vallalar sees the Lord seated inside his own eyes.

tamil: எழுவினும் வலிய மனத்தினேன் மலஞ்சார் ஈயினும் நாயினும் இழிந்தேன்
வழுவினும் பெரியேன் மடத்தினும் பெரியேன் மாண்பிலா வஞ்சக நெஞ்சக்
குழுவினும் பெரியேன் அம்பலக் கூத்தன் குறிப்பினுக் கென்கட வேனே.
translit: eḻuviṉum valiya maṉattiṉēṉ malañcār īyiṉum nāyiṉum iḻintēṉ puḻuviṉuñ ciṟiyēṉ poyviḻain tuḻalvēṉ puṉmaiyēṉpulaittoḻiṟkaṭaiyēṉ vaḻuviṉum periyēṉ maṭattiṉum periyēṉ māṇpilā vañcaka neñcak kuḻuviṉum periyēṉ ampalak kūttaṉ kuṟippiṉuk keṉkaṭa vēṉē.
translation: I possess a mind harder than a pillar. I am lower than a filth-seeking fly or a dog. I am smaller than a worm. I wander about desiring falsehood. I am vile, the lowest of the low in base deeds. I am greater in flaws than any fault, greater in ignorance than any folly. I am worse than a whole assembly of undignified, deceitful hearts. How am I to serve the will of the Dancer in the Hall?
commentary: In an act of spiritual humility, Vallalar compares his stubborn mind to a rigid pillar and measures his worth below the lowest insects, feeling unqualified to serve the divine will. By stripping away every trace of human pride, he makes himself empty and ready to receive grace.

translit: poṉa ḷikkumnaṟ puttiyun tantuniṉ taṉṉa ruṭṭuṇait tāṇmalart tiyāṉamē maṉṉa vaittiṭa vēṇṭumem vaḷḷalē eṉṉai nāṉpala kāliṅki yampalē.
translation: O our Benefactor, you must grant me the good intellect that yields pure gold and make the meditation on your gracious lotus feet endure within me forever. Why must I repeat this to you so many times here?
commentary: Vallalar asks for a transformed, golden intellect that remains fixed on the divine presence. He speaks with the familiar impatience of a close relationship, asking God why he should have to repeat his request so many times when his needs are already known.

translit: tāyum tantaiyum caṟkuru nātaṉum āyum teyvamum nī-eṉ ṟaṟintaṉaṉ pāyum mālviṭai ēṟum paramaṉē nīyum kaiviṭa eṉṉai niṉaittiyō.
translation: I have realized that you are my mother, my father, my true Guru, and the supreme deity I seek. O Supreme Lord who mounts the leaping great bull, do you intend to abandon me?
commentary: Vallalar finds every form of earthly guidance and love fulfilled in God alone. Seeing the divine as mother, father, and true teacher, he wonders aloud how a master who holds all these intimate roles could abandon him.

translit: oḻiyā mayalkoṇ ṭuḻalvēṉ avamē aḻiyā vakaiyē aruḷvāy aruḷvāy poḻiyā maṟaiyiṉ mutalē nutalēy viḻiyāy viḻiyāy viṉaitūḷ paṭavē.
translation: I wander in vain, gripped by unceasing delusion. Grant your grace, grant your grace so that I may not perish. O source of the showering Vedas, O Lord with an eye upon your forehead, open your eye so that my karma is shattered into dust.
commentary: Vallalar begs for rescue from the endless confusion of worldly life. He asks the Lord to open the spiritual eye on his forehead, a traditional image of divine fire, so his karma is instantly shattered into dust.

tamil: உலகெ லாம்நிறைந் தோங்கு பேரருள் உருவ மாகிஎவ் உயிரும் உய்ந்திட
அலகில் ஆனந்த நாடகஞ் செய்யும் அம்பொற் சேவடிக் கபயம் என்னையும்
translit: ulake lāmniṟain tōṅku pēraruḷ uruva māki-ev uyirum uyntiṭa ilaku vāṉoḷi yāmmaṇi maṉṟiṭai eṉṟumniṉṟē alakil āṉanta nāṭakañ ceyyum ampoṟ cēvaṭik kapayam eṉṉaiyum tilaka nīviḻai vāynaṭa rācaci kāmaṇiyē.
translation: Taking the form of supreme grace that fills and rises over all worlds so that all souls may be saved, you stand forever in the ruby hall of shining supreme light. You perform the boundless dance of bliss. I take refuge at your beautiful golden, red feet. O crest-jewel Nataraja, O excellent one, please accept me too.
commentary: The divine takes the form of limitless grace to save all living beings. Vallalar takes refuge in Nataraja (the dancing form of God), who moves in a hall of pure light, and asks for his protection.

tamil: என்னிருகண் காள்உமது பெருந்தவம்எப் புவனத்தில் யார்தான் செய்வர்
முன்னிருவர் காணாமல் அலைந்தனரால் இனுங்காண முயலா நின்றார்
நன்னிருபர் தொழுதேத்தும் அம்பலத்தே ஓரிடத்தோர் நாள்ஆ தித்தர்
பன்னிருவர் ஒளிமாற்றும் பரஒளியைப் பார்த்துயர்ந்தீர் பண்பி னீரே.
translit: eṉṉirukaṇ kāḷumatu peruntavamep puvaṉattil yārtāṉ ceyvar muṉṉiruvar kāṇāmal alaintaṉarāl iṉuṅkāṇa muyalā niṉṟār naṉṉirupar toḻutēttum ampalattē ōriṭattōr nāḷā tittar paṉṉiruvar oḷimāṟṟum para-oḷiyaip pārttuyarntīr paṇpi ṉīrē.
translation: O my two eyes, who in any world could perform your great penance? The two primal gods wandered without seeing it, and they still strive to see it. In the hall praised and worshipped by good kings, on a single day in a single place, you saw the supreme light that eclipses the brilliance of twelve suns. You saw it and attained greatness, O eyes of excellent virtue.
commentary: The vision of the supreme light is a rare gift. Vallalar speaks directly to his own eyes, marveling at their good fortune to witness a brilliance greater than twelve suns. This reality remains hidden even from the greatest traditional gods, who still search for it in vain.

tamil: சேணாடர் முனிவர்உயர் திசைமுகன்மால் உருத்திரன்அத் திரளோர் சற்றும்
காணாத காட்சியைநான் கண்டேன்சிற் றம்பலத்தின் கண்ணே பன்னாள்
ஆணாகப் பிறந்தடியேன் அருந்தவம்என் புரிந்தேனோ அறிகி லேன்முன்
பேணாத பிறப்பெல்லாம் பிறப்பலஇப் பிறப்பேஎன் பிறப்பாம் அந்தோ.
translit: cēṇāṭar muṉivaruyar ticaimukaṉmāl uruttiraṉat tiraḷōr caṟṟum kāṇāta kāṭciyaināṉ kaṇṭēṉciṟ ṟampalattiṉ kaṇṇē paṉṉāḷ āṇākap piṟantaṭiyēṉ aruntavameṉ purintēṉō aṟiki lēṉmuṉ pēṇāta piṟappellām piṟappala-ip piṟappē-eṉ piṟappām antō.
translation: I saw a vision in the hall of consciousness that the celestials, the sages, the exalted four-faced Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, and all those hosts cannot see at all. Being born as a man for many days, I do not know what rare penance I, this lowly servant, performed. All those uncherished past births were not true births. Oh wonder, this birth alone is my true birth.
commentary: Experiencing the supreme light transforms the meaning of human existence. Vallalar says his vision of the divine outshines anything achieved by traditional gods like Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra. Having seen this truth, he dismisses all previous lives as meaningless and declares this current life his only real birth.

tamil: இருளற ஓங்கும் பொதுவிலே நடஞ்செய் எங்குரு நாதன்எம் பெருமான்
அருளெனும் வடிவங் காட்டிஒண் முகத்தே அழகுறும் புன்னகை காட்டித்
தெருளுற அருமைத் திருக்கையால் தடவித் திருமணி வாய்மலர்ந் தருகில்
translit: iruḷaṟa ōṅkum potuvilē naṭañcey eṅkuru nātaṉem perumāṉ aruḷeṉum vaṭivaṅ kāṭṭi-oṇ mukattē aḻakuṟum puṉṉakai kāṭṭit teruḷuṟa arumait tirukkaiyāl taṭavit tirumaṇi vāymalarn tarukil poruḷuṟa iruntōr vākkaḷitteṉṉuḷpukuntaṉaṉ putumai-ītantō.
translation: Dancing in the hall that rises to dispel darkness, our Lord and Guru revealed His form of grace. He revealed a beautiful smile on His radiant face. He gently stroked me with His precious divine hands to bestow clarity. Opening His beautiful ruby mouth, He sat near me with profound meaning, gave me a promise, and entered into me. Oh, what a wonder this is.
commentary: The divine does not remain distant or abstract. Vallalar describes an intimate encounter where God appears as a loving teacher, offering a smile, a gentle touch of clarity, and a direct promise. The wonder is that this vast presence then enters and merges with his own being.

tamil: பொன்என்கோ மணிஎன்கோ புனிதஒளித் திரள்என்கோ பொற்பின் ஓங்கும்
என்என்கோ என்என்கோ எம்பெருமான் திருமேனி இருந்த வண்ணம்
translit: poṉeṉkō maṇi-eṉkō puṉita-oḷit tiraḷeṉkō poṟpiṉ ōṅkum miṉeṉkō viḷakkeṉkō viricuṭarkkōr cuṭareṉkō viṉaiyaṉēṉyāṉ eṉeṉkō eṉeṉkō emperumāṉ tirumēṉi irunta vaṇṇam muṉeṉkō taṟutavattāl kaṇṭukaḷit tiṭappeṟṟēṉ mukkaṇmūrtti.
translation: Shall I call it gold? Shall I call it a ruby? Shall I call it a mass of sacred light? Shall I call it lightning rising in beauty? Shall I call it a lamp? Shall I call it the flame behind all expanding flames? What shall I, a man of karma, say? What shall I say? Such was the state of our Lord's sacred body. By some flawless penance I performed in the past, I received the blessing to see the three-eyed Lord and rejoice.
commentary: Human language fails when trying to describe the physical beauty of the divine form. Vallalar grasps at comparisons like gold, rubies, lightning, and pure flame, finding them all inadequate to capture the reality of God's radiant body. He rejoices at having been granted the spiritual sight to witness it.

tamil: நெஞ்சகத்துன் மார்க்கனைமா பாதகனைக் கொடியேனை நீச னேனை
கஞ்சமல ரவன்நெடுமாற் கரும்பொருளைப் பொதுவினில்யான் கண்டுய்ந் தேனே.
translit: vañcakarkkel lāmmutalāy aṟakkaṭaiyāy maṟattoḻilē valikkumpāvi neñcakattuṉ mārkkaṉaimā pātakaṉaik koṭiyēṉai nīca ṉēṉai añcaleṉak karuṇaipurin tāṇṭukoṇṭa aruṭkaṭalai amutaitteyvak kañcamala ravaṉneṭumāṟ karumporuḷaip potuviṉilyāṉ kaṇṭuyn tēṉē.
translation: I am the foremost among all deceivers. I am the lowest in virtue. I am a sinful-hearted follower of wicked paths who insists on cruel deeds. I am a great sinner, a cruel man, and a lowly wretch. Yet He showed me grace, told me not to fear, and took me under His rule. He is the ocean of grace, the nectar, and the rare reality sought by the divine lotus-born Brahma and tall Vishnu. I saw Him in the public Hall and found my salvation.
commentary: The measure of God's mercy is that it requires no perfection from us. Vallalar heaps the worst faults upon himself, calling himself a deceitful and cruel sinner, to show that divine grace rescues even the lowest among us. This grace is a rare reality that even the great gods struggle to find, yet it is openly available to all.

translit: nātāpoṉ ampalat tē-aṟi vāṉanta nāṭakañcey pātā turumpiṉum paṟṟāta eṉṉaip paṇikoṇṭellām ōtā tuṇara uṇartti-uḷ ḷēniṉ ṟuḷavucoṉṉa nītā niṉaimaṟan teṉniṉaik kēṉinta nīṇilattē.
translation: O Lord! O feet that perform the dance of conscious bliss in the Golden Hall! You took me into your service even though I am worth less than a piece of straw. You made me realize everything without any formal instruction. O righteous one, you stood within me and revealed the inner secrets. If I forget you, what else could I possibly think of in this vast world?
commentary: Spiritual knowledge comes from within, not from books or formal teaching. Addressing the Divine dancing in the Golden Hall, Vallalar marvels that he was given total realization without any schooling. When God reveals inner secrets directly to the soul, the mind becomes anchored in that truth, leaving no room to think of anything else.

tamil: கந்த நாண்மலர்க் கழலிணை உளத்துறக் கருதுகின் றவர்க்கெல்லாம்
பந்த நாண்வலை அவிழ்த்தருள் சிதம்பரை பரம்பரை யுடன்ஆடும்
அந்த நாள்மகிழ் வடைபவர் உளர்சிலர் அவர்எவர் எனில்இங்கே
இந்த நாள்முறை திறம்பல ராய்உயிர்க் கிதம்செயும் அவர்அன்றே.
translit: kanta nāṇmalark kaḻaliṇai uḷattuṟak karutukiṉ ṟavarkkellām panta nāṇvalai aviḻttaruḷ citamparai paramparai yuṭaṉāṭum anta nāḷmakiḻ vaṭaipavar uḷarcilar avarevar eṉiliṅkē inta nāḷmuṟai tiṟampala rāyuyirk kitamceyum avaraṉṟē.
translation: He unties the tightening net of worldly attachments for all who deeply meditate in their hearts on His pair of feet, which are like fragrant fresh flowers. He dances with the supreme goddess of consciousness. There are a few who attain joy on that day of His dance. If you ask who they are, they are indeed the ones who remain unwavering in their righteous path today and perform acts of kindness for all living souls.
commentary: The joy of liberation is reserved for those who practice compassion. While many meditate on God to escape worldly attachments, the ones who experience the bliss of the divine dance actively perform acts of kindness for all living souls. Vallalar calls this active kindness Jeevakarunyam (jīvakāruṇyam, compassion for all living beings), and teaches it is the only way to reach grace.

translit: veṭṭai māṭṭi viṭāpperun tuṉpanōy viḷaiva teṇṇilar vēṇṭicceṉ ṟētoḻuk kaṭṭai māṭṭik koḷvāreṉa vēṇṭippeṇ kaṭṭai māṭṭik koḷvārtaṅ kaḻuttilē tuṭṭai māṭṭiṉ kaḻuttaṭik kaṭṭaiyō tuṇikkum kaṭṭaiya tāmintak kaṭṭaitāṉ eṭṭai māṭṭi uyirviṭak kaṭṭaimēl ēṟum pōtum iḻukkiṉṟa kaṭṭaiyē.
translation: Men do not consider the unyielding great sorrow and afflictions that result from lust. Just as someone willingly goes and locks himself in the wooden stocks, they willingly tie the wooden trap of a woman around their necks. Is this merely like the heavy log tied around the neck of a rogue beast? No, this trap is one that completely destroys. Even when life ends and they mount the wooden block of the funeral pyre, this attachment is the trap that keeps dragging them down.
commentary: Worldly attachment, driven by lust, is a trap people willingly lock around their necks. Drawing on classical ascetic warnings, Vallalar compares physical desire to heavy wooden stocks that bind a beast of burden. This attachment is so deep it drags the soul down even as the body is placed on the funeral pyre.

translit: puṇṇaik kaṭṭikkoṇ ṭē-ataṉ mēloru puṭavai kaṭṭip putumaikaḷ kāṭṭiṭum peṇṇaik kaṭṭikkoḷ vārivar koḷḷivāyp pēyaik kaṭṭikkoṇ ṭālum piḻaipparkāṇ maṇṇaik kaṭṭikkoṇ ṭē-aḻu kiṉṟa-im maṭaiyap piḷḷaikaḷ vāḻviṉai nōkkuṅkāl kaṇṇaik kaṭṭikkoṇ ṭūrvaḻi pōmkiḻak kaḻutai vāḻvil kaṭai-eṉal ākumē.
translation: They marry a woman who is essentially a festering wound wrapped in a sari, displaying deceptive charms. These men might actually survive if they tied themselves to a fire-mouthed demoness instead. They weep as they cling to this worldly earth. When you observe the lives of these foolish men, their existence is lower than the life of an old, blindfolded donkey wandering along the village paths.
commentary: To break the spell of physical desire, Vallalar strips away the illusion of bodily beauty. He describes the flesh in stark, ascetic terms as a festering wound wrapped in cloth. Men who trade spiritual freedom for physical lust tie themselves to the earth in a blind, foolish existence, lower than the life of an old, blindfolded donkey wandering in circles.

translit: uṭukka vō-oru kantaikku mēlilai uṇṇa vō-uṇa vukkum vaḻiyilai paṭukka vōpaḻam pāykkum katiyilai pāril nallavar pālceṉṟu piccaitāṉ eṭukka vōtiṭam illai-eṉ pāluṉak kirakkam eṉpatum illai uyiraittāṉ viṭukka vōmaṉam illai-eṉ ceykuvēṉ veṇpi ṟaiccaṭai vittaka vaḷḷalē.
translation: To wear, I have nothing more than a single rag. To eat, I have no way to get food. To sleep, I have not even an old mat. I lack the strength to go to good people on earth and beg for alms. Towards me, you have no pity at all. Yet I have no will to give up my life. What shall I do, O wise benefactor with the white crescent moon on your matted hair?
commentary: Worldly poverty brings a feeling of helplessness. Lacking food, shelter, or even the physical strength to beg, Vallalar feels abandoned by divine mercy. Yet the will to live remains, turning this despair into a direct plea to God.

translit: toṭukka vōnalla coṉmalar illaināṉ tutikkavō patti cuttamum illai-uḷ oṭukka vōmaṉam eṉvacam illai-ū ṭuṟṟa āṇava mātima laṅkaḷait taṭukka vōtiṭam illai-eṉ maṭṭilē tayavu tāṉniṉak killai uyiraiyum viṭukka vōmaṉam illai-eṉ ceykuvēṉ viḷaṅku maṉṟil viḷaṅkiya vaḷḷalē.
translation: To string a garland, I have no good flowers of words. To praise you, I have no purity of devotion. To withdraw inward, my mind is not under my control. I lack the strength to block the internal impurities starting with ego. Towards me, you have no compassion. And I have no will to give up my life. What shall I do, O benefactor shining in the radiant hall?
commentary: Spiritual poverty hurts just as much as physical poverty. Vallalar confesses a lack of devotion, mental focus, and the strength needed to fight off his own ego. Stripped of spiritual achievements, he waits helpless before the divine presence in the radiant hall.

tamil: இறகெடுத்த அமணர்குலம் வேரறுத்த சொக்கேஈ தென்ன ஞாயம்
அறுகடுத்த சடைமுடிமேல் மண்ணெடுக்க மாட்டாமல் அடிபட் டையோ
விறகெடுத்தீர் என்செய்வீர் விதிவசந்தான் யாவரையும் விடாது தானே.
translit: iṟakeṭutta amaṇarkulam vēraṟutta cokkē-ī teṉṉa ñāyam aṟukaṭutta caṭaimuṭimēl maṇṇeṭukka māṭṭāmal aṭipaṭ ṭaiyō piṟakeṭuttīr vaḷaiyalviṟṟīr coṟkēḷāppiḷḷaikaḷaip peṟṟatōṣam viṟakeṭuttīr eṉceyvīr vitivacantāṉ yāvaraiyum viṭātu tāṉē.
translation: O Cokkanatha who completely uprooted the clan of Jains holding feathers! What justice is this? Alas, unable to carry earth on your matted hair adorned with arugam grass, you were beaten! Later you took forms and sold bangles. This is the sin of begetting children who do not listen to your words. You carried firewood. What will you do? The force of fate spares no one.
commentary: Praise is hidden inside playful mockery, a traditional Tamil poetic style. Vallalar teases the Lord by bringing up old legends where the god took human form to labor as a commoner, hauling firewood and carrying earth. He jokingly blames these divine struggles on the everyday burden of having disobedient children.

translit: caccitā nantaciṟ capaiyil nāṭakam paccitān tiruvurup pāvai nōkkiṭa meccitā kāramā viḷaippar mellaṭi uccitāḻ kuvarnamak kuṭaiyar neñcamē.
translation: My heart! Our Lord performs his dance in the conscious-bliss hall of Chit Sabhai. He performs it wonderfully so that the beautiful green-hued goddess watches and appreciates it. We bow our heads to his soft feet.
commentary: The Lord performs a dance of joy in the Chit Sabhai (the hall of consciousness). He dances so the divine mother can watch and appreciate his movements. Vallalar tells his own heart to bow down to this graceful presence.

translit: tattā taṉattattait tāveṉ ṟaraṅkaṉ ṟaṉinaṭippā tattā taṉattattait tāveṉ ṟaraṅkaṉ ṟaṉañcollumē.
translation: Chanting "O grandfather, give the wealth," the Lord of the stage performs his solitary dance. Chanting "O grandfather, give the wealth," the Lord of the stage performs his solitary dance. Chanting "O grandfather, give the wealth," the wealth of the Lord of the stage speaks.
commentary: The rhythmic words mimic the beats of a musical performance. Vallalar pictures the Lord dancing alone on the cosmic stage, matching his solitary movements to a simple, repetitive chant.

translit: immai yaṟaiyaṉaiya vēcūra mātarumā immaiyumai yimmaiyaiyō eṉceyta - tammaimataṉ māmāmā māmāmā māmāmā māmāmā māmāmā māmāmā mā.
translation: What have these fierce and cruel women done to me in this life? Cupid has targeted them and launched a vast shower of great mango arrows.
commentary: Vallalar uses a specialized verse form built on a single repeated sound to mimic a relentless rain of arrows. In traditional lore, the god of love shoots arrows made of mango blossoms to stir romantic longing. Vallalar describes feeling overwhelmed by these worldly passions and the distractions they bring.

translit: āviyī raintai aparattē vaittōtil āviyī raintai akaṟṟalām - āviyīr aintuṟalā māviyī raintaṟalā māviyī raintiṭalā mōriraṇṭō ṭāyntu. tirucciṟṟampalam
translation: If you place the ten vital breaths in the transcendent space and chant, you can dispel the ten flaws of the soul. You can attain the ten powers of the soul. You can sever the ten bonds of the soul. You can establish the ten states of the soul, examining them along with the unique two.
commentary: By drawing the vital breath upward into a transcendent space of awareness and chanting, a person can clear away deep-seated flaws. This focused meditation unties worldly bonds and unlocks the spiritual strength of the soul, preparing it for higher states of divine realization.

sections.title: The Light of the State of Virtue

note: Editor's note: Vallalar wrote this verse at the head of a letter to Irukkam Rathina Mudaliar.
tamil: மருவாணைப் பெண்ணாக்கி ஒருகணத்தில் கண்விழித்து வயங்கும் அப்பெண்
உருவாணை உருவாக்கி இறந்தவரை எழுப்புகின்ற உறுவ னேனும்
கருவாணை யுறஇரங்கா துயிருடம்பைக் கடிந்துண்ணுங் கருத்த னேல்எங்
குருவாணை எமதுசிவக் கொழுந்தாணை ஞானிஎனக் கூறொ ணாதே.
translit: maruvāṇaip peṇṇākki orukaṇattil kaṇviḻittu vayaṅkum appeṇ uruvāṇai uruvākki iṟantavarai eḻuppukiṉṟa uṟuva ṉēṉum karuvāṇai yuṟa-iraṅkā tuyiruṭampaik kaṭintuṇṇuṅ karutta ṉēleṅ kuruvāṇai ematucivak koḻuntāṇai ñāṉi-eṉak kūṟo ṇātē.
translation: Even if a master possesses the miraculous power to transform a man into a woman in a single moment, change that female form back into a male, and raise the dead, if he lacks compassion and kills to eat the bodies of living beings, I swear upon my Guru and our supreme Siva that he can never be called an enlightened being.
commentary: Miraculous supernatural abilities do not make a person enlightened. A person might perform the most astonishing magic, like changing someone's sex in an instant or bringing the dead back to life, but if they lack compassion and kill living beings to eat them, they lack true wisdom. Vallalar swears upon his teacher and upon God that a meat-eater can never be a spiritual master. Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings) is the absolute foundation of spiritual life, and no amount of mystical power can replace it.

sections.title: The Light of the State of Grace

note: Editor's note: this verse is held to recall the wonder at Karunguzhi, where the lamp in Vallalar’s room burned with water. It is found in a palm-leaf manuscript in his own hand.
tamil: மெய்விளக்கே விளக்கல்லால் வேறுவிளக் கில்லைஎன்றார் மேலோர் நானும்
பொய்விளக்கே விளக்கெனஉட் பொங்கிவழி கின்றேன்ஓர் புதுமை அன்றே
செய்விளக்கும் புகழுடைய சென்னநகர் நண்பர்களே செப்பக் கேளீர்
translit: meyviḷakkē viḷakkallāl vēṟuviḷak killai-eṉṟār mēlōr nāṉum poyviḷakkē viḷakkeṉa-uṭ poṅkivaḻi kiṉṟēṉōr putumai aṉṟē ceyviḷakkum pukaḻuṭaiya ceṉṉanakar naṇparkaḷē ceppak kēḷīr neyviḷakkē pōṉṟorutaṇṇīrviḷakkum erintatucan nitiyiṉ muṉṉē.
translation: The great ones declared that the lamp of truth is the only lamp and there is no other lamp. I boil over and spill out within, considering the lamp of falsehood to be the true lamp. This is no wonder. O friends of Chennai city, renowned for your brilliant deeds! Listen to what I say. Just like a lamp lit with ghee, a lamp lit with water burned before the sanctum.
commentary: A famous event from Vallalar's life shows the literal power of divine grace. He recounts a miracle he experienced firsthand: a sanctum lamp that normally required ghee (clarified butter) burned using only water.

sections.title: The State of the Grace of the Sacred Medicine

tamil: பனகஅணைத் திருநெடுமால் அயன்போற்றப் புலவரெலாம் பரவ ஓங்கும்
கனகமணி அம்பலத்தே பெரியமருந் தொன்றிருக்கக் கண்டேன் கண்டேன்
அனகநடத் ததுசச்சி தானந்த வடிவதுபே ரருள்வாய்ந் துள்ள
தெனகமமர்ந் திருப்பதெல்லாம் வல்லதுபேர் நடராசன் என்ப தம்மா.
translit: paṉaka-aṇait tiruneṭumāl ayaṉpōṟṟap pulavarelām parava ōṅkum kaṉakamaṇi ampalattē periyamarun toṉṟirukkak kaṇṭēṉ kaṇṭēṉ aṉakanaṭat tatucacci tāṉanta vaṭivatupē raruḷvāyn tuḷḷa teṉakamamarn tiruppatellām vallatupēr naṭarācaṉ eṉpa tammā.
translation: Sacred Vishnu on his serpent bed and Brahma praise it. All the wise exalt it. I saw, I saw a single great medicine residing in the exalted golden jeweled hall. It performs a pure dance. It is the form of truth, consciousness, and bliss. It is filled with great grace. It rests within my heart. It is all-powerful. Its name is Nataraja, O friend.
commentary: The Divine is a supreme medicine curing the soul of suffering and ignorance. This healing reality is saccidananda (truth, consciousness, and bliss). Vallalar sees this power dancing in the golden hall of the universe while resting intimately within his heart. He names this grace Nataraja, the dancing Lord.

tamil: ஒருகருணை மருந்துதிரு அம்பலத்தே இருந்திடக்கண் டுவந்தேன் அந்தோ
அருவுருவங் கடந்ததுபே ரானந்த வடிவதுநல் லருள்வாய்ந் துள்ள
திருமையும்நன் களிப்பதெல்லாம் வல்லதுபேர் நடராசன் என்ப தம்மா.
translit: tiruneṭumāl ayaṉtēṭat turiyanaṭu oḷittateṉat teḷintōrcollum orukaruṇai maruntutiru ampalattē iruntiṭakkaṇ ṭuvantēṉ antō aruvuruvaṅ kaṭantatupē rāṉanta vaṭivatunal laruḷvāyn tuḷḷa tirumaiyumnaṉ kaḷippatellām vallatupēr naṭarācaṉ eṉpa tammā.
translation: As sacred Vishnu and Brahma searched, the realized ones say it hid in the center of the transcendent state. Seeing this unique compassionate medicine residing in the sacred hall, I rejoiced. Ah! It transcends form and formlessness. It is the form of immense bliss. It is filled with good grace. It perfectly grants divine wealth. It is all-powerful. Its name is Nataraja, O friend.
commentary: Vishnu and Brahma tried to find the ultimate truth through their vast powers and failed. Sages say it remains hidden in turiya, the transcendent spiritual state beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. Vallalar rejoices to see this compassion shining in the sacred hall of grace. This medicine escapes human categories of form or formlessness, yet grants every divine blessing.

translit: āṇṭavaṉnī yākiluṉak kaṭiyaṉumnā ṉākil aruḷuṭaiyāy iṉṟiravil aruḷ iṟaiyāy vantu nīṇṭavaṉē mutaliyarum tīṇṭaritām poruḷiṉ nilaikāṭṭi aṭimuṭiyiṉ neṟimuḻutum kāṭṭi vīṇṭavaṉē kālaiyilnī viḻittavuṭaṉ eḻuntu vitimuṭittup puriti-itu viḷaṅkumeṉap pukalvāy tāṇṭavaṉē aruṭpotuvil taṉimutalē karuṇait taṭaṅkaṭalē neṭuntakaiyē caṅkaraṉē civaṉē.
translation: If you are the Lord and I am your devotee, O Lord of Grace, come tonight as the supreme sovereign of Grace. Show me the state of the Reality that is difficult for Vishnu and the other gods to touch. Show me the entire path from the base to the crown. Tell me, "As soon as you wake up in the morning, arise, complete your prescribed duties, and do this. This will become clear to you." O Dancer, the supreme source in the public hall of Grace, the vast ocean of compassion, the great noble one, Sankara, Siva.
commentary: Vallalar demands direct guidance: if their bond is real, the Divine must tell him exactly what to do upon waking, revealing a truth that even major gods like Vishnu (the preserver) cannot reach. He uses Sankara and Siva, traditional names for the Hindu god of destruction and grace, to address the single, supreme source of compassion.

translit: tiruneṟimeyt tamiḻmaṟaiyām tirukkaṭaikkāp pataṉāl tiruvuḷaṅkāṭ ṭiyanāḷil terintilaṉ ic ciṟiyēṉ peruneṟi-eṉ uḷattiruntu kāṭṭiyanāḷ aṟintēṉ piḻaipaṭāt teyvamaṟai ituveṉappiṉ puṇarntēṉ oruneṟiyil eṉatukarat tuvantaḷitta nāḷil uṇarāta uḷavai-elām oruṅkuṇarntu teḷintēṉ teruṇeṟitan taruḷummaṟaic cilampaṇinta patattāḷ civakāma vallimakiḻ tirunaṭatteḷ ḷamutē.
translation: On the day you revealed your divine will through the Tirukkataikkappu, the true Tamil Veda of the sacred path, this small one did not understand. I understood it on the day you dwelt in my heart and showed the great path. Later I realized that this is the flawless divine Veda. On the day you joyfully placed it in my hands on the singular path, I grasped and became completely clear about all the secrets I had not realized before. O clear nectar of the sacred dance that brings joy to Sivakama Valli, whose feet wear the anklets of the Vedas that grant the path of clarity.
commentary: Spiritual understanding unfolds in stages. Vallalar admits he did not initially grasp the Tirukkaṭaikkāppu (the sacred closing verses of the ancient Tamil saints). The teachings became clear only when the Divine entered his heart. True clarity comes through direct inner experience rather than reading scripture. Sivakama Valli is the goddess representing the divine energy and grace accompanying the dancing Lord.

sections.title: Song of Praise to Siva Chidambaram

translit: ulaka muñcarā caramum niṉṟuniṉ ṟulavu kiṉṟapē rulakam eṉpatum kalakam iṉṟi-eṅ kaṇuni ṟaintaciṟ kaṉamvi ḷaṅkuciṟ kakaṉam eṉpatum ilaka oṉṟiraṇ ṭeṉala kaṉṟatōr iṇaiyil iṉpamām itayam eṉpatum tilakam eṉṟanaṅ kuruci tamparam civaci tamparam civaci tamparam.
translation: It is called the vast world where the universe and all moving and stationary things constantly abide and move about. It is called the space of consciousness where the mass of consciousness shines and fills everywhere without disturbance. It is called the heart of incomparable bliss that shines beyond the duality of one and two. It is our Guru Chidambaram praised as the foremost crown jewel. It is Siva Chidambaram, Siva Chidambaram.
commentary: Chidambaram is far more than a physical temple. It is the pure space of awareness and the inner heart of supreme bliss beyond the illusion of separateness.

translit: varamu ṟuñcutan taracu kantarum maṉama ṭaṅkuciṟ kaṉana ṭantarum uramu ṟumpatam peṟava ḻaṅkupē roḷina ṭantarum veḷivi ṭantarum paramu ṟuṅkuṇaṅ kuṟika ṭantaciṟ parama mākiyē paravu māmaṟaic ciramu ṟumparam paraci tamparam civaci tamparam civaci tamparam.
translation: It grants the boon of absolute independent bliss. It grants the dance of the mass of consciousness where the mind becomes still. It grants the dance of supreme light bestowed to attain the firm state, and it grants the open expanse of space. Becoming the supreme consciousness beyond all qualities and attributes, it rests at the crown of the great praising Vedas. It is the supreme Chidambaram. It is Siva Chidambaram, Siva Chidambaram.
commentary: This sacred space quiets the mind and grants a vision of divine light in motion. It exists beyond human descriptions, resting at the peak of ancient scriptures.

translit: nitti yamparā parani rātaram nirkku ṇañcatā nilaya niṭkaḷam catti yamkaṉā kaṉami kuntatōr taṟpa ramcivam camara cattuvam vitti yañcukō tayani kētaṉam vimalam eṉṟunāl vēta muntoḻum citti yaṅkuciṟ kaṉaci tamparam civaci tamparam civaci tamparam.
translation: It is eternal, the supreme of supremes, and self-supported. It is without attributes, the eternal abode, and indivisible. It is truth, the boundless mass of absolute reality, Siva, and the state of perfect harmony. It is the seed of knowledge and the abode where bliss arises. The four Vedas worship it as the immaculate. It is the Chidambaram of the mass of consciousness where divine powers function. It is Siva Chidambaram, Siva Chidambaram.
commentary: The divine space is self-sustaining, eternal, and free from limiting qualities. It is the harmony of truth and the seed from which all spiritual knowledge grows.

translit: aruḷa ḷittumey yaṉpar tammai-uḷ ḷaṅkai nellipōl ākku kiṉṟatum poruḷa ḷittunāṉ maṟaiyiṉ antamē pukalu kiṉṟatōr pukaḻa ḷippatum veruḷa ḷittiṭā vimala ñāṉavāṉ veḷiyi lēveḷi viravi niṟpatām teruḷa ḷippatum iruḷke ṭuppatum civaci tamparam civaci tamparam.
translation: Bestowing grace, it makes the truth as perfectly clear as a gooseberry on the palm of the hand for true devotees. Bestowing substance, it grants the glory praised by the very conclusion of the four Vedas. It grants the clarity of space merging entirely into the flawless expanse of celestial knowledge that never causes fear, and it destroys all darkness. It is Siva Chidambaram, Siva Chidambaram.
